decision.title: RCA: ACP panel — default "Manual" mode blocks every edit; no permissive default, no plan-mode alert
decision.rationale:
# RCA: ACP panel — default "Manual" mode blocks every edit; no permissive default, no plan-mode alert

## Summary

In the Maude Desktop ACP chat panel, every `Edit`/`Write` gets interrupted while `Read`/`Bash` pass — the exact symptom in the reported screenshot (Claude itself is confused: *"Edit je zablokovaný natvrdo… Write i Edit se přeruší pokaždé. Bash projde vždy"*). Root cause: **a fresh ACP session starts in Claude Code's `default` permission mode — displayed as "Manual" since Claude Code 2.1.200 — which requires a manual approve/deny decision for every file edit.** Maude sets **no** default permission mode at session creation, so the adapter's own default (`default`/Manual) always wins. This is a *deliberate* posture from [DDR-179](../../decisions/DDR-179-acp-permission-gate-retires-ddr125-f2.md) ("a user who wants zero interruption must explicitly select Bypass/Don't-Ask"), but it makes the out-of-box editing experience feel broken.

The ticket (+ the follow-up: *"bash taky musí fungovat default… a nebo mít interaktivní potvrzení když po mně chce ACP použít tools které nejsou allowed. Ale z našich design skill by mělo být jasné jaké tools defaultně povolit"*) asks for three things, mapped to three gaps:
1. **Default the panel to enough permissions to edit *and run its own tools*** — today it defaults to Manual (prompts for every edit AND every non-pre-approved `Bash`). The panel's workflow shells out to the `maude` CLI + design helpers constantly, so those must pass un-prompted. **Preferred solution: inject a curated `allowedTools` allow-list** (file tools + `Bash(maude …)`) sourced from what the design plugin actually invokes — *not* a blanket mode flip. This keeps the mode picker honest (no DDR-179 reversal) while making the design workflow frictionless.
2. **Anything NOT on the allow-list → interactive confirmation** — the approve/deny UI (`PermissionPrompt.jsx`) already exists and is wired; with a curated `allowedTools` it fires exactly for the un-listed surface (arbitrary `Bash`, WebFetch, unknown MCP) — precisely "pop a permission like `AskUserQuestion`". This is the ticket's own preferred shape.
3. **When in Plan mode (or any non-editing mode), show a highlighted alert in the panel** — today the *only* signal is a tiny composer footnote ("Manual — you'll be asked"); there is **no prominent banner** telling the user "you can't edit anything right now".

## Root Cause

### Why edits are blocked

The mode roster is defined by the bundled ACP adapter (`@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp`, `buildAvailableModes`):

| id | display name | behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `auto` | Auto | model classifier approves/denies (only if model supports) |
| **`default`** | **Manual** | *"Standard behavior, prompts for dangerous operations"* — **the out-of-box default** |
| `acceptEdits` | Accept Edits | *"Auto-accept file edit operations"* |
| `plan` | Plan Mode | *"Planning mode, no actual tool execution"* |
| `dontAsk` | Don't Ask | *"deny if not pre-approved"* |
| `bypassPermissions` | Bypass Permissions | bypass all checks (only if not root) |

The `"Manual"` label in the screenshot's bottom bar is the **`default` mode** (`acp-agent.js` `buildAvailableModes`: *"Claude Code 2.1.200 renamed this mode to 'Manual'… the wire id stays 'default'"*). Model = Opus, effort = Default, fast = Off round out the four selectors.

In `default`/Manual mode the adapter calls `requestPermission` for every non-pre-approved tool call. `Read` needs no permission; `Bash` passed because the user's own `~/.claude` allow-rules (Maude narrows `settingSources: ['user']`, `apps/studio/acp/bridge.ts:222`) pre-approve it. `Edit`/`Write` have no allow rule → each one raises a permission request. Those either surface the inline `PermissionPrompt` card (easy to miss / annoying to click per-edit) or, on turn-cancel / the 120 s `PERMISSION_TIMEOUT_MS` / the `MAX_PENDING_PERMISSIONS` cap, resolve to `cancelled` → "Tool use aborted" → the "přerušeno" the user saw.

### Why Maude never overrides it

- `newSessionParams()` (`apps/studio/acp/bridge.ts:205`) sets `_meta.claudeCode.options.settingSources` and `plugins` but **no `permissionMode`**. The adapter's `resolvePermissionMode(undefined)` returns `"default"`.
- The client's `loadPersistedPicks()` (`apps/studio/client/panels/ChatPanel.jsx:171`) returns `{}` when the user has never chosen a mode → `desiredModeId` stays `null` → `applyDesiredConfigOnce` (`bridge.ts:495`) skips `setSessionMode` → the session runs on the adapter default.

Net: **every fresh chat = Manual mode, unless the user manually picks another mode or has `permissions.defaultMode` in their own `~/.claude/settings.json`.** Confirmed by grep — no `defaultMode`/`acceptEdits`/`permissionMode` is set anywhere in `apps/studio/acp`, `apps/studio/client`, or `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src`.

### Why the user gets no clear signal

The current mode is only reflected by `modeFootnote()` (`ChatPanel.jsx:204`) — a one-line composer note ("Manual — you'll be asked" / "X — no prompts"). There is **no banner/alert** for the modes that actually *disable* editing:
- **`plan`** — "no actual tool execution": all edits are refused with no interactive approve path.
- **`dontAsk`** — "deny if not pre-approved": edits without an allow-rule are silently denied.

Grep of `ChatPanel.jsx` / `CapabilityBar.jsx` confirms only a usage banner, an error card, and the footnote exist — nothing mode-driven and prominent.

## Impact

- **Who:** every Maude Desktop user who opens the ACP chat panel and asks Claude to edit a canvas/file (or run any tool) without first hunting for the mode picker and switching off Manual. That's the default first-run path.
- **Severity:** High UX / "looks broken". The headline feature of the panel — "ask Claude to change my design" — appears not to work; even Claude-in-the-panel can't diagnose it and proposes ugly workarounds (write via `Bash node`). No data loss.
- **Workaround (today):** user manually opens the mode selector and picks **Bypass Permissions** (today the only mode where both edits *and* `Bash`/`maude` calls run un-prompted, since no allow-list is injected). Undiscoverable + over-broad — the ticket exists precisely because it isn't obvious.

## Proposed Fix

> ⚠️ **Touches a deliberate DDR — surface it, don't silently widen it.** [DDR-179](../../decisions/DDR-179-acp-permission-gate-retires-ddr125-f2.md) deliberately chose "no silent auto-approve by default; the mode picker must be honest," which itself retired [DDR-125](../../decisions/DDR-125-acp-multichat-parallel-and-security-posture.md) F2's blanket auto-approve (prompt-injected tool-call bursts from the DDR-054-untrusted served project). The curated allow-list below is a **narrow, defensible complement** to DDR-179 (pre-approve known first-party tooling; still prompt for everything else) — materially different from the blanket bypass DDR-179 killed — but it still needs a **DDR documenting the allow-list, its source of truth, and the residual**. It is NOT a mode flip and keeps the picker honest.

Three coordinated changes:

### 1. Inject a curated `allowedTools` allow-list, sourced from the design plugin  *(the core ask)*

The SDK's `allowedTools` (`sdk.d.ts:1331`: *"tool names auto-allowed without prompting… execute automatically without asking"*) is exactly the mechanism the follow-up describes. Keep the mode at `default`/Manual (**no DDR-179 reversal, picker stays honest**); auto-approve only the tools the design workflow actually uses, and let **every other tool fall through to the existing `PermissionPrompt`**.

- **The list (derive it, don't hand-freeze it):** per [DDR-062](../../decisions/DDR-062-plugins-reach-executable-logic-via-maude.md), *all* design-plugin executable logic is reached through **`maude design <verb>`** — so the Bash surface collapses to one scoped rule. Proposed seed:
  - File tools: `Read`, `Edit`, `Write`, `Glob`, `Grep`, `NotebookEdit`
  - Maude CLI: `Bash(maude:*)` (covers every `maude design screenshot|server-up|prep|slug|draw-*|canvas-rects|fetch-asset|probe-footage|…` verb + `maude config|init`) — verify the exact `allowedTools` specifier syntax (`Bash(maude:*)` prefix-match) against the installed SDK before shipping.
  - The design plugin's own `agent-browser`/`playwright`/`svgo` deps run *inside* `maude design …` (child processes of the Bash call), so they need **no** separate entry — the scoped `Bash(maude:*)` covers the whole helper surface. That's the payoff of DDR-062.
- **Source of truth (the user's key point — "z našich design skill by mělo být jasné"):** don't scatter a literal array. Derive/centralize it so it stays in sync with the plugin — a single exported constant next to `resolveSessionPlugins()`/`newSessionParams()`, cross-checked (a test) against `plugins/design/dependencies.json` + the `maude design` verb dispatch table (`cli/commands/design.mjs`). When a new `maude design <verb>` ships, `Bash(maude:*)` already covers it; only a genuinely new *tool* (not a maude verb) would need a list edit, and the test flags drift.
- **Where to inject:** add `options.allowedTools = MAUDE_DEFAULT_ALLOWED_TOOLS` in `newSessionParams()` (`apps/studio/acp/bridge.ts:222`, the same `options` object that already carries `settingSources`/`plugins`/`settings` and rides `_meta.claudeCode.options` → SDK via `...userProvidedOptions`). Confirm the adapter forwards `allowedTools` from that spread (it forwards `plugins`/`settings` the same way — should be free, but assert it in a test like `acp-session-plugins.test.ts` does for plugins).
- **Residual to document in the DDR:** `Edit`/`Write` auto-approve means injected *content* Claude reads could edit files unprompted — but edits land in the served project (already the edit target) and are reversible via `_history/` snapshots; and `Bash` is scoped to `maude:*` only, so arbitrary command execution (`rm`, `curl`, …) **still** prompts. That's a tight, defensible surface, not a blanket bypass.

### 2. Interactive confirmation for everything off the allow-list  *(ticket #2 — already built, just becomes the norm)*

`PermissionPrompt.jsx` already renders an inline approve/deny card (`ChatPanel.jsx:1642`), wired end-to-end (`bridge.ts:775 requestPermission` → `index.ts:190 permission-request` frame → client). With §1's `allowedTools` in place and the mode left at Manual, it fires **exactly** for the un-approved surface — the "interaktivní potvrzení když po mně chce ACP použít tools které nejsou allowed" the follow-up asks for. Small polish: the card sits at the bottom of the thread — confirm it's prominent enough (auto-scroll into view) and consider distinct copy for mode-changing (`ExitPlanMode`) decisions per the DDR-179 addendum follow-up. **No new plumbing** — the mechanism is done; §1 just makes it the everyday behavior instead of firing on every edit.

> Fallback (only if the maintainer wants zero prompts *ever*, incl. arbitrary Bash): default the mode to `bypassPermissions` (seed `picks.mode`, fall back to `acceptEdits` when `ALLOW_BYPASS` is off / root). That fully reverses DDR-179 and drops the interactive gate the follow-up explicitly wants — so the allow-list above is the recommended path; keep this only as the documented alternative in the DDR.

### 3. Prominent highlighted banner when the current mode blocks editing  *(ticket #3)*

Add a dismissible-but-sticky banner at the top of the chat thread (mirror `RateLimitBanner`, `role="status"`/`alert`) that renders when `caps.modes.currentModeId` is an edit-blocking mode:
- **`plan`** → e.g. *"Plan Mode — Claude is planning and won't edit files. Switch to Accept Edits to apply changes."* with an inline one-click switch to `acceptEdits`.
- **`dontAsk`** → *"Don't-Ask mode — edits without a pre-approval rule are denied silently."*
- Drive it purely off the mode id (`NO_EDIT_MODE_IDS = new Set(['plan','dontAsk'])`) so it stays truthful as the dynamic roster evolves — same discipline as `modeFootnote`.

**Files to change:** `apps/studio/acp/bridge.ts` (`newSessionParams` — inject `options.allowedTools`; the `MAUDE_DEFAULT_ALLOWED_TOOLS` constant + its drift test), `apps/studio/client/panels/ChatPanel.jsx` (new mode-banner component for #3), `apps/studio/client/styles/6-acp-chat.css` (banner styles), a new **DDR** (allow-list + source of truth + residual; noted as complementing DDR-179, not reversing it). After any client change: rebuild the committed release bundle (`cd apps/studio && MAUDE_SKIP_RUNTIME_BUILD=1 bun run build.ts --release`, commit `dist/client.bundle.js` + `dist/styles.css`) — whatever is committed is what ships.

## Testing Requirements

- **Unit:** `newSessionParams()` output carries `_meta.claudeCode.options.allowedTools` = the Maude set (`Read`/`Edit`/`Write`/`Glob`/`Grep`/`NotebookEdit` + `Bash(maude:*)`), and still carries `settingSources`/`plugins` unchanged — mirror `acp-session-plugins.test.ts`.
- **Drift test:** `MAUDE_DEFAULT_ALLOWED_TOOLS` stays in sync with the design plugin's tool surface — cross-check the `Bash(maude:*)` scope against `cli/commands/design.mjs`'s verb dispatch and `plugins/design/dependencies.json`, so a future helper that is NOT reached via `maude design` fails loudly instead of silently prompting.
- **Adapter contract test:** assert the installed adapter/SDK actually auto-approves an `allowedTools` entry (no `requestPermission` for a listed tool) AND still calls `requestPermission` for an *un*-listed tool (e.g. `Bash(curl …)`) — guards both directions against an adapter bump. Colocate with the `acp-*` bridge tests.
- **Unit:** banner predicate — renders for `plan`/`dontAsk`, absent for `default`/`acceptEdits`/`bypassPermissions`; the one-click switch sends the right `set-mode` frame.
- **Desktop E2E** (`apps/desktop/e2e/`, WebdriverIO — memory `feedback_prefer_dom_driven_e2e_not_computer_use`): fresh chat → ask Claude to edit the active canvas + run a `maude design` helper → assert both land with **no** permission card; ask for an off-list command → assert the `PermissionPrompt` appears; switch to Plan Mode → assert the highlighted banner appears. Add `data-testid` hooks (e.g. `chat-mode-banner`).
- Manual dogfood in the packaged `.app` (not just `tauri dev`) per memory `feedback_native_app_verification_ceiling`.

## Complexity

**Medium.** The code changes are small and localized (one `allowedTools` constant + injection, one banner component, two contract tests). The weight is the **DDR** — documenting the curated allow-list, its source of truth (design plugin), and the `Edit`/`Write` auto-approve residual, framed as complementing (not reversing) DDR-179. Get the allow-list scope + the `Bash(maude:*)` specifier syntax verified against the installed SDK first; the implementation is a short follow-on. The `bypassPermissions`-default fallback would be *lower* effort but reverses DDR-179 and drops the interactive gate the follow-up wants — so it's the alternative, not the plan.

decision.title: RCA: Maude Desktop is not self-contained on a fresh machine — ACP panel hangs (no node), install times out, and the bundled `maude` CLI can't run its helpers (no bun + broken pkgRoot)
decision.rationale:
# RCA: Maude Desktop is not self-contained on a fresh machine — ACP panel hangs (no node), install times out, and the bundled `maude` CLI can't run its helpers (no bun + broken pkgRoot)

_Reported by Michal on behalf of a real user (Martina Snášelová), 2026-07-15. Brand-new MacBook Air, no `node` / `npm` / `brew` / Claude Code preinstalled. Project path: `/Users/martinasnaselova/Martina Snášelová/vinarium_venuse`._

## Summary

On a machine with **no `node` on PATH**, Maude Desktop's ACP chat panel spawns the Claude Code ACP adapter with a runtime that cannot execute JavaScript, so the ACP handshake never happens and the panel spins at **"Working…" forever**. The culprit is `resolveAgentRuntime()` (`apps/studio/acp/probe.ts:164`): with no `node`, it falls back to `process.execPath`, which inside the `bun --compile` `maude-server` sidecar is **the sidecar binary itself, not a JS interpreter**. Spawning `[sidecar, adapterEntry]` just re-runs a second copy of the embedded dev-server (a compiled Bun binary only executes a passed script under `BUN_BE_BUN=1`), so the adapter never speaks ACP. `conn.initialize()` (`bridge.ts:466`) has **no timeout**, so the hang is silent and permanent. The user independently confirmed the diagnosis: **the panel started working the moment they ran `brew install node`** — which makes `Bun.which('node')` resolve and gives the adapter a real runtime.

A second, independent bug caused the earlier failure they saw: the in-app "Set up AI editing" installer reported **"Install timed out"** because the client-side poll cap (`INSTALL_POLL_MAX_MS = 90000`, `ReadinessList.jsx:95`) is shorter than the fresh-machine `claude.ai/install.sh` download, even though the server-side install is fire-and-forget and keeps running.

A **third cluster** (see "Second root-cause cluster" below) surfaced once the panel ran: the ACP agent reported it **could not run `maude design import-brand` / `import-asset`**. The desktop *does* bundle a `maude` CLI, but it is effectively non-functional on a fresh machine for three compounding reasons — a `pkgRoot` mismatch that makes the compiled `maude` unable to locate its own staged `.sh` helpers, a hard `bun` dependency in 15 of those helpers with no bundled `bun`, and a PATH-precedence rule that makes the broken bundled copy shadow any `maude` the user installs themselves. The net effect: the desktop app is **not actually self-contained** — it ships compiled binaries but not the `node`/`bun` runtimes its own code shells out to, contradicting the DDR-166 "zero-terminal / no manual install" promise.

## Evidence (from the 5 screenshots)

- **IMG_0867 / IMG_0868** — "AI editing isn't ready yet": Claude Code "Not found on PATH", "Installing Claude Code…" → **"Install timed out — you can also run the command below yourself."** The readiness list shows **"Claude agent bridge — Bundled — the chat panel can spawn it" with a green ✓** (misleading — see Contributing #2).
- **IMG_0870 (primary symptom)** — After manual install + login, the Assistant panel shows a `/design:setup-ds …` message and hangs at **"Working… 0:53"** with zero streamed output.
- **IMG_0871 (context)** — `claude` run in the terminal at `/Users/martinasnaselova/Martina Snášelová/vinarium_venuse` works fine (shows the folder-trust prompt, then runs). Terminal `claude` is the standalone native binary and never touches the adapter/node path — which is why it works while the panel does not.
- **IMG_0869 (out of scope, separate bug)** — local whisper model download fails: *"model download redirected off huggingface.co (cas-bridge.xethub.hf.co)"*.

## Root Cause

`apps/studio/acp/bridge.ts:400`
```ts
const proc = Bun.spawn([resolveAgentRuntime(), adapterEntry], { cwd, env, stdin:'pipe', stdout:'pipe', stderr:'pipe' });
```
`apps/studio/acp/probe.ts:164`
```ts
export function resolveAgentRuntime(): string {
  return process.env.MAUDE_ACP_RUNTIME || Bun.which('node') || process.execPath;
}
```

Runtime resolution order: `MAUDE_ACP_RUNTIME` (never set — confirmed absent from `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/sidecar.rs`, which sets `NO_OPEN`, `PATH`, `MAUDE_BUNDLED_CLI_PATH`, `MAUDE_AGENT_BROWSER`, `MAUDE_DEV_SERVER_BIN`, `MAUDE_CANVAS_ORIGIN_SPLIT` but **not** the ACP runtime) → `Bun.which('node')` (**null on a node-less machine**; the sidecar inherits the login-shell PATH, `sidecar.rs:153`) → **`process.execPath`**.

Inside the `bun --compile` sidecar, `process.execPath` is the compiled `maude-server` binary. A compiled Bun executable **does not run a script argument** — it runs its own embedded entrypoint and treats extra argv as data — unless `BUN_BE_BUN=1` is set. The adapter spawn sets no such env. So the "adapter" subprocess is actually a second `maude-server`, which never emits ACP ndJSON on stdout. `conn.initialize()` in `start()` (`bridge.ts:466`) awaits the handshake response with **no timeout** (unlike `loadSession`, which is guarded by `withTimeout` at `bridge.ts:303`), so `ensureStarted()` never resolves and the first `prompt()` hangs indefinitely → **"Working…" with no output, no error**.

### Reproduction of the mechanism (local smoke test)

Built a trivial `bun build --compile` binary and exercised the exact spawn shape:

```
$ ./myapp                 → EMBEDDED_APP_RAN;  execPath = .../myapp ;  argv = ["bun","/$bunfs/root/myapp"]
$ ./myapp other.js        → EMBEDDED_APP_RAN   (other.js IGNORED — just appended to argv)
$ BUN_BE_BUN=1 ./myapp other.js → OTHER_SCRIPT_RAN   (now the script actually runs)
```

This confirms: (1) `process.execPath` in a compiled binary is the binary, not `bun`; (2) `[compiledBinary, adapterEntry]` runs the embedded app and silently drops `adapterEntry`; (3) `BUN_BE_BUN=1` is what makes a compiled binary behave as the `bun` CLI. Combined with the user's "installed node → fixed" observation, the root cause is confirmed from both directions.

### Why this contradicts DDR-166 ("zero-terminal ACP cold start")

The panel is supposed to work on a fresh machine with no terminal setup, yet it silently depends on the user having installed `node` themselves. The `process.execPath` fallback was intended to mean "fall back to our own Bun" (per the doc comment in `probe.ts`) — correct in **dev** (where `process.execPath` is a real `bun` that runs scripts) but broken in the **compiled sidecar** (where it is the sidecar binary). The two production release binaries shipped with this latent break.

## Second root-cause cluster — the bundled CLI can't run on a fresh machine

The desktop **does** bundle a `maude` CLI: `tauri.conf.json` `externalBin` ships `binaries/maude` (a `bun --compile` binary), `sidecar.rs` stages it as a single-entry PATH dir and **prepends** it (DDR-166 T0b / DDR-168), and `stage-resources.mjs` copies the whole `apps/studio/` tree (all 33 `bin/*.sh` helpers included) into `Contents/Resources/`. Verified present in the installed v0.45.1 `.app`. Yet three compounding defects make it unusable:

### Gap 2 — compiled `maude` resolves `pkgRoot` to the wrong directory (breaks *every* `maude design <verb>`)

Reproduced on the real installed v0.45.1 `.app`:
```
$ /Applications/Maude.app/Contents/MacOS/maude --version
maude: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/Applications/Maude.app/Contents/MacOS/package.json'
$ /Applications/Maude.app/Contents/MacOS/maude design import-brand
maude design import-brand: helper not found at
  /Applications/Maude.app/Contents/MacOS/apps/studio/bin/import-brand.sh. Reinstall maude…
```
The binary lives at `Contents/MacOS/maude`; the staged assets live at `Contents/Resources/apps/studio/`. `resolvePkgRoot()` (`cli/lib/pkg-root.mjs`) walks up from `realpathSync(process.execPath)` looking for a dir with **both** `apps/studio/bin/screenshot.sh` **and** `cli/commands/design.mjs`. Walking up from `Contents/MacOS/` reaches `Contents/` → `Maude.app/` → `Applications/` — **none** is a valid `pkgRoot`, because (a) `apps/studio` sits under the *sibling* `Contents/Resources/`, not any ancestor, and (b) `cli/` is **not staged at all** (`cli/commands/design.mjs: NO` in the bundle). The walk-up therefore fails and falls through to `return dirname(process.execPath)` = `Contents/MacOS/`. Every `maude design <verb>` then dispatches to `Contents/MacOS/apps/studio/bin/<verb>.sh`, which does not exist.

The doc comment in `resolvePkgRoot()` (lines 66–68) asserts "matches the Tauri desktop layout too … share a common ancestor within the walk-up depth" — this is **false**: `Contents/` is the common ancestor, but `apps/studio` is under `Contents/Resources/`, not `Contents/`, and no `cli/` is staged, so `isPkgRoot` never matches. **Control:** `node cli/bin/maude.mjs design import-brand` (repo root = valid pkgRoot) reaches the helper correctly — so the CLI code is right; only the **bundle layout** is broken. This is the exact "green in `tauri dev`, broken in the packaged `.app`" class the `native-app verification ceiling` note warns about — `tauri dev`'s walk-up eventually reaches the real repo root, the `.app`'s never does.

### Gap 3 — 15 design helpers hard-depend on `bun`, which is not bundled

`import-asset.sh` / `import-brand.sh` / `import-tokens.sh` (and 12 others: `fetch-asset`, `handoff`, `annotate`, `draw-build`, `svg-optimize`, `ingest-footage`, `probe-footage`, `transcribe`, `audio-search`, `prep`, `server-up`, `ensure-browser`) all `exec bun run …_<verb>.mjs`. The import trio hard-exits if `bun` is absent:
```
import-brand.sh: bun is required (hard dependency — see plugins/design/dependencies.json).
```
`externalBin` ships **no `bun`** (only `maude-server`, `agent-browser`, `maude`), and `sidecar.rs` builds the helpers' PATH from the login shell + the bundled-maude link only. On a fresh machine (no `bun`), these helpers fail even once Gap 2 is fixed — confirmed by the ACP agent ("bun chybí — je to tvrdá závislost helperu"). Note the irony: `maude-server` and `maude` **are** compiled Bun, so a Bun-capable runtime is already in the bundle — just not exposed as `bun` to the helpers.

### Gap 4 — the broken bundled CLI shadows a user's own install

`sidecar.rs` **prepends** the bundled `maude` link to the ACP agent's PATH (DDR-168: "bundled copy is authoritative — a ceiling, not a floor"). So even after the user runs `npm i -g @1agh/maude@0.45.1` (whose npm layout resolves `pkgRoot` correctly and *does* ship the helpers), the agent's `maude` still resolves to the **broken** bundled binary first. The ACP agent diagnosed exactly this itself ("v PATH je na prvním místě bin-link z aplikace, jejíž adresář `apps/studio/bin/` vůbec neexistuje") and only got unblocked by calling the npm helper via an explicit absolute path. DDR-168's "bundled always wins" turns the Gap-2 bug into one the user cannot even work around by installing `maude` manually.

### Fix direction for the cluster

- **Gap 2:** stage `cli/` + a top-level `package.json` into `Contents/Resources/` so it becomes a valid `pkgRoot`, and have `sidecar.rs` set `MAUDE_PKG_ROOT=<…/Contents/Resources>` (the override branch already exists in `resolvePkgRoot`, gated on `isPkgRoot`). Alternatively, teach `resolvePkgRoot()` a desktop-aware probe of `dirname(execPath)/../Resources`. Add a bundled-`.app` assertion to the desktop-e2e / packaging check so this can't silently regress again.
- **Gap 3:** expose a Bun runtime to the helpers — cleanest is to reuse the already-bundled compiled binary as `bun` (a `maude-server`/`maude` invoked with `BUN_BE_BUN=1` behaves as the `bun` CLI — proven in the primary-cluster repro) via a `MAUDE_BUN`/PATH shim the `.sh` helpers honor, or ship a real `bun` externalBin. This is the **same underlying fix as Gap 1** (the ACP adapter's missing runtime): the desktop needs one bundled, self-contained JS runtime that both the adapter and the design helpers use, instead of depending on a user-installed `node`/`bun`.
- **Gap 4:** resolves once Gap 2/3 land (the bundled CLI actually works); until then, the prepend makes things strictly worse on a fresh machine.

## Impact

- **Severity: High.** Every user installing Maude Desktop on a machine without Node — i.e., the exact non-developer audience the product targets — gets a permanently-hung AI panel with no error and no guidance. The one visible readiness row for the bridge is a green checkmark, so nothing points at the cause. Workaround is undiscoverable without deep knowledge (`brew install node`).
- Secondary: the "Install timed out" message pushes users to a manual `curl | bash` that itself is flaky on a fresh box (the user needed two attempts — partly Anthropic's installer on a cold machine, but Maude's 90 s cap gives up while its own background install is still downloading).

## Proposed Fix

**Primary — give the adapter a real runtime that never depends on a user-installed node.** The sidecar already *is* Bun, so make the compiled-self fallback runnable instead of a footgun:

1. `apps/studio/acp/probe.ts` — have `resolveAgentRuntime()` signal when it is falling back to `process.execPath` (the compiled self), e.g. return `{ runtime, viaBunBeBun }` or expose a `runtimeNeedsBunBeBun()` helper. Prefer this bundled-bun path so ACP is self-contained per DDR-166 (drop the silent dependence on the user's `node`; keep `Bun.which('node')`/`MAUDE_ACP_RUNTIME` only as an explicit override).
2. `apps/studio/acp/bridge.ts:400` — when using the compiled-self fallback, set `env.BUN_BE_BUN = '1'` before `Bun.spawn([runtime, adapterEntry], { env, … })`. `BUN_BE_BUN` is a no-op on a normal `bun`/`node`, so it is safe to set on the fallback path unconditionally. Ships **zero extra bytes** and mirrors the dev path, which already runs the adapter under Bun successfully.

   _Verify:_ the adapter + `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` are "authored for Node" — must be confirmed working under Bun against a **real compiled build on a node-less machine** (or a PATH with `node` removed). Dev dogfooding already runs them under real Bun, so this is expected to hold; if a Bun/Node incompatibility surfaces in the SDK, fall back to option (Alt) below.

   _Alt (heavier, most robust):_ bundle a small standalone `node` (or a second `bun`) as a Tauri `externalBin` and have `sidecar.rs` pass its path via `MAUDE_ACP_RUNTIME`. Guarantees a Node runtime but adds a runtime to the bundle.

**Secondary — defense in depth (ship together):**

3. **Handshake timeout.** Wrap `conn.initialize()` in `start()` (`bridge.ts:466`) with the existing `withTimeout(...)` helper so a non-speaking adapter surfaces as a clear error ("AI editing couldn't start — …") instead of an infinite "Working…". This turns any future runtime regression from a silent hang into a diagnosable failure.
4. **Preflight runtime row.** `apps/studio/readiness.ts` currently checks `claude / maude / plugins / agent-browser / adapter` but **not a runnable ACP runtime**. Add a check that the adapter can actually run (real node/bun present, or the BUN_BE_BUN fallback wired) and flip the "Claude agent bridge" row to error/amber with remediation when it can't — so the green ✓ never lies again.
5. **Install poll cap.** `ReadinessList.jsx:95` `INSTALL_POLL_MAX_MS = 90000` is too short for the multi-hundred-MB `claude.ai/install.sh` on a fresh/slow network. Raise it substantially and/or key the deadline off the server-side install child still being alive (`getInstallState()` phase === 'running') rather than a fixed wall-clock, keeping an honest "Installing…" state instead of flipping to "timed out" while the download is still in flight.

**Out of scope (file separately):** IMG_0869 — local whisper model download rejects HuggingFace's 302 redirect to `cas-bridge.xethub.hf.co`. Different code path from `maude design fetch-asset`; own ticket.

## Testing Requirements

- **End-to-end, node-less:** on a machine (or CI leg / container) with `node` removed from PATH, launch the packaged `.app`, open a project, send an ACP prompt, and assert a real streamed response — the regression test for the whole class. The `apps/desktop/e2e/scenarios/acp-cold-start.e2e.ts` harness is the natural home; add a variant that stubs `Bun.which('node')` → null (or runs with a scrubbed PATH) and asserts the adapter still starts.
- **Unit:** `resolveAgentRuntime()` returns the BUN_BE_BUN-fallback signal when `node` is absent and `process.env.MAUDE_ACP_RUNTIME` is unset; returns `node`/override when present.
- **Unit:** `start()` rejects (not hangs) when the spawned adapter never completes the handshake within the timeout.
- **Unit/behavioral:** preflight reports the bridge as not-ready when no runnable runtime exists.
- **Behavioral:** install poll stays in "Installing…" while `getInstallState()` is `running`, and only errors on an actual `done`-with-error or a genuinely exceeded (raised) deadline.
- **Packaged-`.app` (Gap 2/3/4) — the whole class the current tests miss:** an assertion that runs against the **bundled `.app`** (not `tauri dev`): `Contents/MacOS/maude --version` prints the version (pkgRoot resolves), `maude design import-brand` reaches the helper's own usage/`bun`-check (not "helper not found"), and a design verb that shells to `bun` succeeds with no user-installed `bun` on PATH. Wire it into the desktop-e2e / packaging gate so "works in dev, broken in bundle" can't ship again.

## Complexity

**Medium.** The primary fix is a few lines (`probe.ts` + `bridge.ts` + `BUN_BE_BUN`), but it must be verified against a real compiled, node-less build (the exact gap that let this ship), and the SDK-under-Bun assumption needs confirming. The defense-in-depth items (timeout, preflight row, install cap) are small and independent.

decision.title: RCA: ACP chat panel — background subagent activity is invisible after the turn "ends"
decision.rationale:
# RCA: ACP chat panel — background subagent activity is invisible after the turn "ends"

> Manual RCA (no tracker ticket). Reported 2026-07-03 via `/flow:bug-rca`.
> Symptom (user, paraphrased): *"In the ACP panel you can't tell that subagents are running in the background — when the turn ends it looks like nothing is happening. While subagents run, the 'working' spinner should stay up. Anything running in the background that the main agent waits on should be visualised."*

## Summary

The Maude native ACP chat panel already has the machinery to show live work — `acp-runtime.js` tracks in‑flight tool calls (`activeTools`, `onActivity`) and turn‑busy (`onBusy`), and `ChatPanel.jsx` renders three "Working…" indicators. **None of them is the bug.** The bug is that the panel treats the ACP `turn-end` frame as *"everything is done"*, but the `claude-agent-acp` adapter (≥ 0.49.0, issue #773 behaviour) **resolves the prompt turn at the main agent's first `result` — before background subagents finish.** Every in‑feed activity indicator is gated on assistant‑ui's `isRunning`, which flips to `complete` the moment our adapter generator returns at `turn-end`. So when the main agent stops but spawned subagents keep churning, the panel goes fully idle ("Ready"), the activity list is force‑cleared, and — worse — the subagents' subsequent output is dropped from the live feed.

This is **not** a missing feature and **not** a recent regression (the `ActivityBar` + `isRunning` gating shipped in the original phase‑26–32 desktop PR `188efc5`). It is a lifecycle mismatch between three layers, confirmed from source in all three.

## Empirical confirmation (2026-07-03 — live `/design:critic` repro)

A real repro on `pnpm dev:desktop` (project `~/git2/maude-git-smoke`, chat `c-mr4ncplt-fqufn`) turned the code-level RCA into ground truth. Transcript timeline:

- **10:05:14** user runs `/design:critic`.
- **10:06:39–10:07:35** the main agent spawns **9 `Agent`-tool subagents** (the critics — `toolName:"Agent"`, `kind:"think"`, `title:"Task"`; confirms `isSubagentTool`'s Task/Agent check), and all 9 top-level `Agent` tool_calls report `completed` (dispatch-ack) by 10:07:35.
- **10:07:43 `stop` (end_turn)** — the ACP prompt settles here, on the message *"All 9 critic agents are running in the background. I'll be notified as they complete, then consolidate…"*.
- **10:07:43 → ~10:17:23** the substantive work streams **after the stop**: **98 nested tool_calls** (`parentToolUseId` set — the critics reading/writing their `critique/001-*` reports) + **11 top-level** (the main agent consolidating) + **105 `agent_message_chunk` text frames** = **5,467 chars** of running commentary AND the **fully-completed panel report** (9 ranked blockers, aspiration axis 4.3/5, clean panels, the `001-PANEL.md` path, and the recommended `/design:edit … --perfect` next step).
- No `stop` bounds that post-settle output; the next `stop` is only at **10:21:29**, after the user's unrelated 2nd prompt.

**Verdict flip:** the `/design:critic` loop **works end-to-end** — 9 critics ran, all reported, the consolidation completed, `001-PANEL.md` was written to disk. The user saw **none of it**: everything after 10:07:43 arrived with the client's `turnHandler` already `null` (the prompt generator returned at `turn-end`) and was **dropped** at `acp-runtime.js:87`. The panel with 9 blockers went to `/dev/null`-on-screen (kept only in the transcript). So **facet F2 (dropped live output) is not a latent edge case — it IS the bug the user reports**; F1 (spinner vanishes) is the milder symptom on top.

**Recoverable on reload (verified):** `readChatMessages` (`transcript.ts:124-182`) flushes on `stop` and starts a **new** assistant message for the post-stop chunks, so reopening the chat reconstructs the full panel report as a second assistant bubble. Immediate user workaround: reopen the chat (or read `.design/_history/ui-project-pricing/critique/001-PANEL.md`).

**Fix implication:** Stage 1 (committed — keep the activity indicator alive) is **necessary but insufficient** here — it would show intermittent "Working…" during the drain but still render none of the 5,467-char answer. **Stage 2 (do not drop post-`turn-end` frames — stream them into an appended assistant bubble, exactly as the transcript loader already models) is the real fix and is now the priority, not a follow-up.**

## Root Cause

The failure is a chain across the adapter, assistant‑ui, and our own glue. Each link is confirmed from code (not inferred):

### Link 1 — the adapter settles the turn early, by design

`@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp@0.49.0` → `dist/acp-agent.js`:

- The user turn is settled at the **first non‑cancelled `result`** message, with **no check that outstanding tool calls have completed** (`settleActive(...)` at `acp-agent.js:1188-1189`; the whole `result` handler `1042-1191` never inspects `toolUseCache`).
- The SDK's true "everything is done" signal — the trailing `idle` — is **deliberately absorbed, not used to settle** (`869-885`). The code's own comment: *idle "can lag (the SDK flushes held‑back results / **drains background agents** first)"* (`872-875`).
- `task-notification`‑origin messages (autonomous follow‑up work a background agent triggers) are **excluded from the turn lifecycle entirely** — every stopReason / usage / settle side‑effect is guarded `!isTaskNotification` (`1042-1047`, `1188`).
- The Task/Agent subagent tool itself is emitted as an ordinary `tool_call` with `kind:"think"`, `title` = the subagent's `description` (or literal `"Task"`), `status:"pending"` (`tools.js:16-34`, `acp-agent.js:3341-3358`). Its `tool_call_update: completed` fires **only** when its `tool_result` arrives (`acp-agent.js:3363-3435`, status stamped at `3432`) — there is no early/spawn‑time completion.
- The adapter's consumer **stays alive after settle** and keeps forwarding `tool_call` / `tool_call_update` / `agent_message_chunk` for the still‑running background agent (`acp-agent.d.ts:72-75`; comment `1184`).

**⇒ `prompt()` / `stopReason` resolves while background (or `task-notification`‑origin) subagents are still running.** For a strictly *synchronous inline* Task whose `tool_result` precedes the `result`, turn‑end correctly fires after it finishes — but nothing in the adapter guarantees that ordering, and modern Claude Code runs subagents in the background by default ("subagents run in the background… you'll be notified when one completes"), which is exactly the early‑settle path.

### Link 2 — assistant‑ui `isRunning` is bound to our generator's lifetime

`@assistant-ui/core@0.2.18` (re‑exported by `@assistant-ui/react@0.14.23`):

- For `useLocalRuntime`, `isRunning` is **not a stored flag** — it is derived as *"the last assistant message's `status.type === "running"`"* (`runtime/api/thread-runtime.ts:207-211`).
- That status is set `running` before the adapter is consumed (`local-thread-runtime-core.ts:329,483-487`) and flipped to `complete` **only after the `for await` over our `run()` generator exits** (`:533-534`). Yields without an explicit `status` preserve `running` (`:438`). There is **no idle/stall timer** and **no "no new content ⇒ complete" heuristic** on the local path.

**⇒ `isRunning` stays true exactly as long as our `run()` generator is iterating, and drops the instant it returns.** (Investigator note: a *paused* generator keeps `isRunning` true — so the idle UI is **not** explained by a stall; it's explained by the generator actually *returning*.)

### Link 3 — our glue equates `turn-end` with "all done" and then discards background frames

`apps/studio/client/panels/acp-runtime.js` + `ChatPanel.jsx`:

- `conn.prompt()` (the adapter‑facing async generator) **returns on the `turn-end` frame** (`acp-runtime.js:167-208`). `index.ts` sends exactly one `turn-end` right after `await bridge.prompt()` resolves (`acp/index.ts:204-206`) — i.e. at Link 1's early settle. So our generator returns early → Link 2 flips the message to `complete` → **`isRunning=false`**.
- **All three in‑feed indicators gate on `isRunning`** and therefore vanish together: `StatusRow` (`ChatPanel.jsx:325-336`), `ActivityBar` (`:342-352`, `if (!running) return null`), composer stop‑bar (`:741-752`).
- **Self‑inflicted amplifier A:** `trackActivity` **force‑clears `activeTools` on `turn-end`** (`acp-runtime.js:62-67`), so even the "what's running" list is wiped at the premature end.
- **Self‑inflicted amplifier B (latent output loss):** after the generator's `finally`, `turnHandler=null` (`:205`). Background frames still arrive (`onFrame` runs `trackActivity` unconditionally) but are **dropped at `if (turnHandler) turnHandler(frame)`** (`:87`) → the subagent's continued `agent_message_chunk` text + tool results **never render in the live feed**.
- The menubar "Assistant working" badge and the **"finished" notification** are also driven off `onBusy`/turn‑end (`ChatPanel.jsx:1020-1027`), so the user can even get a *"done"* ping while subagents are still working.

**Net:** main agent stops → `turn-end` → `isRunning=false` → StatusRow shows "Ready", ActivityBar unmounts, stop‑bar reverts to the composer, `activeTools` is cleared, and any further subagent output is dropped live. Precisely *"vypadá to, že se nic neděje."*

## Impact

- **Who:** every native desktop (and web‑serve) ACP chat user, whenever the agent uses background subagents — the common case with Claude Code's default background Task behaviour.
- **Severity:** **Medium.** Two facets:
  1. **Visibility (the report):** background subagent work is invisible; the panel looks hung/idle and even signals "done" prematurely. Pure UX, high annoyance, erodes trust ("is it stuck?").
  2. **Live output loss (latent, surfaced by this RCA):** post‑turn‑end subagent output is dropped from the live feed. **Not permanent data loss** — the bridge still writes every update to the transcript (`_chat/<id>.jsonl` via `appendTranscript`), so it replays as `initialMessages` on the next panel reload. But in the live session it silently disappears.
- **Workaround today:** none in‑session; reopen/reload the panel to see the transcript‑replayed tail.

## Proposed Fix

The adapter's early settle is **intentional** (issue #773: unlock the composer as soon as the main answer is done, don't make the user wait for background drain). So the fix is **not** to defer `turn-end` / re‑lock the composer — that would undo #773. The fix is to **decouple "is background work still happening" from `isRunning`, keep it visible while the composer stays unlocked**, and stop discarding background frames.

**Stage 1 — Visibility (addresses the report; Low/Medium, client‑only, no server/protocol change):**

1. `acp-runtime.js` — **stop force‑clearing `activeTools` on `turn-end`** (`:62-67`); let the list be driven purely by `tool_call` / `tool_call_update` (add on call, remove on completed/failed). Clear only on `error` and socket close. `trackActivity` already runs on every frame regardless of `turnHandler`, so background subagent tool calls keep updating the list post‑turn‑end.
2. `acp-runtime.js` — expose a derived **`backgroundActive`** signal (e.g. `activeTools.size > 0`, optionally also "an `update` frame arrived < N s after turn‑end") via a subscription, so the client has a truth‑source for "the main agent is still waiting on something" independent of `isRunning`.
3. `ChatPanel.jsx` — render the activity indicator on **`isRunning || backgroundActive`** instead of `isRunning` alone. Keep the **composer** on `isRunning` (preserve #773 — it unlocks at turn‑end). Classify **subagents distinctly** (Task/Agent ⇒ `kind:"think"`, `title` = description) and label them explicitly, e.g. *"◇ 2 subagenti běží · 0:42"* with a live spinner, so a quiet 60–90 s stretch reads as "actively working," not "hung."
4. `6-acp-chat.css` — style the persistent background indicator; respect `prefers-reduced-motion` (existing pattern at `:988-996`).
5. Suppress/adjust the premature **"finished" notification** + menubar badge so they fire at true quiescence, not at the main‑agent settle when `backgroundActive` is true.

**Stage 2 — Live output recovery (addresses the latent facet; Medium/High, optional follow‑up):**

Route post‑turn‑end `update` frames into the feed instead of dropping them at `turnHandler=null`. Options: (a) append them as a follow‑up assistant message via the runtime API, or (b) a small server frame‑protocol change (`acp/index.ts`) that tags background/`task-notification` updates and a client sink that renders them. Requires care around assistant‑ui's completed‑message model. Gate this on whether users actually hit dropped‑output in practice (transcript replay already recovers it on reload).

### Files to change

| File | Change | Stage |
| ---- | ------ | ----- |
| `apps/studio/client/panels/acp-runtime.js` | don't clear `activeTools` on `turn-end`; expose `backgroundActive` / `onBackground` | 1 |
| `apps/studio/client/panels/ChatPanel.jsx` | gate indicators on `isRunning \|\| backgroundActive`; subagent classification + richer label; keep composer on `isRunning`; fix premature finished‑ping | 1 |
| `apps/studio/client/styles/6-acp-chat.css` | persistent background‑activity indicator styles (+ reduced‑motion) | 1 |
| `apps/studio/acp/index.ts` (+ `acp-runtime.js`) | optional: tag + route post‑turn background frames for live render | 2 |
| `apps/studio/dist/client.bundle.js` + `dist/styles.css` | rebuild committed bundle release‑minified (`cd apps/studio && MAUDE_SKIP_RUNTIME_BUILD=1 bun run build.ts --release`) | 1 |

## Testing Requirements

- **Unit (`bun:test`, `apps/studio/test/`):** extract the activity/subagent classification from `acp-runtime.js` into a pure function and test the frame sequence: `tool_call(Task)` → `turn-end` → later `tool_call_update(completed)`. Assert the Task **stays** in `activeTools` across `turn-end` (guards the amplifier‑A fix) and that a Task‑kind call is classified as a subagent. (Client `.js` panel modules are already unit‑tested this way — cf. `chat-context.test.ts`, `slash-commands.test.ts`.)
- **Component:** `ActivityBar` renders when `backgroundActive && !isRunning`.
- **Live (native panel — per the native‑app‑verification ceiling):** in the ACP panel, prompt something that spawns background subagents; confirm the "◇ N subagenti běží" indicator + spinner persist after the main agent's text finishes, the composer is usable meanwhile, and the indicator clears only when subagents actually finish. Optional confirmation capture: read `.design/_chat/<id>.jsonl` and check `role:'stop'` timestamp lands **before** the subagents' `tool_call_update: completed` (empirically re‑confirms the early settle).

## Complexity

**Medium** overall. Stage 1 (the reported visibility bug) is **Low/Medium** — client‑only, ~2 files + CSS + bundle rebuild, no server/protocol change, preserves the #773 composer‑unlock UX. Stage 2 (live recovery of dropped background output) is **Medium/High** and optional — recommend shipping Stage 1 first, then deciding on Stage 2 from real usage.

---

### Evidence appendix (source citations)

- **Adapter early settle:** `claude-agent-acp@0.49.0/dist/acp-agent.js:1042-1191` (result handler, `settleActive` `1188-1189`, no tool‑state gate), `869-885` (idle absorbed, "drains background agents first" `872-875`), `1042-1047` (`isTaskNotification` excluded), `tools.js:16-34` + `acp-agent.js:3341-3358` (Task ⇒ `kind:think`, pending), `3363-3435` (completed only at tool_result), `acp-agent.d.ts:72-75` (consumer kept alive, forwards background output).
- **assistant‑ui `isRunning`:** `@assistant-ui/core@0.2.18/.../runtime/api/thread-runtime.ts:207-211` (derived from last‑message status), `runtimes/local/local-thread-runtime-core.ts:329,438,483-487,519-537` (running set/preserved; `complete` flip only after `for await` exits `:533-534`); no idle timer / no auto‑status on local path.
- **Our glue:** `apps/studio/client/panels/acp-runtime.js:62-67` (force‑clear on turn‑end), `:86-87` (trackActivity unconditional, turnHandler‑gated dispatch), `:167-208` (prompt generator ends on turn‑end; `finally` nulls turnHandler), `apps/studio/acp/index.ts:204-206` (single `turn-end` after settle); `apps/studio/client/panels/ChatPanel.jsx:325-352` (StatusRow/ActivityBar gated on `isRunning`), `:741-752` (composer stop‑bar), `:886-900` (activeTools state + bottom‑of‑feed ActivityBar), `:1020-1027` (busy → finished ping / menubar).

decision.title: RCA: Artboard content reacts to studio-chrome resize (and font size shifts on zoom)
decision.rationale:
# RCA: Artboard content reacts to studio-chrome resize (and font size shifts on zoom)

> **CONFIRMED + FIXED (2026-07-02).** Read the actual mock (`~/git/maude-hub-test/repo-a/.design/ui/project/Pricing.tsx`) — root cause is exactly two viewport `@media (max-width: 1024px/768px)` blocks in the hero CSS (lines 266–267). A headless A/B reproduced all three reported states — radar inline (iframe ≥1024), radar stacked+shrunk (768–1024), radar `display:none` (<768). Fix: a **named `@container pr`** scoped to the fixed 1280px `.pr-surface` box replaces the `@media` queries → the hero resolves against the artboard width, never the studio iframe. Verified identical at 1440/900/700px iframe widths, radar never hidden. The DCArtboard is `width={1280}`, so the breakpoints simply never fire now. **Process note:** the first pass of this RCA reasoned from the engine without reading the mock — the diagnosis was right but the "fix" (maude-side hardening) never touched the broken file and wasn't in the user's compiled binary, so the bug persisted. Lesson: read the failing artifact first.

> Ticket source: manual paste (2 screenshots). Original (cs): *"jak je možný že artboard reaguje na rozšíření studio chrome? … fonty lehce mění velikost když dělám zoom. Cokoliv uvnitř artboardu by vůbec nemělo reagovat na žádný pan/zoom/canvas width/sidebar open atd."*

## Summary

The artboard **container** is correctly isolated — `.dc-artboard` is a fixed-pixel box (`width: rect.w`, `height: rect.h`) positioned in world coordinates, and pan/zoom is a single transform on the world plane. But the **content authored inside** a mock is not isolated, because it uses CSS constructs that resolve against the **iframe viewport** rather than the artboard box:

- **`@media` breakpoints** (Tailwind `md:` / `lg:` / `sm:` prefixes, raw `@media (min-width: …)`) — these evaluate against the iframe viewport width.
- **Viewport units** (`vw`, `vh`, `svh`, `dvh`, `vmin`, `vmax`; Tailwind `min-h-screen` / `h-screen` / `w-screen`; `clamp(…, Nvw, …)` fluid type) — these always resolve against the iframe viewport, and **no ancestor property can re-root them**.

The canvas iframe **is** the studio's canvas stage. Widening the Assistant panel, toggling the sidebar, or the offline banner appearing/disappearing changes the iframe's viewport dimensions. That flips media-query breakpoints and recomputes viewport-unit lengths **inside** the artboard — so the mock re-lays-out even though the engine's zoom never changed (both screenshots are at 38 %). The dramatic reflow in the two screenshots (the radar graphic moving from inline-right of the hero to stacked-below-and-larger) is a **breakpoint flip**, not a continuous scale.

The secondary symptom — *"fonts slightly change size when I zoom"* — is a separate, zoom-triggered re-rasterization effect in the world-transform engine (details below).

## Root Cause

### Primary — mock content resolves against the iframe viewport, not the artboard

The isolation invariant the user expects ("nothing inside the artboard should react to pan/zoom/canvas width/sidebar") holds for the **frame chrome** but is **not enforced for author content**. Verified facts from `apps/studio/canvas-lib.tsx`:

1. **Artboard is a fixed-size box.** `DCArtboard` renders `<article … style={{ left, top, width: rect.w, height: rect.h }}>` (canvas-lib.tsx:1740). The container's size never tracks the iframe. ✔
2. **The engine does not re-fit on chrome resize.** The initial-fit `ResizeObserver` is **one-shot** — it only fires when the host first gains a size (`if (!hadSize && host.clientWidth > 0 …)`, canvas-lib.tsx:928-937). Once `hadSize` is true, later resizes (panel widen, sidebar toggle) never re-fit and never change zoom. This matches both screenshots showing **38 %**. So the reflow is **not** an engine-driven viewport/zoom change.
3. **No containment context on the artboard.** There is **no** `container-type`, `contain`, or `@container` anywhere in canvas-lib (`.dc-artboard-body` is just `flex: 1; position: relative; overflow: hidden;`, canvas-lib.tsx:255-258). So the artboard is not a containment root — `@media` and `vw/vh` inside it fall through to the iframe viewport.
4. **A transformed ancestor re-roots `position: fixed` but NOT `@media`/`vw/vh`.** `.dc-world` carries `transform` + `will-change: transform` (canvas-lib.tsx:210-221), which makes it the containing block for `position: fixed` descendants — so fixed positioning is already contained and is **not** the escape. Viewport units and media queries are unaffected by any ancestor `transform` / `zoom` / `contain` — by spec they resolve against the viewport. There is no CSS mechanism to redirect them to a nested box.

**Net:** any mock authored with responsive breakpoints or viewport units is wired directly to the studio's canvas-stage dimensions. Changing studio chrome changes those dimensions → the artboard reflows. This repo's own canvases (`.design/ui/*.tsx`) mostly avoid these constructs and therefore **don't** reflow — confirming this is a content/authoring escape the engine doesn't guard against, not an engine regression. The affected `Pricing.tsx` lives in the downstream project (`repo-a`).

### Secondary — zoom re-rasterizes text ("fonts change size on zoom")

The world-plane zoom takes a per-engine path (`writeTransform`, canvas-lib.tsx:710-727):

- **Blink (Chrome):** CSS `zoom: N`. `zoom` is layout-affecting — the browser re-flows and re-rasterizes text at each zoom step (chosen deliberately for crispness at high zoom, comment at 688-693). Side effect: glyphs re-hint / can re-wrap slightly between zoom levels → perceived size change. If the mock also uses `vw`-based fluid type, that compounds here.
- **WebKit (Safari + Tauri WKWebView shell, `IS_WEBKIT`):** `transform: translate() scale()`, with the compositor layer **released on settle** (`will-change: auto`, canvas-lib.tsx:706-708, 762-766) so WebKit re-rasterizes text crisply at the settled scale. That settle-time re-raster can produce a subtle sub-pixel hinting shift → the same perceived "font size wobble."

Either path re-rasterizes text as a function of zoom, which is what the user observes. This is largely inherent to raster-scaling a design surface; it is a fidelity trade-off, not a correctness break, and is **independent** of the primary reflow bug.

### Hypotheses considered and eliminated

| Hypothesis | Verdict | Disconfirming / confirming evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Engine auto-refits zoom on chrome resize | **Eliminated** | ResizeObserver refit is one-shot (canvas-lib.tsx:928-937); both screenshots are 38 % |
| `position: fixed` in mock escapes to viewport | **Eliminated** | `.dc-world` transform re-roots fixed positioning (canvas-lib.tsx:210-221) |
| Continuous `vw/vh` scaling | **Contributing** | No containment root; `vw/vh` resolve against iframe viewport |
| `@media` breakpoint flip | **Confirmed (dominant for the dramatic reflow)** | Radar moves inline→stacked = layout-mode change, not continuous scale; media queries resolve against iframe viewport |

The two content hypotheses are not mutually exclusive — the mock almost certainly uses both. **Distinguishing experiment:** slowly drag the Assistant panel wider. A `@media` cause snaps at a threshold (discrete layout change); a pure `vw` cause scales continuously. The screenshots show a snap → breakpoints are the primary driver, viewport units a secondary contributor.

## Impact

- **Who:** every user viewing a canvas whose mock uses responsive breakpoints or viewport units (i.e. most full-page landing/marketing/app-shell mocks). Affects both the web browser and the native desktop shell.
- **Severity:** Medium. No data loss; purely visual/fidelity. But it undermines the core promise of a design canvas — that a frame renders identically regardless of workspace chrome — and makes screenshots / exports non-deterministic w.r.t. panel state.
- **Workaround (today):** author mocks at a fixed design width with fixed-px / `%` layout and no viewport units; keep the Assistant panel/sidebar at a constant width when comparing or exporting.

## Proposed Fix

Two independent problems → two tracks. Recommend Tier 1 now; Tier 2 as a follow-up DDR if a hard guarantee is required.

### Tier 1 — enforce artboard isolation for author content (recommended, pragmatic)

1. **Establish a containment root on the artboard body (engine).** Add `container-type: inline-size` (or `size`) to `.dc-artboard-body` in `ENGINE_CSS` (canvas-lib.tsx ~255). The body already has a definite size (`rect.h`), so this is safe. This unlocks the *isolated* responsive path: authors use `@container` / `cqw` / `cqh`, which resolve against the artboard box, not the iframe — the reflow disappears while responsive design still works.
   - Files: `apps/studio/canvas-lib.tsx` (ENGINE_CSS), then rebuild committed bundles per CLAUDE.md rebuild rule.
2. **Ban viewport-relative constructs in canvas mocks (lint/guard).** Add a check to `/design:smoke` and/or `design-system-keeper` that greps `<designRoot>/ui/*.tsx` for artboard-isolation violations: `\b(vw|vh|vmin|vmax|svh|dvh|lvh|svw|dvw)\b`, Tailwind `(min-|max-)?[hw]-screen`, `text-\[[^\]]*v[wh]\]`, `clamp\([^)]*v[wh]`, and raw `@media (min-width` inside a canvas. Emit a warning (blocker if it stacks) with the container-query remedy.
   - Files: `plugins/design/skills/design-system/*` (smoke) + `plugins/design/agents/design-system-keeper.md`.
3. **Update generator guidance.** In `plugins/design/commands/new.md` + the `frontend-design` skill prompt, add an explicit hard-stop: *"Artboard content is self-contained at a fixed design width. Never use viewport units (`vw/vh`, `min-h-screen`, `h-screen`, `w-screen`) or `@media` width breakpoints — they resolve against the studio viewport and make the artboard reflow with the panel/sidebar. Use fixed px, `%`, `h-full` against the sized artboard body, or `@container`/`cqw` for responsiveness."*
4. **Fix the specific `Pricing.tsx`** (repo-a, not this repo): swap `min-h-screen`/`h-screen` → artboard-fixed height / `h-full`; `w-screen`/`vw` widths → `%`/px; responsive `md:`/`lg:` prefixes → `@container` equivalents; `vw` fluid type → fixed rem or `cqw`. (Run via `/design:edit` in repo-a.)

### Tier 2 — hard isolation guarantee (optional, phase-sized, needs a DDR)

To make *any* author CSS obey the invariant regardless of discipline, render each artboard's content in a **nested same-origin iframe** sized to `rect.w × rect.h` and scaled by the world transform. Then `@media`, `vw/vh`, and `position: fixed` all resolve against the artboard box → true isolation. This is a significant refactor (DOM selection/inspection, HMR broadcast, coordinate mapping, comments/annotations overlay, and drag all cross the new iframe boundary) and should be its own plan + DDR, not a quick fix.

### Zoom re-rasterization (secondary symptom)

Largely inherent. If it must be reduced: (a) fixing the `vw` fluid type via Tier 1 removes the zoom-coupled component on the Blink path; (b) unifying both engines on `transform: scale` would stop layout reflow on zoom entirely, but reverses a deliberate crispness decision (Blink CSS-`zoom` was chosen for sharp text at high zoom) — that needs its own DDR. Recommend documenting it as a known trade-off unless Tier 1 alone doesn't satisfy the user.

## Testing Requirements

- **Engine:** with `container-type` added, a canvas mock using `@container`/`cqw` must render identically at panel-open vs panel-closed. Add a `desktop-e2e` / `agent-browser` scenario: open a canvas, screenshot, widen the Assistant panel, screenshot, assert the artboard DOM layout is unchanged (pixel-diff of the artboard region, chrome excluded).
- **Lint:** unit test the smoke/keeper regex against a fixture canvas containing each banned construct (must flag) and a clean container-query canvas (must pass).
- **Regression guard:** ensure the one-shot refit still fits correctly on first mount (don't let `container-type: size` collapse the body to 0 height — verify artboards still render at their `rect.h`).

## Complexity

**Tier 1: Low–Medium** (one engine CSS line + bundle rebuild, one lint rule, guidance edits, one downstream mock fix). **Tier 2: High** (nested-iframe architecture, separate DDR + phase).

decision.title: RCA: Can CI safely regenerate `apps/studio/dist/runtime/*.js` instead of committing it?
decision.rationale:
# RCA: Can CI safely regenerate `apps/studio/dist/runtime/*.js` instead of committing it?

## Summary

The v0.22.0 incident (a 13 kB stub `motion_react.js` shipped instead of the working 155 kB+ bundle) was blamed on "Bun.build's output being environment-sensitive," and the team worked around it by committing the runtime bundles to git and setting `MAUDE_SKIP_RUNTIME_BUILD=1` in CI (`.github/workflows/build-binaries.yml`, `publish-main` job). That workaround is sound, but "environment-sensitive" undersells the actual cause: **Bun.build itself isn't nondeterministic given identical inputs — the inputs (the resolved `node_modules` tree) are unpinned**, so different machines/CI runs can legitimately resolve a different `motion` version and get a differently tree-shaken bundle. Two compounding gaps make this possible today, and both are still present.

## Root Cause

Two unpinned inputs feed `bun install` → `Bun.build` for `apps/studio`:

1. **`apps/studio/bun.lock` is gitignored** (`.gitignore:75`). Per DDR-176, `apps/studio` has its own package-manager root, independent of the pnpm workspace at the repo root — but unlike a normal Bun/npm project, its lockfile is never committed. The CI workflow comment says this explicitly:

   > `Drop --frozen-lockfile: bun.lock is gitignored and gets generated on whatever host first ran it.`

   Without a committed lockfile, every `bun install` (local dev, every CI matrix cell, every contributor machine) re-resolves the dependency graph from the semver ranges in `apps/studio/package.json`. Two runs on two different days — or two runners in the same CI matrix if package registries serve slightly different states — can land on different exact versions of `motion` and its transitive deps.

2. **`motion` is a caret range** (`apps/studio/package.json:55` → `"motion": "^12.42.2"`). `motion`/`framer-motion` ships internal code paths (e.g. `AcceleratedAnimation`) that are conditionally exported / dead-code-eliminated by the bundler depending on the exact package version's internal module graph. A caret range means any `12.x.y` with `x ≥ 42` is eligible — a legitimate patch/minor release of `motion` upstream, resolved on one machine but not another (because the other machine cached an older resolution or ran `bun install` before the new version was published), is enough to change what Bun.build's tree-shaker decides is reachable. That's the actual mechanism behind the 13 kB vs 155 kB divergence: not the bundler misbehaving, but the bundler correctly bundling two genuinely different inputs.

`bun-version: '1.3.x'` in the three workflow files (`build-binaries.yml`, plus two more) is a secondary, smaller source of drift — a floating minor pin means CI could pick up a new Bun patch release with different bundler internals mid-cycle, independent of any dependency change.

The `check-runtime-bundles.sh` floor-check (comparing on-disk bundle size to `.min-sizes.json`) is a good regression gate, but it's a symptom-level catch (would only fail loud on the *next* accidental regen with a bad resolve) — it does not address why the resolve differs across environments in the first place.

## Impact

- **Current state (bundles committed, `MAUDE_SKIP_RUNTIME_BUILD=1`)**: safe. The npm tarball and every platform binary ship byte-identical `dist/runtime/*.js`, because CI never re-resolves or re-bundles them at release time. No user-facing risk today.
- **If reverted to a standard `.gitignore`'d `dist/` + CI-time build** without first fixing the two unpinned inputs above: the exact class of bug that broke v0.22.0 (parses clean, 200s over HTTP, throws `ReferenceError` at module-eval time — undetectable by a green CI build) could recur, and worse, could recur *silently varying by which CI runner in the matrix happens to resolve which `motion` patch*, making it non-reproducible to debug.
- No current user impact; this is a release-process risk assessment, not an active bug.

## Proposed Fix

To make CI-time regeneration safe enough to drop the git-committed workaround:

1. **Commit `apps/studio/bun.lock`.** Remove the `apps/studio/bun.lock` line from `.gitignore:75`. This is the highest-leverage fix — it pins the entire resolved dependency graph (`motion` and everything transitive) to one exact state, shared by every CI runner and every contributor.
2. **Switch CI back to `--frozen-lockfile`** for `apps/studio`'s `bun install` once the lockfile is committed (currently deliberately dropped per the comment at `build-binaries.yml:128-129`, because there was nothing to freeze against).
3. **Pin `bun-version` to an exact patch** (e.g. `'1.3.5'`, not `'1.3.x'`) in all three workflow files that call `oven-sh/setup-bun@v2`, removing the secondary drift source.
4. **Keep `check-runtime-bundles.sh` regardless of which approach wins.** It's cheap insurance against a *future legitimate* dependency bump producing a differently-shaken bundle — that's a real risk independent of environment nondeterminism, and the floor-check is the only thing that would catch it before publish.
5. **Do not flip the switch in one step.** Land 1–3 first, then run the full CI matrix (all 7 targets) several times over a few days/dependency-bump cycles, diffing `dist/runtime/*.js` output across runs to confirm byte-for-byte reproducibility before removing the git-committed bundles and `MAUDE_SKIP_RUNTIME_BUILD=1`. Given this bug shipped through a full release before being caught (and the sibling DDR-176 incident shipped through *two* releases for a related "works locally, breaks in the compiled sidecar" class of drift), the team should be conservative about re-enabling CI-time regeneration as the sole source of truth.

## Testing Requirements

- Add a CI check (or extend `check-runtime-bundles.sh`) that runs `bun install --frozen-lockfile` twice in a row (fresh cache) and diffs the resulting `dist/runtime/*.js` output, failing if it's not byte-identical — a direct reproducibility assertion, not just a size floor.
- Once `bun.lock` is committed, add a lint/CI step asserting `apps/studio/bun.lock` is not stale relative to `apps/studio/package.json` (mirrors the existing root `pnpm-lock.yaml` freshness checks, if any).
- Before removing the git-committed bundles, run the full 7-target matrix build 3+ times and diff outputs, as above.

## Complexity

**Low** for steps 1–3 (lockfile commit + CI flag flip + exact Bun pin — small, mechanical changes). **Medium** overall because of the verification bar: given this exact area shipped broken through v0.22.0 (and a related class of drift shipped through v0.44.0/v0.45.0 per DDR-176), the safe rollout requires a multi-run reproducibility soak before trusting CI-time regen again — that's process/verification time, not code complexity.

decision.title: RCA: Canvas DS token injection — non-default-DS UI canvases render with the wrong design system
decision.rationale:
# RCA: Canvas DS token injection — non-default-DS UI canvases render with the wrong design system

- **Source:** manual (no tracker ticket; root-caused live during `/design:new --ds=maude`)
- **Date:** 2026-06-04
- **Area:** `plugins/design/dev-server/client/app.jsx` → `canvasUrl()`; `plugins/design/dev-server/api.ts` → `buildIndexData()`
- **Severity:** High (every UI canvas authored under a non-default DS renders unstyled in the live browser)
- **Status:** Workaround in place (canvas self-imports its DS); proper fix pending.

## Summary

In a multi-DS project, the dev-server **client** injects the wrong design-system tokens for every **UI canvas** under `<designRoot>/ui/`. `canvasUrl()` always sets `?tokens=`/`?components=` to `designSystems[0]` (the default DS, here `project`), **ignoring the canvas's own `meta.json` `designSystem`**. A canvas authored for `maude` (artboards wrapped in `.maude[data-theme]`, classes referencing maude tokens) therefore loads `project` tokens — which are scoped to `.mdcc[data-theme]` and never cascade into a `.maude` subtree — so every `var(--*)` is undefined and the canvas renders unstyled/white. Only `system/<ds>/preview/` **specimens** get the correct per-DS tokens (they have dedicated handling). Reproduced on `.design/ui/Studio.tsx` (DS=maude).

## Root Cause

`client/app.jsx` `canvasUrl(p, cfg, opts)` (~L97–131) resolves the token URLs as:

```js
const ds0 = cfg?.designSystems?.[0];                       // = "project" (designSystems[0])
const specMatch = rel.match(/^system\/([^/]+)\/preview\//); // specimen?  → per-DS tokens
const tokens = specMatch
  ? specDsEntry?.tokensCssRel || `system/${specMatch[1]}/colors_and_type.css`
  : ds0?.tokensCssRel || cfg?.tokensCssRel;                 // UI canvas → ALWAYS ds0
// …components resolved the same ds0-first way (L124–131)
```

- **Specimen path** (`system/<ds>/preview/…`) parses the DS slug out of the path and loads that DS's `tokensCssRel` + `_layout.css` + `_components.css`. Correct.
- **UI-canvas path** (`ui/…`) has no DS slug in its path, so the code falls back to `ds0` (`designSystems[0]`) unconditionally. The per-canvas `designSystem` declared in the sidecar is **never consulted.**

Two contributing facts make this a silent latent bug rather than an obvious one:

1. **The data isn't on the client tree node.** `api.ts` `buildIndexData()` emits canvas groups as `{ paths: string[], kind: 'canvas', dsFolders? }` (L1211–1218) — a flat list of file paths, **no per-canvas `designSystem`**. So even if `canvasUrl()` wanted to honor the DS, the caller (`canvasUrl(t.path, cfg)`, L1613) has nothing to pass. The server *does* read `meta.designSystem` elsewhere (`canvas-header.ts:56` — `m.designSystem ?? opts.dsName ?? 'project'`), proving the sidecar field is authoritative; it just never reaches the index payload.

2. **CSS scoping turns "wrong tokens" into "no tokens".** Token files scope their ladder to `:root, .<rootClass>[data-theme]`. `project` → `.mdcc`; `maude` → `.maude`. A maude canvas's `.maude[data-theme="dark"]` wrapper gets *no* match from the `.mdcc`-scoped project sheet, and the project sheet's `:root` block doesn't beat anything because the canvas authors against the higher-specificity `.maude[data-theme]` scope. Result: undefined custom properties → white fallback.

This has been latent since multi-DS support landed (DDR-048 era): the specimen branch got per-DS handling, the UI-canvas branch was left on the single-DS `ds0` assumption that was correct only while every canvas shared the default DS.

### Why it was masked (process gap)

`/design:new`'s step-9 reality-check screenshots are captured by the orchestrator passing the **explicit** target-DS tokens to the screenshot helper (`&tokens=system/maude/colors_and_type.css&components=…`). That reproduces an *idealized* host, not the **live client's** behavior, so the screenshots looked perfect while the browser render was broken. The reality check verified "does the TSX render under correct tokens" but not "does the live client inject the correct tokens for this canvas." The user caught it by opening the canvas in the actual browser.

## Impact

- **Who:** any UI canvas (`ui/*.tsx`) whose `meta.designSystem` is **not** `designSystems[0]`. In this repo that's every `maude` canvas (`project` is `designSystems[0]`/default). Single-DS projects and default-DS canvases are unaffected (`ds0` happens to be correct).
- **What:** the canvas renders unstyled/white in the live browser (canvas-browser tab AND gallery thumbnails — `canvasUrl(p.path, cfg, { thumbnail: true })`, L1865). Handoff/export of such a canvas also picks the wrong tokens unless the canvas self-imports.
- **Severity:** High for multi-DS projects — the newer DS is unusable for full-screen canvases without a per-canvas workaround. Low blast radius for single-DS users (the common case), which is why it went unnoticed.
- **Workaround (already applied to `Studio.tsx`):** the canvas self-imports its DS — `import "../system/maude/colors_and_type.css"` + `_components.css`. The `.maude[data-theme]` scope (specificity 0,2,0) wins over any host `:root` pollution, so it renders in maude regardless of what the client injects. Verified by re-screenshotting with the *wrong* (project) tokens injected. Self-import is also a net positive for handoff (self-contained registry-item).

## Proposed Fix

**Recommended — make the client honor `meta.designSystem` (server + client):**

1. **`api.ts buildIndexData()`** — when emitting each canvas path, read its sidecar `designSystem` (the value `canvas-header.ts` already resolves) and attach it. Either enrich the node to `{ path, designSystem }` objects, or add a parallel `pathMeta: Record<path, { designSystem }>` map on the group so the existing `paths: string[]` stays backward-compatible. Default to `defaultDesignSystem` when the sidecar omits it.
2. **`client/app.jsx canvasUrl()`** — accept the per-canvas DS (`opts.ds` or a third resolution branch) and, for a UI canvas, resolve tokens/components from `designSystems.find(d => d.name === ds)` instead of `ds0`. Keep the specimen branch as-is; keep `ds0` as the fallback when no DS is known (single-DS / legacy).
3. **Callers** (L1613 tree tab, L1865 thumbnail) — pass the node's `designSystem` through.
4. **Rebuild the client bundle release-minified** and commit (`cd plugins/design/dev-server && MAUDE_SKIP_RUNTIME_BUILD=1 bun run build.ts --release` → commit `dist/client.bundle.js` + `dist/styles.css`), per CLAUDE.md's "never boot source dev-server without rebuilding --release" rule.

**Keep the self-import too (defense-in-depth + handoff).** Even after the client fix, a non-default-DS canvas self-importing its tokens is harmless and makes the registry-item drop self-contained. Consider teaching `/design:new` step 8 to emit the self-import automatically for non-default-DS canvases.

**Close the process gap (prevents recurrence):** `/design:new` step-9 reality check should screenshot through the **same URL the live client builds** (i.e. let the client/`canvasUrl` logic choose tokens, or explicitly inject `designSystems[0]` to mirror today's client) so the check fails loud when the live render would be wrong — instead of passing the explicit target-DS tokens that mask the injection bug.

## Testing Requirements

- **Unit (`bun:test`, client logic):** extract/test the token-resolution so `canvasUrl('ui/Studio.tsx', cfg, { ds: 'maude' })` yields `tokens=system/maude/colors_and_type.css` + `components=system/maude/preview/_components.css`; `{ ds: 'project' }` and `{}` (unknown) fall back to `ds0`; specimen paths unchanged.
- **Unit (`api.ts`):** `buildIndexData()` attaches each canvas's `designSystem` from its sidecar; missing sidecar → `defaultDesignSystem`.
- **Integration / `/design:smoke`:** add a runtime computed-style gate that opens a non-default-DS UI canvas through the **client-built** URL and asserts a maude token resolves (e.g. computed `--bg-0` ≈ `oklch(0.165 …)`, not the project value). This is exactly the class of "build-green ≠ user-visible-green" regression `/design:smoke` exists to catch (DDR-021/DDR-068).
- **Regression guard:** the smoke gate should fail on today's `ds0`-only behavior.

## Complexity

**Medium.** The logic change is small and localized (one resolution branch + one index-data field), but it touches the server↔client contract, requires threading DS through two call sites, and needs a release-minified client-bundle rebuild + commit. The process-gap fix in `/design:new` is independent and low-risk. Self-import workaround is already shipped, so the canvas is unblocked while the proper fix is scheduled.

## Decision note

Worth a DDR: **"UI canvases resolve tokens from `meta.designSystem`, not `designSystems[0]`"** — codifies that the per-canvas DS is authoritative for token injection and that the reality-check must mirror the live client. Pairs with DDR-048 (multi-DS config) and DDR-061 (DS-context cache).
