decision.title: RCA: Export fails in Maude Desktop — `/$bunfs/root` (video) and `posix_spawn 'node'` (PNG)
decision.rationale:
# RCA: Export fails in Maude Desktop — `/$bunfs/root` (video) and `posix_spawn 'node'` (PNG)

**Ticket (pasted):** "nefunguje export v maude desktop (browser jsem nezkoušel). Export do mp4 ani gif nefunguje: `export failed: FileNotFound: failed to open root directory: /$bunfs/root` (nefunguje ani png pokud je to video artboard). Když je to normální artboard do png: `export failed: ENOENT: no such file or directory, posix_spawn 'node'`. Je potřeba důkladně vyzkoušet všechny typy exportů jak v maude desktop, tak v maude browser."

**Date:** 2026-07-04 · **Status:** root cause confirmed (code inspection, error strings map to exact lines) · **Fix:** shared foundation LANDED (see below); desktop render-backend rearchitecture PENDING an architecture decision.

## Implementation status (2026-07-04)

**Landed (foundation — shared by every fix approach):**
- New `apps/studio/exporters/_runtime.ts` — `exportShimPath()` (resolves shims via `DEV_SERVER_ROOT`, killing Defect 1 / `/$bunfs/root`) + `resolveExportRuntime()` (runtime ladder `MAUDE_EXPORT_RUNTIME → Bun.which('node') → Bun.which('bun')`, throwing an actionable error instead of the cryptic `posix_spawn 'node'`, killing Defect 2's opaqueness).
- All six render exporters (`png/pdf/svg/html/pptx/video.ts`) repathed + switched off hardcoded `'node'`; `_browser-bundles.ts` `getEncodeLibBundle` entry repathed via `DEV_SERVER_ROOT`.
- `test/exporters/runtime.test.ts` guards both (no `/$bunfs`, ladder, actionable throw). Full dev-server suite green (1904 pass / 0 fail); lint clean.
- **Effect:** fully **fixes export for `npm i -g @1agh/maude` compiled installs** (`maude design serve` — real `DEV_SERVER_ROOT`, `node` + `node_modules` present); **fixes the source dev-server / browser path** (unchanged behavior, no regression); and in **desktop** converts the two cryptic errors into a clear, actionable message.

**Increment 2 — Defect 3 LANDED (Option A: stage the render-runtime + browser fallback).** Confirmed empirically: after Increment 1, a `tauri dev` video export advanced past Defects 1+2 to `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: 'playwright'` from the real staged path `target/debug/apps/studio/bin/_pw-launch.mjs` — proving the repath + runtime ladder work. Increment 2 makes the render dependencies reachable in the bundle:
- `apps/desktop/scripts/stage-resources.mjs` — generalized the ACP closure-walker (`collectClosure` + `stageClosure`) and now also stages the render-export runtime `playwright` (+ `playwright-core`), `mediabunny`, `gifenc` into the bundle's `node_modules` (previously excluded by the blanket filter). `@types/*` + `fsevents` skipped; browsers are NOT in these packages (~22 MB JS). Build-time gate asserts all three staged.
- `apps/studio/bin/_pw-launch.mjs` — `launchChromium` gains an **additive** `executablePath` fallback: only when Playwright's own browser is absent (fresh bundle), it retries against a resolved Chrome-family engine (env override → `_ensure-browser.mjs --no-download` → system Chrome / provisioned `chrome-headless-shell`). Zero change to the working fast path (dev machines with an ms-playwright cache).
- **Verified without the native app:** `stage-resources` stages all 4 pkgs; `playwright` resolves from the staged shim dir; `Bun.build` of the staged `video-encode-lib.ts` compiles (resolves `mediabunny`+`gifenc`). Lint clean; dev-server + exporter suites green.
- **Remaining verification (needs the user / native app):** re-run `tauri dev` (auto re-stages via beforeDevCommand) and exercise the full export matrix (png/pdf/svg/html/pptx/mp4/gif/webm × static/animated/video-comp) in the bundled `.app`. Also confirm the `executablePath` fallback on a machine with no ms-playwright cache.

Trade-off note: Option A ships a second browser-automation stack (playwright) alongside the bundled `agent-browser` used for screenshots — both drive the same chrome-headless-shell. A future consolidation onto `agent-browser` (Option B) would remove ~22 MB + the redundancy, but needs the non-PNG capability R&D (printToPDF, script injection, frame-stepping).

## Summary

Every export format that renders through a headless browser (`png`, `pdf`, `svg`, `html`, `pptx`, `mp4`, `webm`, `gif`) is **completely broken in the Maude Desktop app** and has been since the desktop shell shipped. The export pipeline was written for the dev-server runtime and never migrated to survive the compiled-Bun-sidecar packaging. It makes **three assumptions that are all false inside the packaged `.app`**:

1. It locates its helper scripts via `import.meta.dir` → in a `bun --compile` binary this is the virtual `/$bunfs/root`, not a real disk path (**the DDR-045 bug, never applied to the exporters**).
2. It shells out to **`node`** — the desktop sidecar is a compiled **Bun** binary and has no bundled `node`; a Finder-launched `.app` can't rely on one being on PATH.
3. Even with 1+2 fixed, the shims `import { chromium } from 'playwright'`, but the desktop bundle **excludes `node_modules`** (`stage-resources.mjs:69`), so `playwright` isn't present, and playwright's Chromium binary is never provisioned (the desktop only provisions `chrome-headless-shell` for the *screenshot* path via `agent-browser`).

The two different error strings the user sees are **two faces of the same defect set** — whichever assumption the code hits first determines the message. The `browser` (dev-server / `maude design serve`) path was not tested by the user; it is *architecturally* expected to work (real `node` + `node_modules/playwright` + Chromium all present) but **must be verified** — especially the newer DDR-148 video path.

## Root Cause

All render-based exporters (`apps/studio/exporters/{png,pdf,svg,html,pptx,video}.ts`) share an identical, dev-server-only invocation pattern. Two representative lines:

```ts
// png.ts:24  &  video.ts:23  (same in pdf/svg/html/pptx)
const PNG_PLAYWRIGHT = path.join(import.meta.dir, '..', 'bin', '_png-playwright.mjs');
// png.ts:69  &  video.ts:84  (same in pdf/svg/html/pptx)
const proc = Bun.spawn(['node', ...args], { ... });
```

### Defect 1 — `import.meta.dir` → `/$bunfs/root` (produces the video error)

`import.meta.dir` inside the `bun --compile` sidecar resolves to the **virtual** `/$bunfs/root/...`, not the real on-disk `Resources/apps/studio/...`. This is exactly the class of bug **DDR-045** documents ("every dev-server module that needs a filesystem-relative path MUST import from `apps/studio/paths.ts`… NEVER compute `dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))` locally"). The exporters were never migrated — they still compute paths locally.

**Why video shows `FileNotFound: failed to open root directory: /$bunfs/root`:** `runVideo()` (video.ts:49) calls `getEncodeLibBundle()` **before** it spawns anything. That helper (`_browser-bundles.ts:85`) does:

```ts
const entry = path.join(import.meta.dir, 'video-encode-lib.ts');   // → /$bunfs/root/exporters/video-encode-lib.ts
const built = await Bun.build({ entrypoints: [entry], ... });      // Bun.build tries to open /$bunfs/root → FileNotFound
```

`Bun.build` attempting to resolve an entrypoint under the virtual root emits precisely `FileNotFound: failed to open root directory: /$bunfs/root`. The video path dies here, **before** it ever reaches the `node` spawn.

### Defect 2 — `Bun.spawn(['node', …])` → `posix_spawn 'node'` (produces the PNG error)

The PNG exporter has **no** encode-lib step, so it goes straight to the spawn (png.ts:69). The desktop sidecar is a compiled Bun binary; there is no bundled `node`, and a `.app` launched from Finder/Dock inherits the truncated launchd PATH. DDR-128 mitigates this by best-effort injecting the user's login-shell PATH (`sidecar.rs:107`), but this user has no `node` reachable that way (they are a Bun/pnpm user). `posix_spawn` fails to find the `node` executable → `ENOENT: no such file or directory, posix_spawn 'node'`. This is the first wall the static-artboard PNG path hits.

> The "PNG of a **video** artboard → `/$bunfs/root`" observation: the ⌘E dialog (`export-dialog.tsx`) offers only `png/pdf/svg/html/pptx/canva/zip`; **mp4/gif/webm are requested from the separate temporal export panel** (`client/app.jsx:776–799`, DDR-148 timeline surface). PNG itself has no comp-specific branch, so a video artboard exported *as PNG* is expected to fail with the same `posix_spawn 'node'`. The exact routing when the export is invoked from the video/timeline surface should be confirmed in the test sweep (item T-mix below) — but it resolves to one of these same two defects regardless.

### Defect 3 — latent: `playwright` + Chromium absent from the desktop bundle

Even after fixing Defects 1 & 2, the external `.mjs` shims do `import { chromium } from 'playwright'` and `chromium.launch()` (`_png-playwright.mjs:10,40` → `_pw-launch.mjs`). Two problems in the packaged app:

- **`node_modules` is excluded from the bundle** — `stage-resources.mjs:69`: `if (rel.startsWith('/node_modules') …) return false;`. The comment there reasons that the *compiled binary embeds server deps*, so the general `node_modules` "is NOT needed." True for the server — **but the exporter shims are external scripts run by a separate process; they are outside the compiled binary's embedded module graph and lost their `playwright` dependency when `node_modules` was excluded (v0.31.0–v0.32.0).**
- **No Chromium for playwright.** `launchChromium()` passes no `executablePath`, so it relies on playwright's own downloaded browser. The desktop only ever provisions `chrome-headless-shell` for the *screenshot* path via the bundled `agent-browser` binary (`_ensure-browser.mjs`, pinned by `MAUDE_AGENT_BROWSER` in `sidecar.rs:126`). The export shims don't use either.

### Why the dev-server / browser path works (and desktop doesn't)

| Assumption | Dev-server (`maude design serve`) | Desktop compiled sidecar |
|---|---|---|
| `import.meta.dir` | real `apps/studio/exporters` path | virtual `/$bunfs/root` ✗ |
| `node` on PATH | yes (terminal PATH) | not bundled; login-PATH best-effort ✗ |
| `node_modules/playwright` | present | excluded from bundle ✗ |
| playwright Chromium | resolvable / auto-installs | not provisioned ✗ |

Only `zip` and `canva` exporters are browser-free (pure fs/text) and should function in desktop today; every render format is broken there.

## Impact

- **Severity: High.** Export — a headline feature (⌘E + the DDR-148 video showreel path) — is **100% non-functional for all render formats in the shipped desktop app**, the primary distribution surface. Only `zip`/`canva` may work.
- **Affected users:** every Maude Desktop user attempting PNG/PDF/SVG/HTML/PPTX/MP4/WebM/GIF export.
- **Regression window:** the `node_modules` exclusion (Defect 3) landed v0.31.0–v0.32.0; Defects 1 & 2 have existed since the exporters were authored (never DDR-045-migrated). Video (DDR-148) is broken in desktop from its first ship.
- **Workaround:** run exports from the dev-server / browser (`maude design serve`) instead of the desktop app — pending verification that path is healthy.

## Proposed Fix

Two tiers. Ship the minimal fix to unbreak, plan the proper fix to make it robust.

### Minimal fix (unblock)
1. **Kill Defect 1 — route every shim + encode-lib path through `paths.ts`.** Replace `path.join(import.meta.dir, '..', 'bin', '_x-playwright.mjs')` with `path.join(DEV_SERVER_ROOT, 'bin', '_x-playwright.mjs')` in `png.ts:24`, `pdf.ts:25`, `svg.ts:24`, `html.ts:23`, `pptx.ts:38–39`, `video.ts:23`; and `_browser-bundles.ts:85` entry → `path.join(DEV_SERVER_ROOT, 'exporters', 'video-encode-lib.ts')`. (`DEV_SERVER_ROOT` already resolves correctly in desktop — `MAUDE_DEV_SERVER_ROOT` is set to `Resources/apps/studio` in `sidecar.rs:162`.)
2. **Kill Defect 2 — stop hard-coding `node`.** Resolve a runtime with `Bun.which('node')` and fail with an actionable message when absent; longer-term prefer not spawning an external interpreter at all (see proper fix).
3. **Kill Defect 3 — make `playwright` + Chromium reachable.** Either (a) stop excluding `node_modules/playwright` from the desktop stage (`stage-resources.mjs` allowlist the one package the shims need), **or** point the shims at the already-provisioned engine by passing `executablePath` (from `_ensure-browser.mjs`) into `launchChromium()`.

### Proper fix (recommended — matches how screenshots already work in desktop)
**Eliminate the `node bin/*.mjs` external-shim architecture for export.** The server is Bun and can drive the browser **in-process**, removing Defects 1 and 2 entirely (no shim path to resolve, no `node` to spawn):
- Import/orchestrate the capture inside the server process, and drive the **bundled `agent-browser`** engine (already pinned via `MAUDE_AGENT_BROWSER`, already provisions `chrome-headless-shell`) the same way `screenshot.sh` does — a proven-working desktop render path — instead of playwright-in-a-subprocess.
- This also removes the playwright-dependency-in-the-bundle problem (Defect 3) for good.

**Files to change:** `apps/studio/exporters/{png,pdf,svg,html,pptx,video}.ts`, `apps/studio/exporters/_browser-bundles.ts`, `apps/studio/exporters/_pw-launch.mjs` (executablePath plumbing), `apps/desktop/scripts/stage-resources.mjs` (only if keeping the playwright-subprocess design), and a shared helper for runtime/browser resolution. Note the CLAUDE.md rebuild rule if any client bundle is touched (it isn't for the server-side fix).

## Testing Requirements

The ticket explicitly demands a full sweep. Matrix = **format × environment × artboard type**:

- **Formats (10):** png, pdf, svg, html, pptx, mp4, webm, gif, zip, canva.
- **Environments (2):** Maude Desktop (bundled `.app`, *not* `tauri dev` — per the native-app verification-ceiling rule) **and** Maude Browser (`maude design serve` / dev-server).
- **Artboard types:** static mock · animated (WAAPI) mock · **video-comp** artboard (T-mix — confirm PNG-of-video-artboard routing and the timeline/temporal export trigger).

Verification approach:
- **Desktop:** DOM-driven E2E via the `desktop-e2e` harness (WebdriverIO, `data-testid`) — add a scenario that drives ⌘E for each dialog format and the temporal panel for mp4/gif/webm, asserting a non-error result and a non-zero payload. (DOM-driven, not computer-use.)
- **Browser:** drive `/_api/export` per format via the export panel (or direct POST) and assert real bytes + correct content-type.
- **Regression guards:** unit test that the shim/encode-lib paths resolve under a simulated `/$bunfs` `import.meta.dir` (assert they use `DEV_SERVER_ROOT`); a bundle-content assertion that whatever the shims need is actually staged.
- Add the pass/fail matrix to the RCA/fix PR so "works in browser" can never again be assumed to mean "works in desktop."

## Complexity

**Medium** for the proper fix (in-process/agent-browser rearchitecture of the render exporters + desktop E2E coverage). **Low** for a minimal unblock (paths.ts repath + runtime/browser resolution + one `stage-resources` allowlist), but the minimal path leaves the fragile external-`node`+playwright-subprocess design in place and should be treated as a stopgap.

decision.title: RCA: Desktop app — new file doesn't appear in the file tree and there's no way to refresh it
decision.rationale:
# RCA: Desktop app — new file doesn't appear in the file tree and there's no way to refresh it

> Ticket source: manual paste (tracker = `github`, no issue number).
> Reported (CZ): *"na desktop app nefunguje úplně reload file tree — když vytvořím nový soubor, tak se neobjeví v listu a nejde to nijak reloadnout, musím přepnout repos tam a zpět, aby se list reloadnul, což je otravný. Takže buď opravit ten watcher, nebo tam aspoň přidat nějaké reload tlačítko, protože cmd+r nefunguje."*
> Want: fix the watcher **or** add a manual reload button (because ⌘R does nothing for the tree).

## Summary

The Maude file tree (`groups` state in `client/app.jsx`) is **not** a live view of disk — it's a snapshot from `GET /_index-data`, re-fetched by `loadTree()` only on: mount, an in-app create/delete handler, and the `canvas-list-update` WebSocket message (DDR-124). On the desktop app two things compound:

1. **The auto-refresh occasionally misses.** `canvas-list-update` for externally-written canvases is driven by `fs-watch.ts`'s recursive `fs.watch` on `.design`. In the desktop app the dev-server runs as a **`bun --compile` standalone sidecar binary** (`apps/desktop` → `binaries/maude-server-<triple>`, spawned with `--root <project>`), and recursive `fs.watch`/FSEvents is the documented weak spot in compiled Bun binaries — events can be dropped (subdirectory creates, bursts, post-respawn). When the watcher misses, no `fs:any` → no `canvas-list-update` → stale tree.

2. **There is no manual escape hatch in the desktop app.** When the auto-refresh misses for *any* reason, the user is stuck:
   - The native menu (`menu.rs`) binds only `CmdOrCtrl+O`; there is **no Reload/Refresh item**.
   - In-webview `⌘R` is intercepted (`app.jsx:6788`) and calls `reloadActive()` — it reloads the active **canvas iframe**, not the tree. So "cmd+r nefunguje" is literally accurate for the tree.
   - There is no refresh button in the FILES panel header.
   - The **only** thing that re-runs `loadTree()` from a cold tree is switching projects (re-navigation) — hence the "přepnout repos tam a zpět" workaround.

So even though DDR-124's `canvas-list-watch.ts` fix shipped in the same PR as the desktop app (it's present in the sidecar binary — not version drift), the desktop context exposes both a reliability gap in the watcher **and** the absence of any user-driven recovery.

## Root Cause

### Layer 1 — the auto-refresh can silently miss (watcher reliability in the compiled sidecar)

- Tree refreshes **only** on `canvas-list-update` (DDR-124). For external writes (`/design:new` via the ACP chat, agent `Write`, terminal `cp`, `git checkout`) that event comes from `canvas-list-watch.ts`, which subscribes to `fs:any` emitted by `fs-watch.ts:32`.
- `fs-watch.ts:38` uses `node:fs` `watch(designRoot, { recursive: true }, …)`. The header comment asserts "Bun ships a working recursive fs.watch" — true for `bun run`, but **inside a `bun --compile` standalone binary** (how the desktop sidecar ships, `build.ts` step (c)) recursive FSEvents watching is unreliable: it can miss creates in newly-created subdirectories, under bursts, or after a sidecar respawn (the supervisor in `sidecar.rs` respawns the child, and a respawn drops the in-flight WS broadcast queue while the webview reconnects).
- Net: an external canvas create lands on disk, but no `fs:any` fires (or fires after the WS reconnect window), so `canvas-list-update` is never delivered → tree stays stale.
- **Confidence:** the *symptom* (stale tree, no event) is certain; the *exact* miss mechanism (compiled-binary `fs.watch` drop vs. respawn/WS-reconnect race vs. the 150 ms debounce/diff) needs a live repro on the compiled `.app` to pin down. The next-layer fix makes this layer non-blocking regardless of which it is.

### Layer 2 — no manual recovery in the desktop app (the real reason the user is stuck)

- `menu.rs` accelerators: only `CmdOrCtrl+O`. No reload.
- `app.jsx:6788` — `⌘R` → `reloadActive()` (canvas iframe), never the tree.
- `reloadTree` already exists and is correct (`app.jsx:6304`: `const reloadTree = useCallback(() => loadTree(), [loadTree])`) but **nothing user-facing calls it** — there's no button and no shortcut bound to it.
- The FILES header (`app.jsx:~1460`) shows a `st-live` "live · file index synced" pill — which misleadingly claims sync while the tree is stale — but it isn't clickable.

## Impact

- **Who:** all desktop-app users (macOS sidecar in particular).
- **Severity:** Medium. No data loss — purely workflow friction — but it breaks the core dogfood loop "build a canvas from the ACP chat → watch it appear," which is the headline Phase-31 experience. The only workaround (switch projects back and forth) is disruptive (kills + respawns the sidecar, re-navigates the webview).
- **Workaround today:** File ▸ Open Project to the same repo, or switch projects and back.

## Proposed Fix

Do **both**; the manual affordance is the guaranteed, low-risk fix the user explicitly asked for, and a focus-refresh backstop neutralizes the watcher gap without chasing the exact `fs.watch` miss.

### A. Manual refresh affordance (primary — Low risk, fully reliable)

- **Refresh button in the FILES panel header** (`apps/studio/client/app.jsx`, header block near `app.jsx:1460`, next to the `+` / `st-live` pill). Wire it to the existing `reloadTree` (`app.jsx:6304`). Cheapest option: make the `st-live` pill itself clickable → `reloadTree()` (it already represents "file index synced").
- **Keyboard shortcut.** `⌘R` is taken by canvas reload, so bind **`⌘⇧R` → reloadTree()** in the keydown handler (`app.jsx:6788` block). Optionally also have `⌘R` refresh the tree *in addition to* the iframe (low risk, matches user muscle memory) — decide during implementation.
- **Native menu item** (optional but nice): add **View ▸ Refresh Files** with `CmdOrCtrl+Shift+R` in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/menu.rs`, emitting a Tauri event the webview listens for → `reloadTree()`. Keeps the affordance discoverable from the menubar.

### B. Watcher hardening (backstop — Low risk, kills the symptom)

- **Refresh on window/webview focus.** Add a `window.addEventListener('focus', () => reloadTree())` (debounced) in `app.jsx`. `/_index-data` is a cheap read; this catches *any* missed fs event the instant the user returns to the window — and people invariably tab away to the ACP chat / terminal and back. This single change makes the stale-tree symptom effectively disappear regardless of the Layer-1 cause.
- **Optional deeper fix** (only if focus-refresh proves insufficient): verify recursive `fs.watch` actually fires inside the compiled sidecar (boot-time self-test + log), and if it's genuinely dropping events, add a low-frequency `/_index-data` poll or a shallow `readdir` poll of `cfg.canvasGroups` as a fallback in `canvas-list-watch.ts`.

### Files to change

- `apps/studio/client/app.jsx` — refresh button in FILES header; `⌘⇧R` shortcut; `window` `focus` → `reloadTree()` listener. **Then rebuild the committed bundle release-minified** (CLAUDE.md rule): `cd apps/studio && MAUDE_SKIP_RUNTIME_BUILD=1 bun run build.ts --release` and commit `dist/client.bundle.js` + `dist/styles.css`. Whatever is committed is what ships.
- `apps/studio/client/styles/4-components.css` — button styling (reuse `st-iconbtn`).
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/menu.rs` (optional) — View ▸ Refresh Files menu item + accelerator + webview event emit.
- `apps/studio/fs-watch.ts` / `apps/studio/canvas-list-watch.ts` (optional, Layer-1 deeper fix only) — compiled-binary watch self-test / poll fallback.

## Testing Requirements

- **Live desktop repro** (per the native-app verification ceiling — dogfood the bundled `.app`, not just `tauri dev`; system `screencapture` + computer-use can drive the WKWebView): create a canvas via the ACP chat / terminal `cp` into `.design/ui/…`, confirm it does **not** appear, then confirm (a) the new Refresh button, (b) `⌘⇧R`, and (c) tabbing away + back (focus-refresh) each surface it.
- **Client unit/behavioral:** focus event triggers exactly one `reloadTree()` (debounced); `⌘⇧R` calls `reloadTree` and not `reloadActive`; `⌘R` still reloads the canvas iframe.
- **Existing coverage:** `canvas-list-watch` already has tests (`apps/studio/test/`) — keep them green; add a compiled-binary watch self-test assertion if the Layer-1 deeper fix is taken.
- Run `/design:smoke` afterward (committed-bundle vs source-bundle regression class).

## Complexity

**Low** for A + the focus-refresh backstop (B first bullet) — this fully resolves the ticket as written. **Medium** only if the Layer-1 deeper fix (proving/replacing recursive `fs.watch` in the compiled sidecar) is pursued.

decision.title: RCA: Desktop print-ready PDF export — "Saving…" hangs forever on Save As
decision.rationale:
# RCA: Desktop print-ready PDF export — "Saving…" hangs forever on Save As

## Summary

Reported manually (pasted terminal log + screenshot, no numbered GitHub issue — `tracker.provider` is `github` in this repo's `.ai/workflows.config.json`, but the report has no parseable issue reference). Repro: in Maude Desktop, open `~/git/alligators/.design/ui/AlligatorsAcko.tsx`, export as **print-ready PDF, scope "Canvas → separate"**. The background job finishes ("EXPORT READY" toast, correct filename `ui-alligatorsacko.pdf`), but clicking **Save…** gets stuck on a spinning "Saving…" button indefinitely — the app appears frozen. Confirmed live on this machine: the job's output file already sits on disk at 542 MB (`~/git/alligators/.design/_export-jobs/5a3cbddb-.../ui-alligatorsacko.pdf`), and the desktop process was still hung on the save step at the time of the report.

Root cause is two-layered: (1) the print-ready PDF pipeline has no output-size guard and legitimately produced a ~540 MB file for this canvas, and (2) the native "Save As" code path ships that entire byte payload through Tauri's JSON-based IPC bridge via a plain `Array.from(Uint8Array)`, which is architecturally incapable of handling a payload that size without freezing the renderer for an extremely long time (in practice, indistinguishable from "always hangs").

## Root Cause

**Layer 1 — the export is legitimately oversized, with no guard.**
`apps/studio/exporters/pdf.ts` (DDR-182, "print artboards") renders each artboard to its own vector `page.pdf()` via Playwright, then a pdf-lib post-pass adds bleed/trim boxes and marks. `AlligatorsAcko.tsx` has 2 near-duplicate player-showcase artboards ("Canvas → separate" = one file per artboard, concatenated), each embedding the same large photographic assets at full size (`acko-group-real.png`, `acko-bust3.png`, ~2000–3000px). Because each artboard is captured independently through Chromium at print DPI, the same photos get re-rasterized/re-embedded fresh in every page — there is no cross-page image object reuse. `png.ts` got an explicit output-size guard in DDR-182 ("16,000px / ~600MB" ceiling) specifically because raising the DPI ceiling made an unbounded high-DPI request "a real OOM/hang risk that didn't exist before" — but that guard was scoped to the raster PNG exporter only. `pdf.ts` has no equivalent guard, so a multi-artboard, photo-heavy, print-DPI PDF export can silently produce a payload in the hundreds of MB with no warning to the user before they hit Save.

**Layer 2 — the "Save As" path can't survive a payload that size.**
`apps/studio/client/export-center.jsx` `saveNative()`:
```js
const bytes = Array.from(new Uint8Array(await got.blob.arrayBuffer()));
return saveExport(filename, bytes);
```
`saveExport` (`client/github.js:100`) calls `invoke('save_export', { filename, bytes })` (`@tauri-apps/api/core`), which JSON-serializes its arguments over the WebView↔Rust IPC bridge. For a 542 MB file that's ~542 million array elements: `Array.from` alone has to allocate and populate a JS array that size, and the IPC layer then has to `JSON.stringify` it (each byte becomes up to 3 ASCII digits + a comma, multiplying the payload several-fold in transit) — both synchronous, main-thread operations. This blocks the renderer's JS thread for a very long time (likely minutes, possibly appearing to never finish, and risking an OOM in the WebView process on a payload this large). The `st-btn-spin` element the user sees keeps animating throughout because it's a pure-CSS `@keyframes` animation running on the compositor thread, independent of the blocked JS main thread — which is exactly why the UI *looks* like it's still working ("Saving…" with a live spinner) while nothing is actually progressing. This matches the screenshot precisely.

This is a straight architectural gap, not a regression from a single commit: `saveNative`/`Array.from` was added 2026-07-10 (`6aee6da7`, background export job queue) when exports were PNG/small-scope by default; DDR-182 (2026-07-16) is what made routinely-huge PDF payloads reachable, and nothing in the desktop save path was revisited for that.

Confirmed root cause via direct evidence rather than inference: the 542 MB file sitting on disk today, matching the report's timestamp and filename, plus tracing both the exporter (no size guard) and the save path (JSON-array IPC) code.

## Impact

- **Who:** Any Maude Desktop user exporting a print-ready ("Canvas → separate" or any DPI-heavy) PDF from a canvas with more than a couple of large embedded photos/artboards.
- **Severity:** High for this workflow — the export silently succeeds server-side, but the user-facing "Save…" step hangs the whole app with no error, no progress indicator, and no way to tell if it's still working or dead. The only recovery is force-quitting Maude; the finished export bytes remain safely on disk at `_export-jobs/<id>/<filename>` (recoverable by hand, but the user has no way to know that from the UI).
- **Workaround today:** none in the UI. Advanced workaround: the file can be manually copied out of `<designRoot>/_export-jobs/<jobId>/<filename>` while the app is still hung (confirmed present in this repro), or the app can be force-quit and relaunched (the finished job stays queryable via `GET /_api/export-jobs` after restart, though the same Save… hang will recur if retried through the UI).
- **Not desktop-specific in cause 1**: the browser/web build uses `autoDownloadBlob` (`<a download>` blob URL), which doesn't suffer the IPC-JSON blow-up — so layer 2 is desktop-only, but layer 1 (an unguarded, oversized PDF) affects every build and is wasteful/slow regardless of save path.

## Proposed Fix

**Fix the hang (layer 2 — required, this is the reported bug):**
Stop shipping the export bytes through Tauri's JSON invoke argument entirely. `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/server_json.rs` already resolves the running dev-server's local URL, and `reqwest` is already a dependency (used in `oauth.rs`). Change `save_export` (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:107`) to:
1. Accept `jobId`/download URL (or just `filename` + resolve the job route) instead of a `bytes: Vec<u8>` argument.
2. Open the native save dialog first (as today).
3. On a chosen path, have the Rust command itself `reqwest::get` the `_api/export-jobs/download` URL and stream the response body directly to disk (`tokio::fs::File` + chunked write, or `std::io::copy` over a blocking reqwest response) — never routing the bytes through the WebView's JS heap or the IPC channel at all.
4. Update `client/export-center.jsx` `saveNative()` / `client/github.js` `saveExport()` to pass the job id (already available) instead of fetching bytes into the renderer first; drop the `fetchJobBytes` + `Array.from` step for the native path (the web/browser `autoDownloadBlob` path is unaffected and stays as-is).

This also fixes the *existing* smaller-scale version of the same bug for large video (MP4/WebM) exports, which route through the identical `saveNative` and could already be multi-hundred-MB.

**Guard the export (layer 1 — should ship alongside, prevents recurrence in other canvases):**
Add an output-size/DPI ceiling check to `apps/studio/exporters/pdf.ts` mirroring `_png-playwright.mjs`'s DDR-182 guard — e.g., warn or hard-cap when a "canvas as separate" print-DPI export's estimated/actual byte size crosses a threshold (e.g. ~150–200 MB), surfaced as a `failed` job with an actionable error ("this export is unusually large — consider lowering DPI or exporting artboards separately") rather than silently producing a 542 MB file the UI then can't hand off.

**Files to change:**
- `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs` (`save_export` command — fetch-and-stream instead of accepting raw bytes)
- `apps/studio/client/export-center.jsx` (`saveNative`, drop the bytes round-trip)
- `apps/studio/client/github.js` (`saveExport` signature)
- `apps/studio/exporters/pdf.ts` (+ its playwright shim) — output-size guard, mirroring `_png-playwright.mjs`

## Testing Requirements

- New desktop E2E scenario (`apps/desktop/e2e/`, per the project's DOM-driven WebdriverIO harness) that runs a "canvas as separate" print PDF export on a large fixture canvas and asserts Save… completes within a bounded time and produces a file of the expected size at the `MAUDE_E2E_SAVE_PATH` — this is the regression guard for the hang itself.
- Unit test on the new PDF size guard (`pdf.ts`) analogous to whatever `_png-playwright.mjs`'s 16,000px/600MB guard test looks like.
- Manual verification: re-run the exact repro against `AlligatorsAcko.tsx` post-fix and confirm Save… completes promptly for the existing 542 MB job.

## Complexity

Medium. The IPC redesign (fetch-and-stream in Rust) touches a cross-cutting save path shared by every export format, so it needs the "no-break exhaustive verify" treatment (per-feature inventory: PNG/SVG/HTML/PPTX/MP4/GIF/WebM/ZIP saves must all still work) — but the change itself is a well-contained, mechanical swap of "ship bytes over IPC" for "have Rust fetch the bytes itself," with an existing precedent (`reqwest` + `_server.json` resolution already used elsewhere in the same crate). The PDF size guard is small and localized, following the DDR-182 PNG precedent almost verbatim.

decision.title: RCA: desktop app dev-server sidecar crash-loops on startup (won't start at all)
decision.rationale:
# RCA: desktop app dev-server sidecar crash-loops on startup (won't start at all)

**Date:** 2026-07-14
**Status:** ✅ RESOLVED (same day) — verified via `pn dev:desktop`.
**Tracker:** none (ad-hoc — reported directly in a Claude Code session, no ticket filed)
**Reported via:** user running `pn dev:desktop`; sidecar spawned, then immediately crashed and respawned 3× before Tauri gave up ("sidecar gave up after 3 restarts"), so the desktop app never reached a usable state.

## Summary

`pn dev:desktop` (Tauri) spawns the compiled dev-server binary
(`apps/studio/dist/maude-darwin-arm64`, built via `bun build --compile`) as a
sidecar. It crashed on every launch attempt, respawned 3 times, then gave up.
Three independent, previously-latent bugs stacked on top of each other, all
introduced by the same day's commits (DDR-167 hardened SVG import, DDR-172
`import-tokens`, DDR-173 brand-upload panel) wiring new modules into
`http.ts`'s import graph — which, for the first time, pulled `svgo` (and its
transitive deps `csso`/`css-tree`) into the **compiled server binary**, an
invariant DDR-071 had explicitly relied on being false ("SVGO … is not in
server.ts's import graph, so it isn't compiled into the standalone binary").
Fixing bug 1 unmasked bug 2, fixing bug 2 unmasked bug 3 — each fix moved the
crash one module further down the same import chain. A fourth, unrelated
issue (all 10 auto-selected dev-server ports already occupied by leaked
processes from past sessions) surfaced only after all three code bugs were
fixed, and was operational, not a code defect.

## Reproduction

1. On a machine with several past `maude`/`tauri dev` sessions accumulated,
   run `pn dev:desktop` from a clean `apps/studio` build.
2. Tauri's `BeforeDevCommand` syncs `apps/studio/dist/maude-darwin-arm64` into
   the sidecar location and launches it with `--root <repo>`.
3. Observe repeated `[maude:server] error: Cannot find module '...' from
   '/$bunfs/root/maude-darwin-arm64'` crashes, 3 respawn attempts, then
   `[maude] sidecar gave up after 3 restarts`.

## Root Cause

### Bug 1 — `createRequire(import.meta.url).require('*.json')` isn't embedded by `bun build --compile`

`css-tree` (pulled in transitively via `svgo` → `csso` → `css-tree`, versions
2.2.1 and 3.2.1 both present in the tree) reads three of its own data files
this way in `lib/data-patch.js`, `lib/data.js`, and `lib/version.js`
(`csso`'s `lib/version.js` does the same for its own `package.json`):

```js
import { createRequire } from 'module';
const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);
const patch = require('../data/patch.json'); // or mdn-data/*.json, or ../package.json
```

`bun build --compile` bundles the whole reachable module graph into one
file, but this pattern routes the JSON read through a *runtime* `require()`
call obtained via `createRequire`, which the bundler does not statically
recognize as an embeddable asset reference (unlike a bare top-level CJS
`require('./x.json')`, which bundlers do special-case). At runtime inside
the standalone binary, the relative path resolves against the virtual
`/$bunfs/root/<binary-name>` filesystem and 404s — first observed as
`Cannot find module '../data/patch.json'`, then, once that was patched,
`Cannot find module 'mdn-data/css/at-rules.json'`, then
`Cannot find module '../package.json'`. Three separate call sites in the
same dependency tree, same underlying pattern, surfacing one at a time as
each was fixed and module evaluation reached the next.

**Why this had never bitten the compiled server binary before:** DDR-071
(2026-06-01) added `svgo` specifically as a *non-server* dependency — "SVGO
is imported only by `draw/optimize.ts`, reached via the `svg-optimize` /
`draw-build` bun helpers — it is **not** in `server.ts`'s import graph, so it
isn't compiled into the standalone binary." That invariant held until today.

### Bug 2 — new `http.ts` imports made `svgo` reachable from `server.ts` for the first time

Commit `ea5e7e5b` ("hardened SVG import", DDR-167) added
`bin/_import-asset.mjs`, imported statically at the top of `http.ts`
(`import { ImportAssetError, importSvg, SVG_MAX_BYTES } from
'./bin/_import-asset.mjs'`) to back a new privileged route
`POST /_api/import-asset`. `_import-asset.mjs` imports `optimizeSvg` /
`isValidSvg` from `draw/optimize.ts`, which imports `svgo`. That single new
top-level import is what broke DDR-071's invariant: `server.ts` → `http.ts`
→ `bin/_import-asset.mjs` → `draw/optimize.ts` → `svgo` → `csso` →
`css-tree`, all now eagerly evaluated at process startup, before
`Bun.serve` ever runs.

### Bug 3 — the `import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(argv[1]).href` CLI-guard class, recurring

Once Bug 1/2's module-resolution crash was fixed, the binary crashed again —
this time not with a module-not-found error, but by silently running the
*wrong* code path: invoking the binary with `--root <repo>` produced
`import-asset: unknown flag --port` / `import-tokens: <token-file>
required`, i.e. `bin/_import-asset.mjs`'s (and later `_import-brand.mjs`'s,
and `_import-tokens.mjs`'s) own CLI `main()` ran and hijacked the process
instead of `server.ts` starting the HTTP server. Each of these `bin/*.mjs`
files is dual-purpose — a library (imported by `http.ts` for its exported
functions) *and* a standalone CLI (invoked directly via `maude design
import-asset <path>`) — gated by:

```js
if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href) {
  main();
}
```

Inside a `bun --compile` standalone binary, every bundled module's
`import.meta.url` collapses to the same synthetic binary-internal path
(not each module's original source path), so this comparison against
`process.argv[1]` (the real on-disk binary path) spuriously evaluates
`true` for modules that are *not* actually the entry point — hijacking the
process the moment their code is reached in the bundle's evaluation order.

**This is the identical bug class as a prior incident**
(`_ensure-browser.mjs` CLI-guard regression, v0.38.0, "Starting…" desktop
hang — see project memory `project_v0380_starting_hang_ensure_browser_cli_guard`),
already fixed there via `import.meta.main ?? (argv-compare fallback)`. Three
newly-added files (`_import-asset.mjs` DDR-167, `_import-brand.mjs`
DDR-173, `_import-tokens.mjs` DDR-172 — all landed the same day, all reached
via the `http.ts` → `_import-brand.mjs` → `_import-tokens.mjs` chain in
addition to the direct `http.ts` imports) were written with the old,
already-known-buggy pattern instead of the established fix, because the
lesson from the v0.38.0 incident was never generalized into a rule the new
files' authors would hit (it lives only in one file's inline comment + a
memory entry, not in a lint/test/CLAUDE.md guard).

### Bug 4 (operational, not code) — all 10 auto-selected ports already occupied

After all three code bugs were fixed, the sidecar reached `Bun.serve` and
failed with `EADDRINUSE` — ports 4399–4408 (the server's full auto-retry
range) were all held by leaked `maude`/`maude-server`/`bun` processes from
past sessions across multiple projects (4 separate duplicate instances for
this repo alone, 3 for `studyfi-design`, plus `alligators` and
`maude-git-smoke`). Not a regression — just accumulated cruft from sessions
that didn't get torn down. Resolved by killing all 10 stray processes
(user-confirmed).

## Impact

- **Severity: High** — the desktop app could not start at all, for any
  project, until fixed. Affects every local `pn dev:desktop` run against
  this checkout.
- **Blast radius beyond this incident:** the CLI-guard bug class (Bug 3) is
  latent in at least 7 more `apps/studio/bin/*.mjs` files that currently
  aren't reachable from `server.ts` (`_fetch-asset.mjs`, `_import-brand.mjs`
  — now fixed —, `_canvas-rects-static.mjs`, `_import-tokens.mjs` — now
  fixed —, `_motion-sample-playwright.mjs`, `_ingest-footage.mjs`,
  `_probe-footage-playwright.mjs`, `read-annotations.mjs`): the moment any
  of them gets imported into `http.ts` (as three of them just were, in one
  day), the same class of startup hijack recurs. Not fixed here (out of
  scope — none of the remaining ones are currently reachable from
  `server.ts`), but worth a follow-up sweep or a structural guard.

## Fix Applied

**Bug 1 (dynamic JSON `require` not bundler-embeddable):** `pnpm patch` for
three packages, replacing the `createRequire(import.meta.url)` +
`require('*.json')` pattern with a static `import ... with { type: 'json'
}` (bundler-inlinable, no runtime file lookup):
- `patches/css-tree@2.2.1.patch` (`lib/data-patch.js`, `lib/data.js`, `lib/version.js`)
- `patches/css-tree@3.2.1.patch` (same three files)
- `patches/csso@5.0.5.patch` (`lib/version.js`)
- Registered in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` → `patchedDependencies`.

**Bug 3 (CLI-guard hijack):** `apps/studio/bin/_import-asset.mjs`,
`_import-brand.mjs`, `_import-tokens.mjs` — replaced the bare
`import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(argv[1]).href` guard with the
established `import.meta.main ?? (...)` pattern already used in
`_ensure-browser.mjs`.

**Bug 2** required no code change — it's the correct, intended new
behavior (DDR-167's `/_api/import-asset` route); it just means DDR-071's
"svgo never reaches the compiled binary" note is now stale and should be
corrected in a DDR-071 addendum if that file is revisited.

**Bug 4:** killed the 10 stray processes (user-confirmed, not autonomous).

Rebuilt the server binary after each patch layer with
`MAUDE_SKIP_RUNTIME_BUILD=1 bun run build.ts --release
--target=bun-darwin-arm64` (per CLAUDE.md's runtime-bundle rule — this flag
avoids regenerating the committed, environment-sensitive
`dist/runtime/*.js` bundles as a side effect of an unrelated rebuild).

## Testing Requirements

- Manual: ran the rebuilt `dist/maude-darwin-arm64` directly with an
  explicit free port (`MDCC_DEV_PORT=4777`), confirmed clean boot + a
  working `GET /_health` response before touching the desktop app.
- End-to-end: `pn dev:desktop` after freeing the port range — confirmed by
  the user ("funguje").
- **Follow-up (not done here, flagged for later):** a lint/test rule that
  fails the build if any `apps/studio/bin/*.mjs` file's CLI guard uses the
  bare `import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(argv[1]).href` form instead of
  `import.meta.main ?? (...)`, so the next dual-purpose CLI/library module
  someone wires into `http.ts` can't reintroduce Bug 3. Candidate location:
  a `bun:test` over `bin/*.mjs` source text, alongside the existing
  `plugin-cli-reachability.test.mjs`-style convention tests.

## Complexity

**Low** per individual fix (a bundler-compat patch + a one-line guard
swap, repeated 3–4 times), but **discovery was iterative** — each fix
unmasked the next module in the same import chain, requiring 4 separate
rebuild-and-retest cycles to reach a clean boot. The underlying lesson
(new `http.ts`-reachable modules can silently reintroduce either bug class)
is the part worth institutionalizing, per the Impact section above.

decision.rationale:
# RCA: Ticket — design-system awareness hardening (/design:new, /design:edit a všechny canvas-generující nástroje)

_2026-07-02 · zdroj: ruční hlášení uživatele (tracker: github, bez čísla issue) · vyšetřeno přes /flow:bug-rca s hypothesis debate (DDR-130, relay tier, short-circuit po blind openings)_

## Summary

Uživatel hlásí, že `/design:new` a `/design:edit` generují canvasy, které ignorují uložené logo design systému, vymýšlejí si vlastní ikony a komponenty a neberou layout z existujících showcase specimenů — přestože `config.json` deklaruje default DS. Požadavek: DS-first "za každou cenu" (invence povolena jen tam, kde specimen neexistuje). Vyšetřování třemi nezávislými investigator sedačkami (H-ASSET / H-ENFORCE / H-DELIVERY) konvergovalo bez cross-challenge na **složenou root cause o třech vrstvách**: (1) brand-asset slepota — logo a ikonografie se nikdy nesbírají do žádné generační vrstvy; (2) advisory enforcement — DS-fidelita je architektonicky "nudge, ne gate", varování se nikdy neopravují; (3) delivery mezera na new-path — priors se předávají jako cesty a názvy tříd, ne jako obsah, a generátor (`frontend-design`) je kontraktem invent-first. Nejde o regresi — je to díra v pokrytí, jejíž layoutovou třetinu už identifikoval a částečně zalepil DDR-127 (2026-06-22, 10 dní před ticketem); logo/ikony/komponenty zalepené nikdy nebyly.

## Investigation record (hypothesis debate)

| Sedačka | Hypotéza | Verdikt | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rca-h-asset` | H-ASSET: brand-asset slepota (coverage gap) | **primary** (vlastní symptomy logo+ikony) | 0.80 |
| `rca-h-enforce` | H-ENFORCE: advisory enforcement posture | **primary** (vlastní symptomy shell+komponenty) | 0.72 |
| `rca-h-delivery` | H-DELIVERY: context-delivery plumbing | contributing / co-primary pro showcase symptom | 0.72 |

Žádný faktický rozpor — sedačky si rozdělily symptomový prostor a navzájem se ko-implikovaly; short-circuit per debate-protocol krok 4 (eskalace by byla divadlo). Všechna load-bearing tvrzení ověřena lead-synthesis pass proti souborům (file:line níže).

## Root Cause

**Symptom → příčinná mapa** (tři symptomy z ticketu, tři vrstvy):

### Vrstva 1 — brand-asset slepota (logo, ikony) — proximate cause symptomů 1+2

DS předvídatelně shipuje `preview/logo.tsx` + `preview/iconography.tsx` (`_MAPPING.md`; reálně `.design/system/maude/preview/`), ale **žádná z pěti generačních vrstev je nikdy nečte ani nejmenuje**:

- `plugins/design/commands/new.md:468` — step 5a globuje priors jen z `preview/components-*.tsx`; `:492` přidává jen `ui_kits-*-showcase.tsx`. Logo/iconography do envelope nikdy nevstoupí. (Identická třída chyby, kterou DDR-127 § Context dokumentuje pro showcase — fix opravil showcase a brand assety nechal být.)
- `plugins/design/commands/edit.md:184` — DDR-061 cache pack = `{classNames, tokenNames, libExports}`; žádný asset inventář.
- `plugins/design/agents/design-system-keeper.md` — passes A/A.5/A.6/B; žádný pass "použils DS logo / DS ikony?". Vymyšlené inline `<svg>` logo nemá class root → je neviditelné pro všechny existující audity.
- `plugins/design/agents/ux-research-agent.md:384` — ux-patterns payload explicitně vylučuje visual identity.
- `plugins/design/skills/design/SKILL.md:~820` — jediné asset pravidlo v envelope je negativní ("NO inline images/icons that aren't sourced from the project's assets folder") bez ukázaného inventáře; a **directive 10 ("Brand mark featured at human scale") si logo aktivně objednává, zatímco k němu nevede žádná cesta** → generátor si ho vymyslí. Ověřeno.

Dvojité utěsnění díry: `SKILL.md:405` routing gate `HAS_LOGO = grep -cE "logos?/|wordmark|brand-mark"` je path/word-only — vymyšlené inline `<svg>` skóruje 0, takže `brand-critic` se na `/design:new` vůbec nezapojí (není ani v minimálním panelu, `new.md:~896`). A step 9.6 (`new.md:830-865`) vymyšlený mark reroutuje na `draw-agent`, který ho **deterministicky přestaví** — nikdy nezkontroluje, že DS už kanonické logo shipuje; invence se tak "vypere" do verifikovaného artefaktu.

### Vrstva 2 — advisory enforcement ("za každou cenu" nemá žádnou bránu) — proximate cause symptomu 3 + důvod, proč vrstva 1 přežívá do outputu

- `DDR-127 § Alternatives considered` — hard-block reuse **záměrně odmítnut**; grounding je "strong default, enforced as a visible nudge, not a gate". Přesný opak uživatelova požadavku.
- `design-system-keeper.md:229-235` — nálezy jsou warnings; self-promote na blocker až při ≥5 token mismatch NEBO ≥3 pattern reinventions. `:67` — **skip-list Pass A obsahuje `icon` a `card`**, takže vymyšlené ikony/karty se do prahu ani nepočítají. `:188` — Pass A.6 (shell reinvention) "never self-promotes to blocker".
- `SKILL.md:561,582,614-619` — auto-fix loop počítá a opravuje jen **blockery** (top-3/iteraci); warnings přežijí všech 8 iterací do finálního outputu.
- `design-critic.md:84-92` — tvrdé DS blockery existují jen na token/estetické úrovni (hex, radii, banned aesthetics) — ne na úrovni reuse komponent/assetů/shellu.
- `brand-critic.md:15-23` — čte `<designRoot>/system/<project>/assets/` (hardcoded `<project>`, ne multi-DS; maude drží logo v `preview/logo.tsx`) a při chybějící složce měkce degraduje na "tokens + voice cues only".

### Vrstva 3 — delivery mezera na new-path (showcase/priors jako cesty, ne obsah) — spolu-příčina symptomu 3

- `new.md:458-515` + `SKILL.md:~806-816` — priors, komponenty i showcase se do envelope interpolují jako **cesty + class-root řetězce** (grep/jq/ls, nikdy `Read`); generátor má "liftovat same paddings, same border treatment" (`new.md:541`), ale paddingy žijí v souborech, které na new-path nikdo neotevře. Kontrast: edit-path DDR-127 **explicitně čte obsah** showcase (`edit.md:173-176`).
- `SKILL.md:~806` — envelope instruuje "Read `{designRoot}/system/README.md`" — **soubor neexistuje** (reálné jsou `system/<ds>/README.md`); instrukce se rozřeší na nic. Ověřeno (`ls`).
- Generace běží přes `frontend-design` skill, jehož kontrakt je invent-first: "commit to a BOLD aesthetic direction… NEVER converge on common choices… Don't hold back… avoid generic fonts" — nulové povědomí o DS/priors/logu. Bez inline obsahu + explicitního DS-pinu jede skill designově *proti* DS. Ověřeno (`~/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/frontend-design/*/skills/frontend-design/SKILL.md`).
- Sekundárně na edit-path: `edit.md:80-95` LOAD_CSS heuristika je převážně EN style-verbs — česká zpětná vazba ("barva", "zarovnej", "mezery") pre-load DS slovníku často mine. (Edit-only; nevysvětluje new-path.)

**Proč se to děje (původní intent):** envelope discipline (creative brief, ne wireframe) + DDR-043 (bias-free templates) + DDR-127's "reference, not prescription" jsou vědomé volby proti over-prescription. Vedlejší efekt: neexistuje žádná vrstva, kde by "DS má kanonický specimen X → použij X" bylo (a) doručeno jako obsah a (b) vynuceno jako gate. Uživatelův požadavek je legitimní nová policy úroveň, ne oprava regrese.

## Impact

- **Kdo:** každý projekt s bootstrapped DS — každý `/design:new` a každý podstatný `/design:edit`. Nejviditelnější na brand integritě (mock s cizím logem je pro handoff/prezentaci nepoužitelný) a na duplicitních komponentách, které pak driftují.
- **Závažnost:** vysoká pro produktový slib pluginu ("DS-first iterace") — přímo popírá dokumentovaný Tier-0/pattern-priors princip; žádná ztráta dat, žádný security dopad.
- **Workaround:** ruční iterace (`/design:edit "použij logo ze system/maude/preview/logo.tsx"`) funguje, ale stojí 1–3 iterace na canvas a popírá automatizaci; `--ds=<name>` + `meta.designSystem` fungují korektně pro tokeny (DDR-093), problém je v assetech/komponentách/shellu.
- **Pozn. k symptomu 3:** DDR-127 (10 dní před ticketem) layoutovou část částečně řeší (edit-path čte obsah; keeper Pass A.6 audituje) — uživatelova zkušenost může předcházet DDR-127, ale new-path path-only delivery + info/warning severity znamenají, že symptom může přetrvávat i po něm.

## Proposed Fix

Dvoustranný fix — **delivery** (aby reuse proběhl na první pas) + **gate** (aby invence neprošla), zrcadlí a dotahuje DDR-127. Samotná delivery je DDR-127 past (nudge ignorovatelný), samotný gate stojí fix-iteraci za každou invenci.

**A. Delivery (first-pass reuse):**
1. `new.md` step 5a: rozšířit sběr o `preview/logo.*` + `preview/iconography.*` (+ `assets/` strom, existuje-li) → nová envelope subsekce `## Brand assets (canonical — reuse, don't invent)` s **inline obsahem** mark JSX/SVG (ne jen cestou); directive 10 odkázat na tento slot.
2. New-path parity s edit-path: orchestrátor **Read + inline obsah** showcase a top-N priors do envelope (dnes jen cesty); opravit mrtvou cestu `system/README.md` → `system/<ds>/README.md`.
3. Envelope anti-invent pin: pokud existuje default/`--ds` DS, explicitní blok "the DS IS the aesthetic direction — fonts/colors/icons/logo/shell are PINNED; invent only where no specimen exists" (přebíjí invent-first kontrakt `frontend-design`).
4. DDR-061 cache pack: přidat `logoSpecimenPath` / `assetNames` / markup snippety klíčových komponent.
5. `edit.md` step 1.5: doplnit české style-verbs do LOAD_CSS (nebo gate zrušit — ~6 KB read je levnější než minutí).

**B. Gate ("za každou cenu"):**
6. Nový keeper pass (brand-asset reuse): inline `<svg>` mark v canvasu + DS shipuje `logo.tsx` → finding; vyřadit `icon`/`card` ze skip-listu Pass A (nebo je počítat do prahu).
7. Config knob `dsFidelity: "strict" | "advisory"` (default advisory = dnešní chování, zero regression): ve strict módu jsou asset/komponent/shell reinvence **blockery** (řízená revize DDR-127 pro opted-in projekty), Pass A.6 → blocker když showcase existuje, a auto-fix loop musí keeper DS-fidelity nálezy čistit. **Integrace s existující `--opt-out` osou, ne vedle ní** (doplněno po diskusi s uživatelem): `dsFidelity` a `opt_out_scope` jsou dvě polohy téže osy "jak moc DS váže" — strict vynucuje reuse jen do míry, kterou canvas scope nepovolil jinak; explicitní `--opt-out=full` na konkrétním canvasu vyhrává i ve strict módu (uživatelův vědomý free-use beats project policy). Jedna osa, žádné dva soupeřící přepínače.
8. Routing fixy: `HAS_LOGO` v `SKILL.md:405` rozšířit o inline `<svg>` mark detekci; `brand-critic` do default panelu `/design:new`, když DS shipuje brand assety; opravit jeho asset path na DS-aware `system/<ds>/{preview,assets}/`.
9. `new.md` step 9.6 / `edit.md` 4.6: před rerouting vymyšleného marku na `draw-agent` zkontrolovat kanonické DS logo a **substituovat**, ne přestavovat invenci.

Dotčené soubory: `plugins/design/commands/new.md`, `plugins/design/commands/edit.md`, `plugins/design/skills/design/SKILL.md`, `plugins/design/agents/design-system-keeper.md`, `plugins/design/agents/brand-critic.md`, config schema pro `dsFidelity` (+ DDR pro revizi DDR-127 severity a nový knob; CLAUDE.md pointer).

## Testing Requirements

Repo nemá test suite pro plugin markdown — verifikace = dogfood ve scratch projektu + artefaktové gaty:

1. **Distinguishing experiment jako regresní test:** `/design:new` v maude DS s briefem vyžadujícím header → assert `_history/<slug>/000-envelope.md` obsahuje Brand-assets subsekci s inline obsahem loga; assert vygenerovaný canvas nese DS mark (signatura z `logo.tsx`), ne nové `<svg>` logo.
2. **Keeper fixture:** canvas s vymyšleným (token-čistým) logem + 2 vymyšlenými ikonami + 1 reinvented kartou → advisory: ≥3 warnings viditelné v panelu; strict: ≥1 blocker, který fix-loop musí vyčistit.
3. **Routing:** inline-`<svg>`-logo fixture → `brand-critic` se zapojí na `/design:new`.
4. **Edit path:** česká style zpětná vazba ("změň barvu tlačítka") → DS pre-load proběhne.
5. **Back-compat:** bez `dsFidelity` (advisory) žádná změna verdiktů proti dnešku; DS bez showcase/loga → žádný nový fail (graceful skip, vzor DDR-127).

## Complexity

**Medium** — čistě instruction-markdown + agent specs + jeden config knob (žádný dev-server kód). Největší riziko je spec-koherence: severity revize se dotýká DDR-127 rozhodnutí (potřebuje DDR) a musí zůstat project-agnostic + bias-free (DDR-043).

---

### Debate appendix — kill tests & distinguishing experiments (pro fix fázi)

- **H-ASSET kill test (negativní napříč 5 vrstvami):** najdi jakoukoli generation-direction cestu, která globuje `preview/logo.tsx`/`iconography.tsx` do envelope/promptu/cache/ux-payload/meta — neexistuje.
- **H-ENFORCE kill test:** spusť keeper+panel na fixture z Testing #2 — predikce blockers==0 (ikony/karta skip-listed, logo bez class rootu, brand-critic nerouted, warnings se neopravují).
- **H-DELIVERY A/B:** stejný envelope (A) s cestami vs (B) s inline obsahem priors/loga — pokud B liftuje a A vymýšlí, delivery je primární; pokud vymýšlejí oba, rozhoduje enforcement/skill-pin.

decision.title: RCA: DS preview na :4555 renderuje specimeny bez CSS (5 blank + button/input všude)
decision.rationale:
# RCA: DS preview na :4555 renderuje specimeny bez CSS (5 blank + button/input všude)

**Datum:** 2026-05-31 · **Provider:** github (ticket vložen manuálně) · **Server:** `http://localhost:4555` (canvasOrigin `:53935`), `.design/system/project`

## Summary

Část design-system preview specimenů se zobrazuje bez stylů. Jsou to **dvě nezávislé regrese se stejným kořenem** — po migraci specimenů z HTML na TSX (`import`-driven CSS) se sdílené stylesheety přestaly načítat do canvasů, do kterých je nikdo explicitně neimportuje. Dev-server (`canvas-build.ts:170`) injektuje **pouze** CSS, které vyprodukoval bundler z `import` grafu daného souboru — žádné globální injektování sdílených `_*.css`. Import graf má dvě díry:

- **Příčina A — 5 specimenů nemá import tokenů ani layoutu** → renderují se prakticky prázdné / jako změť: `components-diff-view`, `components-monospace-table`, `iconography`, `selection`, `ui_kits-desktop-showcase`.
- **Příčina B — `_components.css` (kde žijí `.btn`, `.input`, `.select`, `.textarea`) neimportuje žádný specimen** → nativní button/input prvky jsou bez stylu „skoro všude" (12 specimenů).

Předchozí commit `745bcf0` tytéž soubory už „opravoval", ale spravil jen blank mount (chybějící `import { ThemeToggle }`), ne chybějící CSS. „Verified rendering via agent-browser" zachytilo „DOM se mountuje", ale ne „je to bez stylů" — klasická mezera *build green ≠ user-visible green* (DDR-021).

## Root Cause

### Mechanismus

Každý preview specimen je samostatný canvas bundlovaný Bun.buildem. Styl získá **jen** z toho, co (tranzitivně) `import`uje. Sdílené soubory:

| Soubor | Co definuje | `@import` řetězení |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `system/project/colors_and_type.css` | **design tokeny** (`--bg-*`, `--fg-*`, `--accent`, `--font-mono`, `--space-*`, `--border-*`, `--type-*`, `--tracking-*`) | nic |
| `preview/_layout.css` | specimen chrome (`.specimen-hd`, `.specimen`, `h2[data-no]`, …) | `@import url("../colors_and_type.css")` |
| `preview/_components.css` | `.btn`, `.input`, `.select`, `.textarea`, badges, pills… | **nic — a nikdo ho neimportuje** |

Funkční specimen (např. `components-callout.tsx`) importuje:
```js
import "../colors_and_type.css";   // tokeny
import "./_layout.css";             // chrome (a přes @import zase tokeny)
import { ThemeToggle } from "./_specimen-controls";
import "./components-callout.css";  // vlastní třídy
```

### Příčina A — 5 specimenů bez tokenů + layoutu

Diagnostika (anchored na reálné `import` řádky, ne na text v obsahu specimenu):

| Specimen | `colors_and_type.css` | `_layout.css` | screenshot |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `components-diff-view` | ✗ | ✗ | 5,4 KB (bílá plocha) |
| `components-monospace-table` | ✗ | ✗ | 5,5 KB (bílá plocha) |
| `iconography` | ✗ | ✗ | 5,8 KB (bílá plocha) |
| `selection` | ✗ | ✗ | 5,4 KB (bílá plocha) |
| `ui_kits-desktop-showcase` | ✗ | ✗ | 134 KB, ale rozsypaný layout + špatné fonty |

Tyto soubory importují jen `./_specimen-controls` + (někdy) vlastní `.css`. Vlastní `.css` (`.diff{background:var(--bg-1)…}`, `table.mono{…var(--font-mono)…}`) se sice načte, ale je celé postavené na CSS proměnných z `colors_and_type.css`, které v tomto bundlu **neexistují** → `border:1px solid var(--border-default)` je invalid (žádné ohraničení), `background:var(--bg-1)` → transparentní, `font-family:var(--font-mono)` → default. Bez `_layout.css` navíc chybí celý specimen chrome → vizuálně „bez CSS". (U `ui_kits-desktop-showcase` je vlastní `.css` dost velké, aby vznikla aspoň tmavá změť, ale chrome a typografie chybí stejně.)

Jediné, co se v blank specimenech zobrazí, je LIGHT/DARK toggle z `_specimen-controls.tsx` — má vlastní inline styly nezávislé na tokenech.

### Příčina B — `.btn` / `.input` se nenačítá nikde

`.btn`, `.input`, `.select`, `.textarea` jsou definované **výhradně** v `preview/_components.css`. Ten **neimportuje žádný preview specimen** (jediný importér v celém `.design` je `ui/Sync Hub Admin.tsx`), a `_layout.css` ho `@import`em netahá (řetězí jen `colors_and_type.css`). Výsledek: ve všech 12 specimenech, které vykreslují `.btn`/`.input`/`.select`/`.textarea`, jsou tyto prvky **nativní prohlížečové** (šedý OS button, světlý input).

Postižené specimeny (12): `colors-accent`, `colors-themes-side-by-side`, `components-buttons`, `components-code-block`, `components-dialogs`, `components-inputs`, `components-tooltips`, `elevation`, `empty-state`, `focus`, `radii`, `state-system`. Proto „**skoro všude rozbité button elementy**" a u `components-inputs` „**jen částečně, konkrétně input elementy**" (zbytek stránky importuje tokeny+layout, takže chrome je OK, rozbité jsou jen form prvky).

### Proč „dřív to nedělalo"

Časová osa (git):

1. **HTML éra** — dev-server linkoval sdílené stylesheety (`colors_and_type.css` + `_layout.css` + `_components.css`) do **každého** canvasu globálně přes HTML shell. Vše nastylované zadarmo.
2. **`0f6b847` „self-contained project DS specimens"** — migrace na TSX + per-file `import`. Načítání CSS se přesunulo do import grafu. Vznikly obě díry: 5 souborů nedostalo token/layout importy (+ chyběl jim `ThemeToggle` → mount crash → blank), a `_components.css` se do grafu nezapojilo vůbec.
3. **`745bcf0` „repair 5 project DS specimens that rendered blank"** — opravilo **jen** mount crash (doplnilo `import { ThemeToggle }`), takže 5 souborů přestalo být úplně blank. CSS importy nedoplnilo → příčina A zůstala jako „renderuje, ale bez stylů". Příčinu B commit neřešil vůbec.

`canvas-build.ts:170` potvrzuje: *„Gather any sibling CSS the bundler produced from `import "./<slug>.css"`"* — žádné globální injektování. Import graf je jediný zdroj pravdy a má díry.

## Impact

- **Severity:** Medium (vizuální/dogfooding; ne runtime crash, ne produkční npm artefakt). Postihuje vlastní `.design/` tohoto repa, ne plugin distribuovaný uživatelům.
- **Rozsah:** 5 specimenů úplně bez stylů + 12 specimenů s nestylovanými button/input prvky.
- **Workaround:** žádný pro uživatele; oprava = doplnit importy.

## Proposed Fix

Implementace patří do `/flow:bug-fix`. Návrh (minimální, mirroruje původní global-injection chování):

**Příčina B (jeden řádek, opraví všech 12 najednou):** do `preview/_layout.css` přidat
```css
@import url("./_components.css");
```
hned za stávající `@import url("../colors_and_type.css")`. Tím každý specimen, co už importuje `_layout.css`, dostane `.btn`/`.input` zadarmo.

**Příčina A (5 souborů):** do `components-diff-view.tsx`, `components-monospace-table.tsx`, `iconography.tsx`, `selection.tsx`, `ui_kits-desktop-showcase.tsx` doplnit nad jejich stávající importy:
```js
import "../colors_and_type.css";
import "./_layout.css";
```
(Po fixu B stačí i jen `_layout.css`, protože ten už tranzitivně tahá tokeny i `_components.css`. Explicitní `colors_and_type.css` ponechat kvůli čitelnosti a paritě s ostatními.)

**Soubory ke změně:**
- `.design/system/project/preview/_layout.css` (+1 `@import`)
- `.design/system/project/preview/{components-diff-view,components-monospace-table,iconography,selection,ui_kits-desktop-showcase}.tsx` (+2 importy každý)

## Testing Requirements (prevence — aby se to nevracelo)

Symptom unikl, protože `/design:smoke` flaguje jen **blank iframe + error overlay**, ne „renderuje, ale bez stylů". Doporučené guardy:

1. **Statický import-lint** nad `system/*/preview/*.tsx`: assert, že každý specimen importuje `_layout.css` (a tím tranzitivně tokeny + komponenty). Deterministické, bez renderu — chytí příčinu A i regresi B u kteréhokoli nového specimenu. Kandidát: rozšířit `/design:smoke` step nebo nový check v `dev-server/test/`.
2. **Orphan-CSS check:** assert, že každý sdílený `preview/_*.css` je dosažitelný z import grafu aspoň jednoho canvasu (chytí „nikdo neimportuje `_components.css`").
3. **Computed-style smoke:** po mountu v `/design:smoke` ověřit, že `getComputedStyle(body).fontFamily` / `backgroundColor` odpovídá DS tokenu, ne prohlížečovému defaultu (`Times`/`rgb(255,255,255)`). Chytí třídu „mountuje se, ale bez stylů", kterou `745bcf0` přehlédl.
4. **Procesní:** vizuální verifikace musí porovnávat proti nastylovanému baselinu, ne jen „je tam obsah" — viz DDR-021. Při opravě „blank" vždy ověřit i styl, ne jen mount.

## Complexity

**Low** (oprava: 6 souborů, ~11 řádků). Prevence (lint/smoke guardy): **Medium**.

## Ověřeno

agent-browser screenshoty všech 38 specimenů (`/tmp/spec-shots/*.png`): 4 fully-blank (~5 KB), `ui_kits-desktop-showcase` rozsypaný, `components-buttons`/`components-inputs` mají chrome OK ale nativní form prvky, kontrola `components-callout` plně nastylovaná. Statická diagnostika import grafu i vizuál se shodují.

decision.title: RCA: DS scaffold files never appear in the file tree — even after a manual reload (stale boot-time config)
decision.rationale:
# RCA: DS scaffold files never appear in the file tree — even after a manual reload (stale boot-time config)

> Ticket source: manual paste (tracker = `github`, no issue number).
> Reported (CZ): *"podle acp chatu vpravo by uz meli pribyvat nejake design system files, ale ani kdyz udelam file tree reload tak nic nevidim ve file tree… podle aktualni struktury uz tam ty soubory videt jdou"* — the ACP chat is running `/design:setup-ds` and scaffolding a full design system (34 preview specimens + README/SKILL/tokens under `.design/system/kanban-glass/`); the files ARE on disk in `/Users/iagh/git/maude-git-smoke`, but the FILES tree shows only "UI CANVASES (2)" and **a manual tree reload does not help**.

## Summary

This is **not** a recurrence of the watcher-event bugs (`issue-acp-new-canvas-not-in-filetree.md`, `issue-desktop-filetree-no-manual-reload.md`) — those were "the tree isn't *nudged*"; both fixes shipped (DDR-124 `canvas-list-watch.ts`, manual refresh button + focus backstop). The tell here is that the **manual reload also shows nothing**: `loadTree()` re-fetches `GET /_index-data` fine, but the *server's answer itself* omits every `system/**` file.

Root cause: the dev-server reads `.design/config.json` **exactly once, at boot** (`createContext()` → `loadConfig()`), and `/design:setup-ds` **mutates that file mid-session**. The smoke project's config at server boot was the seeded e2e fixture:

```json
"canvasGroups": [{ "label": "UI kit", "path": "ui" }],
"designSystems": []
```

The scaffold then rewrote it on disk to add `{ "label": "Design system", "path": "system" }`, the `designSystems: [kanban-glass]` entry, `tokensCssRel`, `defaultDesignSystem`, … The running server never re-reads it, so:

- `buildIndexData()` (`api.ts:1689`) iterates the stale `cfg.canvasGroups` → only `ui/` is ever listed → the 34 scaffolded specimens under `system/kanban-glass/` are invisible in `/_index-data` no matter how often the client reloads the tree.
- `canvas-list-watch.ts:89` captured `groupPaths` from the boot cfg at construction → writes under `system/` fail the `isCanvasCandidate` gate → no `canvas-list-update` is ever emitted for them either (the auto-refresh path is equally blind).
- The client's `cfg` (fetched once from `/_config` at boot, `app.jsx:5998`) is equally stale — `designSystems`/`tokensCssRel` for the new DS would be wrong even if the tree showed the files.

## Root Cause

`ctx.cfg` is a boot-time snapshot with no invalidation path:

1. `context.ts:225` — `createContext()` calls `loadConfig(repoRoot)` once; `ctx.cfg` and the derived `ctx.paths.tokensUrlRel` / `ctx.paths.systemDirRel` are never recomputed.
2. `fs-watch.ts` **does** see the `config.json` write (it emits `fs:json` + `fs:any` for it — config.json is not in the skip list), but **no subscriber reloads the config**. The event is broadcast to WS clients as `fs:json` and otherwise ignored.
3. Every module that would behave correctly with a fresh config reads it via the shared `ctx.cfg` object reference (`const { cfg } = ctx` in `api.ts:398`), so they'd all pick up an **in-place** mutation automatically. The one construction-time value copy is `canvas-list-watch.ts:89`'s `groupPaths`.

`/design:setup-ds` editing `config.json` while a server is running is not exotic — it is the *documented first-bootstrap flow* (the ACP panel dogfood loop: scaffold a DS from chat → watch it appear). Any config edit mid-session (adding a canvas group, adding a second DS, changing `defaultDesignSystem`) hits the same wall today and silently requires a server restart.

## Impact

- **Who:** anyone running `/design:setup-ds` (or hand-editing `.design/config.json`) while a Maude window is open — the primary first-run experience. The desktop app makes it worse: the sidecar respawn (project switch) is the only "restart".
- **Severity:** Medium-high UX. No data loss — files are on disk and appear after a server restart — but the headline flow "bootstrap a DS from the ACP chat" ends with an apparently empty result, and the manual refresh button (shipped precisely to recover from stale trees) demonstrably does nothing, which reads as "the scaffold failed".
- **Workaround today:** restart the dev-server (kill + re-invoke, or desktop project-switch there-and-back).

## Proposed Fix

Hot-reload the config when `.design/config.json` changes on disk; mutate the shared objects **in place** so every existing capture sees the fresh values; then nudge both refresh paths.

1. **`context.ts`** — export `reloadConfig(ctx): boolean`: re-run the existing `loadConfig(ctx.paths.repoRoot)`, deep-compare with the current cfg (JSON), and on change mutate `ctx.cfg` in place (delete removed keys + `Object.assign`) and recompute `ctx.paths.tokensUrlRel` + `ctx.paths.systemDirRel` in place. `designRoot` is deliberately NOT hot-reloadable (the fs-watcher and every path root hang off it) — log a warn that a restart is required and keep the old value.
2. **`canvas-list-watch.ts`** — read `ctx.cfg.canvasGroups` inside the `fs:any` handler instead of the captured `groupPaths` const (`snapshot()` already reads live).
3. **`server.ts`** — subscribe to `fs:json`; when the design-root-relative path is exactly `config.json`, debounce briefly and call `reloadConfig(ctx)`. On change: `canvasListWatch.refresh()` (its set-diff now sees the new group → emits the same `canvas-list-update` adds the tree already listens for) and `ctx.bus.emit('config-updated', …)`.
4. **`ws.ts`** — relay `config-updated` to WS clients (one line, next to the `canvas-list-update` relay).
5. **`client/app.jsx`** — extract the boot `/_config` fetch into a callback and re-run it on the `config-updated` WS message (functional merge, same as boot). Rebuild the committed bundle release-minified per the CLAUDE.md rule.

## Testing Requirements

- **`test/config-reload.test.ts`** (bun:test): a captured `const cfg = ctx.cfg` reference sees the new `canvasGroups` after `reloadConfig`; derived `paths.tokensUrlRel`/`systemDirRel` recompute; unchanged file → `false` (no spurious emits); invalid JSON mid-edit → keep the old cfg (no crash, no downgrade to defaults).
- **canvas-list-watch:** after mutating `ctx.cfg.canvasGroups` (simulating the hot reload), a write under the NEW group passes the gate and `refresh()` emits `added` for the group's pre-existing files.
- **No-false-positive:** an unrelated `.json` write (e.g. a `.meta.json`) must not trigger a config reload.
- Full `bun test` suite in `apps/studio/` stays green; `/design:smoke` class unaffected (no committed-bundle drift beyond the deliberate rebuild).

## Complexity

**Low-Medium.** The reload itself is small and self-contained; the risk concentrates in the in-place mutation contract (any FUTURE module that copies a cfg *value* at construction time re-introduces the bug — the canvas-list-watch fix and a comment on `reloadConfig` are the guardrails) and in keeping `designRoot` immutable.
