decision.title: RCA: Ticket `plugin-name-prefix-doubling` — `/design:design:new`, `flow:flow:a11y-auditor`
decision.rationale:
# RCA: Ticket `plugin-name-prefix-doubling` — `/design:design:new`, `flow:flow:a11y-auditor`

- **Reported:** 2026-07-28 (user screenshot of slash autocomplete showing `/design:design:new`, `/design:design:edit`, `/design:design:init`)
- **Tracker:** none — manual paste (`integrations.tracker.provider: github`, but no issue was filed)
- **Investigator:** single-pass. Step 4.5 hypothesis debate **skipped deliberately** — the root cause is not contested (it is predicted verbatim in DDR-006's own "Negative" section) and I hold both a positive and a negative control (below). Session policy also forbids unrequested subagent spawning.

## Summary

Claude Code changed how it registers plugin commands and agents. It now prepends the plugin namespace (`<plugin>:`) itself, **unconditionally, on top of whatever `name:` frontmatter declares**. Maude bakes that same prefix *into* `name:` by design — [DDR-006](../../decisions/DDR-006-plugin-namespace-in-name-frontmatter.md) made `name: design:new` mandatory and load-bearing back in May 2026, to work around Claude Code [issue #22063](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/22063) (setting `name:` used to *strip* the namespace, so `/flow:resume` registered as bare `/resume` and collided with the built-in).

That bug has since been fixed or reworked upstream. The workaround is now the defect: `<plugin>:` (runtime) + `design:new` (frontmatter) = `design:design:new`.

DDR-006 called this exact outcome:

> **Depends on a Claude Code behavior that may change.** If the underlying bug (#22063) gets fixed and Claude Code starts namespacing automatically when `name:` is bare, our explicit prefix will either be redundant (best case) or get double-prefixed (worst case, e.g. `/flow:flow:resume`).

Worst case landed. Nothing in Maude changed — this is upstream drift, and the repo has already begun silently and inconsistently adapting to it (see Impact §3).

## Root Cause

`name:` frontmatter is no longer the fully-qualified slash name. Claude Code 2.1.220 treats it as the **bare slug** and adds the namespace itself.

### Evidence

**Positive control — a file WITH the prefixed `name:` registers doubled.**

`plugins/design/agents/a11y-critic.md:2` declares `name: design:a11y-critic`. This session's agent registry lists it as **`design:design:a11y-critic`**. Same for all 31 prefixed agents across both plugins (`flow:flow:a11y-auditor`, `design:design:signature-moment-critic`, …). The user's screenshot shows the identical doubling on the slash-command surface.

**Negative control — a file WITHOUT `name:` frontmatter registers with exactly ONE prefix.**

`plugins/design/agents/_draw-design-rules.md` and `plugins/flow/agents/_security-regex-catalog.md` have no YAML frontmatter at all (they open directly with a markdown `#` heading). They register as **`design:_draw-design-rules`** and **`flow:_security-regex-catalog`** — single prefix, derived from filename.

The two controls together isolate the cause exactly: the runtime supplies `<plugin>:` in both cases. The only variable is whether our own `name:` adds a second one.

### Secondary finding — the doubling is surface-dependent

Not every Claude Code surface resolves the name the same way. Measured in this session:

| Surface | Key derived from | Design plugin example | Doubled? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Slash-command autocomplete (the screenshot) | `<plugin>:` + `name:` | `/design:design:new` | **yes** |
| Agent registry (`Agent` tool `subagent_type`) | `<plugin>:` + `name:` | `design:design:a11y-critic` | **yes** |
| Skill-tool listing of commands | `<plugin>:` + **filename** | `design:new` | no |
| Skill registry (`plugins/*/skills/*/`) | `<plugin>:` + **directory name** | `design:design-system` | no |

Skills escape entirely — `plugins/design/skills/design-system/SKILL.md` declares `name: design:design-system`, but the skill registry ignores the field and keys on the directory, so it lands on `design:design-system` by coincidence. (`design:design` looks doubled but is not: the skill directory is literally `skills/design/`.)

This inconsistency is itself an upstream defect worth reporting — the same `name:` field is authoritative on two surfaces and ignored on two others.

### Ruled out

- **Double plugin load** (the DDR-168 "bundled ACP copy + marketplace copy" hazard). Would produce two *separate* registry entries, not one entry with a stuttered prefix. `installed_plugins.json` shows exactly one install each of `design@maude` / `flow@maude` (v0.47.0, user scope, `gitCommitSha a6c6b36b`).
- **YAML parse artifact.** `name: design:new` is valid YAML — a colon not followed by a space does not split a scalar. Values arrive intact.
- **A Maude-side regression.** `git log` on the affected files shows no `name:`-touching commit; the last edits to `commands/new.md` are unrelated feature work.

## Impact

**Severity: Medium.** Every user-facing entry point is cosmetically wrong, and there is latent functional breakage in agent routing. Commands remain invocable, so nothing is hard-down.

**1. UX / discoverability (certain, universal).** Every one of the 54 slash commands autocompletes with a stutter. The namespace-narrowing benefit DDR-006 bought still works (`/design:` filters correctly) but every row reads badly. Affects 100% of users on current Claude Code.

**2. Docs ↔ reality mismatch (certain).** `/design:help` and `/flow:help` render `/<name>` directly — DDR-006 step 2 explicitly changed them to avoid double-prefixing, which now *causes* it. So `/flow:help` prints `/flow:plan` while autocomplete offers `/flow:flow:plan`. `README.md`, both `CATEGORIES.md`, the Fumadocs site pages, and the GitHub issue templates all document the single form.

**3. Agent-spawn routing (latent, partially already broken).** 20 `subagent_type:` references in plugin markdown name agents in a form that is no longer the registry key:

```
plugins/design/commands/new.md:929    subagent_type: "design:design-system-keeper"   → registry has design:design:design-system-keeper
plugins/design/commands/draw.md:75    subagent_type: "design:draw-agent"
plugins/design/commands/import.md:201 subagent_type: "design:reconstruct-agent"
… (17 more)
```

The repo has **three coexisting reference forms**, which is the strongest signal that this is already biting in practice:

| Form | Example | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| bare (pre-DDR-006 leftovers) | `subagent_type: security-auditor` | `flow/commands/validate-security.md:61,67`, `execute.md:106`, `review-code.md:132`, `design/commands/critic.md:44` |
| single-prefixed (DDR-006 canonical) | `subagent_type: "design:draw-agent"` | 20 sites across design commands + skills |
| **double-prefixed** | `design:design:signature-moment-critic` | `design/skills/design-system/_bootstrap.md:1263-1269` (7 refs) |

`_bootstrap.md` was hand-patched to the doubled form by some earlier session — i.e. someone hit a real resolution failure and fixed it locally rather than at the root. Whether Claude Code fuzzy-resolves the single form is **unverified**; the `_bootstrap.md` patch suggests it does not, at least sometimes.

**4. Guard coverage gap.** `cli/lib/plugin-cli-reachability.test.mjs` bans direct `dev-server/bin/*.sh` calls in plugin markdown, but nothing lints `name:` frontmatter or `subagent_type:` forms. DDR-006's verification was a one-time manual grep, so the drift in `_bootstrap.md` passed CI unnoticed.

**Workaround for users, right now:** type the doubled form, or use `/design:help` and then hit Tab from `/design:design:` — everything works, it just reads wrong.

## Proposed Fix

Revert DDR-006's decision #1: `name:` goes back to the **bare slug**, and the `<plugin>:` prefix becomes the runtime's job.

**Do NOT start with the 114-file sweep.** DDR-006 exists precisely because the naive assumption about this behavior was wrong once already, and the secondary finding above shows the surfaces disagree with each other. Reproduce DDR-006's own methodology — probe one file first.

### Step 0 — Empirical probe (blocking gate)

Mirror DDR-006's `resume.md` experiment. Change `name:` in exactly **two** files:

- `plugins/flow/commands/pause.md`: `name: flow:pause` → `name: pause`
- `plugins/design/agents/copy-critic.md`: `name: design:copy-critic` → `name: copy-critic`

Then `/plugin marketplace update maude` + `/reload-plugins` in a scratch project, and record:

1. Does autocomplete show `/flow:pause` (fix confirmed) or bare `/pause` (upstream unchanged — abort, do nothing)?
2. Does `subagent_type: "design:copy-critic"` resolve? Does `"copy-critic"`? Does `"design:design:copy-critic"` stop resolving?
3. Does bare `/pause` also stay reachable (collision surface)?

Everything below is conditional on probe outcome 1 being "fix confirmed".

### Step 1 — Sweep `name:` frontmatter

Strip the `<plugin>:` prefix from `name:` in **114 files**:

| Location | Files | Affected today? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `plugins/design/commands/` | 23 | yes |
| `plugins/flow/commands/` | 31 | yes |
| `plugins/design/agents/` | 20 | yes |
| `plugins/flow/agents/` | 11 | yes |
| `plugins/design/skills/` | 8 | no (registry ignores the field) |
| `plugins/flow/skills/` | 21 | no (registry ignores the field) |

The 29 skill files are cosmetic-only, but sweep them in the same pass — leaving them prefixed re-creates the "which convention applies where?" ambiguity that produced the three-form mess.

Filenames already equal the intended slug everywhere, so this is a pure prefix strip. `init.md` keeps its DDR-006 bare-verb carve-out unchanged (`name: init`, namespaced to `/flow:init` by the runtime — same end state, so DDR-006 decision #3 survives intact).

### Step 2 — Re-fix the help renderers

`plugins/design/commands/help.md:17` and `plugins/flow/commands/help.md:16` currently instruct: *"The `name:` field is the fully-qualified slash name … so render it directly with a leading `/`."* Change to render `/<plugin>:<name>`, i.e. re-instate exactly what DDR-006 step 2 removed. Both files' render templates (`| /<name> |`) need the prefix too.

### Step 3 — Normalize all three agent-reference forms to one

Bring every `subagent_type:` reference to whatever the probe proves correct (expected: bare slug):

- 7 doubled refs in `plugins/design/skills/design-system/_bootstrap.md:1263-1269`
- 20 single-prefixed refs across `design/commands/{new,edit,draw,import,reel,video-analyze}.md` + `skills/design-system/_DISCOVERY-v1.md`
- 5 already-bare refs in `flow/commands/{validate-security,execute,review-code}.md` + `design/commands/critic.md` — verify, don't assume

Note `cli/lib/reconstruct-toolset.test.mjs:191` asserts on the literal string `subagent_type: "design:design-critic"` — that test must move with the sweep or it goes red.

### Step 4 — Add the missing guard

A new check in `cli/lib/` (alongside `plugin-cli-reachability.test.mjs`), wired into `quality.yml`:

- no `^name: (design|flow):` in `plugins/**` — catches re-introduction of the prefix
- no `(design|flow):(design|flow):` anywhere in `plugins/**` — catches the doubled form
- every `subagent_type:` value resolves to an actual file in `plugins/*/agents/`

This is the durable fix. The class of bug is "convention depends on unversioned upstream behavior"; the only real protection is a test that fails when the convention drifts.

### Step 5 — Docs + decision record

- Supersede DDR-006 with a new DDR (check the decisions dir **and** the uncommitted README index diff before claiming a number — numbering races on shared `main`). Record the new rule, the probe evidence, and the surface-dependency table, so the next reversal has data instead of assumption.
- Update `CLAUDE.md` § "Plugin command naming" (currently states the prefix is mandatory and load-bearing — it becomes actively harmful).
- Update both `CATEGORIES.md`, `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, the site Fumadocs pages, and the GitHub issue templates.
- Do **not** rewrite `CHANGELOG.md`, `.ai/plans/archive/**`, or `.ai/state/STATE.md` — same reasoning DDR-006 used: they record historical state.

### Known tradeoff to surface before committing

Reverting re-opens the original collision on **older Claude Code versions**: `flow:resume` → bare `resume` collides with built-in `/resume`, and `flow:init` / `flow:status` with `/init` / `/status`. If the auto-namespacing fix is recent, users pinned to an older CLI get DDR-006's original bug back. Options, in order of preference:

1. Ship the revert and document a minimum Claude Code version in `README.md` / the marketplace description.
2. Ship it unconditionally — the plugins already track current Claude Code closely and users update.
3. Do nothing and accept the stutter — only defensible if the probe shows agent-spawn routing still resolves the single form, which would drop severity to cosmetic.

This is a product call, not a technical one. Recommend option 1.

### Also worth doing (out of scope for the fix)

File an upstream issue on the surface-dependency inconsistency (§ Secondary finding): the same `name:` field is authoritative for slash commands + agents but ignored for skills + the Skill-tool command listing. Reference #22063 and #43695.

## Testing Requirements

- **Manual probe (Step 0)** — the gate. Two files, `/plugin marketplace update maude` + `/reload-plugins` in a scratch project (`cd /tmp/scratch && claude`, per the README's local-development recipe — never from this repo's own directory).
- **Post-sweep autocomplete check** — `/design:` and `/flow:` narrow to their own plugin, every row single-prefixed; `/flow:resume` and native `/resume` both present as distinct rows; `/flow:init` distinct from native `/init`.
- **Agent-spawn smoke** — run `/design:critic` (spawns a panel) and `/design:new --quick` (spawns `design-system-keeper` at `new.md:929`) end to end. A silent no-op is the failure mode to watch for, not an error.
- **New automated guard (Step 4)** — three greps, must go red against the current tree before the sweep and green after. Add to `quality.yml`.
- **`cli/lib/reconstruct-toolset.test.mjs`** — update the literal assertion at line 191 in the same commit.
- **No dev-server involvement.** Nothing here touches `apps/studio/`; do not boot the server or run `bun test` in that tree, which risks clobbering the committed `dist/` bundles.

## Complexity

**Medium.** The individual edit is trivial (strip a prefix), but the blast radius is 114 plugin files plus docs, tests, and site content, and correctness hinges entirely on the Step-0 probe. Getting it wrong re-breaks every slash command for every user — which is exactly how the repo got here.

Sequencing: Step 0 alone (~15 min, needs a scratch session). Steps 1–5 (~2h) only after the probe confirms.

decision.title: RCA: Safari / WKWebView canvas zoom — fonts don't scale + trackpad zoom not smooth
decision.rationale:
# RCA: Safari / WKWebView canvas zoom — fonts don't scale + trackpad zoom not smooth

> Ticket (pasted, no tracker ID): *"Potřebuji appku připravit pro Safari. Všiml jsem si pár věcí co je tam problém. Například zoom v canvasu není úplně tak smooth hlavně na touchpadu. Fonty zůstávají stejně velké ale měly by se zmenšovat v artboardech v canvasu při zoomování. Ale věřím že tam toho může být víc. V Chrome browseru to funguje všechno perfektně."*

## Summary

The canvas pan/zoom engine (`apps/studio/canvas-lib.tsx`) drives the **scale** dimension with the CSS **`zoom`** property, co-located with `transform: translate()` for pan on the same `.dc-world` element, using a Blink-specific translate compensation (`v.x / z`). CSS `zoom` is a historically non-standardized, **non-interoperable** property: Blink (Chrome) and WebKit (Safari **and the Tauri WKWebView native shell**) diverge in (a) how `zoom` cascades scale into descendant text/layout when co-located with a `transform`, and (b) whether a `zoom` change is GPU-composited or forces a main-thread relayout+repaint. The engine was authored and tuned against Blink's `zoom` semantics, so on WebKit it produces exactly the two reported symptoms — artboard text not scaling with the world, and janky trackpad-pinch zoom — while Chrome works perfectly.

**This is not just a "Safari browser" issue.** The branch in flight (`native-app`, Phase 26 / DDR-106) ships a **Tauri v2 shell, which on macOS renders the entire dev-server UI through WKWebView — the same WebKit engine as Safari.** Every WebKit rendering divergence found here will hit the native desktop app's own users, not only people who open the web build in Safari. DDR-106 already notes the cross-origin canvas iframe "must survive WKWebView"; the zoom engine is the next thing that must.

## Root Cause

### Primary: scale is driven by CSS `zoom`, co-located with `transform`

`writeTransform` (`apps/studio/canvas-lib.tsx:671-678`) writes **both** properties to the same element:

```js
const z = v.zoom || 1;
el.style.transform = `translate(${v.x / z}px, ${v.y / z}px)`; // pan
el.style.zoom = String(z);                                    // scale
```

The author deliberately chose `zoom` over `transform: scale()` to keep text crisp at high zoom (`canvas-lib.tsx:656-661` — *"`transform: scale` upscales a cached layer, which produces the pixelation users see at zoom > ~1.5"*), and asserts `zoom` is *"supported in Chrome / Safari / Edge (always)"*. "Supported" is true; **"renders identically" is not.** Two concrete WebKit ≠ Blink divergences explain the report:

1. **Descendant text not scaling (`fonty zůstávají stejně velké`).** When `zoom` and a `transform` sit on the *same* box, WebKit promotes that box to a composited layer (the `transform` + `will-change: transform` at `canvas-lib.tsx:200` force layer promotion) and resolves `zoom` against that layer differently than Blink does. The `v.x / z` translate compensation at line 675 is a Blink-only correction (Blink multiplies a co-located `translate` by the zoom factor; WebKit's resolution order differs), which is direct evidence the geometry was calibrated to one engine. The net WebKit effect the user sees: the artboard frame geometry responds to the gesture but descendant `font-size` does not track it the way Blink's "effective zoom" relayout does. (Artboard text is sized in **`px`** tokens — `--type-xs: 11px`, `.design/system/*/…tokens.css` — so this is *not* the separate WebKit "`zoom` ignores `rem`" bug; it is the co-located `zoom`+`transform` cascade divergence.)

2. **Trackpad pinch not smooth (`zoom … není smooth hlavně na touchpadu`).** `zoom` is a **layout-affecting** property. In WebKit, each change triggers a main-thread relayout + repaint of the whole artboard subtree; it is not composited. The trackpad-pinch path (`canvas-lib.tsx:920-937`) fires a high-frequency stream of small `ctrlKey` wheel deltas, so WebKit relayouts the entire world dozens of times per second → visible jank. Blink has an optimized `zoom` fast path, so Chrome stays smooth. `transform: scale()`, by contrast, is GPU-composited on every engine and never relayouts — which is exactly why pinch is smooth in Chrome's *other* zoom surfaces and why it would be smooth here on WebKit too.

### Why "Chrome works perfectly"

Both symptoms are WebKit-specific. Blink's `zoom` implementation (a) relayouts descendants so `px` fonts scale, and (b) has a fast compositing path so pinch stays smooth. The code is correct *for Blink*; it was never exercised on WebKit before the native shell made WKWebView a first-class target.

### Surrounding sweep (the "věřím že tam toho může být víc")

A broader WebKit-compat pass over `apps/studio/client` + `canvas-lib.tsx` came back **otherwise clean** — no `backdrop-filter` (un-prefixed), no `requestIdleCallback`, no `scrollend`, no `structuredClone`/`findLast` reliance, `navigator.clipboard` is optional-chained (`app.jsx:824,6430`). The CSS `zoom` engine is the single dominant WebKit divergence in the canvas surface. The likely "more" the user senses is the **family of zoom-derived symptoms** that all flow from this one root cause: zoom-around-cursor anchoring drift (the `/z` compensation is wrong on WebKit), minimap rect math (`canvas-lib.tsx:2055-2058` divides by `vp.zoom`), and any HUD/overlay positioned in world coords — all inherit the same mis-calibration. Fixing the scale primitive fixes the cluster.

## Impact

- **Who:** (1) Safari web-build users today; (2) **every macOS user of the `native-app` Tauri shell** once it ships — WKWebView *is* the renderer, so this is a launch-blocking defect for the native app, not a nice-to-have browser-parity fix.
- **Severity:** High. Zoom + legible-at-zoom text is the core interaction of a canvas tool; "fonts don't shrink" makes zoomed-out overviews unreadable and "pinch is janky" makes the primary navigation gesture feel broken.
- **Workaround:** Keyboard zoom (`Cmd +/-/0/1`) and button zoom share the same `zoom`-property path, so they suffer the font-scaling bug too but avoid the high-frequency jank. No real user-facing workaround; use Chrome.

## Proposed Fix

**Stop relying on CSS `zoom` for the live gesture.** Recommended, lowest-risk-for-best-result: a **hybrid that the codebase is already wired for** — `isInteracting` state already exists (`canvas-lib.tsx:601,638,1114`):

- **During an active gesture** (`isInteracting === true`): scale via `transform: scale(z) translate(...)` on `.dc-world`. GPU-composited → **smooth pinch on WebKit**, uniform scaling of all descendants incl. text → **fonts scale**, no relayout. Drop the `/z` translate hack on this path (plain `transform: scale(z) translate(x,y)` keeps screen-px translate correct on both engines).
- **On settle** (`onSettle`, `SETTLE_MS` after the gesture, `canvas-lib.tsx:688-695`): swap to crisp rendering — either re-rasterize the composited layer (toggle `will-change` off/on, or a 1-frame opacity nudge), or apply the `zoom` property *alone* (no co-located transform) for the static crisp state. This preserves the author's original crispness goal (the reason `zoom` was chosen) without paying its cost during interaction.

This resolves **both** reported symptoms at the source and is engine-correct on Blink and WebKit.

Files to change:
- `apps/studio/canvas-lib.tsx` — `writeTransform` (671-678): branch on `isInteractingStateRef`; gesture path uses `transform: scale()`, settle path uses crisp `zoom`/re-raster. Re-verify zoom-around-cursor math (`zoomAt` 744-755), `fit`/`reset`/`jumpTo` easing (765-840), and minimap projection (2055-2058) under the new transform convention.
- `apps/studio/client/styles/0-reset.css` — add `-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%` to `html, body` as a belt-and-suspenders guard against WebKit text-inflation re-growing shrunk text (cheap, no Blink effect).
- Rebuild the committed release bundles after the change (`cd apps/studio && MAUDE_SKIP_RUNTIME_BUILD=1 bun run build.ts --release`) per CLAUDE.md "In-app What's New" / bundle rules; `canvas-lib.tsx` ships via the dev-server.

**Alternatives considered:**
- *Pure `transform: scale()` everywhere* — simplest, smooth + correct on all engines, but reintroduces the >1.5× upscale pixelation the author explicitly avoided. Acceptable if the hybrid proves too fiddly; pixelation is mild on Retina/HiDPI and can be softened by raising the rasterization scale.
- *Pure `zoom`, isolated onto its own nested element* (outer `.dc-pan` = `transform: translate`, inner `.dc-world` = `zoom` alone) — fixes the **font-scaling** divergence (un-co-locates the two properties so WebKit applies a clean layout zoom) and removes the `/z` hack, **but does not fix smoothness** (WebKit `zoom` still relayouts on every pinch tick). Only viable if smoothness is dropped from scope.

## Testing Requirements

Repo has no unit-test harness for the dev-server UI (CLAUDE.md), so verification is live-render based:

1. **Confirm the exact WebKit mechanism before/after** — boot the dev server, open a canvas in **Safari** *and* in the **Tauri shell (WKWebView)**, and during a zoom run probe artboard text with `getComputedStyle(el).fontSize` at zoom 0.5 / 1.0 / 2.0. Pre-fix WebKit should show font-size *not* tracking zoom; post-fix it should track on both engines. (Use a computed-style probe, **not** a screenshot — per the `reference_css_var_alias_scope_trap` memory, screenshots can lie about computed values.)
2. **Smoothness** — trackpad pinch-zoom in Safari/WKWebView: visually confirm no relayout stutter post-fix; optionally sample frame timing.
3. **Cross-engine parity** — re-run the same in Chrome to confirm **no regression** (per `feedback_no_break_exhaustive_verify`: this is exactly the risky dev-server-refactor class — inventory every zoom-dependent feature and verify each).
4. **Feature matrix to re-verify** (all share the transform primitive): wheel pan, shift-wheel horizontal pan, spacebar/middle-mouse/hand-tool drag pan, `Cmd +/-/0/1`, `Cmd+Opt+1..9` jump-to-artboard, zoom-around-cursor anchoring, `fit`/`reset` easing, minimap rect, snap guides, and selection halos — in **both** WebKit and Blink.
5. **Run `/design:smoke`** after the bundle rebuild to catch any blank/unstyled-iframe regression (DDR-021/DDR-068).

## Complexity

**Medium.** The change is localized to one function (`writeTransform`) plus a one-line CSS guard, but the *verification* surface is wide — every pan/zoom/projection consumer must be re-checked on two engines, the committed bundle must be rebuilt release-minified, and the fix lands on the in-flight `native-app` branch where it is effectively launch-blocking for the WKWebView shell.

decision.title: RCA: Sidecar cache consumers skipped by the agent — cache populated by ≈0 real runs
decision.rationale:
# RCA: Sidecar cache consumers skipped by the agent — cache populated by ≈0 real runs

> No tracker (`integrations.tracker.provider = none`). Discovered 2026-05-29 while
> verifying Phase C ([`phase-c-sidecar-monitor-background.md`](../../plans/archive/phase-c-sidecar-monitor-background.md))
> end-to-end with a real `/design:edit` run in `/tmp/maude-scratch`.

## Summary

The Phase C sidecar cache (`cli/lib/cache.mjs` + the `maude cache` CLI) is mechanically sound, but the **consumers** that should read/populate it are wired as LLM-executed markdown bash-block instructions. In a real, fully-qualifying `/design:edit` run the agent did the expensive work (read `_components.css` / `colors_and_type.css` / `canvas-lib.tsx` via the `Read` tool) and **silently skipped the literal `maude cache get/put` calls** — leaving the cache empty and `maude cache stats` at "no activity". The cache benefit (skipping CSS/canvas-lib reads, codebase rescans, 30–90 s WebSearch, security re-audits on repeat work) is therefore **not realized in practice**.

## Root Cause

- **The cache `get`/`put` are LLM-executed bash instructions inside command/skill/agent markdown, not deterministic code.** The agent reads the markdown and decides what to run; it optimizes for the visible *goal* of the step and treats cache plumbing as optional.
- **Confirmed for `design-context` (worst case).** In `edit.md §1.5` / `new.md §1.5` the `maude cache get/put` lines are *buried inside a larger bash block* whose visible purpose is "pre-load the DS context by reading the CSS + canvas-lib". A real run met all three gates (`SEL_VALID=1` from a selection-anchored edit on `<aside class="ka-sidebar">`, `.tsx`, `css_mode: "inline"`), so the cache block should have fired. Instead the log shows the agent did "read 3 files" (the goal) and ran **no** `maude cache` call. Proof: after the run `/tmp/maude-scratch/.ai/cache` was empty and `maude cache stats` reported "no cache activity recorded yet" — a get-miss *records a miss*, so a zero-activity stat means no `get` ran at all.
- **Same structural class affects every consumer** — each is an agent-executed bash gate that can be bypassed by going straight to the expensive operation it was meant to skip:
  - `design-context` — `edit.md §1.5`, `new.md §1.5` — **🔴 buried under a file-read; confirmed skipped.**
  - `codebase-intelligence` — `skills/codebase-intelligence/SKILL.md` ("Check before rescanning") — 🟡 better-framed, unverified.
  - `research/domain` + `research/project` — `agents/ux-research-agent.md` ("Check before any WebSearch") — 🟡 better-framed, unverified.
  - `security/<head-sha>` — `done.md`, `validate.md`, `validate-security.md` (bold **"First"**) — 🟢 best-framed (cache-check *is* the action), unverified.
  - `validate` (skip-if-clean) — `validate.md` step 0 — 🟡 unverified.
  - `scenario` (covers-skip) — `scenario/SKILL.md` — 🟡 unverified.
- **The cache mechanism itself is correct** — 29 unit + CLI-e2e tests pass; a manual `put → get(hit) → list → stats → clear` round-trip works. The *only* recorded activity in any project's `_stats.json` is that manual demo (`security: 1 hit / 1 miss`). Nothing committed (the `research/domain` + `codebase-intelligence` layers were specced as committed-and-shareable per C1, but were never populated → never committed).

## Impact

- **Severity: Medium.** No correctness bug — work still completes correctly; the cache simply never saves the cost it was built to save. The Phase C wall-clock/token wins are largely unrealized.
- `design-context`: **confirmed non-functional in practice** (a repeat `/design:edit` on an unchanged DS pays the full read cost every time — the C5 win is zero).
- The committed-layer promise (a teammate on the same commit getting a `codebase-intelligence` / `research/domain` freshness hit without rescanning/re-searching) cannot hold while nothing is ever written.
- The other consumers are **unverified, not proven broken** — the wiring is one day old (landed in `3676bb6`, 2026-05-29) and the only real consumer run observed so far is the one `/design:edit` (which skipped). They share the risk class; severity for each is unknown until exercised.

## Proposed Fix

Two tiers — do the tactical one first, then the structural one for durability:

1. **Tactical (markdown hardening).** Lift every `maude cache get/put` out of the multi-purpose "read files / scan" bash block into a **dedicated, imperative MUST-run gate** worded so the agent can't treat it as plumbing — e.g. "Run this **first**; do **not** read the CSS / run WebSearch / rescan until the `get` returns empty." Mirror the `security`-layer framing (bold **"First"**), which is the least-skippable shape today. Start with `design-context` (confirmed broken).
2. **Structural (the reliable fix).** Move `get`/`put` **out of agent discretion into deterministic `maude` code** — the only fix that survives LLM non-determinism. The agent should call **one** command that internally checks the cache, computes on miss, writes, and returns the result:
   - `design-context`: a `maude design context <ds> <tokens-sha>` that returns the vocabulary pack (cache-checked + populated internally).
   - `codebase-intelligence`: a `maude` wrapper that returns the map path or regenerates+caches.
   - `research`: hardest (it runs as a subagent that *does* WebSearch) — keep a prominent first-step gate; a full move would mean the subagent calls a `maude` research-cache wrapper before/after.

**Files:** `plugins/design/commands/{edit,new}.md` (§1.5); `plugins/flow/skills/codebase-intelligence/SKILL.md`; `plugins/design/agents/ux-research-agent.md`; `plugins/flow/commands/{validate,done,validate-security}.md`; `plugins/flow/skills/scenario/SKILL.md`. Structural tier additionally: `cli/commands/design.mjs` (+ a flow-side helper) for the new cache-owning subcommands.

## Testing Requirements

- Agent-discretion can't be unit-tested directly (LLM non-determinism). After the **structural** fix the agent calls one deterministic command, so assert at the CLI level that the command performs a `get` then (on miss) a `put` per invocation — CLI-testable.
- **E2E proxy:** run a consumer twice on an unchanged input and assert `maude cache stats` shows a miss on run 1 and a hit on run 2 (`design-context` via `/design:edit`, `codebase-intelligence` via `/flow:plan`, `research` via `/design:setup-ds`). For the markdown-only tier this is only verifiable via real slash-command runs + a stats check (manual).
- **Regression guard idea:** a lint/test that flags a `maude cache get/put` line living inside a larger multi-purpose bash block (the `design-context` anti-pattern) rather than a dedicated gate.

## Complexity

**Medium.** Tactical markdown hardening: **Low**. Structural move-into-`maude`: **Medium–High** (touches the CLI + every consumer, and requires the cache to become a `maude`-owned operation rather than an agent step).

decision.title: RCA: Ticket sync-cold-start-empty-hub-clobbers-local — Linked-mode cold-start empties local canvases against a fresh hub
decision.rationale:
# RCA: Ticket sync-cold-start-empty-hub-clobbers-local — Linked-mode cold-start empties local canvases against a fresh hub

> No tracker ticket — surfaced live while pairing two repos as peers against a
> self-hosted hub (`test.studyfi.com/hub`). Provider is `github` but this had no
> issue number; documented manually. Observed 2026-06-02.

## Summary

When a peer's dev-server connects (linked mode) to a hub that has **no state yet
for a canvas slug** (a fresh / never-seeded hub), the per-canvas sync agent's
cold-start reconcile runs in the default `hub-wins` direction and **writes the
hub's empty body over the non-empty local file**, silently truncating the canvas
to 0 bytes. In the field this emptied **all 73 `.tsx` canvases** of a freshly
linked project (`AI-StudyMate`) on first `maude design serve` after the project
opted into TSX sync (`linkedHub.syncTsx: true`, DDR-072). Content was recoverable
only because it was committed to git (`HEAD` held 8–61 kB per file; disk = 0 B).
The only surfaced warning was a `cold-start-hub-wins` entry in `_sync.json` —
not a loud stop.

## Root Cause

`plugins/design/dev-server/sync/agent.ts` → `reconcile()`, the hub-wins HTML
branch (pre-fix lines ~319–329):

```js
if (localHtml !== docHtml) {
  if (localHtml !== null && localHtml.trim() !== '') {
    opts.onConflict?.({ slug, kind: 'cold-start-hub-wins' }); // LOG ONLY
  }
  const hash = hashBytes(docHtml);
  echoGuard.record(paths.html, hash);
  writer(paths.html, docHtml);   // ← writes docHtml even when it is ''
}
```

An **empty** hub doc (`docHtml === ''`) at cold-start is ambiguous: it almost
always means "the hub has never seen this slug" (fresh hub), NOT an authoritative
"this canvas is blank". The code treated it as authoritative and wrote the empty
string to disk, truncating the file. The `onConflict` callback only *logs*; it
does not gate the write.

The tell that this was an oversight rather than intent: **every other type in the
same `reconcile()` already guards against empty-doc writes** — comments
(`docCommentsStr !== ''`), annotations (`docAnnotations !== ''`), meta
(`docMeta !== null`), css (`docCss !== null`). The HTML body — the one that
matters most — was the single branch missing the guard. The shared-doc projection
path (DDR-064, `migrate-seed.ts`) even documents the canonical rule explicitly
("never clobbers non-empty local with an empty doc value" / "hub-wins if the
synced doc holds state; adopt local files only when the hub was empty"); the
agent path never adopted it.

Introduced in `c21c7d4` (phase-9 task 4, bidirectional file sync agent); the
`cold-start-hub-wins` notification was layered on in `f50ffad` but did not change
the destructive write. Latent until a non-empty local project first connected to
an empty hub — which DDR-072 (project-level TSX opt-in) made reachable for TSX
projects.

Two contributing conditions amplified discovery:

1. The admin invite UI minted **label-scoped** tokens (DDR-053 default), which
   authorize no canvas slug → `permission-denied` masked the first sync attempts;
   only after minting a `scope: '*'` token did sync actually run and the clobber
   fire. (Separately fixed — see "Related".)
2. Loss is silent at the UX layer: no blocking prompt, only a `_sync.json`
   conflict row.

## Impact

- **Who:** any linked-mode peer whose local project has real canvas content and
  connects to a hub with no prior state for those slugs (first peer to a fresh
  hub; a re-provisioned/empty hub; a slug the hub never received).
- **What:** local `.html` canvas bodies (and opted-in `.tsx` bodies, DDR-060/072)
  truncated to 0 bytes on disk. Comments/annotations/meta/css were NOT affected
  (already guarded).
- **Severity:** **High** — silent local data loss of the primary work product.
  Mitigated in practice only by git (uncommitted canvas work would be
  unrecoverable). Default `serve` re-triggers the loss on every cold-start while
  the hub stays empty.
- **Workarounds (pre-fix):** link with `--adopt` (push-on-first-connect bypasses
  the hub-wins branch and seeds local up); or keep canvases committed and
  `git restore` after a loss.

## Proposed Fix

**(Implemented this session.)** In the hub-wins HTML branch, never overwrite a
non-empty local body with an empty hub doc; seed the doc **from local** instead so
the body survives AND the hub gets our content (matching the comments/annotations/
meta/css branches and the projection path's documented rule):

```js
if (localHtml !== docHtml) {
  if (docHtml === '' && localHtml !== null && localHtml.trim() !== '') {
    applyHtmlToDoc(doc, localHtml, origin); // seed up; never truncate disk
    lastHtml = localHtml;
  } else {
    if (localHtml !== null && localHtml.trim() !== '') {
      opts.onConflict?.({ slug, kind: 'cold-start-hub-wins' });
    }
    const hash = hashBytes(docHtml);
    echoGuard.record(paths.html, hash);
    writer(paths.html, docHtml);
  }
}
```

- **Files changed:** `plugins/design/dev-server/sync/agent.ts` (guard);
  `plugins/design/dev-server/test/sync-agent.test.ts` (regression test).
- **Behavioural change:** a fresh hub now gets seeded from the first peer's local
  content instead of destroying it — strictly safer, and the desired default.
- **Edge case acknowledged (not blocking):** two peers each holding different
  non-empty content that simultaneously seed an empty hub will CRDT-merge (Y.Text
  interleave), not lose data — far better than the old clobber. The
  transaction-guarded `migrate-seed` (projection path) is the long-term answer if
  the shared-doc flag is ever turned on.

## Testing Requirements

- **Added:** `empty hub doc does NOT clobber a non-empty local body — seeds local
  up instead (data-loss guard)` in `sync-agent.test.ts` — asserts the local file
  is preserved, the hub receives the local body (`htmlFromDoc(docA)`), and no
  `cold-start-hub-wins` conflict is raised.
- **Regression-guarded by existing tests:** `hub-wins (default): overwrites disk
  when doc differs` (non-empty hub still wins), `identical disk + doc states: no
  disk write`, and the adopt-mode tests — all still green (sync suite 182/182).
- **Suggested follow-up (not in this fix):** a `sync-runtime`-level test that
  drives the full `start()` → `onceSynced` → `reconcile` path against an empty
  in-memory hub provider, to lock the behaviour end-to-end (not just at the agent
  unit level).

## Complexity

Low (fix). The defect is a single missing guard mirroring four sibling branches;
the change is ~10 lines + one test. Shipping it to users is the larger task:
the dev-server ships as a `bun --compile` binary, so the fix reaches end users
only via a new npm release (version bump across the three manifests + changeset),
and a DDR documenting the "empty hub never clobbers local" invariant is warranted.

## Related

- **Wildcard-token UX gap** (fixed alongside): admin invite UI only minted
  label-scoped tokens (useless for sync); added a "Hub-wide" scope control to the
  invite form (`plugins/design/hub/src/admin/{index.html,app.js,style.css}`).
- **Peers/tokens card unbounded height** (fixed alongside): added `.tbl-scroll`
  (max-height + sticky header) in the hub admin UI.
- DDRs: [[DDR-053]] (scope-bound tokens), [[DDR-054]] (linked-mode trust),
  [[DDR-060]] (TSX-only sync), [[DDR-064]] (shared-doc projection + migrate-seed),
  [[DDR-072]] (project-level TSX opt-in).

decision.title: RCA: Ticket "add elements to artboard from toolbar nefunguje" — no placeholder to drop on empty artboard
decision.rationale:
# RCA: Ticket "add elements to artboard from toolbar nefunguje" — no placeholder to drop on empty artboard

## Summary

The user clicked the toolbar "+" button, picked "Div" from the Div/Text/Image popover, and expected to see a draggable placeholder they could drop onto an artboard. Nothing happened. Root cause: this affordance was never a drag-and-drop feature — it's a one-click "append after the last existing element" action (Stage I3 of `feature-element-editing-robustness`), and it silently no-ops when the target artboard has no existing elements to anchor on, which is exactly the state shown in the screenshot (an apparently-empty/near-empty artboard). There's a UX-model mismatch (icon menu implies drag-drop; implementation is click-to-append) layered on top of a genuine empty-canvas gap (no fallback, no feedback).

## Root Cause

`apps/studio/tool-palette.tsx` implements the "+" popover (`dc-tp-insert-popover`, lines ~483-515) with three items: Div / Text / Image. Selecting one calls `insertViaPalette(kind)` (lines 351-375):

1. It calls `resolveInsertAnchor()` (lines 296-310) to find the **last direct child element carrying `data-cd-id`** inside the active artboard's `.dc-artboard-body`.
2. If found, it `postMessage`s `insert-request` / `insert-image-request` to the parent shell (`apps/studio/client/app.jsx:8513-8549`), which calls `insertElementShell` (`app.jsx:9272`) to write the new node into source, positioned `after` that anchor element. This is a direct, immediate DOM/source write — there is no drag ghost, no drop target, no placeholder at any point in the flow.
3. **If `resolveInsertAnchor()` returns `null`** (no child with `data-cd-id` yet, or no artboard at all), `insertViaPalette` just `return`s — no toast, no visual feedback, no fallback insertion point.

This null path is intentional and already covered by `apps/studio/test/tool-palette-insert-anchor.test.ts:71-82`, and the code comments at `tool-palette.tsx:284-296` explicitly call it "a documented v1 limit."

The user's artboard evidently had no elements bearing `data-cd-id` yet, so the click was a guaranteed no-op — matching "nefunguje" (doesn't work) exactly. Separately, even on a non-empty artboard the actual behavior ("instantly append after the last element") doesn't match the placeholder/drag-and-drop mental model that a floating icon-menu naturally suggests.

This is unrelated to the whiteboard/stickers work-in-progress (`apps/studio/stickers/`, `scripts/build-stickers.mjs`, `.ai/plans/feature-whiteboard-annotation-improvements.md`) — that's a separate, uncommitted feature for the FigJam-style annotation layer, not artboard element insertion.

## Impact

- Anyone trying to add a first element to a brand-new/empty artboard via the "+" toolbar hits a completely silent dead end — no error, no clue why nothing happened.
- Even once an artboard has ≥1 element, the interaction model (click → instant append at the end) is a mismatch against user expectations set by the UI (icon-based popover suggests a placeholder/drag interaction).
- Workaround exists: the per-element right-click context menu's "Insert ▸ …" (`apps/studio/canvas-shell.tsx:1482-1523`) works once at least one element already exists, since it anchors on the clicked target rather than "last child of artboard."
- Severity: Medium — feature is not broken for populated artboards, but is a hard dead-end for empty ones with zero feedback, and the affordance is misleading either way.

## Proposed Fix

Minimum (bug-level fix):
- In `resolveInsertAnchor()` / `insertViaPalette`, when no `data-cd-id` child exists, fall back to inserting as the artboard body's first/only child (append to `.dc-artboard-body` directly, no `refId` needed) instead of no-op.
- If no artboard exists at all, show a toast/inline hint ("Select or create an artboard first") instead of silently doing nothing.

Better (affordance-level fix, needs product decision):
- Either relabel/redesign the "+" menu to make clear it performs an immediate append (e.g., show it appearing at the bottom of the artboard after click, perhaps with a brief highlight animation confirming the action), or actually implement the drag-to-place interaction the icon menu currently implies. That's a larger UX change and should go through `/design:setup-ds`-style scoping rather than being bundled into this bug fix.

Files to change:
- `apps/studio/tool-palette.tsx` (`resolveInsertAnchor`, `insertViaPalette`)
- Possibly `apps/studio/client/app.jsx` (`insertElementShell`) if the fallback needs a new "append to body, no anchor" code path
- `apps/studio/test/tool-palette-insert-anchor.test.ts` — update/extend to cover the new empty-artboard fallback behavior instead of asserting `null`

## Testing Requirements

- Unit test: `resolveInsertAnchor()` on an artboard with zero `data-cd-id` children should return a valid "insert as first child" target instead of `null` (or a distinct anchor shape indicating "append to body").
- Unit test: `insertViaPalette` on a fully empty artboard actually triggers an insert postMessage.
- Manual/agent-browser check: click "+" → Div on a freshly created empty artboard, verify a div actually appears.
- Manual/agent-browser check: click "+" with no artboard on canvas at all — verify a user-visible toast/feedback appears instead of silence.

## Complexity

Low (minimum fix) — the anchor-resolution and insert-request plumbing already exists; the fix is extending the fallback path and adding user feedback for the true "no artboard at all" case. The affordance-redesign option is a separate, larger effort.

decision.title: RCA: Undo/redo & canvas history coverage gaps (inspector CSS edits + text rewrite + more)
decision.rationale:
# RCA: Undo/redo & canvas history coverage gaps (inspector CSS edits + text rewrite + more)

> **Status: Phase 1 RESOLVED** (1a/1b 2026-06-30 commit `5f45ec8`; **1c added
> 2026-07-07**, follow-up ticket "undo/redo nefunguje uplne na vsechny akce…
> napriklad hide layer, css inspect panel, zmeny pozice atd.").
> `fix(studio): make inspector CSS / inline text / attr edits undoable (Cmd+Z)`.
> Session-scoped Cmd+Z for css/text/attr shipped (new `edit-source` command +
> cross-origin record/apply-edit bridge + undo-stack `record()` primitive).
> Changeset: `.changeset/undoable-inline-edits.md` (patch).
>
> **Re-audit 2026-07-07** (the follow-up ticket's "go through every canvas
> action" ask) confirmed the CSS-inspector-panel and position-change (artboard
> move + Phase 12.4 free-move absolute/fixed element drag, commit `69f2842`)
> examples named in the new ticket are BOTH already correctly wired — free-move
> reuses `edit-css` + `recordSourceEdit` for both `left`/`top` (`app.jsx`
> `repositionElement`). The **hide-layer eye icon was a real, separate,
> previously-undiscovered gap**: `InspectorPanel`'s `toggleVisibility`
> (Phase 12.3 W3.1) only ever posted the `apply-style` live-DOM-preview message
> — per its own code comment, "Live-only … not persisted to source" — so it was
> neither durable across reload nor undoable; a forwarded Cmd+Z popped an
> unrelated command exactly like the original CSS-panel bug. **Fixed (Phase
> 1c)**: `serializeArtboardTree` (`canvas-shell.tsx`) now reports each
> `LayerNode.hidden` from the live inline `style.display`, and `toggleVisibility`
> POSTs `/_api/edit-css` (`property:'display'`, `value:'none'` / `reset:true`)
> + calls `recordSourceEdit` (the same `edit-source` command from 1b), exactly
> mirroring `CssKnobs`' commit/reset. No new command kind needed — reuses
> `edit-source-command.ts` generically (`op:'css', key:'display'`), so
> `test/edit-source-command.test.ts`'s do()/undo() round-trip already covers
> the mechanism; verified live via agent-browser (hide → Cmd+Z → Cmd+Shift+Z).
>
> **Deferred follow-ups (still not done):** durable `_history` snapshot for
> inline edits (needs a DDR — `.bak` vs `writeSnapshot` format reconciliation),
> and **Phase 2 (comments undo, "undo delete" from `_trash/`, canvas
> create/rename/duplicate undo)** — out of scope for this pass; each needs its
> own inverse-op design, not a rewiring of an existing write path. See the
> Proposed Fix section.

> Manual ticket (pasted, CZ): *"Zjistil jsem, že undo/redo nefunguje úplně na všechno — například když ručně měním nějaké CSS styly v inspectoru. Ale důkladně bych prozkoumal, jestli jsme ještě na něco nezapomněli, co by stálo za to mít jako historii canvasu — třeba přepis textu atd."*
>
> Provider: `github` (config), but supplied as a manual paste → investigated directly. Saved under a descriptive slug.

## Summary

Maude has **three independent, non-integrated "history" mechanisms**, and the interactive direct-manipulation edit surfaces added in Phase 12 (DDR-103/104) fall into the gap between all of them:

1. **Client undo stack** (Cmd+Z) — in-memory, per-canvas, *inside the canvas iframe*. Fed by **only two** command kinds: `move-artboards` (artboard drag / equal-spacing) and `annotation-strokes` (the entire FigJam draw layer: draw, erase, add image, add link, resize, rotate, delete, group, align…).
2. **`_history/<slug>/*.bak`** (consumed by `/design:rollback`) — whole-file backups written **only by the `/design:edit` slash command** via Bash `cp` before an AI edit.
3. **`history.ts writeSnapshot()`** (`<ts>.html`+`<ts>.json` blobs) — written **only by the sync/collab conflict path** (`sync/index.ts`, reasons `pre-sync-local` / `pre-sync-hub`).

The user-reported edits — **manual CSS in the inspector, inline text rewrite, custom attributes, comments, and canvas lifecycle** — write straight to disk via `/_api/edit-*` (or `_comments/<slug>.json`) and are covered by **none** of the three. So Cmd+Z does nothing (or worse — see Impact), and `/design:rollback` can't recover them either. Confirmed root cause; the reported CSS case is one instance of a systemic gap.

## Root Cause

### The mechanism (reported CSS case)
- The inspector's CSS controls are `CssKnobs` in **`apps/studio/client/app.jsx:4159`**. On commit it calls `post('/_api/edit-css', …)` (`app.jsx:4257`) and optimistically nudges the iframe via `dgn:'apply-style'`. **It never pushes to an undo stack and never snapshots.**
- The server handler `editCss` (**`apps/studio/api.ts:1245`**) writes the inline `style.<prop>` straight to the canvas `.tsx` source via `editAttribute(...)` and returns a delta. **No `history.writeSnapshot` call.** Same for `editText` (`api.ts:1298`) and `editAttr` (`api.ts:1321`).

### Why it can't be undone — two compounding reasons
1. **Origin split.** `CssKnobs` runs in the **shell** (main origin). The undo stack (`use-undo-stack.tsx` / `undo-stack.ts`) lives **inside the canvas iframe** (untrusted canvas origin, DDR-054). They are separate React trees on separate origins; the shell can only reach the iframe stack via postMessage (`dgn:'undo'`, `client/app.jsx:2612`). So a shell-side edit *cannot* call `undoStack.push()` directly.
2. **The feature was simply never wired to the stack.** The inline **text edit** is the proof: it runs *inside* the iframe (`canvas-shell.tsx:1595` `commitEdit`, contenteditable per DDR-103) where `undoStack` is in scope (`canvas-shell.tsx:1374`) — and it **still** doesn't push. It posts `dgn:'edit-text'` → `/_api/edit-text` → source, full stop. So this is not only an origin problem; the Phase-12 edits were designed as fire-and-forget source writes.

### Why a forwarded Cmd+Z makes it *worse*
The shell's Edit▸Undo / Cmd+Z forwards `dgn:'undo'` to the active iframe (`app.jsx:2612-2613`). The iframe stack contains only `move-artboards` / `annotation-strokes` records — so after a CSS/text edit, "Undo" pops the **last layout or annotation op instead**, e.g. silently moving an artboard the user never touched. Undo appears to "do the wrong thing," not just "do nothing."

### The systemic shape
The command-undo-stack (DDR-050) and the `_history` snapshot stack (DDR-102 + `/design:edit` `.bak`) evolved independently and cover disjoint mutation sets. Every *new* interactive surface added since landed in the seam between them.

## Coverage matrix (complete inventory)

| Mutation | Entry point | Persists to | Cmd+Z undo? | `/design:rollback`? |
| --- | --- | --- | :---: | :---: |
| Move / resize artboard, equal-spacing | drag → `PATCH /_api/canvas-meta` | `.meta.json` (layout) | ✅ `move-artboards` | ❌ |
| Annotation strokes (draw/erase/resize/rotate/delete/group/align) | `PUT /_api/annotations` | `<slug>.annotations.svg` | ✅ `annotation-strokes` | ❌ |
| Media drop (image / link) | `POST /_api/asset` + strokes | `assets/` + `.annotations.svg` | ✅ `annotation-strokes` | ❌ |
| **Inspector CSS edit** ← reported | `POST /_api/edit-css` | canvas `.tsx` source | ❌ | ❌ |
| **Inline text rewrite** ← user-flagged | `POST /_api/edit-text` | canvas `.tsx` source | ❌ | ❌ |
| **Custom CSS prop / HTML attr** | `POST /_api/edit-attr` | canvas `.tsx` source | ❌ | ❌ |
| Bind property to design token | `POST /_api/edit-css` (value = `var(--…)`) | canvas `.tsx` source | ❌ | ❌ |
| Comment add / edit / delete / reply / resolve | WS `comments-*` / `POST /_api/comments/<id>/reply` | `_comments/<slug>.json` | ❌ | ❌ |
| Canvas create / rename / duplicate | `POST /_api/canvas` | `.tsx` + `.meta.json` | ❌ | ❌ |
| Canvas delete | `DELETE /_api/canvas` | soft-move → `_trash/` | ❌ (recover only by hand from `_trash/`) | ❌ |
| AI edit (`/design:edit`) | slash command | canvas `.tsx` source | ❌ | ✅ `.bak` |
| Sync/collab conflict | `sync/index.ts` | `_history/<slug>/<ts>.*` | ❌ | ✅ (but see adjacent bug) |

**Table is the original 2026-06-30 snapshot — status deltas since:**
- Inspector CSS edit / inline text / custom attr / token-bind → **✅ Cmd+Z** since Phase 1b (`edit-source` command, commit `5f45ec8`).
- Element reorder (drag / Layers-panel drag / Alt+arrow) → **✅ Cmd+Z** since Phase 12.1 (`reorder` command, not in this table originally).
- Free-move absolute/fixed element drag (`left`/`top`) → **✅ Cmd+Z** since commit `69f2842` (routes through `edit-css` + `edit-source`, same as CSS panel).
- **Layers-panel hide/show (eye icon)** → was NEITHER persisted NOR undoable (client-only preview, not in this table originally) — **✅ fixed 2026-07-07 (Phase 1c)**, same `edit-css` + `edit-source` mechanism.
- **Element delete / insert (div/text/image) / duplicate, artboard insert / resize / delete** → **✅ Cmd+Z** (feature-element-editing-robustness Stage I/D4, 2026-07-07). These are STRUCTURAL edits (they renumber positional `data-cd-id`s, per DDR-138/139) — unlike the CSS-shaped rows above, they do NOT go through `edit-source-command.ts`; they reuse the reorder-log whole-file-snapshot revert (`commands/reorder-command.ts`, the same `{canvas, seq}` server-side seq-log Phase 12.1 built for element reorder), rather than a new `delete-element-command.ts`/`insert-element-command.ts` pair the original plan sketched — confirmed a sound simplification, not a gap. Closes this doc's own "canvas create/rename/duplicate/delete" row for the ELEMENT-level (not canvas-file-level) case; the canvas-file-level row below is still unaddressed.
- Comments, canvas create/rename/duplicate/delete (the CANVAS FILE itself, not an element inside one) → **still ❌**, unchanged (Phase 2, not attempted this pass).

**The whole bottom-middle block (edit-css / edit-text / edit-attr / token-bind / comments / canvas-lifecycle) is recoverable by nothing in-app — only git (for versioned `.tsx`/`.meta.json`/`.annotations.svg`) or a manual `_trash/` rescue.**

### Adjacent bug spotted (note, not the focus)
`/design:rollback` does `ls _history/<slug>/` and `cp`s the chosen file back over the canvas (`rollback.md:32-35`). That dir mixes `/design:edit`'s `<NNN>-<ts>.bak` files with sync's `<ts>.html` **and** `<ts>.json` (meta) files. After a collab conflict, a rollback could `cp` a `.json` meta blob over a `.tsx` canvas. Low-frequency, but worth fixing when the formats are unified.

## Impact

- **Who:** every Maude user doing direct GUI iteration (inspector CSS, double-click text edit, attrs, comments).
- **Severity: Medium.** No data loss — sources are on disk/git — but a core editor expectation (Cmd+Z) is silently broken, and worse, a forwarded undo can mutate something the user didn't touch. This directly erodes trust in the tool (the ticket's own framing).
- **Workaround today:** git restore of the `.tsx`, or manually re-editing the value back. `/design:rollback` does **not** help for these.

## Proposed Fix

Target end-state: **one origin-spanning undo that records every direct edit, with a coarse `_history` snapshot as the durable backstop, surfaced by a single Cmd+Z and a single `/design:rollback`.** Phased so the reported pain is fixed cheaply first.

### Phase 1 — make the `/_api/edit-*` family reversible (fixes reported CSS + text + attr)
**1a (Low risk, do first): server snapshot before every inline source write.** In `editCss` / `editText` / `editAttr` (`api.ts`), snapshot the current source before `editAttribute`/`runEditText`. Reuse the existing helper but **emit the `.bak` filename shape `/design:rollback` already reads** (`<NNN>-<ts>-inline.bak`), not the `writeSnapshot` `<ts>.html/.json` shape — avoids the format-mismatch bug above. **Coalesce scrub bursts:** a slider drag fires many `edit-css` commits; snapshot only on the first edit of a burst (or throttle ~1/s) so we don't write 100 backups per drag.

**1b (Medium: true Cmd+Z).** Register new command kinds `edit-css` / `edit-text` / `edit-attr` whose `do()`/`undo()` re-POST `/_api/edit-*` with after/before values (`before` = `authored[prop]` / `original` text, both already known at commit time):
- **Text edit** (`canvas-shell.tsx:1595`): push directly — `undoStack` is already in scope, capture `original`→`text`.
- **CSS / attr** (shell-side `CssKnobs`): the shell posts a new `dgn:'push-undo'` postMessage carrying the `CommandRecord` to the active iframe, which pushes it. Add `push-undo` to the **parent-origin-only** allowlist (DDR-054 — never let the untrusted canvas inject undo commands).

Files: `apps/studio/api.ts`, `apps/studio/commands/edit-css-command.ts` (+ text/attr, mirroring `move-artboards-command.ts`), `apps/studio/undo-stack.ts` (`CommandSinks` gets an `editPostFn` sink), `apps/studio/client/app.jsx` (CssKnobs commit → also post `push-undo`), `apps/studio/canvas-shell.tsx` (text commit → push; accept `push-undo`), and the postMessage allowlist in `canvas-shell.tsx:1489`.

### Phase 2 — comments + canvas lifecycle
- Comments: command kind that re-issues the inverse WS op (add↔delete, patch-with-before-body, resolve↔unresolve).
- Canvas **delete** already soft-moves to `_trash/` — cheapest win is an "Undo delete" that restores from `_trash/`. Create/rename/duplicate lower priority.

### Phase 3 (architectural — DDR-worthy)
Unify the three mechanisms behind one façade so a single Cmd+Z and a single `/design:rollback` see every mutation class, and reconcile the `.bak` vs `writeSnapshot` filename formats in `_history/<slug>/` (closes the adjacent rollback bug). Record as a DDR (supersedes/extends DDR-050 + DDR-102 scope).

## Testing Requirements

- `bun:test` for each new command builder — `do()`/`undo()` round-trip (mirror `test/undo-stack.test.ts`, `test/move-artboards-command.test.ts`).
- Server test: `editCss`/`editText`/`editAttr` write exactly one `.bak` before the source edit, and a scrub burst coalesces to **one** snapshot + **one** undo entry (not N).
- Canvas-origin gate test: the new `push-undo` postMessage verb is **parent-origin-only** (`test/canvas-origin-gate.test.ts`).
- Scenario (`/design:smoke` or `desktop-e2e`): edit CSS in inspector → Cmd+Z → value reverts; double-click text edit → Cmd+Z → text reverts; confirm undo no longer pops an unrelated artboard move.

## Complexity

**Medium overall.** Phase 1a: Low. Phase 1b: Medium (cross-origin command bridge). Phases 2–3: Medium–High. Recommend shipping **1a + 1b-for-text/attr** first (immediate, low-risk relief), then 1b-for-CSS, then 2–3 under a DDR.

decision.title: RCA: Ticket video-artboard-frame-reset-on-edit — Video artboard resets to frame 0 on every edit / reload, ignoring the Timeline's selected frame
decision.rationale:
# RCA: Ticket video-artboard-frame-reset-on-edit — Video artboard resets to frame 0 on every edit / reload, ignoring the Timeline's selected frame

## Summary

Editing a video artboard's source — via the ACP chat panel, an agent, manual inspector edits, or a direct text rewrite — causes the artboard's Remotion `<Player>` to visibly "restart" to the beginning, even when the Timeline panel has a specific frame selected and playback is paused. The same happens on a manual `⌘R` (Reload canvas). The user confirmed the Timeline panel's own selection UI stays put across the reload — only the artboard's rendered frame snaps back.

## Root Cause

The Timeline's selected frame and the Remotion `Player`'s live frame are two independent sources of truth that are only kept in sync via one-way `postMessage` events, and nothing re-establishes that sync after the `Player` remounts.

- **`apps/studio/video-comp.tsx`** mounts `<Player initialFrame={posterFrame} .../>` (~line 419), where `posterFrame` (~lines 304–306) is a pure function of `durationInFrames` — `capturing ? 0 : round(durationInFrames * 0.35)`. It has no awareness of, and never reads, the Timeline's actual selected frame.
- **`apps/studio/client/app.jsx`** owns `timelineFrame` (state declared ~line 6857) and pushes it to the artboard only via an outbound `{dgn:'timeline-seek', frame, id}` postMessage (~line 10381), and only in response to a user scrub (`onSeek`, ~line 7251). Nothing re-sends `timeline-seek` after a remount.
- **On every canvas edit**, the writer (ACP/agent/inspector/text edit) touches the `.tsx` source, the file watcher's `classifyChange` (`hmr-broadcast.ts` ~lines 155–172) marks it `mode:'module'`, and `canvas-comment-mount.tsx`'s `remount()` (~lines 605–657) tears down and remounts the canvas subtree by bumping a `key={attempt}` (~line 653) — a full component-identity change. `VideoComp`/`<Player>` unmount and remount fresh, so `Player` re-initializes at `posterFrame`, not wherever the Timeline was parked.
- **On `⌘R`** (`reloadActive`, `app.jsx` ~line 7941), the handler does `el.src = el.src` — a literal iframe navigation reload. This is even more destructive than the soft-remount path, but produces the same symptom: `app.jsx`'s `timelineFrame` state survives (it's in the parent shell, not the iframe) — which is why the Timeline panel visually "stays selected" — but the freshly-loaded iframe's `VideoComp` boots at `posterFrame` again, and the shell never re-sends `timeline-seek` to the newly (re)announced comp. The `timeline-comps` handler (`app.jsx` ~lines 8720–8740), which fires when `VideoComp` re-registers itself after any remount, only updates the comp metadata list (`setActiveComps`) — it never re-seeks the new `Player` instance to `timelineFrame`.

**This is the same bug class already fixed once for pan/zoom.** `canvas-lib.tsx` (~lines 707–730) hoists a module-scope `liveViewport` mirror *outside* the remounting React tree specifically because "a full page load clears it," and "an edit landing mid-gesture snapped the camera back to a stale pan/zoom" (RC3 fix, referenced inline as `rca/issue-canvas-hmr-optimistic-update-consistency`). No equivalent mirror or re-seed exists for the Timeline's selected video frame.

## Impact

- Any user or agent workflow that edits a video artboard while scrubbed to a specific frame loses that frame on every edit — disruptive when iterating on a specific beat/frame (e.g. reviewing frame 812/899 as in the reported screenshot).
- Affects all edit paths equally (ACP panel, agent-driven edits, manual inspector edits, direct text rewrites) because they all funnel through the same file-write → HMR-remount pipeline, plus the manual `⌘R` reload path.
- Not data-destructive, and playback state (play/pause) itself isn't corrupted — only the frame position is lost, defaulting to a fixed ~35%-through "poster frame" instead of the last-selected/last-known frame.

## Proposed Fix

Mirror the pan/zoom precedent: keep the last-known Timeline frame per comp outside the remounting boundary, and use it (instead of the static `posterFrame` formula) whenever a `Player` (re)mounts.

1. **`video-comp.tsx`**: add a module-scope mirror (parallel to `registry()`/`liveViewport`), e.g. `liveTimelineFrame: Map<string, number>`, updated on every `frameupdate` (alongside the existing `postToShell({dgn:'timeline-frame', ...})` call, ~lines 380–398) and on every incoming `timeline-seek` (~line ~360). On mount, compute `initialFrame` from this mirror when an entry exists for `compId`, falling back to the current `posterFrame` formula only when there's no prior frame recorded (first-ever mount / capture).
2. **`app.jsx`**: when a `timeline-comps` announce arrives for a comp that already has a known `timelineFrame` for that active canvas (i.e., a remount, not first mount), re-send `{dgn:'timeline-seek', frame: timelineFrame, id}` to re-sync the fresh `Player` instance — closing the gap where the shell state survives but is never pushed back down (~around the `timeline-comps` handler, `app.jsx` ~lines 8720–8740).
3. Since `⌘R`'s `reloadActive()` does a hard iframe navigation (`el.src = el.src`), the module-scope mirror in step 1 is cleared just like `liveViewport` is on a full reload — so step 2 (the shell re-sending `timeline-seek` once the reloaded iframe re-announces its comp) is the piece that actually fixes the `⌘R` case; step 1 alone only survives soft (module-level) remounts.
4. Respect existing intent: don't fight `autoPlay`/loop semantics — if the comp is mid-playback when the edit lands, it's fine to resume playing from the restored frame; only the *paused, parked-on-a-frame* case needs the frame preserved verbatim (matches the ticket's ask: "zůstane na tom stejnem dokud to uzivatel rucne neposune nebo pusti video").

### Files to change
- `apps/studio/video-comp.tsx` — module-scope frame mirror + `initialFrame` fallback logic.
- `apps/studio/client/app.jsx` — re-seed `timeline-seek` on comp re-announce (`timeline-comps` handler).

## Testing Requirements

- Manual/agent-browser scenario: open a video artboard, scrub the Timeline to a mid-point frame while paused, trigger an edit via each of: ACP panel, agent-driven edit, manual inspector attribute edit, direct text rewrite — assert the artboard stays on the same frame after each.
- Same scenario via `⌘R` (Reload canvas).
- Regression check: autoplay comps (`autoPlay` prop set) still start playing on first mount; looped/paused comps still respect explicit user scrub/play/pause afterward.
- Capture-path check (`hideChrome()`/`capturing` branch) still forces `posterFrame`/`0` — the mirror must not leak into render/export capture, which needs deterministic frames driven by the render shim, not the last live-preview position.

## Complexity

Low — two localized changes (a mirror map + one re-seed call) following an already-established pattern (`liveViewport`) in the same codebase; no schema or protocol changes needed since `timeline-seek` already exists as a message type.

decision.title: RCA: Ticket "video artboards autoplay + Timeline loop defaults on"
decision.rationale:
# RCA: Ticket "video artboards autoplay + Timeline loop defaults on"

## Summary

User report (Czech): after the video-artboard header badge / "Open Timeline" feature shipped, video artboards appear to autoplay, and the Timeline panel's loop toggle defaults to ON. Desired: every video artboard should open PAUSED (already the case — see below), and loop should always default OFF so the user opts in per-session.

## Root Cause

Two independent `loop` defaults both default to `true`:

1. `apps/studio/client/app.jsx:6915` — `const [timelineLoop, setTimelineLoop] = useState(true);`. This is the Timeline panel's loop-toggle state, sent to the iframe via the `timeline-loop` postMessage whenever the user presses Play (`app.jsx` `onPlay`) or hits Space (`app.jsx` ~7402).
2. `apps/studio/video-comp.tsx:242,296` — `VideoCompProps.loop` JSDoc says "Default true"; `VideoComp({ …, loop = true })` seeds `loopState` (the `<Player loop={loopState}>` prop) with `true` before the Timeline ever sends a `timeline-loop` message.

Because both default true, the FIRST time a user presses Play on any video artboard it loops indefinitely once it reaches the end — with no explicit action from the user to turn looping on. That reads as "it keeps autoplaying / never stops" even though the composition genuinely starts PAUSED.

**The "initial state should be stop" half is already correct in current source** — `video-comp.tsx:315`, `const play = (autoPlay ?? false) && !capturing;`, defaults to `false` (paused), landed 2026-07-04 (commit `83931cecb`, "Default to PAUSED in preview so the comp is editable on open"). I verified this live twice against the current committed source: a synthetic `Badge Test` canvas and a copy of the real `Maude Video Intro.tsx` (TransitionSeries + real MP4 `<Video>` clips) both opened on the poster frame and stayed on that exact frame across a 2s+ observation window — no autoplay reproduced. If the user is still seeing genuine autoplay-on-open, the likely explanation is a stale running dev-server/binary (their session's `_server.json` showed a server started before this session, pid no longer resolvable) rather than a source bug — worth a hard-restart of their dev server to rule out, but not something this fix can address in source.

## Impact

- Any user who presses Play once on a video artboard gets stuck-in-loop playback by default, with no prior opt-in — surprising, and reads as a bigger "won't stop autoplaying" bug than it is.
- Low severity, cosmetic/UX-default only — no data loss, no crash.

## Proposed Fix

Flip both defaults to `false`, keep them user-toggleable exactly as today:

- `apps/studio/client/app.jsx:6915` — `useState(true)` → `useState(false)`.
- `apps/studio/video-comp.tsx:242` (JSDoc) + `:296` (`loop = true` destructure default) → `false`, update the "Default true" comment to "Default false".

No schema/message-protocol changes — `timeline-loop` message shape is unchanged, only the seed value flips.

Files to change:
- `apps/studio/client/app.jsx`
- `apps/studio/video-comp.tsx`

## Testing Requirements

- Live-verify: open a video artboard, confirm it opens paused on the poster frame (already true); open the Timeline panel, confirm the loop button shows OFF by default; press Play, let the comp reach the end, confirm it stops instead of looping; toggle loop ON, confirm it now loops; confirm the toggle state doesn't leak across a fresh canvas load (new `timelineLoop` state per mount, already the case since it's local `useState`).
