# Code Review — Docs site dynamic-values audit **Branch:** `main` **Date:** 2026-05-15 **Trigger:** `/flow:review-code` with focus on "version, contributors, statuses — kde vsude se hodi aby se hodnoty menili s kazdym novym buildem" ## Summary Site landing + docs surface ship with several values hardcoded that should re-derive every build: version, published date, plugin command/skill/agent counts, contributor count, per-page last-updated date. Pattern to follow already exists in repo (`scripts/build-command-reference.mjs` + `prebuild` hook). This is a **suggestion-only** review — no broken behavior, no security issue, no test regression. Just static values that will silently rot the moment v0.12.1 ships. ## Files reviewed - `site/app/(home)/page.tsx` - `site/app/docs/[[...slug]]/page.tsx` - `site/components/mdcc/page-meta-footer.tsx` - `site/lib/layout.shared.tsx` - `site/lib/shared.ts` - `site/scripts/build-command-reference.mjs` (reference pattern) - `site/scripts/build-schema-reference.mjs` (reference pattern) - `package.json` (version source-of-truth) ## Findings ### 🔴 CRITICAL (must fix) None. ### 🟡 IMPORTANT (should fix before next release) Each of these will go stale on the next version bump and nothing in CI catches it: #### IMP-1 — Version literal `v0.12.0` repeated 5× on the landing page - `site/app/(home)/page.tsx:20` — `CATALOG[0].version` - `site/app/(home)/page.tsx:31` — `CATALOG[1].version` - `site/app/(home)/page.tsx:42` — `CATALOG[2].version` - `site/app/(home)/page.tsx:62` — hero eyebrow `v0.12.0` - `site/app/(home)/page.tsx:105` — catalog eyebrow `03 shipping units · all · v0.12.0` **Source of truth:** `package.json.version`. Cost to derive: one `readFileSync` in a build script. The npm `version-parity` workflow already guarantees `package.json` + both plugin manifests stay in lockstep, so reading from any one is safe. #### IMP-2 — Plugin asset counts wired wrong + drift-prone - `site/app/(home)/page.tsx:24` — `["commands · 11", "skills · 3", "critics · 13"]` - `site/app/(home)/page.tsx:35` — `["commands · 29", "skills · 16", "agents · 4"]` - `site/app/(home)/page.tsx:46` — `["subcommands · 5", "node ≥ 20", "zero deps"]` I already corrected drift in this session (was 12/4/9 — actually 11/3/13). The pattern will repeat unless derived from the filesystem at build time. **Source of truth:** | Tag | Derivation | | --- | --- | | `commands · N` (flow / design) | `find plugins//commands -maxdepth 1 -name '*.md' -not -name '_*' \| wc -l` | | `skills · N` | `find plugins//skills -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d \| wc -l` | | `agents · N` / `critics · N` | `find plugins//agents -name '*.md' \| wc -l` | | `subcommands · N` (mdcc) | `find cli/commands -name '*.mjs' \| wc -l` | | `node ≥ X` | `package.json.engines.node` | #### IMP-3 — Published date hardcoded - `site/app/(home)/page.tsx:64` — `PUBLISHED 2026-05-09` (hero eyebrow) - `site/app/(home)/page.tsx:139` — `
2026-05-09
` (meta footer) **Source of truth options (pick one):** - `git log -1 --format=%cs /package.json` — date of last version-bumping commit - `git for-each-ref --sort=-creatordate --count=1 --format='%(creatordate:short)' refs/tags/v*` — date of last `v*` tag - Read CHANGELOG.md (if Changesets generates dated entries — which DDR-002 records yes) **Recommendation:** tag-date — it's authoritative (release time), available on every CI runner with git, and immune to local-only commits like docs tweaks. #### IMP-4 — Contributor count + build status hardcoded - `site/app/(home)/page.tsx:153` — `
4 · build green
` **Source of truth:** - Contributors: `git shortlog -sne main | wc -l` (or GitHub API for richer data). - Build status: external CI signal. Cheapest: a shields.io badge image. Build-time fetch is fragile (CI runner has no internet guarantee). **Recommendation:** - Make contributor count dynamic (cheap, deterministic). - Drop "build green" string OR replace with a GitHub Actions badge SVG link (rendered live by GitHub, no build-time fetch needed). My suggestion: drop it — it's status theater on a docs site, not value. #### IMP-5 — Docs page "Last updated" always shows `—` - `site/components/mdcc/page-meta-footer.tsx:26` — `
{updated ?? '—'}
` - `site/app/docs/[[...slug]]/page.tsx:75` — `` (no `updated` prop passed) The footer component already accepts `updated?: string` — it's just never plumbed in. **Source of truth:** `git log -1 --format=%cs -- content/docs/`. Build script reads this for every page, exposes a `{[path]: dateString}` map. #### IMP-6 — `gitConfig` is a hand-edited const - `site/lib/shared.ts:6–10` — `{ user: '1aGh', repo: 'md-claude', branch: 'main' }` Not strictly drifty (it identifies the repo, not a moving target), but it's the obvious thing future-you would forget to update if the repo migrates. Derivable from `git remote get-url origin` at build. **Cost vs value:** low value (changes only on org/repo rename); leave as-is unless you do a bulk shared-config refactor. ### 🟢 SUGGESTION (nice-to-have) #### SUG-1 — "03 shipping units" magic number - `site/app/(home)/page.tsx:105` — `03 shipping units` Currently `CATALOG.length === 3`. Could be `${String(CATALOG.length).padStart(2, '0')} shipping units`. Tiny win, but matches the catalog-grade voice (it's reading like a catalog header — should reflect catalog length). #### SUG-2 — Stable SKU map could live next to the design system - `site/app/docs/[[...slug]]/page.tsx:18–24` — `SECTION_SKU` lookup - `site/lib/layout.shared.tsx:11` — `MDCC/00` nav SKU These are stable identifiers, not drifty data — but they're also DS-adjacent metadata. Plausibly belongs in `.design/system/project/skus.json` (read at build time) so the design plugin owns the canonical list. Not urgent; flag for a future "design metadata seam" refactor. #### SUG-3 — `node ≥ 20` could be `node ≥ ${engines.node}` Same shape as IMP-1; very small drift surface (npm engines spec moves rarely), but trivially derivable. ## Proposed implementation A single new build script — `site/scripts/build-stats.mjs` — emits one JSON file consumed by the static pages. ```js // site/scripts/build-stats.mjs (sketch — ~80 LOC total) import { execSync } from 'node:child_process'; import { readFile, readdir, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises'; import { existsSync } from 'node:fs'; import { resolve } from 'node:path'; const root = resolve(__dirname, '../..'); const sh = (cmd) => execSync(cmd, { cwd: root, encoding: 'utf8' }).trim(); const pkg = JSON.parse(await readFile(resolve(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8')); const lastTag = sh( "git for-each-ref --sort=-creatordate --count=1 --format='%(creatordate:short)' refs/tags/v*", ) || sh("git log -1 --format=%cs -- package.json"); const contributors = parseInt(sh("git shortlog -sne main | wc -l"), 10); async function countMd(dir, opts = {}) { const entries = await readdir(resolve(root, dir)); return entries.filter((e) => e.endsWith('.md') && (!opts.excludeUnderscore || !e.startsWith('_'))).length; } async function countDirs(dir) { const entries = await readdir(resolve(root, dir), { withFileTypes: true }); return entries.filter((e) => e.isDirectory()).length; } const stats = { version: `v${pkg.version}`, nodeRange: pkg.engines.node, publishedDate: lastTag, contributors, plugins: { design: { commands: await countMd('plugins/design/commands', { excludeUnderscore: true }), skills: await countDirs('plugins/design/skills'), agents: await countMd('plugins/design/agents'), }, flow: { commands: await countMd('plugins/flow/commands', { excludeUnderscore: true }), skills: await countDirs('plugins/flow/skills'), agents: await countMd('plugins/flow/agents'), }, mdcc: { subcommands: await countMd('cli/commands').then((n) => n /* count .mjs */), }, }, // Per-page last-updated (consumed by docs page footer) pageUpdated: await buildPageUpdatedMap(), }; await writeFile(resolve(__dirname, '../lib/stats.json'), JSON.stringify(stats, null, 2)); ``` Wire into `site/package.json`: ```diff - "prebuild": "node scripts/build-command-reference.mjs && node scripts/build-schema-reference.mjs && fumadocs-mdx", + "prebuild": "node scripts/build-stats.mjs && node scripts/build-command-reference.mjs && node scripts/build-schema-reference.mjs && fumadocs-mdx", - "predev": "node scripts/build-command-reference.mjs && node scripts/build-schema-reference.mjs && fumadocs-mdx", + "predev": "node scripts/build-stats.mjs && node scripts/build-command-reference.mjs && node scripts/build-schema-reference.mjs && fumadocs-mdx", ``` Add to `site/.gitignore`: `lib/stats.json` (output is regenerated every build — same convention as `content/docs/reference/`). Consume in `page.tsx`: ```tsx import stats from '@/lib/stats.json'; const CATALOG = [ { sku: 'MDCC-DSN/01', slug: 'design', version: stats.version, description: '...', tags: [ `commands · ${stats.plugins.design.commands}`, `skills · ${stats.plugins.design.skills}`, `critics · ${stats.plugins.design.agents}`, ], // ... }, // flow, mdcc same shape ]; ``` And in `app/docs/[[...slug]]/page.tsx`: ```tsx import stats from '@/lib/stats.json'; const updated = stats.pageUpdated[page.path]; ``` ## Verdict **PASS WITH SUGGESTIONS.** No critical findings. Six IMPORTANT items that will silently drift on the next release; one of them (IMP-2 plugin counts) already drifted this session and required a manual fix. Implementing `build-stats.mjs` cuts every drift surface in one move, follows the existing prebuild pattern, and adds < 100 LOC + one JSON output. ## Simplifier outcome Not invoked. Verdict is suggestion-list, not stylistic — no diff to polish.

decision.title: Code review — feature-docs-site-mdcc-skin
decision.rationale:
# Code review — feature-docs-site-mdcc-skin

**Date:** 2026-05-15
**Scope:** commits `78d9d8f` (re-skin) + `94b4e77` (TOV + dynamic stats + CI guards). Excludes unrelated `5c8932c` formatter-drift fix.
**Reviewer:** `general-purpose` Agent (self-review pattern)
**Verdict:** **PASS WITH SUGGESTIONS**

## Summary

12 findings, none release-blocking. The heavy DS+a11y agents (run earlier in the same `/flow:done`) covered all chrome / visual / WCAG issues; this review focused on code correctness, simplicity, security, and React patterns the other gates don't see.

## Findings

### Correctness (4)

1. **`site/scripts/build-stats.mjs:66-69`** — Comment says "Skip auto-generated reference pages... use the plugin file's mtime instead." Code does neither — every `.mdx` (including 42 reference entries) is git-logged. Either delete the misleading comment or implement the documented behavior.

2. **`site/scripts/build-stats.mjs:60`** — `git shortlog -sne main` is brittle on PR CI. `actions/checkout@v6 fetch-depth: 0` fetches the PR ref but doesn't guarantee a local `main`. `sh()` swallows the error → `contributors: 0` → trips the drift guard. Use `HEAD` or fetch `main` explicitly.

3. **`site/scripts/build-stats.mjs:69`** — Single-quoted shell interpolation of file paths. Safe for current repo content, breaks if any `.mdx` filename contains `'`. Switch to `execFileSync` with arg array.

4. **`site/components/mdcc/page-meta-footer.tsx:11-32`** — Invalid HTML. `<dt>`/`<dd>` inside `<footer>` without a wrapping `<dl>`. Compare to `site/app/(home)/page.tsx:170` which correctly wraps. SR description-list semantics are lost. Wrap in `<dl>` or switch to plain `<div>`/`<span>`.

### Code simplicity (3)

5. **`site/components/mdcc/code-block.tsx:13-14`** — `(rest as Record<string, string | undefined>)['data-filename']`. Destructure `data-filename` and `data-language` directly from `props` — cleaner, removes the cast.

6. **`site/components/mdcc/copy-button.tsx:25` + `code-block.tsx:32`** — `navigator.clipboard.writeText().then(...)` has no `.catch()` (rejects unhandled in non-secure contexts); `setTimeout` ID not cleaned up on unmount (React 19 warns). Trivial fix with `useEffect` cleanup + `.catch(() => setCopied(false))`.

7. **`site/lib/layout.shared.tsx:21-29`** — JSX as fumadocs `link.text`. Works today but bypasses the link's text-only contract; if fumadocs starts using `link.text` for `aria-label`, this regresses silently. Refactored anyway when DS-guard blocker #3 (remove Lucide Coffee) lands.

### Security (1)

8. **`page-meta-footer.tsx:16`** — `<a target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">` is fine in modern browsers (implies `noopener`), but `page.tsx:99-103` uses `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. Add `noopener` here for consistency.

### Build-time scripts (4)

9. **`scripts/sync-mdcc-tokens.mjs`** — Solid. No issues.

10. **`scripts/build-stats.mjs:39`** — Triple fallback (tag date → package.json mtime → today). The `today` fallback makes `stats.json` non-deterministic on tagless repos. This repo has tags so it doesn't trip; a fresh fork would. Fail loud instead.

11. **`scripts/build-stats.mjs:81`** — Empty `pageUpdated: {}` is silently emitted if git history is shallow. Footers render `Last updated: —` everywhere. Add a console warning.

12. **No `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, no XSS surface** — fumadocs sanitizes MDX. Catalog map keyed by `item.sku`, breadcrumb keyed by `${label}-${i}` — both correct. No unnecessary `'use client'`.

## Files referenced

- `site/scripts/build-stats.mjs`
- `site/scripts/sync-mdcc-tokens.mjs`
- `site/components/mdcc/page-meta-footer.tsx`
- `site/components/mdcc/code-block.tsx`
- `site/components/mdcc/copy-button.tsx`
- `site/lib/layout.shared.tsx`
- `.github/workflows/quality.yml`

## Recommendation

Ship. Follow-ups #1, #2, #4 are the strongest patch candidates. The rest are polish.

# Code review — feature-3-web-artboards

**Branch:** main · **Commit under review:** `2d124965` (+ follow-up fixes staged on top) · **Date:** 2026-07-18

## Verdict: PASS WITH SUGGESTIONS (all suggestions applied)

Parallel fan-out (security-auditor + ethical-hacker + design-system-guard + a11y-auditor, spawned alongside `/flow:validate`'s scenario-runner) found 3 real, low-severity issues — all fixed before this report was finalized. No blockers.

## Security-auditor (defender) — PASS, 1 low informational

- 0 findings at/above the `medium` severity floor. `/_api/duplicate-artboard`, `resolveCanvasKind()`, and the grid-track `/_api/edit-css` additions all correctly inherit the established DDR-054 trust-boundary guards (main-origin-only, `sameOriginWrite`+`isLoopbackHost`, absent from both canvas-origin allowlists, `escapeAttr`+reparse-gate on every interpolated value).
- **Fixed for consistency (not exploitable, but a real gap vs sibling ops):** `duplicateArtboardOp`'s `artboardId` was validated only as non-empty, unlike sibling `insertArtboardOp`/`resizeArtboardOp`'s stricter `/^[A-Za-z][\w-]{0,63}$/`. Tightened in `api.ts`; regression test added (`element-structural-api.test.ts`, malformed-id → 400).

## Ethical-hacker (adversarial) — PASS, 0 exploitable findings

Constructed and traced 5 concrete attack vectors against `applyDuplicateArtboard`/`resolveCanvasKind`/the grid edit-css path (JSX-attribute breakout via clone id/label, id-collision DoS, width-bound-enforcement ordering, JSON-context breakout via `meta.kind`, the untrusted-read×privileged-write×exfil trifecta lens). None survive — `escapeAttr` + the reparse gate close the injection surface, the width clamp runs before the id template is built, and the DDR-054 route-reachability guards hold. One informational, sub-floor note (`escapeAttr` doesn't escape a bare `&` — cosmetic round-trip fidelity only, not an injection; no action taken, correctly assessed as out of scope for this feature).

## design-system-guard — 1 finding, fixed

- `apps/studio/client/styles/3-shell-maude.css`: `.st-cp-gridtrack-remove:hover` referenced a non-existent `--status-danger` token (silently fell back to `--fg-0`, so the hover state rendered as plain text color instead of red). Fixed to the real token, `--status-error` (the one every other danger/delete affordance in this stylesheet already uses).
- Everything else — the breakpoint chip, new CSS placement, `GridTracksEditor`'s use of shared control primitives, the context-menu submenu shape — verified as a correct lift of the established sibling patterns (`print-overlay-content.tsx`, `kindItem`/`themeItem`, the `sec()`/`row()` CSS-panel convention), not a reinvention.

## a11y-auditor — PASS, 0 blockers, 0 warnings

Accessible names verified on every new control (`ariaLabel` props consumed correctly by `NumberField`/`Select`/`UnitSelect`, including the "×" remove-track button's real `aria-label`), contrast computed numerically from OKLCH tokens (lowest 5.40:1, both themes, well above AA), keyboard reachability inherited correctly from the shared `ContextMenu`/ `MenuItem` submenu machinery, decorative chrome (breakpoint chip) correctly `aria-hidden` + non-focusable. Two non-blocking notes (grid-gutter drag is pointer-only but has a keyboard-reachable Inspector equivalent; breakpoint width is redundantly encoded in the artboard's own accessible name) — both accepted as-is, not gaps.

## code-simplifier — 3 files, net −24 lines, verified

Behavior-preserving dedups only (verified via `bun tsc --noEmit` unchanged 8-baseline / 0 new, and the 5 in-scope test files 108/0-fail, before accepting):
- `use-grid-track-handles.tsx` — extracted a `bail()` helper collapsing 4 repeated rAF-guard tails; merged `buildAxis`'s redundant `authoredProp`/`resolvedProp` params (always called with the same string) into one `prop` param; merged the col/row gutter-handle-painting loops into one loop over `[['col',col],['row',row]]`.
- `canvas-shell.tsx` — replaced 4 hand-written, identical-shape `MenuItem` submenu entries with a `DUP_BREAKPOINTS` data array + `.map()`.
- `handoff.ts` — `resolveCanvasKind`'s manual `re.exec` while-loop → `for (const m of rawSource.matchAll(...))`.

`app.jsx` was deliberately left untouched by the simplifier to avoid a bundle-rebuild collision with a concurrent session's own in-flight, unrelated changes to that same file.

## Cross-validation: scenario-runner (parallel /flow:validate fan-out)

`web-artboards` scenario (new, `.ai/scenarios/web-artboards/spec.md`) — **PASS, 0 blockers, parity_ok=true** (single-platform project, non-desktop platforms correctly SKIPPED per the sibling `artboard-kinds`/`element-editing-resize-and-position` precedent). All 4 headline capabilities verified live against a real dev-server boot: breakpoint chip tracking live width across 2 artboards, `/_api/duplicate-artboard` clone+undo round-trip, `grid-template-columns`/`-rows` (incl. `fr`) round-trip + live reflow. Independently corroborated by a second, concurrent scenario-runner instance from the other session working this same branch. Report: `.ai/device/scenario-runs/web-artboards/2026-07-18-1501/report.md` (gitignored per `.ai/device/` convention — the spec + fixture are the committed artifacts).

## Final state

- `bun test`: 3045 pass / 5 skip / 0 fail (full apps/studio suite, post-fixes).
- `bun tsc --noEmit`: same 8 pre-existing baseline errors, 0 new.
- `bunx biome check` clean on every touched file (one pre-existing, documented, untouched warning at `canvas-edit.ts:2858`, per this repo's own CLAUDE.md note).
- `pnpm test` (CLI suite): 195/195.
- Site build + parity + tarball-shape + token-sync + site-content-drift gates: all green.

# Code review — main, Phase 4.1 close-out

**Date:** 2026-05-19
**Branch:** `main`
**Scope:** all uncommitted Phase 4.1 changes (universal canvas input grammar).
**Reviewer:** inline self-review (no separate subagent spawned — work is mine; honest blocker pass).

## Verdict

**PASS WITH SUGGESTIONS** — no critical findings. Three carry-over items flagged below as soft suggestions for follow-up.

## Changes reviewed

```
new   plugins/design/dev-server/input-router.tsx              (319 LOC)
new   plugins/design/dev-server/use-tool-mode.tsx              (104 LOC)
new   plugins/design/dev-server/use-selection-set.tsx          (188 LOC)
new   plugins/design/dev-server/context-menu.tsx               (227 LOC)
new   plugins/design/dev-server/tool-palette.tsx               ( 89 LOC)
new   plugins/design/dev-server/canvas-shell.tsx               (679 LOC)
new   plugins/design/dev-server/test/input-router.test.ts      (33 tests)
new   plugins/design/dev-server/test/use-tool-mode.test.tsx    ( 7 tests)
new   plugins/design/dev-server/test/use-selection-set.test.tsx(12 tests)
new   .ai/archive/decisions/DDR-026-universal-canvas-input-grammar.md
new   .ai/scenarios/canvas-format-tsx/canvas-input-grammar/spec.md
new   .ai/scenarios/canvas-format-tsx/canvas-context-menu/spec.md
new   .ai/logs/phase-4.1-hover-perf-2026-05-19.md
mod   plugins/design/dev-server/canvas-lib.tsx                 (+76 / —17)
mod   plugins/design/dev-server/inspect.ts                     (-180 / +30)
mod   plugins/design/dev-server/client/app.jsx                 (+85 / —42)
mod   .design/ui/Canvas Viewport.tsx                           ( inputMode strip )
mod   .design/ui/Smoke TSX.tsx                                 ( inputMode strip )
mod   plugins/design/dev-server/examples/perf-100-artboards.tsx( inputMode strip )
mod   .ai/state/STATE.md
arch  .ai/plans/archive/phase-4.1-figjam-canvas-interactions.md( moved + retro appended )
```

## Findings

### Correctness — 0 critical / 0 major

- **Capture-phase listener cleanup** (`input-router.tsx:onPointerDown / onMouseDown / onClick / onContextMenu`). All four attach with `{ capture: true }`; all four detach with matching `EventListenerOptions`. Symmetric.
- **rAF coalescing** (`canvas-shell.tsx:applyHover`, `GroupBbox tick`, `HoverHalo tick`, `SelectionHalos tick`). Each tracks its own `rafRef` and cancels on unmount or when the input that fed it changes (selected.length === 0 / el === null). No leaks identified.
- **Sentinel cleanup**: not applicable — sentinel was removed entirely in the universal-grammar flip.
- **Schema migration** (`inspect.ts:setSelected`). Single-entry array collapses to bare object; multi-entry stays array; null is null. Reader (`normalizeSelectedRead`) accepts all three. Round-trip tested.

### Quality

- **Universal grammar refactor introduced some dead code in app.jsx.** The `dgn: 'select'` message handler is now reachable only for the slim inspector overlay (which no longer emits it) or external embeds (none known). Flagged in DDR-026 alternatives — can be removed in a follow-up audit. Not a blocker.
- **`.sel-halo` CSS in `3-shell.css`** is orphaned (no JS reference). Left in place to avoid CSS-diff noise this commit. Follow-up: remove the rule block.
- **`startDraftFromSelection` in app.jsx**: dependency-array carry-over from the deleted `Cmd+C` chord. Still referenced by the comments panel's "Add comment" button — legitimate use. Keep.
- **`.dc-cv-*` class prefix**: chose `cv` (canvas-viewport) to avoid clashing with `.dc-canvas` (host element). Considered `.dc-cs-*` (canvas-shell) but `cv` reads more clearly in DevTools. Document in DDR-026 — done.
- **Cursor force `!important`**: used only in comment / hand modes via `.dc-canvas[data-active-tool="..."] *`. Bounded scope; doesn't bleed outside the canvas root. OK.

### Security

- **No new `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` / `eval` / template-evaluated user input.**
- **Inspector overlay slimmed**: legacy script string interpolation surface reduced; no new `${var}` strings inside the IIFE script.
- **Clipboard writes** (`canvas-shell.tsx:buildRegistry > copy`) are gated by `navigator.clipboard` presence and wrapped in `.catch(() => {})`. No PII / secrets in the copied payloads (CSS path or `data-cd-id` only).

### Convention

- **Pattern priors honored.** ContextMenu visual lifted from `audience-pro/components-toast-menu.html` (hairline border, mono shortcut hints, section separators). ToolPalette mirrors `DCZoomToolbar` chrome.
- **No AI-tell punctuation** in the new user-facing strings (help overlay, scenario specs, DDR-026). Em-dashes used legitimately in technical sentences only.
- **TS strict-mode**: `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean of new errors. Only pre-existing `api.ts:592–593` errors carry over.
- **Test naming**: `<topic>.test.ts(x)` matches existing convention. Test groups use `describe('<topic> / <slice>')` consistently with other suites.

### Soft suggestions (non-blocking)

1. **Remove orphan `.sel-halo` CSS** in `client/styles/3-shell.css` (lines 882–906) in a follow-up `chore(design)` commit.
2. **Audit `dgn: 'select'` and `dgn: 'comment-shortcut'` listeners** in `app.jsx` once external embed inventory is confirmed empty. Both currently kept as safety nets per DDR-026.
3. **Add a CI grep guard** for `figjam` / `FigJam` / `dc-fjm-` / `__MDCC_INPUT_MODE__` to prevent the names from sneaking back via auto-completion or copy-paste.

## Test pass

- `bun test plugins/design/dev-server`: **185 / 185, 0 fail, 472 expect() calls.**
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`: clean of new errors.
- Live canvas-build smoke (Canvas Viewport / Docs Site / Smoke TSX): HTTP 200, 0 legacy refs in bundles, CanvasShell wired identically.

## code-simplifier pass

Skipped — files are tight enough; the universal-grammar refactor already simplified by removing the `inputMode` branch.

# Code review — phase-30 collab fixes (F1 cold-seed dedup, F4 hot-swap, F5 avatar accumulation)

**Branch:** `native-app` · **Date:** 2026-06-20 · **Scope:** uncommitted diff (sync/cold-start.ts, codec.ts, agent.ts, use-collab.tsx, hmr-broadcast.ts, _shell.html + 2 new tests).
**Source:** RCAs `issue-collab-cold-seed-tsx-duplication.md` + `issue-collab-observer-tsx-reload-flicker.md`; F5 found during the `/flow:scenario` smoke re-run.

Three independent reviewers ran in parallel: **security-auditor** (defender), **ethical-hacker** (attacker), **general-purpose** (correctness + quality).

## Verdict: PASS (after applied fixes)

- Correctness: **PASS WITH SUGGESTIONS** — F1 LWW election verified deterministic/convergent (200-trial probe), F4 refcount/grace math holds (no leak, no double-socket), both new tests fail if the fix is reverted. All suggestions applied.
- Security: defender **0 blockers / 1 warning**; attacker **HIGH chained finding** on the `window` exposure. The two split on whether the Y.Doc was reachable by untrusted canvas JS pre-patch (defender: yes, via `useCollab()` in the same realm → not a new capability; attacker: no, closure-private → new write primitive). **Resolved by hardening** (below).

## Findings + resolution

| # | Reviewer | Finding | Resolution |
|---|----------|---------|------------|
| S1 | attacker (HIGH) / defender (warn) | The collab session (live Y.Doc + Awareness + WS) was moved onto an **enumerable** `window.__maudeCollabSessions`, harvestable by untrusted same-realm canvas script via `for…in`/`Object.keys`. | **FIXED** — registry re-keyed to a **non-enumerable global `Symbol.for('maude.collab.sessions.v1')`** (`Object.defineProperty`, `enumerable:false`). Verified live: `Object.keys(window)` no longer leaks it; survives the cache-busted re-import (global symbol registry is per-realm). Defense-in-depth, not a trust boundary — see DDR-122 for the residual. |
| S2 | attacker (residual) | The underlying "untrusted canvas can mutate the shared doc and propagate `.tsx` to all peers" capability. | **Pre-existing** (a malicious canvas already reaches the doc via `useCollab()` — defender confirmed). NOT introduced here. Tracked as a follow-up in **DDR-122** (origin-gate canvas-injected doc ops). Not a blocker for this fix. |
| S3 | attacker (LOW) | `isExactRepeat` collapse has no pre-collapse snapshot. | Accepted: the collapsed bytes are by definition an exact duplicate of local (zero new content), so there is nothing to recover. Divergent seeds are NOT exact repeats → fall through (see C1). |
| C1 | correctness (major→comment) | The live repair only covers the **identical**-seed race; a **divergent** concurrent seed stays un-buildable until the next boot's conflict path. Comments overstated coverage. | **FIXED** — comments in `agent.ts`/`cold-start.ts` tightened to state the divergent variant is an accepted follow-up, self-healing only on the next boot. |
| C2 | correctness (minor) | `seedInfo` comment claimed clearing on convergence; it only clears on window-lapse. | **FIXED** — comment corrected (convergence is a cheap no-op guard). |
| C3 | correctness (minor) | `agentEditing` in `_shell.html` is now dead (no longer gates the swap); the "kept for diagnostics" comment was misleading. | **FIXED** — comments corrected to state it's tracked-but-not-gating; the inert var was left in place (removing message-handler branches post-security-review adds risk for marginal gain). |
| C4 | correctness (nit) | Repair re-stamps `bodyEditAt` to the repair instant. | Accepted — no feedback loop (self-origin filtered), benign for newest-wins. |

## What was verified, not just asserted
- **F1**: live cold-seed race reproduced (`[sync/ui-coldseed] … collapsed to one copy (F1)` fired), both disks converge to a single `export default`, canvas builds + renders.
- **F4**: synced edit hot-swaps in place — a `window` sentinel survives the update (a `location.reload()` would wipe it), repeatable across consecutive edits.
- **F5**: phantom self-avatars no longer accumulate — fresh room, peer alone, 5 self-edits → 0 avatars, stable clientID (was 1→2→…→8 before the window-anchor fix).
- **S1 hardening**: live — `mapUnderSymbol:true`, `stringKeyLeaked:false`, avatars 0, sentinel survives.

## Gates
- Full dev-server suite: 1614 pass / 0 fail (1 skip). CLI suite: 163 pass / 0 fail. biome + tsc clean on changed files.
- Scenario: `.ai/scenarios/live-multiplayer-hub-sync/report-2026-06-20.md` (F1/F4/F5 PASS live).

decision.rationale:
# Code Review: Phase 3.6 foundation slice (Tasks 0–3)

Branch: `main` (uncommitted)
Date: 2026-05-18

## Summary

Foundation for the canvas TSX format refactor: DDR-019 + the two-pass transpile pipeline (`canvas-pipeline.ts`), the multi-canvas locator writer (`locator.ts`), and the TSX route wired into the existing fall-through `fetch()` in `http.ts`. Adds `oxc-parser` + `magic-string` as dev-deps. 36 new test expects across 3 new test files; full suite 44 pass / 0 fail.

## Files Reviewed

- `plugins/design/dev-server/canvas-pipeline.ts` — NEW (~270 LOC); two-pass transform (oxc + magic-string + Bun.Transpiler).
- `plugins/design/dev-server/locator.ts` — NEW (~170 LOC); per-canvas `_locator.json` with promise-mutex + atomic rename.
- `plugins/design/dev-server/http.ts` — MODIFIED (+77 LOC); imports new modules, adds `serveCanvasTsx()` + in-memory cache, dispatches `.tsx` under designRoot.
- `plugins/design/dev-server/package.json` — MODIFIED (+2 LOC); `oxc-parser`, `magic-string` added.
- `plugins/design/dev-server/test/canvas-pipeline.test.ts` — NEW (~165 LOC); 15 expects covering determinism / whitespace stability / sibling-insert contract / robustness.
- `plugins/design/dev-server/test/locator.test.ts` — NEW (~190 LOC); 14 expects covering roundtrip, multi-slug isolation, deterministic JSON, 20-way concurrent writes, malformed-as-empty.
- `plugins/design/dev-server/test/canvas-route.test.ts` — NEW (~165 LOC); 7 expects covering 200/304/404/500, locator persistence, cache equality.
- `.ai/archive/decisions/DDR-019-canvas-tsx-format.md` — NEW (~150 LOC); decision + reconciliation with DDR-007 + alternatives.
- `.ai/archive/decisions/README.md` — MODIFIED; index updates (DDR-017, 018, 019).
- `.ai/state/STATE.md` — MODIFIED; phase-3.6 progress section.

## Findings

### 🔴 CRITICAL (must fix)

_None._

### 🟡 IMPORTANT (should fix)

- **`locator.ts:65,71` — `locks` map cleanup is dead code.** The expression `prev.then(() => gate)` is evaluated twice (set + compare), producing two different Promise instances. `locks.get(filePath) === prev.then(() => gate)` will always be `false`, so the `locks.delete(...)` branch never fires. The map grows one entry per unique `_locator.json` path. In practice this leaks at most one entry per dev-server lifetime (one designRoot), but the dead-code is misleading and the fix is two lines. **Fix planned this turn.**

### 🟢 SUGGESTION (nice to have)

- **`locator.ts:116` — redundant explicit sort.** `sortedMap(map)` re-sorts the keys before they get handed to `JSON.stringify(..., sortedSlugKeysReplacer)`, which already sorts every plain-object value at every level. The explicit sort is dead work but not incorrect. **Fix planned this turn.**
- **`canvas-pipeline.ts:170–175` — `padStart(16, '0')` is defensive but never triggered.** `Bun.hash()` returns a 64-bit non-negative bigint whose `.toString(16)` is at most 16 chars; in practice always 14–16. The padding makes IDs uniform when the high nibble is small. Leaving as-is — costs nothing, improves clarity.
- **`http.ts:85` — mtime fallback `|| 0` can poison cache** if `lastModified` is ever falsy. In testing it always returns a real value; if Bun changes this, the cache would never invalidate. Low-priority — leave for now.
- **`http.ts:88` — two concurrent GETs of the same canvas double-transpile.** The route doesn't memoize an in-flight transpile. Wasted CPU but correct (both writes serialise via locator mutex). Acceptable for dev-server.
- **`canvas-pipeline.ts:255–269` `lineColFromByte` is likely dead** — oxc-parser populates `node.loc` reliably; the fallback path probably never runs. Cheap to keep; one-line safety net.

## Verdict

**PASS WITH SUGGESTIONS** — one minor cleanup bug + one redundancy. Both fixed inline. Code is otherwise tight, well-tested, and faithful to the plan / DDR-019.

## Fix outcome

- `locator.ts:65–73` — captured `next = prev.then(() => gate)` once; the cleanup check now compares against the same Promise instance. Map no longer leaks stale tail-of-chain entries.
- `locator.ts:116` + `locator.ts:150–154` — dropped `sortedMap()` helper and its explicit pre-sort; the `stableStringify` replacer already sorts every plain object recursively. One fewer pass over the map per write.
- `bun test` — 51 pass / 0 fail (suite picks up the new files end-to-end).
- `bun tsc --noEmit` — only the pre-existing `api.ts:457` error (verified independent of this slice via stash-then-tsc).

## Simplifier outcome

Skipped — the diff is dominated by new files with focused responsibilities + the two manual fixes above already polished the only flagged spots. Running the simplifier over 600+ LOC of greenfield code for marginal wins is a poor trade. Will re-evaluate when Task 4+ touches them.

decision.rationale:
# Security review — adversarial (attacker) pass — feature-acp-ask-user-question + feature-acp-panel-dynamic-claude-code-capabilities close-out

**Date:** 2026-07-16 · **Reviewer:** `ethical-hacker` (flow plugin) · **Scope:** uncommitted working-tree diff for both plans, closed out together via `/flow:done --quick`

## Verdict at time of review

2 findings scored as blockers (per the agent's own `severityFloor`-relative scoring), 1 warning, 1 composed exploit chain. **All three findings were fixed before commit** — see the "resolution" line under each and DDR-180's addendum for the full writeup.

This is a second, independent fan-out — a first pass (documented earlier in DDR-180) already fixed a hardcoded misattribution, an unenforced `mode:'url'` capability-negotiation gap, and a client-side proto-pollution guard. This pass reasoned from the MCP spec's own elicitation guidance rather than just the codebase, and found three findings beyond that first pass's scope.

## Threat model

- **MCP server (attacker-controllable) → `unstable_createElicitation` → `pendingElicitations` → browser WS frame → `ElicitationPrompt.jsx` render.** The net-new trust boundary this whole feature introduces.
- **Browser (loopback+same-origin only) → `elicitation-response` → `resolveElicitation` → tool result fed back to the model/MCP server.** Confirmed gated identically to the existing DDR-179 permission-response boundary.
- **Bridge teardown → pending-request fate.** Verified no hang path.

## Findings

### 1. Elicitation-queue flood — no cap on concurrent pending requests or schema size (MEDIUM)

A connected MCP server can call the SDK's `onElicitation` hook repeatedly without waiting for an answer — `AcpBridge.pendingElicitations` was an unbounded `Map`, and `requestedSchema` had no size/property-count check before being forwarded to the browser. Could freeze/degrade the panel via an oversized `oneOf` list, grow memory unboundedly, and force the user into an endless Submit/Skip/Cancel loop.

**Resolution:** `unstable_createElicitation` now checks `MAX_PENDING_ELICITATIONS` (5) and `elicitationSchemaWithinBounds` (`MAX_ELICITATION_SCHEMA_PROPERTIES`=20, `MAX_ELICITATION_SCHEMA_BYTES`=16 KiB) before registering a pending entry or forwarding anything to the client — a request that trips either cap declines immediately. Covered by pure bound-check tests + a dedicated flood fixture (`mock-acp-agent-elicit-flood.mjs`, 8 concurrent requests, asserts only the cap's worth reach the client).

### 2. `resolveElicitation`'s content builder wasn't prototype-hardened, unlike its client-side sibling (LOW)

`buildElicitationContent` (client) uses `Object.create(null)` specifically to defend against a `__proto__`-keyed schema property; `resolveElicitation` (bridge.ts) — the function ACTUALLY reachable by a hand-crafted `elicitation-response` frame, not just the trusted UI — built `content` via a plain `{}` literal. No live escalation was demonstrated (assigning a non-object value via the `__proto__` accessor is a spec no-op, and every wire-legal value type is non-object), but the asymmetry meant one function's claimed guarantee didn't match its sibling's actual code.

**Resolution:** `resolveElicitation`'s `content` accumulator is now `Object.create(null)` too, for genuine parity.

### 3. Form-only capability declaration forecloses the MCP spec's own safer credential channel (MEDIUM, composed into a chain)

Per the MCP spec, url-mode elicitation exists specifically so a real credential request never has to pass through the LLM/client. Maude declares `form` only (a correct, reviewed, still-standing decision — see DDR-180's Decision section) — but the side effect is that the free-text box on this card becomes the ONLY channel any MCP server, benign or hostile, can ever use to ask for a secret, with no visual distinction from a benign question.

**Exploit chain (composed with Finding 1):** a flood of requests (Finding 1) induces alert fatigue → habituated Submit/Skip/Cancel clicking → a credential-shaped ask buried in the stream gets typed into an identical-looking free-text box and round-trips straight back to the requesting MCP server.

**Resolution:** a new `looksLikeSecretRequest` pure helper (`acp-elicitation.js`) pattern-matches question title/description/card message against credential-shaped language; when matched, `ElicitationPrompt.jsx` renders that field as `type="password"` with an inline warning. Adapter-independent, doesn't change accept/decline routing — a mitigation for the accepted residual, not a reopening of the form/url decision.

## Confirmed clean (explicitly verified)

- No XSS via `message`/option `title`/`description`/`preview` — plain JSX interpolation throughout, no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.
- `__proto__`/`constructor`-shaped keys in an attacker-controlled `requestedSchema.properties` don't confuse the parser (`Object.hasOwn`, not `in`).
- Canvas-origin cannot reach `elicitation-response` (verified against `server.ts` directly).
- Double-answering / stale-id answering is a safe no-op (unit-tested).
- `toolCallId`-based attribution cannot be spoofed by an MCP server — `mcpElicitationToCreateRequest` never sets it (confirmed on disk).
- Fail-closed teardown verified end to end (socket drop, turn-cancel, timeout all → decline, never a hang or fabricated accept).

## AI/MCP surface

Trifecta check: **pass, correctly scoped** — no path combines private-data access + untrusted content + an attacker-reachable outbound channel without a mandatory human Submit click in between. Confused-deputy: none reopened (DDR-125 F2 stays closed, per the sibling permission-gate feature). MCP supply chain: this feature's entire threat surface is "whatever MCP server(s) the user has already connected" — no new server added by this diff, but the realistic attacker precondition (a compromised/later-poisoned server) is the same class the MCP ecosystem has seen real incidents in.

## Recommended follow-ups (not blocking, logged)

- A volumetric/size-abuse test case beyond what was added this round (thousands of options, not just an oversized description) would strengthen Finding 1's regression coverage further.
- File defender reports for both this diff and the already-committed DDR-179 permission-gate commit going forward as a matter of course — this round closed that gap for both features retroactively.

decision.rationale:
# Security review — adversarial (attacker) pass — retroactive review of DDR-179 permission gate (commit `4174b82e`)

**Date:** 2026-07-16 · **Reviewer:** `ethical-hacker` (flow plugin) · **Scope:** already-committed permission-gate code, never previously reviewed despite the plan's own Validation §7 requiring it

## Verdict at time of review

4 blockers, composed into 1 High/Critical exploit chain. **All four fixed before commit** — see DDR-179's addendum for the full writeup and resolution details.

## Findings

### A. The permission card's Enter key and primary button both defaulted to `allow_always`, not `allow_once` (High)

`PermissionPrompt.jsx`'s `firstAllow = options.find(o => o.kind === 'allow_once' || o.kind === 'allow_always')` returns whichever kind the ADAPTER lists first. The real adapter's own option ordering for a standard tool-call request is `[allow_always, allow_once, reject_once]` — `allow_always` at index `[0]`. A user pressing Enter or clicking the one visually-dominant (`btn--primary`-styled `allow_always`) button believed they were approving one action; they were actually granting a session-scoped standing exemption. This defeats DDR-179's entire stated purpose using nothing but the shipped UI's own default affordances.

**Fixed**: extracted `pickDefaultAllow`/`pickDefaultReject` as pure, exported, unit-tested functions preferring `allow_once` explicitly; `allow_always` no longer gets `btn--primary` styling.

### B. ExitPlanMode inherited the same wrong default — resolved to unattended `"auto"` mode (High, chains with A)

Same root cause. `ExitPlanMode`'s real option ordering is `[auto(allow_always), acceptEdits(allow_always), default(allow_once), plan(reject_once)]`. The bug meant a reflexive Enter/click on an ExitPlanMode card silently flipped the whole session into an unattended mode, after which `requestPermission` is never called again (`bypassPermissions` short-circuit).

**Fixed**: same `pickDefaultAllow` fix resolves this too — now correctly picks `default` ("manually approve edits"), the conservative option.

### C. `pendingPermissions` had no depth cap (Medium, chains with A/B)

Unlike the sibling elicitation channel (already capped earlier in this session after its own flood finding), nothing bounded how many permission requests could queue, and no queue-depth indicator existed — manufacturing the "reflexively mash Enter to clear the pile" precondition that makes findings A/B exploitable in practice via a burst of injected-content-triggered tool calls.

**Fixed**: `MAX_PENDING_PERMISSIONS = 10` in `bridge.ts`, checked before registering a request — deny immediately past the cap. `PermissionPrompt.jsx` now shows a "+N more waiting" indicator.

### D. Unsanitized/unbounded tool-call title rendering (Medium)

`toolCall.title` is model-controlled (for `Bash`, the raw shell command) with no length bound or defensive CSS on `.chat-perm-hd b` — the gate's core value proposition ("you can see what you're approving") had no rendering guarantee.

**Fixed**: `.chat-perm-hd b` clamps to one line with ellipsis; full string reachable via a native `title` tooltip.

## Exploit chain (composed)

A burst of tool calls (manufactured via prompt-injected content the agent reads during a legitimate task — the accepted "hostile repo" threat model DDR-125 already scoped this feature for) exploits the missing queue cap (C) to induce alert fatigue and reflexive fast-clicking. Each reflexive Enter/click resolves to `allow_always` (A) instead of a one-time approval — the user believes they approved one action; they granted standing exemptions. If the burst includes an `ExitPlanMode` request, the same reflex flips the session into unattended `auto` mode (B), after which every subsequent injected-content-directed tool call runs with zero human review.

## Confirmed clean

- No bypass of `resolvePermission`'s optionId validation — an unoffered/stale/unknown id is rejected, not treated as implicit allow.
- Canvas-origin structurally cannot reach `permission-response` (confirmed via `server.ts`/`ws.ts` route registration, not a comment).
- No confused-deputy path between MCP servers (per-request nonce + per-request `optionIds` set).
- The safety-critical decision IS gated on a real human click (correct architecture) — the flaw was entirely in which option the human's OWN affordances (Enter, primary button) were pre-wired toward, not in the backend validation.

## Adversarial-creativity finding

`kindClass()`'s own code comment described its intended behavior correctly ("drives which button style reads as 'the safe default' (allow) vs 'the escape hatch' (reject)") while the code did the opposite — the MOST permissive option got the primary styling. This class of bug survives review indefinitely because it only exists at the seam between two files (`PermissionPrompt.jsx`'s styling logic and the third-party adapter's option-ordering source) that nobody reviews together.

# Security review — defender pass — retroactive review of DDR-179 permission gate (commit `4174b82e`)

**Date:** 2026-07-16 · **Reviewer:** `security-auditor` (flow plugin) · **Scope:** already-committed permission-gate code, never previously reviewed despite the plan's own Validation §7 requiring it

## Verdict

**0 blockers, 1 warning (informational).** Backend logic fully sound.

## Scope

`apps/studio/acp/bridge.ts` (`requestPermission`, `pendingPermissions`, `resolvePermission`, `denyAllPendingPermissions`), `apps/studio/acp/index.ts` (permission-request/-response frame handling), `apps/studio/client/panels/acp-runtime.js`, `apps/studio/client/panels/PermissionPrompt.jsx`, `apps/studio/test/acp-permission.test.ts`, plus the WS route gate in `server.ts`/`ws.ts` and the vendored `@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp` adapter source to verify DDR-179's own claims.

## Key findings

- `bypassPermissions` confirmed to short-circuit adapter-side before `requestPermission` ever fires (traced into the vendored adapter source). `dontAsk`'s exact short-circuit point could not be independently confirmed (lives in the closed-source `claude` CLI binary) — flagged as a verification gap, not a vulnerability, since either plausible behavior (deny-without-prompt or fall-through-to-real-prompt) is safe; worst case is a UX label mismatch.
- Timeout/turn-cancel/teardown all fail closed to deny — traced every code path.
- `/_ws/acp` gated by `isLoopbackHost` + `isSameOriginWs` (CSWSH defense), structurally separate from the canvas-origin route allowlist — confirmed by reading `server.ts` directly.
- An unoffered `optionId` collapses to `cancelled` — validated against the SPECIFIC request's own `optionIds` set, not a global allowlist.
- `ExitPlanMode` builds its own distinct option set and can't be confused with a normal file-edit approval's options (different optionIds, validated per-request).
- DDR-123 guardrails (`scrubAgentEnv`, `CLAUDE_CODE_EXECUTABLE` pin) untouched.

## Note

The implementation's own comments pre-empt most of the exact attack classes checked for (unoffered-optionId pinning, cross-socket bridge isolation, CSWSH). No remediation required from the defender's own scope.

## See also

The ethical-hacker pass run in parallel over the same code found 4 real client-side findings the defender's diff-shaped review didn't surface — the permission card's default UI affordance (Enter key + primary button) resolved to the wrong (most-permissive) option. See the sibling attacker report and DDR-179's own addendum for the full writeup and fixes.

decision.rationale:
# Security review — feature-1-artboard-kinds-foundation

**Date:** 2026-07-16
**Commits reviewed:** `0e001da7` (feature), fixed in `0a25d508`
**Branch:** `main`
**severityFloor:** medium · **includeAi:** true · **scope:** classic, ai

## Verdict

PASS after fix. One MEDIUM finding, independently confirmed by both passes, fixed and regression-tested before this review closed.

## Defender pass (security-auditor)

Reviewed the 3 flagged areas — all PASS:

1. New routes `/_api/set-artboard-kind` + `/_api/set-artboard-guides` (`http.ts`) — correctly main-origin-only (`sameOriginWrite` + `isLoopbackHost`, absent from `CANVAS_SAFE_API` and the canvas `routes` map). Size caps (2KB/8KB) enforced by the streaming `readJson` reader, not bypassable via a lying `content-length`.
2. `applySetArtboardGuides`'s `guides={${JSON.stringify(guides)}}` splice (`canvas-edit.ts`) — safe by construction. `JSON.stringify` always emits balanced, fully-escaped JS; the value sits in a JS expression container (not an HTML/attribute-string context), so no markup breakout is possible. Reparse gate is defense-in-depth.
3. `overlays` lane / `normalizeOverlays` (`api.ts`) — bounds correctly enforced (32 keys, 64-char keys, boolean-only values); path containment reuses the existing `canvasViewPath` → `canvasSourceAbs` guard, no new path construction.

Found 1 net-new MEDIUM (below), outside the 3 flagged areas.

## Adversarial pass (ethical-hacker)

Independently found the same MEDIUM finding via a different framing (threat-modeled from "attacker fully controls canvas source" rather than "review these 3 named surfaces"). Verified 3 additional surfaces as safe:

1. Unvalidated `kind` string reaching `data-dc-kind` — no injection sink (React attribute, static CSS selector, string-compare reads only).
2. `registerKindOverlay` confused-deputy — not reachable from the untrusted canvas (not re-exported via `@maude/canvas-lib`, per-iframe realm isolation).
3. Rate-limiting order on the new API ops — `takeStructuralToken()` runs before any expensive work in both `setArtboardKindOp`/`setArtboardGuidesOp`.

## Finding — MEDIUM (fixed)

**Unbounded `columns`/`rows` band count → client-side DoS.**
`apps/studio/artboard-guides-overlay.tsx`, `computeBands()`. The grid-line path had a documented cap (`MAX_GRID_LINES_PER_AXIS = 400`) but the columns/rows band-generation loop had none. `guides` is an artboard-authored JSX prop — part of the DDR-054 untrusted-canvas surface, reachable via a poisoned dependency, a malicious collaborator's PR/branch (phase-30 branch-scoped multiplayer), or a prompt-injected agent edit — and the value never round-trips through server-side validation before it's read at render time. A canvas author (or malicious peer push) setting `guides={{ columns: { count: 1e9 } }}` mounts a billion `<div>`s in the viewer's tab, causing a freeze/OOM.

Both reviews additionally noted the guides render is default-hidden (`visibility.guides !== true`), but the canvas-origin-reachable `/_api/canvas-meta` PATCH `overlays` lane lets a canvas self-enable its own guide visibility with no user interaction, so "guides are off by default" is not a mitigating control on its own.

**Fix (`0a25d508`):** added `MAX_BANDS_PER_AXIS = 64` and clamped `count` (`Math.min(Math.max(0, Math.floor(def.count)), MAX_BANDS_PER_AXIS)`) before the band loop, mirroring the existing grid-line cap. Regression tests added: `a pathologically large column count is clamped, never a runaway render` and the row-axis equivalent, both in `apps/studio/test/artboard-guides-overlay.test.tsx`.

## Non-blocking notes

- a11y-auditor (parallel fan-out, not a security pass but recorded here for completeness): W1 (kind absent from the artboard's accessible name) was also fixed in `0a25d508`. W2 (chip-icon contrast unverified — needs a live token render) remains open, tracked as a follow-up.
- design-system-guard: 2 non-blocking style notes (hardcoded guide colors, documented + precedent-backed; a `--fg-2` fallback nit). No action taken.

decision.rationale:
# Security review — config hot-reload (commit ac8dea0), defender pass

- **Commit:** `ac8dea0` — `fix(studio): hot-reload .design/config.json so mid-session scaffolds reach the file tree`
- **Scope:** `apps/studio/context.ts` (`reloadConfig`), `server.ts` (fs:json subscriber + 150 ms debounce), `ws.ts` (`config-updated` relay), `canvas-list-watch.ts` (use-time group read), `client/app.jsx` (refetch `/_config`), tests.
- **Severity floor:** `medium` (`.ai/workflows.config.json` has no `security` block → default). No finding reaches the floor.
- **Verdict: PASS WITH SUGGESTIONS.**

## Summary

The change re-reads `.design/config.json` on disk change and mutates `ctx.cfg` + derived
paths in place. The core security properties hold:

- **The `config-updated` WS broadcast is inspector/same-origin only** (concern 3 — clean).
  `ws.ts:212` wires it through `broadcast()`, which filters `ws.data.kind !== 'inspector'`
  (`ws.ts:147-153`). The untrusted canvas origin's socket is `kind: 'canvas-hmr'` and never
  receives it. The payload is a bare `{type:'config-updated'}` with no config values, so even
  a mis-delivery would leak nothing. The follow-on `/_config` refetch (`client/app.jsx`) hits a
  route that is **main-origin only** — `/_config` is explicitly excluded from `CANVAS_SAFE_API`
  (`http.ts:1687` comment + set at `1642-1650`), as is `/_index-data`.

- **`config.json` writes remain trusted-only.** The untrusted canvas origin (DDR-054) has no
  file-write route that can reach `.design/config.json`: the canvas-reachable writes
  (`/_api/canvas-meta`, `/_api/annotations`, `/_api/asset`, comment reply) all derive fixed
  slug-scoped paths, none writes an arbitrary/top-level file. So hot-reloading `config.json`
  does **not** cross a trust boundary that boot-time reading didn't already cross — the writer
  is still the trusted agent / `maude design link` CLI / the server's own adopt-clear.

- **`designRoot` is explicitly guarded** from live swap (`context.ts:283-289` — warn + keep old),
  which is the right call since the fs-watcher and every runtime path hang off it.

- **The in-place mutation is race-safe as written.** `context.ts:294-296` does
  `for(key) delete cfg[key]` then `Object.assign(cfg, next)` with **no `await` between them**;
  the single-threaded event loop guarantees no concurrent request observes the transient empty
  object (concern 5 — clean, but see S3 for brittleness).

- **Path recomputes stay repoRoot-confined.** `tokensUrlRel`/`systemDirRel` are rebuilt via
  `path.posix.join` (`context.ts:299-304`); any traversal in `tokensCssRel` is re-confined by
  the file-serving resolver (`safePathUnderRoot`, repoRoot floor). Same handling as boot
  (`createContext:242`).

The residual items below are all **low / defense-in-depth**, gated behind trusted write access
to `config.json`, and bounded by main-origin-only display + resolver confinement.

## Findings (severity-ordered)

| # | Sev | Location | Issue | Fix |
|---|-----|----------|-------|-----|
| S1 | low | `context.ts:283-304`, `canvas-list-watch.ts:104` | **`config.json` is git-versioned**, so a peer-committed config now hot-applies on `git checkout` / branch-switch / "Get latest" (fs:json fires) **without the operator restart previously required**. Combined with the absence of a designRoot-containment check, a hostile committed `canvasGroups:[{path:"../.."}]` (or `tokensCssRel:"../.."`) live-repoints the file-tree walk (`findHtmlFiles(path.join(designRoot, g.path))`) at repo paths outside `designRoot`. Bounded: results render only to the local main-origin tree (no exfil channel back to the committer), designRoot itself is guarded, and file opens are resolver-confined to repoRoot — so this is info-scope/DoS-ish, not RCE/exfil. | In `reloadConfig` (and ideally `createContext`), validate each `canvasGroups[].path` and `tokensCssRel` resolves **inside** `designRoot`; on violation warn + keep the prior value (the same "keep running config" pattern already used for `designRoot`). |
| S2 | low | `context.ts:294-296` + `server.ts` fs:json handler | **`linkedHub` is hot-swapped into `ctx.cfg`, but the sync runtime lifecycle is boot-bound** (`createSyncRuntime` captures `linkedHub` once at `sync/index.ts:218`, invoked once at `server.ts:429`; the reload handler never re-inits it). Net effect is an inconsistent state, not a redirect: a live `linkedHub` add/change/remove is *not* applied to the running sync (the WS provider stays on the boot URL), yet use-time readers like `resolveSyncable` (`sync/index.ts:912`, `ctx.cfg.linkedHub?.syncTsx`) *do* see the swapped value — so which canvases count as syncable can drift out of step with the hub the socket is actually attached to. | Exclude `linkedHub` from hot-reload the same way `designRoot` is (warn "restart to change hub link" + keep old), OR wire a real sync teardown/restart on hub change. Excluding is simpler and matches the boot-bound reality. |
| S3 | low | `context.ts:294-296` | The delete-all-then-`Object.assign` swap is race-safe **only** because it is synchronous. A future maintainer inserting any `await` between the delete loop and the assign would expose a transient empty `ctx.cfg` to concurrent requests (`cfg.name`, `cfg.canvasGroups` undefined → 500s / mis-gates). The invariant is implicit. | Pin it: add a "no await between delete and Object.assign — cfg must never be observably empty" comment, or compute the key-delete set and merge without a wide empty window. |
| S4 | info | `server.ts` fs:json handler; `context.ts:270` | DoS via config write-thrash is **not reachable from the untrusted canvas origin** (canvas can't write `config.json`); an attacker who can thrash the file already has trusted repo write. Each debounced reload does a synchronous `readFileSync` + `JSON.parse` + 2× full-cfg `JSON.stringify` deep-compare + an async `canvasListWatch.refresh()` full-tree walk. The 150 ms debounce is adequate for the legitimate single-write case, and `config.json` (`.json`, not `.tsx`/`.html`) is correctly rejected by `isCanvasCandidate`, so the watch's own fs:any subscription does not double-fire. No action required. | — (acknowledge in threat model; `readFileSync` blocking the loop is negligible for the small config and matches the pre-existing `createContext` pattern.) |

## Concern-by-concern (as requested)

1. **Privilege escalation via attacker-writable config.json** — No *new* trust boundary is
   crossed: `config.json` is trusted-write-only (canvas origin cannot reach it). The honest delta
   is provenance + timing (S1): the file is versioned, so a peer-committed config now takes effect
   on checkout without a restart, and `canvasGroups`/`tokensCssRel` are applied live without a
   containment check. `designRoot` is guarded; `linkedHub` is lifecycle-bound (S2). Impact stays
   low (main-origin display only, resolver repoRoot-confined).
2. **DoS via write-thrash** — Not reachable from the untrusted origin; 150 ms debounce adequate;
   no double-trigger. See S4.
3. **`config-updated` broadcast reachability** — Inspector-only, confirmed at `ws.ts:147-153,212`;
   canvas-hmr sockets excluded; empty payload. Clean.
4. **Path handling in reloadConfig** — `designRoot` guarded; `tokensUrlRel`/`systemDirRel`
   recompute is resolver-confined to repoRoot; missing containment check on `canvasGroups`/
   `tokensCssRel` is the only gap (S1), pre-existing at boot and now live.
5. **In-place mutation races** — Safe: the delete+assign is synchronous with no `await` window,
   so no torn/empty read is observable. Brittle to future edits (S3).

decision.title: Adversarial security review — config.json hot-reload (commit `ac8dea0`)
decision.rationale:
# Adversarial security review — config.json hot-reload (commit `ac8dea0`)

**Reviewer role:** attacker-pass (ethical-hacker persona)
**Scope:** `git show ac8dea0` — dev-server `.design/config.json` hot-reload
(`context.ts reloadConfig` in-place `ctx.cfg` mutation; `server.ts` debounced
`fs:json`→reload→`canvasListWatch.refresh` + `config-updated` bus emit; `ws.ts`
broadcast; `client/app.jsx` `/_config` refetch).
**Threat surface:** loopback-only dev server (`http://localhost:<port>`), default
cross-origin canvas split (DDR-054), ACP chat agent as a config writer.
**Date:** 2026-07-03

---

## Verdict: **PASS WITH SUGGESTIONS**

The commit is a clean, well-scoped fix. It introduces **no new cross-origin or
remote-reachable vulnerability**. What it changes is *timing*: two pre-existing
"poisoned-config" primitives (canvasGroups path-escape and tokensCssRel
path-escape) go from **restart-gated** to **live**, and both land only in the
user's **own same-origin trusted shell** on a loopback server — not a remote
attacker. The single genuinely dangerous vector the fix could have opened — a
live hub re-point — is **correctly avoided**: the sync runtime is fully
boot-pinned.

The suggestions below are defense-in-depth. They harden pre-existing code, but
this commit — which makes those primitives fire without a restart — is the right
moment to add the clamp.

---

## Threat model: who can write `.design/config.json` at runtime?

| Writer | Reachable? | Weaponizable via this commit? |
| ------ | ---------- | ----------------------------- |
| **ACP chat agent** (`/design:setup-ds`) | Yes — writes config.json legitimately | Already holds `Write` + `Bash`; hot-reload adds ~nothing (see AI surface) |
| **Repo collaborator** via `git checkout`/`pull` | Yes — config.json is a versioned file; checkout fires `fs:json` | Malicious branch's config now takes effect without restart. Impact = same-origin shell only (below) |
| **Hub sync** | **No** — sync moves per-canvas `.tsx`/`.meta.json`/comments/annotations only; it never syncs `config.json` | n/a |
| **Malicious canvas** (untrusted iframe, DDR-054) | **No** — no `CANVAS_SAFE_API` write route targets `config.json` (meta-PATCH writes `<canvas>.meta.json`; asset upload → assets dir; comments → `_comments/`). And the canvas origin cannot even *read* `/_index-data` or `/_config` (neither is in `CANVAS_SAFE_API`) | n/a |
| **Hand edit** | Yes | Same as collaborator |

**Bottom line:** the only writers are already-privileged local actors (the agent,
a collaborator's git tree, the user). The untrusted canvas iframe — the one
principal DDR-054 designates hostile — can neither write config.json nor read
the endpoints the reload feeds.

---

## Findings (severity-ordered)

### 1. LOW — `canvasGroups[].path` `../` traversal into `/_index-data`, now live without restart
- **Chain:** poisoned config sets `canvasGroups: [{label:"x", path:"../../../../home/user"}]` → `buildIndexData` (`api.ts:1690`) does `path.join(designRoot, g.path)` with **no designRoot clamp** → `findFiles` `readdir`-walks the escaped dir and lists `.tsx/.html/.md/.css/.json` filenames (skips `.git`, `node_modules`, `_`-prefixed, dotfiles except `.ai`/`.claude`/`.design`). The same unclamped `path.join(designRoot, g.path)` is in `canvas-list-watch.ts:104`.
- **Reality check:** `/_index-data` is **not** in `CANVAS_SAFE_API`, so the untrusted canvas cannot fetch it. The escaped filenames surface only into the **user's own same-origin file tree**. This is filename disclosure to the local user's own screen, not a remote/cross-origin leak. Pre-existing at boot; this commit removes the restart gate.
- **Fix:** clamp each `groupAbs` to `designRoot` (reject or drop a `g.path` whose `path.resolve` escapes `designRoot`) in `buildIndexData` **and** `canvas-list-watch.ts snapshot()` — ideally at config-load time in `normalizeConfig`/`reloadConfig`.

### 2. LOW — `tokensCssRel` `../` traversal (served as a stylesheet), now live without restart
- **Chain:** poisoned config sets `tokensCssRel:"../../../secret.env"`-shaped value → `tokensUrlRel` (`context.ts:299`) / per-DS `tokensCssRel` flows into the `<link>` the shell + `_canvas-shell.html` load → the generic file route (`safePathUnderRoot`, `http.ts:1577`) re-confines to **repoRoot**, so any repoRoot file's **bytes** can be pulled in as CSS.
- **Reality check:** confined to repoRoot; content lands in the user's own shell/canvas-shell render, not exfiltrated cross-origin (canvas origin's `connect-src 'self'` still holds). Pre-existing at boot; this commit makes it restart-free.
- **Fix:** validate `tokensCssRel` (top-level and per-DS) stays within `designRoot` in `normalizeConfig`/`reloadConfig`; reject `..` escapes.

### 3. INFO — DoS via a config.json rewrite storm
- **Chain:** rapid rewrites of config.json → each debounced (150 ms) reload costs a `readFileSync` + `JSON.parse` + a double `JSON.stringify` deep-compare + `canvasListWatch.refresh()` (a full disk walk of every canvas group). Amplified if `canvasGroups` points at a huge tree via `..` (finding 1), each refresh re-walks it.
- **Reality check:** bounded and debounced; requires local repo-write on a loopback box (already game-over-adjacent). Negligible.
- **Fix:** none required. Optionally cap refresh cadence; the finding-1 designRoot clamp also bounds the walk.

### 4. INFO — functional dead-spot (not a vulnerability, noted for correctness)
`reloadConfig` always reads `<repoRoot>/.design/config.json` (hardcoded in `loadConfig`), but the `fs:json` guard `rel === 'config.json'` fires relative to `designRoot`. If a project sets `designRoot` ≠ `.design`, edits to the *watched* `config.json` and the *read* `.design/config.json` diverge — reload either never fires or reads a different/absent file (safely kept via the `_source` guard). No security impact.

---

## Positives observed (defenses that hold)

- **Vector (c) — live hub re-point — is closed.** `createSyncRuntime` runs **once** at boot (`server.ts:429`) and captures `const linked = ctx.cfg.linkedHub` (`sync/index.ts:218`). `reloadConfig` never re-invokes it. The `onRead` FsReader (`sync/index.ts:373`) dispatches only to **boot-scan** agents/projections; a canvas appearing post-reload that matches no agent is an explicit "harmless no-op" (line 367-368). So the hub URL, token, **and** the syncable canvas set are all boot-pinned — a mid-session `linkedHub`/`syncTsx` swap re-points nothing. `getHubToken` + `checkUrlScheme` + the CI gate remain as further hurdles even across a restart.
- **`config-updated` is inspector-only.** `ws.ts:212` routes it through `broadcast` (filters `ws.data.kind === 'inspector'`), so the untrusted `canvas-hmr` sockets never receive it and the canvas cannot even learn a reload happened.
- **No torn-read window.** `reloadConfig` is fully synchronous (`readFileSync`, no `await`) between the `delete`-all loop and `Object.assign`; Bun's single-threaded JS means no request handler can observe an empty `ctx.cfg`.
- **`_source` guard blocks downgrade-to-defaults.** A half-written / missing / invalid config mid-edit keeps the running config instead of silently resetting to `DEFAULT_CONFIG` — this prevents a truncated-save transient from dropping the running config to a weaker state.
- **No self-triggering write loop.** The reload path only *reads* config.json; nothing in the `fs:json` handler writes it back. (`clearAdopt` does write config.json once, which now triggers one benign reload — not a loop.)
- **No security control lives in config.json.** The canvas origin split / CSP is env-driven (`MAUDE_CANVAS_ORIGIN_SPLIT`), not config-driven, so a config reload cannot disable the sandbox.

---

## Mandatory AI/MCP surface assessment

The ACP chat agent writes config.json as part of `/design:setup-ds`, so an
**indirect prompt injection** (a poisoned synced canvas, hostile web-research
content the agent ingests) could instruct the agent to write a malicious
config.json, now effective without a restart. Realistic impact:

- The agent **already holds `Write` + `Bash`** — a prompt-injected agent is
  game-over on the dev machine independent of this commit. Hot-reloading
  config.json grants it **no capability it did not already have** (it can read
  any file via `Read`, write any file, run any command).
- The one escalation an injected agent **cannot** achieve through config is a
  live sync re-point to an attacker-controlled hub — boot-pinned URL + missing
  token + scheme allowlist all block it (see Positives).
- Findings 1–2 (traversal) are no help to an agent that already has direct
  filesystem read.

Net AI-surface risk from this commit: **negligible**. The load-bearing
mitigation is the boot-pinning of the sync destination, which the commit
correctly preserves.

---

## Recommendation

Ship. As a follow-up hardening (belt-and-suspenders, closes findings 1 & 2 at
the source), add a `designRoot` containment clamp for `canvasGroups[].path` and
`tokensCssRel` inside `normalizeConfig`/`reloadConfig` so a `../` escape is
rejected at config-load time rather than relying on the downstream repoRoot
confinement and the canvas-origin allowlist to keep the blast radius local.

decision.title: # Security defender audit — 6 files scanned (DDR-084 server-up boots compiled binary)
decision.rationale:
## Security defender audit — 6 files scanned (DDR-084 server-up boots compiled binary)

### Evidence sources
- Diff base: `3873a3a` (merge-base main..HEAD)
- Branch: `feat/setup-ds-round2-scaffold-integrity-gates`
- Changed files in scope: `cli/commands/design.mjs`, `plugins/design/dev-server/bin/server-up.sh`,
  `plugins/design/dev-server/bin/visual-sanity.sh`, `plugins/design/skills/design-system/_bootstrap.md`,
  `plugins/design/agents/design-system-completeness-critic.md`,
  `plugins/design/templates/design-system-inspiration/SUB-AGENT-PROMPTS.md`
- Supporting (read, not in requested set but load-bearing for trust model): `cli/install.cjs` (side-channel writer)
- Lockfile changes: no (uncommitted changes are regenerated `dist/runtime/*.js` bundles only — not dep surface)
- severityFloor: medium (no `security` block in config → defaults). scope: default (classic in scope).

### Trust model (the lens for every finding below)
This is a developer CLI. The package install directory (`<pkgRoot>/cli/.platform-binary-path`),
the process environment (`MAUDE_DEV_SERVER_BIN`, `MAUDE_FORCE_SOURCE`), and `$PATH` are ALL already
under the control of the user invoking `maude`. An attacker who can write the side-channel file or
set the env var inside the user's own install already has code-exec as that user by simpler means
(edit `server.ts`, prepend `$PATH`, replace the binary the path points at). So the spawn surface is
evaluated as "does this WIDEN the trust boundary beyond what the user already controls?" — not as a
classic untrusted-input-to-exec sink.

### Blockers (severity >= medium)
None.

### Warnings (below floor / defense-in-depth)

- `plugins/design/dev-server/bin/server-up.sh:72` — A8-adjacent / input-handling (low)
  - Snippet: `CAND="$(cat "$SC" 2>/dev/null)"`
  - Why: `cat` of the side-channel slurps the WHOLE file, including a trailing newline and any
    second line. The Node writer (`cli/install.cjs:97`) writes a single bare path with no newline,
    and `runServe`/`resolveServerBinary` `.trim()` it — but the shell path does NOT trim. A path
    with a trailing newline would make the subsequent `[ -x "$CAND" ]` fail (newline in the path),
    so it fails safe to the `bun server.ts` fallback rather than spawning something wrong. A
    multi-line file would have only the first... actually `$(cat)` collapses to the full content;
    the `[ -x ]` test then fails on embedded newline. Net effect: hostile/garbled content can only
    DENY the binary path (fall back to source), never redirect the spawn to an arbitrary target.
  - Fix (optional, hardening parity): mirror the Node side — `CAND="$(head -n1 "$SC" 2>/dev/null)"`
    or pipe through trimming, so the two readers agree byte-for-byte on the contract.

- `plugins/design/dev-server/bin/server-up.sh:73,87,186` — A1-adjacent / TOCTOU (low, not exploitable under trust model)
  - Snippet: `[ -n "$CAND" ] && [ -x "$CAND" ] && SERVER_BIN="$CAND"` … later `nohup "$SERVER_BIN" --root "$REPO"`
  - Why: classic time-of-check/time-of-use gap between the `[ -x "$SERVER_BIN" ]` guards (lines 73,
    87) and the `nohup "$SERVER_BIN"` spawn (line 186). An attacker who can swap the file at
    `$SERVER_BIN` between check and spawn could substitute a binary. BUT the path is sourced from
    the user's own install dir / own env, and whoever can win that race can also just overwrite the
    target file outright at any time — the race adds no capability beyond what the trust model
    already grants. Quoting is correct throughout: `"$SERVER_BIN"` and `"$REPO"` are double-quoted
    at the spawn site, so there is NO word-splitting / glob / injection even with a path containing
    spaces or shell metacharacters. The binary is exec'd as argv[0], NOT passed through `sh -c`, so
    its path content cannot be interpreted as a command string.
  - Fix: none required. Documented as accepted residual TOCTOU.

- `plugins/design/skills/design-system/_bootstrap.md:181` + `design-system-completeness-critic.md:59`
  — A1-adjacent ReDoS on attacker-influenced generated files (low)
  - Snippet: `grep -rnEi '[3-9](\.[0-9]+)?\s*:\s*1|✓\s*(AA|AAA)|passes (AA|AAA)| ...'`
  - Why: the V24/A4 contrast-claim grep and the V23/A3b React-import grep scan agent-GENERATED
    `preview/*.tsx` + CSS. These files are produced by the bootstrap sub-agents, not by an external
    attacker, so they are not an adversarial input channel. The regexes themselves carry no
    catastrophic-backtracking construct (no nested quantifiers over an alternation, no `(a+)+`
    shape) — `[3-9](\.[0-9]+)?\s*:\s*1` is linear; `grep -E` (POSIX, not PCRE) uses a DFA-class
    engine that is not subject to exponential backtracking regardless. No ReDoS.
  - Fix: none.

- `plugins/design/skills/design-system/_bootstrap.md:146-153` — A9-adjacent / file traversal in scan loops (informational)
  - Snippet: `while IFS= read -r f; do sz=$(wc -c < "$f" ...) ... done < <(find "$DS_PREVIEW" -type f ...)`
  - Why: the non-empty/CSS-comment/React gates iterate `find` output with `IFS= read -r` and quote
    `"$f"` consistently — correct handling of paths with spaces. `wc -c < "$f"` and `grep ... "$f"`
    never pass the filename to a shell-eval context. The `<designRoot>/system/<ds>/` interpolation
    is a documentation placeholder filled by the orchestrating agent from config, not from end-user
    free text. No `eval`, no unquoted expansion, no command substitution over file CONTENT (only
    over `wc`/`grep` output, which is numeric/line data). Clean.
  - Fix: none.

### Dependency surface
- New deps: none. No `package.json` / lockfile changes in the diff.
- The uncommitted `dist/runtime/*.js` are regenerated Bun.build bundles (CLAUDE.md documents these as
  committed + authoritative; `check-runtime-bundles.sh` gates them in CI). Out of this audit's scope
  (not in the requested file set; not a dependency-manifest change).
- Flagged: none.

### Notes (project-specific)
- The side-channel pattern (`cli/.platform-binary-path`) is NOT new in this branch — it predates
  DDR-084 (`runServe` at `design.mjs:201-208` already read+spawned from it; `cli/install.cjs:97`
  writes it). This branch's `resolveServerBinary` (`design.mjs:324`) is a read-only, non-caching,
  never-hard-fail MIRROR of that existing resolution order, and `server-up.sh` gains a shell-side
  reader of the same file. So the change EXTENDS an already-trusted, already-shipped mechanism to a
  second consumer rather than introducing a new exec-from-data sink. Both readers validate
  `existsSync(candidate)` / `[ -x "$CAND" ]` before use and fall back to source on any miss.
- `resolveServerBinary` correctly returns `null` (→ source) in the dev tree and under
  `MAUDE_FORCE_SOURCE=1`; the new tests (`design.test.mjs`) cover dev-tree, force-source, and
  production-side-channel paths. The Node reader `.trim()`s the file; the shell reader does not
  (the only daylight between the two — see the line-72 warning, fails-safe).
- `MAUDE_DEV_SERVER_BIN` env injection at `design.mjs:106` is gated by `BOOT_VERBS` and only set when
  the env is not already present; it carries the resolved path into `server-up.sh` via the `env`
  option of `spawnSync` (not interpolated into a command string). No shell injection vector.
- The `nohup "$SERVER_BIN" --root "$REPO"` spawn redirects to `"$DESIGN_ROOT/_server.log"` with
  proper quoting; `$REPO` derives from `--root`/`$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`/`git rev-parse`/`pwd` (all
  user-scoped) and is quoted at the spawn site.

Summary: 0 blockers, ~4 warnings (all low / defense-in-depth), 0 deps flagged. The process-spawn and
side-channel-read surface is ACCEPTABLE under the stated developer-tool trust model. The single
concrete hardening worth taking is `head -n1` parity for the shell-side side-channel read (line 72).
